home_pitcher_note: Lohse's long winter of uncertainty came to an end when he hooked on with the Cardinals, and the club is delighted to have him. While the projections for his payday were fairly outlandish, Lohse has been a useful pitcher for most of his career. He has four seasons of at least 180 innings and five years with 30 or more starts. Lohse had been scheduled for one more tuneup in a simulated game, but thanks to the rainout, he'll go on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Wells signed a $3.1 million, one-year deal with the Rockies this winter and hoped to make the starting rotation, but his inefficiency early in camp led the club to put him in long relief. Wells disagreed with the decision, but pitched better in his last two spring appearances as the Rockies prepared him for bullpen work. Now, however, after Friday's opener was postponed and no rotation member was available, Wells gets a chance to do what he wanted all along.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer was a revelation for the Cardinals after they plucked him off waivers from the Royals. He still had some trouble keeping the ball in the park, but he did an excellent job of corralling his walk rate. It remains to be seen how Wellemeyer will fare as a full-time Major League starter, having made his first 11 career starts last season in St. Louis. But pitching coach Dave Duncan is a big believer, and that's a good ally to have.
away_pitcher_note: Cook was the Rockies' No. 1 starter last season and struggled to a 5-6, 4.68 ERA performance before the All-Star break. He turned hot in the second half, going 3-1, 2.41 in six starts before suffering an oblique injury.

home_pitcher_note: It seems like forever that Thompson has been a swingman trying to secure a starting job with the Cardinals, but he's been in the organization for fewer than three full seasons. Still, this is a new opportunity for Thompson, getting the call to join the starting rotation from the beginning of the year. His sinker is an exceptional pitch with serious movement, and when it's good, he can throw it a huge percentage of the time.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez gave the Rockies a lift in 16 games after being called up in August. But before being promoted, consistency was an issue, and fastball command was a problem throughout Spring Training.

home_pitcher_note: The overall numbers for 2007 weren't pretty, but September was sparkling. After going 0-4 with the Braves, Redman bounced around the Minors until joining the Rockies in September. In five games, including three starts, Redman went 2-0 with a 3.20 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Owings struggled throughout the spring with his command. Last year, he made the team as the fifth starter and wound up making 27 starts and two relief appearances. Owings doesn't have overpowering stuff, but overcomes it with competitiveness.

home_pitcher_note: Francis received a fortunate do-over. He was trailing the Cardinals, 5-1, in the bottom of the third on Wednesday when rains hit and washed away the game. Francis had given up an Albert Pujols home run and had walked five -- one shy of his career high. The struggles came out of nowhere for Francis, who had a 3.00 ERA in Spring Training. Francis enters his first official start of 2008 in a place where he is comfortable. he is 26-13 with a 4.36 ERA in 50 starts at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Webb's numbers during Spring Training were not pretty, but he looked to be in midseason form on Opening Day against the Reds. The right-hander allowed two runs over six innings in a 4-2 D-backs win. It was Webb's first Opening Day win in three tries. He's known for his devastating sinker, but has developed his curve and change to the point where he can use both at any time in the game. He particularly likes to go with them when he has two strikes on a batter. Webb posted better numbers in 2007 than he did during his NL Cy Young Award season in 2006, but finished second in the balloting to San Diego's Jake Peavy.

home_pitcher_note: Going into last season, the Rockies thought Morales was their top pitching prospect but they didn't expect him to make the Majors. Injuries forced the Rockies to summon him late in the season, and it turned out swimmingly. Morales, however, struggled with fastball command and pitch selection this spring, but his talent and his power fastball justify his inclusion on the staff to begin the season.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez will start the year in the rotation as the club takes things slowly with Randy Johnson, who is recovering from his second back surgery in as many years. Gonzalez's ability to both start and work out of the bullpen made him a valuable part of the staff last year. It's a role he figures to fill again once Johnson returns in mid-April. Gonzalez doesn't throw hard, but has a good feel for pitching and changes speeds effectively.

home_pitcher_note: Cook, looking for secondary pitches to enhance his sinker, mixed his changeup with his new cut fastball in his first start, an 8-3 Rockies loss to the Cardinals. He gave up six runs on four hits in six innings. His seven groundball outs were not as many as a normal start for him, but he left the outing feeling comfortable with how he used his new pitches. He'll need to sharpen the execution.
away_pitcher_note: Glavine surrendered two runs  -- one earned -- in five innings of Monday's home opener against the Pirates.  The veteran southpaw was pushed back from Sunday, when he would have faced the Mets, who employed him the past five years. He was in line for a victory into the seventh inning on Monday and was hurt by two separate two-out errors.

home_pitcher_note: What Jimenez lacked in efficiency, he made up for in persistence in his opening start of the season, a 3-0 road loss to the Cardinals. Jimenez threw 100 pitches in five innings, giving up seven hits and five walks (one intentional), with a couple of wild pitches. But he held the Cards to three runs and struck out four. He struggled against the Braves in his only previous start against them, giving up six runs on six hits and five walks, but getting seven strikeouts, in 4 2/3 innings of a 6-4 loss at Turner Field last Aug. 4.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens enjoyed a successful Atlanta debut on Wednesday night, when he limited the Pirates to two earned runs in 5 1/3 innings and got the win. The 22-year-old right-hander, who was acquired from the Tigers in October, surrendered three hits and both of those runs in the sixth inning. This will be his first career appearance against the Rockies and at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: After not walking anyone in official Spring Training games and walking just one in a Minor League game while camp was in session, Redman put himself in trouble by walking two in the first inning of Friday afternoon's home opener against the Diamondbacks. Redman never established early that he could hit the strike zone with his sinker, and the Diamondbacks hit his elevated pitches. He gave up nine hits, including a home run, and three walks. On the positive side, he struck out four.
away_pitcher_note: James didn't experience any problems during Spring Training with his left shoulder, and now he'll be looking to enjoy a successful season debut. He will make his first start in place of Mike Hampton, who is back on the disabled list with a strained pectoral muscle. James has won 11 games during both of his first two big league seasons. Primarily a two-pitch pitcher who has been susceptible to surrendering home runs, he has been working on a slider.

home_pitcher_note: Webb put to rest the question of whether he could beat the Rockies, allowing just two runs (one earned) on five hits over seven innings on Saturday night in Denver. Webb, who had struggled against the Rockies in 2007, put together his second strong start of the young season. On Opening Day against the Reds, the right-hander allowed two runs over six innings in a 4-2 win. It was Webb's first Opening Day win in three tries. He's known for his devastating sinker, but has developed his curve and change and can use both at any time in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Francis struggled against the Diamondbacks on Saturday, letting up five runs on 12 hits and a walk in 6 1/3 innings.  It was an improvement over his Opening Day washout, when five runs and five walks in 1 1/3 innings were expunged from the record, but it was not enough to satisfy the ace or keep his team in the game. He was especially vulnerable to the longball, giving up three home runs, two after getting ahead of the hitters 0-2 and 1-2, and the third on a 3-1 pitch when his changeup cut back over the plate.

home_pitcher_note: It's been a season of firsts for Haren. He made his first start in Chase Field his last time out and was impressive in allowing three runs over six innings. The right-hander said he got chills taking the mound for the first time in front of a packed house in Arizona's home opener. Haren made his D-backs debut April 2 and aside from one inning where he allowed three runs on a pair of homers, he pitched well. Haren was acquired by Arizona in an eight-player deal with the A's in December.
away_pitcher_note: Morales held the Diamondbacks scoreless on two hits in six innings on Sunday in his first start of 2008. He did struggle with runners on base and faced a lot of two-out traffic, but throughout the outing he hit his spots with a fastball that ranged from 91 to 93 mph. He showed no fear pitching inside to right-handed hitters. This will be his first appearance at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez continues to impress the organization with his flexibility. The right-hander has been a band-aid of sorts for the pitching staff over the past year, pitching in a variety of roles. He figures to be a member of the rotation for a while with Doug Davis headed to the DL. He made his first start of the year last Sunday in Denver after going nine days without pitching and showed no signs of rust as he allowed just one run over five innings. He did not get a decision in the game, which Arizona won in 10 innings. Gonzalez doesn't throw hard, but has a good feel for pitching and changes speeds effectively. He is incorporating a cut fastball more this year and his curveball has improved.
away_pitcher_note: Cook pitched a gem Monday, matching Tom Glavine in an efficient pitchers' duel as the Rockies took their first win at Coors Field. Cook gave up a pair of hits and a run in the first inning, but retired 20 of the next 21 hitters he faced, allowing only one walk the rest of the way as he pitched seven innings on 73 pitches. His good sinker earned 15 groundouts, and he took advantage of an aggressive Atlanta lineup on a cold Colorado night, attacking the bottom of the strike zone and inducing early swings from the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf pitched well for the second time in as many starts this season when the left-hander allowed two runs on five hits over six innings in a loss to the Giants on April 8. Wolf allowed the leadoff hitter to reach base in the second, third, fifth and sixth innings, but still managed to mostly avoid trouble. He walked one, giving him just three walks in two starts. He mixed a fastball, curveball and changeup well.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez found his rhythm against the Braves Tuesday night, earning a 4-3 victory with a quality start in which he yielded three runs on six hits and four walks. Two of his walks came in the first inning and two more came to the opposing pitcher. But after yielding a run in the first on two hits and a walk, Jimenez retired 16 of 19, allowing only one hit before losing steam in the sixth and elevating a two-seam fastball that went for a two-run homer. His two-seamer was otherwise effective, especially with his slider in good form.

home_pitcher_note: Germano, the No. 5 starter in the rotation, tossed seven shutout innings his last time out, tying the longest outing of his career. And he was thrifty, needing 83 pitches to get through the seventh. All told, Germano walked just one batter and had three strikeouts. He has yet to allow a run in 13 innings this season. Germano threw just five pitches in the fourth inning and eight in the sixth inning, getting the Giants out in front of his developing changeup and his curveball. For all his success, the Padres have scored just one run total in his first two starts.
away_pitcher_note: After having uncharacteristic wildness in his first start of the season, on April 4 against the Diamondbacks, Redman held the Braves to three runs (two earned) in five innings while winning Wednesday night at Coors Field. Since joining the Rockies late last season, Redman is 3-1 with a 3.86 ERA in seven games (five starts). After not having his changeup in the game with the Diamondbacks, Redman mixed that pitch with his fastball and worked both sides of the plate against the Braves. A San Diego-area native (Escondido High School), Redman is 0-0 with a 1.74 ERA in 10 1/3 innings, covering two games, at PETCO Park.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy didn't always have his best stuff, but he got better as the game went on in his last start against the Dodgers on Friday. He allowed seven hits and two runs over the first three innings, but just one run on two hits over the last three innings. Peavy, who is off to a 3-0 start, walked two and struck out four and defeated the Dodgers for the second time this season. He now faces the Rockies for the first time since the Padres lost the Wild Card play-in game in Denver on Oct. 1.
away_pitcher_note: Francis has to be happy to see anybody but the Diamondbacks, who have hit five home runs against him in his two starts this season. Francis has thrown a fair number of strikes, but not the quality of strikes that could keep the ball in the park against the D-backs' lineup. So he moves to PETCO Park and the Padres, who got the best of him last year (1-3, 6.61 ERA in five starts).

home_pitcher_note: Sampson struggled somewhat in his last start against the Cardinals. In that game on April 9, he gave up six hits and three earned runs in four innings. In two starts this season, Sampson has surrendered 12 hits and five earned runs in 10 2/3 innings. He has consistently been around the plate with just two strikeouts and one walk thus far.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching six scoreless innings against the Diamondbacks in his first start of the year, Morales struggled on Saturday, giving up seven runs and seven hits in just four innings, with Justin Upton's three-run homer in the fifth chasing him. Morales had his best stuff for just one inning, the fourth. He has dominating stuff, but his inexperience shows when he gets into trouble and can't make adjustments.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is enjoying a solid April, and his seven strong innings in Houston's 5-1 win over Florida on Sunday is making people take notice of the little lefty with the big curveball. Rodriguez's 2.33 ERA ranks among the Major League leaders, as does his strikeout total, which climbed to 19 with the seven he recorded against Florida. He's also spectacular at home. Rodriguez has allowed one earned run in 14 1/3 innings at home this season, good for a 0.63 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: For the second time, Cook pitched when the Rockies were in a losing streak and helped the club win. Cook went six innings and held the Diamondbacks to three runs and eight hits on Sunday. He ran into trouble in the fifth, when he left several sinkers up and eventually gave up a two-run triple to Jeff Salazar. But the anxiousness that dogged Cook in the past, especially when he was tabbed the Rockies' ace and had trouble controlling the urge to do too much, is not present this season.

home_pitcher_note: Chacon was brilliant in his last outing at Philadelphia, scattering four hits over eight scoreless innings. Despite lowering his ERA from 3.75 to 2.25, he didn't pick up the win as the Phillies rallied for four runs in the bottom of the ninth inning to win, 4-3. Chacon struck out five and walked two and threw 68 of his 109 pitches for strikes. This was Chacon's second straight quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez pitched well for four innings at PETCO Park on Tuesday night, displaying top-shelf velocity and an effective slider. But in the fifth, he committed a throwing error and relied too heavily on his fastball. The result was a six-run Padres inning in a 6-0 loss for the Rockies. Jimenez has bordered on dominant at points in all his starts, but must learn how to quickly find his rhythm when things get tight.

home_pitcher_note: On Wednesday night, Redman was effective with his changeup while holding the Padres to two runs and three hits over five frames to earn a win. Instead of simply throwing the fastball in the strike zone and having batters chase the changeup, he threw the change for strikes, baffling San Diego. Redman is pitching through a heel injury, but as long as he stays in the strike zone and gets quick outs the pain does not affect his pitching.
away_pitcher_note: After a six-walk performance against the Mets on April 9, Kendrick returned to attacking the strike zone on April 16, and it resulted in his best performance of the season. The right-hander allowed three runs in six innings in a start at Coors Field last season.

home_pitcher_note: After three bad outings -- one wiped out mercifully by rain, two that counted -- Francis was in top form in his last outing. He threw seven shutout innings, gave up three hits and struck out seven at San Diego, but wound up with a no-decision because Jake Peavy threw eight shutout innings. Francis has not been pitching outside effectively, but that didn't matter against the Padres. He was getting strikes and bad swings on the outside part of the plate.
away_pitcher_note: Myers has found a groove. After two subpar starts to start the season, the right-hander has allowed four runs in 15 innings. He's coming off a stellar start in which he held the Astros to one run and five hits in seven innings on April 17. Myers has thrived at Coors Field, with a 4-0 record and a 2.63 ERA there in four outings.

home_pitcher_note: After helping the club to the playoffs in a late callup last season, Morales is finding things more difficult as a member of the Opening Day rotation. But just when Morales was starting to look overwhelmed, he took a giant leap forward in his last start, a victory over the Astros. His team scored six first-inning runs but he gave up four in the bottom of the frame. But by doing what the Rockies asked -- quickening his tempo, not thinking as much -- Morales righted himself and didn't give up a run for the next four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hill is breathing a lot easier now. The young lefty picked up his first win in his last start on Friday against the Pirates. He had spent a week working on the side, and it paid off. Against Pittsburgh, he gave up one run on three hits and three walks while striking out four. Hill still has some issues to resolve, but this was an important first step. However, Coors Field may not be the best place for his next start. He is 0-2 with an 11.32 ERA in two games there.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Saturday at Houston, Cook overcame a high early pitch count and held the Astros to two runs, one earned, and four hits in seven innings. Cook has his sinker working and is able to throw a cut fastball to take hitters off of it. He has become the Rockies' most dependable pitcher.
away_pitcher_note:
Marquis earned his first win of the season against the Pirates on Saturday, tossing six innings of one-run ball. His sinker was sharp, he said, which led to seven strikeouts and only one walk. Marquis gave up six hits in what was his longest outing of the season. He'll need that
sinker at Coors Field against the reigning National League champs.

home_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda bobbed and weaved through a third quality start in Atlanta. He was hit relatively hard and needed 118 pitches just to get through six innings, but he was able to strand 10 runners and keep his club in the game. He was behind in many counts as his command wavered, particularly with the cut fastball, and too many pitches caught too much of the plate.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez's talent is evident, but his inexperience is preventing him from achieving results that match it. Against the Astros on Sunday, he gave up four hits and walked five with two out. For the 5 2/3 innings he was in the game, he gave up five hits and struck out six. Jimenez struggled last season in his only start at Dodger Stadium, giving up five earned runs in four innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Dodgers scored early and often against the Reds and Penny knew what to do with the lead, extending his record at Great American Ball Park to 5-0 while allowing one earned run over six innings. He faces his favorite opponent in this start, as he's 12-2 with a 2.92 ERA lifetime against the Rockies and was 2-0 last year. Penny not only is effectively spotting his fastball, but he is finally incorporating his splitter as a regular part of his repertoire.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, at home against the Phillies, Redman struck out five and forced nine ground-ball outs. He gave up just four fly balls, but three were home runs (one caromed off the wall in right-center for an inside-the-park homer). Working with a less-than-blazing fastball and a changeup that is his best pitch, Redman has little room for mistakes up and over the plate. This time, though, Dodger Stadium is more forgiving than Coors Field and the Dodgers' lineup doesn't match that of the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Loaiza got the call, taking over for Hong-Chih Kuo, who had taken over for Loaiza after one start. That's the way it's been for the Dodgers and their fifth starter this year. In Loaiza's only start, he allowed four runs in the first inning, then retired 10 consecutive hitters. In his only start against Colorado last year, he allowed three runs in 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After a rough start, Francis has gone seven innings in each of his last two starts. Tuesday night wasn't as good as his previous start, when he pitched seven shutout innings in San Diego. But he left with a 6-4 lead against the Phillies, only to see the bullpen falter. Francis would have had an even more sparkling outing if not for two hiccups -- the fourth inning, when he walked the opposing pitcher to load the bases and walked in a run, and the seventh when he left a pitch over the plate for a Jayson Werth homer. But he looked more like the pitcher that won 17 games last year than he did in his first two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Although Cain pitched well enough to win, he received a no-decision in his most recent outing, and that actually represented an improvement in his luck. Cain had perhaps his strongest performance of the season, allowing one run and five hits in seven innings last Wednesday at San Diego. But he left trailing 1-0 because San Diego's Greg Maddux was doing his usual number (zero) on the Giants. Bengie Molina's ninth-inning homer off Trevor Hoffman rescued Cain from another hard-luck loss. Since the beginning of last season, the Giants have scored no more than one run in 17 of Cain's 37 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Morales battled through six innings on Wednesday and held the Cubs to three runs on eight hits. The Cubs made him pay when he left the ball up in the zone, but when he kept the ball down, he was successful. Morales did not have his best stuff; however, unlike last year when he would rattle easily, he pitched his way out of jams and avoided big innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum worked 6 1/3 shutout innings last Thursday in a 1-0 victory at San Diego to extend his scoreless streak to 16 2/3 innings. The right-hander continued to throw predominantly fastballs while striking out nine, hiking his season total to 36 in 29 1/3 innings. This will be Lincecum's third start of the year at AT&T Park, where he's 1-0 with a 2.25 ERA. Lincecum faced Colorado twice last season, posting a 1-0 record with a 4.50 ERA. He has been particularly tough on National League West foes during his brief career, owning a 4-1 record with a 1.97 ERA in 10 games.
away_pitcher_note: Cook has become the most consistent starter and a stopper for the Rockies, ending losing streaks in his last two starts. He had his sinker working on Thursday against the Cubs. He worked eight innings, holding Chicago to two runs on four hits and retiring 16 straight at one point. When Cook is getting groundball outs by using his sinker, he's tough to beat with the reigning best defensive club in the Majors behind him.

home_pitcher_note: Last Friday might have been Sanchez's coming-out party. He took a two-hit shutout into the ninth inning against the Cincinnati Reds and left the game having allowed one run and four hits in a 3-1 victory. A bruised left ring finger left Sanchez unable to throw a changeup, so he stuck with his fastball, sinker and slider -- with impressive results. Sanchez has always struggled to maintain a consistent release point, but his effort against the Reds indicated that he's making progress.
away_pitcher_note: After lasting 2 1/3 innings in his last start, at Dodger Stadium on Friday night, Jimenez may be on thin ice in the rotation. Jimenez's total inability to throw quality strikes, or even strikes at all in some cases, led to his giving up six runs on seven hits, with three walks, a hit batter and three wild pitches while facing just 17 hitters against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: After two awful starts to open the year, Francis has posted a 2.57 ERA in his last three. But he doesn't have a win, and the Rockies have dropped two of the three games. He's limiting mistakes, having given up just 14 hits in his last 21 innings. His first step to recovery was getting pitches to the proper location on his arm side (outside to right-handers), and lately he has been able to use the other side of the plate for strikes and for balls when he wants. In his last start, held the Dodgers to two run in seven innings and he is 4-1 with a 2.64 ERA in 10 starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: In Penny's last outing, he once again took advantage of an early hitting frenzy, coming out of the first inning of an 11-3 win over the Rockies with a 10-2 lead and continuing to hold Colorado's potent hitting attack in check over seven innings, his longest outing of the season. Beginning with the final out of the first inning, he retired 13 in in a row. Penny is now 13-2 against the Rockies in his career, having won both decisions against the National League champions in 2007 and adding last Saturday night's performance.

home_pitcher_note: By demoting left-handed rookie Franklin Morales to Triple-A Colorado Springs, moving lefty Jeff Francis to Friday night and pushing lefty Mark Redman to Tuesday against the Cardinals, the Rockies created an opening for Saturday, then completed a trade with the Royals for De La Rosa, who was 3-0 with a 1.64 ERA in four starts for the Royals' Triple-A affiliate in Omaha. De La Rosa was the player to be named in the Spring Training deal that sent right-handed reliever Ramon Ramirez to the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Loaiza made his second start and got into the fifth inning on Sunday against the Rockies at Dodger Stadium. He maintained his stuff through four scoreless frames before the Rockies tagged him for both runs in the fifth inning. Loaiza allowed two earned runs, five hits, one walk and struck out one. He made the most out of 70 pitches, throwing 44 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Tuesday night marked the fourth time Cook has started and the Rockies have ended a losing streak. Cook not only stays smooth throughout his outings, but he is showing a knack for making a big pitch. He fanned just three in seven innings against the Giants, when he gave up two unearned runs but won, 3-2. However, with runners at the corners and one out in the seventh, he picked Eugenio Velez off first then struck out Ray Durham -- who entered the game with favorable numbers against Cook.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe dreads Coors Field (5.87 ERA there). In his Tuesday night no-decision in Florida, he didn't seem to show any signs of the tight elbow that shortened his previous start, but was unable to protect a five-run lead. Three of the six runs he allowed in five innings were unearned, but he wasn't able to stop the damage when betrayed by his defense. He allowed an uncharacteristic four extra-base hits.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenesz's spot in the rotation was in jeopardy before he turned in an encouraging 5 1/3 innings during which he gave up three hits, including a home run, and finished with a no-decision in the Rockies' 3-2 loss to the Giants on Wednesday. By being able to repeat his delivery, Jimenez had his liveliest fastball of the year and was able to change speeds and throw his breaking ball.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro showed that he knows how to pitch with a big lead. After a rocky beginning to his last game, he came out firing once he got a seven-run lead. It led to a lot of hard contact, but only one walk over the final five innings. Control has been Pineiro's key since he's come to St. Louis. He's thrown strikes consistently, and it's worked out.

home_pitcher_note: The good thing for Redman in his last start was the six scoreless innings he threw against the Dodgers on Saturday. The bad thing was he gave 10 runs in the first inning. Redman became unnerved after walking in a run in the middle of the inning. He didn't have much of a fastball and his changeup wasn't fooling hitters. Poor beginnings are an issue for him. But the next start is a shot at redemption in a different venue -- Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Looper has one bad start this year, but a couple of times now he's done the one thing he wasn't able to do last year: He's showing an ability to get by when he doesn't have his best stuff or command. Last year, he alternated good outings with brutal ones, as he wasn't able to survive when he wasn't sharp. This time, in six games, he has only one true clunker. That's a perfectly fine ratio, and one he'll try to keep up.

home_pitcher_note: Francis had a 3-1 lead over the Dodgers with one out in the sixth inning on Friday, but he also had thrown 100 pitches and faced loaded bases when manager Clint Hurdle decided to pull him. The bullpen faltered during a seven-run inning and Francis took the loss. The lefty was not as effective as he had been in going seven innings in each of his previous three starts, but he was able to make big pitches when he was in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright showed no ill effects on Friday from the heavy workload he shouldered in his previous start. Nonetheless, the Cards took no chances, getting him out after 6 1/3 innings. The fact that that was his shortest outing of the year tells you how things have been going for the right-hander. Wainwright is enjoying an excellent year, pitching well and getting deep into games.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had a rough outing in his season debut Saturday against the Dodgers, equaling a career high with nine runs on nine hits and three walks in four plus innings. He got some bad breaks as he gave up six runs in the first two innings, but he struggled with fastball command, and his slider and curve were ineffective, leaving only his changeup as a go-to pitch. He retired nine of 10 batters after the first six runs, but he couldn't record an out in the fifth inning, departing after a three-run homer on a hanging slider.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse had his worst start of the season in his last outing on Saturday, when the Cubs tagged him for eight earned runs on nine hits in six innings. He walked two batters and did not strike out anyone. The right-hander's ERA jumped from 2.36 after his first six starts to 3.79, which ranks third among the Cardinals' five starters. On the season, Lohse has struck out 14 and walked 10 in 40 1/3 innings of work. He's allowed 41 hits and opponents are batting .315 against him.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy picked up his fourth victory of the season in his last start on May 3 against the Marlins, though he got off to a rough start. Peavy allowed a two-run, opposite-field home run to Mike Jacobs in the first inning, but settled down thereafter. Showing as nasty a slider as he has this season, the Cy Young winner struck out eight in going 5 2/3 innings. He retired 12 of the final 14 batters that he faced in the game. He'll make his second start against the Rockies. Peavy tossed eight scoreless innings against Colorado on April 17 in a game the Padres would lose, 2-1, in 22 innings.
away_pitcher_note: You can't blame Aaron Cook for the Rockies' poor start. In fact, things would be worse without him, as Cook has stopped Rockies' losing streaks no less than five times already this season. The red-headed sinker-baller also has won five consecutive decisions, and the Rockies are 6-1 in his seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Maddux was unsuccessful in his fourth bid at career victory No. 350, as he allowed four earned runs on 11 hits in 5 2/3 innings in his last start against the Marlins on May 4. Maddux didn't have nearly the same amount of movement on his pitches as he's had in previous starts this season, which is always a key component success. Maddux was around the plate as usual, as he had one walk and it was intentional. But the Marlins took advantage of fastballs up in the strike zone, as evidenced by the home run Dan Uggla hit to center field in the second inning. This will be Maddux's first start against Colorado this season.
away_pitcher_note: The roller-coaster ride continues for the promising but still inconsistent young right-hander. He has pitched just well enough in his last two starts to secure his spot in a somewhat shaky rotation, but continues to battle with location and limiting damage in big innings. Jimenez also leads the Majors with eight wild pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Young was hurt by several balls he got up in the strike zone of his last start, when the Braves got home runs from Chipper Jones -- who seems to be hitting them off everyone these days -- and Mark Kotsay on Tuesday at Turner Field. Young allowed five runs on nine hits with two walks and four strikeouts. Home runs have been more of a problem this season for Young, who has allowed seven. He allowed 10 last season in 173 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Reynolds, 22, will make his Major League debut with the Rockies in need of a fifth starter after moving Mark Redman to the bullpen. He was the second overall pick in the 2006 Draft, the Rockies highest selection ever. Reynolds is 1-2 and has a 4.86 ERA this season with Triple-A Colorado Springs. He has pitched well as of late with the Sky Sox, throwing eight innings and yielding two runs on April 27. He only pitched two innings in each of his past two starts as it appeared the Rockies wanted him well-rested in case they needed him for this start.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson picked up the win against the Phillies his last time out despite allowing four runs on five hits over six innings. The win was No. 286 for Johnson. The left-hander is still working out the kinks in his command, but he seemed to get a jump in velocity this time around as his fastball touched 94 mph and his slider checked in at 86 with some of its old bite.
away_pitcher_note: Francis has made seven starts this season and this is the longest he's gone without a win to start a season in his career. He had pitched better as of late; however, he admittedly was off his game on Wednesday against St. Louis. He struggled locating pitches and a high pitch count forced him to leave the game after five innings. However, he was able to hold the Cardinals to three runs. Even with his struggles, Francis has been the Rockies best option in the starting rotation this season other than Aaron Cook.

home_pitcher_note: The Diamondbacks have lost Owings' last three starts after winning his first four and Owings has allowed 15 runs in 17 2/3 innings during those games. Owings did throw a quality start his last time out, lasting seven innings. In starting the season 4-0, Owings threw either 96 or 97 pitches in each of his starts. He has allowed only 36 hits and 14 walks in 43 2/3 innings this year, an efficiency he'll try to sustain against the Rockies. He allowed only two hits and one run in 6 2/3 innings to beat the Rockies April 4 in Denver.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa kept the Cardinals off balance on Thursday mixing his slider, fastball and changeup. His command was much better than his first start and he seemed more comfortable on the mound -- a four-run first-inning lead will do that. He held the Cards to two runs in 5 2/3 innings and had five strikeouts to just one walk. The Rockies need De La Rosa to pitch well and stay in the rotation, as they are hurting for starting pitchers.

home_pitcher_note: Webb has won all eight of his starts this year, eclipsing Randy Johnson, who won his first seven starts of the 2000 season. Hot starts are nothing new for Webb, who started the 2005 season 6-0 and opened the 2006 campaign with franchise-best 8-0 mark. He tossed a complete game in his last outing against the Phillies, allowing three runs. His outing before that was a little shaky. The right-hander allowed four runs on five hits over six innings in that one. Three of the runs came on a Carlos Delgado homer in the sixth inning. Webb's changeup has become a valuable strikeout pitch when he gets to two strikes. Webb won the NL Cy Young Award in 2006 and finished second in the voting to San Diego's Jake Peavy last year.
away_pitcher_note: Cook won his sixth straight game on Friday night against the Padres. He allowed one run over seven innings en route to the Rockies' 4-2 win over San Diego. Although Cook wasn't sharp in the first four innings, he got settled and out-dueled NL Cy Young winner Jake Peavy. Cook is one of the most reliable starters for the Rockies right now and only looks to improve. Rockies manager Clint Hurdle feels this is the best he's seen out of Cook. Said Hurdle: "He's staying in a real good place in the game. Obviously, the string is the most impressive and might be as impressive as anybody we had here."

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander didn't allow many hits in his last start, but a three-run homer to Adrian Gonzalez proved to be the back-breaker. Jimenez allowed three runs on five hits and three walks with a career-high 11 strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings to take the loss for his first decision in his last five starts. His lone win came at home against the Braves on April 15 and Jimenez has failed to get past six innings in seven of his eight starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn earned his third victory of the season in a 9-6 victory over the Red Sox on Sunday. At times the right-hander struggled, but worked through six innings, giving up four earned runs on nine hits. He also struck out five batters, walked one and hit two batters. The Twins rookie showed some grit in working out of two jams that could have led to big innings for Boston. He will look to build on his success as Minnesota opens up Interleague Play against the Rockies on Friday in Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old right-hander was not in awe of big leaguers in his Major League debut and will likely get another shot. The Rockies have optioned left-hander Mark Redman to Triple-A Colorado Springs to get regular work and are hoping Reynolds can pitch well enough to keep the spot in the rotation. Reynolds allowed four runs on six hits and two walks with a strikeout, but also gave up two homers to take the loss.
away_pitcher_note: The Twins knew that they were getting an innings-eater when they signed Hernandez at the start of Spring Training. But he's been even better than expected to start the year. Hernandez picked up his sixth win of the season, holding the Red Sox to just three runs on 10 hits over six innings. He didn't get his sixth win in 2007 until July 24. The Twins are now 8-1 in games that Hernandez starts, giving the team lots of confidence when he's on the mound. He's gotten his fair share of run support too, but he'll have the chance to help his own cause when he faces the Rockies at Coors Field in Interleague Play. Renowned for his bat, Hernandez is a career .232 hitter with nine home runs in 789 at-bats.

home_pitcher_note: Francis gave up 13 hits, matching a career high, and eight runs in 4 2/3 innings of a loss at Arizona on Tuesday night. He left insisting he pitched better than his numbers. It was true that a number of the hits were soft, but his difficulties pitching inside against right-handed hitters and the slight location misses with his fastball and changeup were every bit as much a problem. After a good three-start string, Francis has given up 25 hits in 15 innings over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey was effective if not efficient in his last start. The right-hander allowed just three runs over his 5 2/3 innings, throwing a total of 107 pitches in that span. The Blue Jays put together some long at-bats against Slowey, raising him pitch count quickly. Home runs also continue to be a problem. He's given up 20 homers over 16 career appearances. For his next start he'll face the Rockies for the first time in his career at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa cruised for three innings in his last start, a loss to the Diamondbacks, but gave up four runs and was gone after 4 2/3 innings. He probably deserved a better fate, but his pitch count rose quickly in the innings in which he experienced trouble. Still, he fanned six and has 15 strikeouts in 14 1/3 innings in his three starts since joining the club in a trade with the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Misch allowed Houston three first-inning runs, including two on a Lance Berkman homer, but recovered to blank the Astros over the next five innings on Wednesday. Demonstrating enviable command, Misch walked none and struck out six, He's still looking for his first Major League victory after appearing in 23 games, including seven starts. Misch appeared twice against Colorado last season, posting no record and a 2.08 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Cook had set a record with wins in six straight starts until he was by the Diamondbacks on Thursday night at Chase Field. Cook was in decent shape after four innings, having held the D-backs to one run and given them a fighting chance against Brandon Webb. However, Cook gave up a three-run homer to Chris Snyder during a four-run fifth inning. He gave up five runs and 10 hits in five innings. Cook stopped the Giants on April 29, holding them to two runs and 10 hits in seven innings of a 3-2 victory.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum received a no-decision although he appeared bound for a victory in his most recent start last Thursday against Houston. He struck out 10 in six innings and left with a 7-3 lead. But the bullpen allowed Houston five runs in the final two innings, dooming the Giants to an 8-7 loss. It marked the 10th time in Lincecum's relatively brief career that he had struck out at least 10 in one game. Asked what pitches were working for him, Lincecum replied that sometimes it was his fastball, sometimes his changeup and sometimes his curveball, reflecting the breadth of his skill.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez pitched one of his best efforts of the season on Friday, holding the Twins to two runs on eight hits and a walk over seven innings, his longest stint of the season. He used his two-seam fastball to good effect low in the zone, striking out five and throwing 67 strikes against 27 balls. Jimenez showed an ability to avoid the big innings that had plagued him in earlier starts. He has lost his last three decisions, despite posting back-to-back quality starts and posting a 3.95 ERA over the course of his last two trips to the hill.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez pitched well enough to win in his most recent outing, Friday against the Chicago White Sox. He blanked Chicago on three hits through six innings and had two outs in the seventh before Nick Swisher's broken-bat single prolonged the inning. Up came .136-hitting Alexei Ramirez, who homered for the game's only runs. Ramirez homered on a changeup, the pitch that actually worked well for Sanchez much of the night. Sanchez received no decision April 30 against Colorado at AT&T Park and fell just short of a quality start, allowing two runs in 5 2/3 innings. He also walked five, which prevented him from pitching deeper into the game.

home_pitcher_note: Reynolds is off to a good start in his first two big league appearances, showing poise on the mound and promising stuff. He has shown the confidence to throw a hard breaking curve and a changeup in secondary counts, and is commanding a good sinking fastball. The 6'7", 21-year-old was born with a downhill plane, a handy characteristic for a pitcher, particularly in Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Perez earned his second straight victory, pitching into the eighth inning for the first time in nine starts this season, while beating the Yankees on Sunday. He allowed three hits and two walks, struck out four in  7 2/3 innings and won for the second time in five starts. He has a 2-3 record and 7.24 ERA in six career appearances and 32 1/3 innings at Coors Field. His career record against the Rockies is 5-5.

home_pitcher_note: Francis, the Rockies' Opening Day starter, finally earned his first win in his ninth trip to the hill Sunday, holding the Twins to two runs on six hits and two walks (one intentional) in 6 1/3 innings.  His command was much improved, and he was especially effective with his offspeed stuff, most notably his changeup, which he was able to give some sink at times, and other times have it cut away from left-handers.  He gave up leadoff extra-base hits in four of the seven innings he was on the mound and a one-out triple in another inning, stranding all but one of those runners.  He only had one multihit inning, with the Twins only runs coming on a leadoff double and a full-count, two-run homer from Justin Morneau.
away_pitcher_note: Mets manager Willie Randolph pulled Claudio Vargas after just 66 pitches on Tuesday in hopes that he could bring the right-hander back on three days' rest to start against the Rockies. Vargas allowed four runs on five hits in five innings against the Braves, taking the loss, his second in as many starts this season. Vargas also lost May 14 against the Nationals, when he was charged with three hits, two runs and four walks in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cook has lost two straight starts after winning a club-record six straight. He grasped for control during the first four innings of his last start, against the Giants, giving up four runs in the first four innings. But after a brief pointer from pitching coach Bob Apodaca to stay compact in his delivery, he pitched three strong innings to last through the seventh. He's trying to take that feeling into his next start.
away_pitcher_note: It now appears the standard M.O. for Maine's opponents is to foul off pitches by the dozens in an effort to tire the Mets starter. Maine has thrown 325 pitches in his three most recent starts, covering 18 1/3 innings. His loss to the Braves on Tuesday was his first after four consecutive victories. He needed 99 pitches to achieve 12 outs.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer has had a strong May, going 3-1 with a 4.18 ERA in four starts, including the most recent one, which was his best of the season -- no runs in six innings against the Nationals. Moyer also has walked only four batters this month, covering 14 innings.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa's numbers for the season aren't good, and his high pitch counts are preventing him from getting deep into games, but in his last three starts, he won one and pitched well enough to keep the Rockies in the other two. On Monday night, he pitched 5 1/3 innings and gave up three runs, two earned, in a no-decision that the Rockies eventually won over the Giants. De La Rosa labored for the first three innings, then corrected himself by slowing down his upper body and pitched well the rest of the time he was in the contest.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick pitched five-plus innings, taking a no-decision in his last start on Thursday at Houston. He allowed five runs on eight hits and a walk, striking out two. In his last seven starts, Kendrick is 2-0 with five no-decisions and the Phillies are 6-1 in those starts. He hasn't lost since April 16 vs. Houston. Kendrick is 0-1 with a 7.00 ERA in two career starts against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez had what may have been the best performance of his career, matching his career high with seven innings and making them all scoreless for the first time. He was extremely efficient, putting his strikeouts on the shelf (only one despite entering the game averaging 8.11 K's per nine innings) in favor of the ground ball, recording 16 of his 21 outs with grounders. He focused on the bottom of the strike zone, getting balls in play rather than the swings and misses that come from his hard breaking ball and slider and his high fastball, and he hit 96 mph in his final inning.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Eaton went seven innings and allowed three runs on eight hits in a 4-3 loss to the Astros. Manager Charlie Manuel called it the best he'd ever seen Eaton, who has seven no-decisions and three losses in his 10 starts this season. Including the Astros loss, he has had five quality starts with nothing to show for them. Against the Rockies, he's 8-12 with a 6.32 ERA in 25 career games.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Reynolds struck out four Mets his first time through the order and entered the sixth inning having given up just two hits. A double play not turned opened the door for Reynolds to give up back-to-back home runs to Carlos Delgado and Fernando Tatis, and he wound up with a no-decision in the Rockies' 13-inning victory. However, Reynolds struck out five in six innings, and used his fastball, breaking pitch and changeup as "out" pitches as he continued to demonstrate the talent and poise that made him the second overall pick in 2006.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis had beaten the Pirates twice this season, but he couldn't pull it off a third time. He did not get a decision in his last start against Pittsburgh, giving up three runs on seven hits and three walks over 5 1/3 innings. Against the Rockies last year, Marquis was 1-0 with a 2.19 ERA. Pitching at Wrigley should be a little bit of an advantage for Marquis, who is winless in four road starts. He's 2-2 with a 5.14 ERA in five home games.
away_pitcher_note: Francis displayed rushed mechanics and no fastball command -- which eliminated his changeup -- during a five-run, 37-pitch first inning in Saturday afternoon's loss to the Mets. Francis gave up just one run the rest of the way, and he lasted six innings. He finished by tying his season high with eight strikeouts. Still, innings like the first on Saturday are not what the Rockies need from their No. 1 pitcher, who says he feels healthy but is making mistakes in his windup and delivery.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a decision in his last start against the Pirates, which was another extra-inning loss for the Cubs. The lefty gave up three homers for the first time since doing so in back to back starts one year ago. Two of those were by light-hitting Luis Rivas. For the game, Lilly was charged with four runs on 10 hits and two walks over six innings. He was mad at himself after the game for not going deeper -- the bullpen was overworked -- and at some mistakes in pitch selection.
away_pitcher_note: After dropping his past two decisions, Cook regained his form against the Mets that helped him reel off a club-record six straight wins earlier this season. Cook was in complete control from the first inning against New York, pitching the first complete game by a Rockies pitcher since Aug. 27 of last year. He gave up just one run on four hits, threw 118 pitches (72 for strikes) and recorded 16 groundball outs. Cook has had success against the Cubs in the past (he's 3-1 with a 2.32 ERA) and had one of his best outings of the year against the Cubs in April, giving up two runs on four hits in victory. This will be Cook's first start at Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster posted his eighth quality start of the season in his last outing against the Dodgers. The right-hander gave up seven hits over seven innings, the fourth time in his 11 starts he's pitched seven. Dempster also struck out three and escaped some tough jams. He's made the conversion from closer to starter look easy, but Dempster deserves credit for the hard work he's put in.
away_pitcher_note: It's full circle for Rusch, a former Cub. Rusch last pitched for the Cubs in 2006, but the club released him after the season because of a blood clot in his right lung. Rusch made a comeback with the Padres this season, but was released after 12 appearances -- the last of which was against the Rockies on May 9. Since signing with the Rockies, Rusch has given up one run in 11 innings at Triple-A Colorado Springs. Rusch replaces lefty Jorge De La Rosa, who has been moved to the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Gallagher is making a case to stay in the rotation. The right-hander held the Dodgers to one run on four hits over seven innings and picked up the win in the longest outing of his young career. He picked a perfect night to pitch, as the temperature was 42 degrees with a wind chill that made it feel like 35. He wore short sleeves, so it must not have bothered him. Neither did a comebacker by Andre Ethier in the first that deflected off the middle finger of his right hand.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez had his worst outing of the season Tuesday at Philadelphia. Jimenez labored through 36 pitches in the first inning and wound up giving up 10 hits and seven earned runs in four innings. Jimenez struck out four, walked two and threw 94 pitches, 57 for strikes. Despite giving up seven runs, the Rockies offense once again was unable to give him any run support.

home_pitcher_note: Derek Lowe turned in his best start of the year, one of the best in several years and was in position for his first win in nearly five weeks with seven scoreless innings against the Cubs. He scattered four hits and had the pressure on throughout, as the Dodgers' offense gave him only one run support. He has lost his last four decisions to the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Reynolds had all kinds of command issues in his last start in Philadelphia, as he walked eight batters and allowed five hits and six earned runs in 5 2/3 innings. Three of those walks led to home runs by Chase Utley and Geoff Jenkins in the fifth inning. Reynolds threw 101 pitches, but only 51 for strikes. This will be the fifth career Major League start for the 22-year-old righty, who is searching for his first victory.

home_pitcher_note: Penny was hammered again by the Mets in general and David Wright in particular. Penny's fastball was hitting 93 mph consistently, so his arm seems to be sound, but something is very wrong for a two-time All-Star whose ERA has nearly doubled from last year. In his last six starts he's 0-4 with a 9.43 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Francis had inconsistent location against a tough Cubs lineup. At times he paid, at times he made key pitches. He went five innings before being removed for a pinch hitter in the sixth, and he held the Cubs to three runs -- one on a Derrek Lee homer -- and six hits, striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw allowed a first-inning home run and was wild throughout a 3 2/3-inning outing, being charged with four runs on five hits and four walks. His fastball was a little too lively, his curveball erratic and he didn't seem to use the changeup as much as he did in an impressive debut against St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Friday at Wrigley seemed to be a typical Cook start in 2008. He was forcing grounder after grounder. But he gave up three home runs in his final 1 1/3 innings, and wound up charged with 10 hits and seven runs in 6 1/3 innings in a no-decision. At least Dodger Stadium doesn't have the issue of winds kicking up and blowing balls out of the park, as what happened to Cook against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez was hit on his left knee by a line drive from Cubs shortstop Ryan Theriot in his last start but he'll take the hill Friday against the Brewers. Jimenez allowed four runs, three earned, on seven hits and three walks to take the loss against the Cubs. The right-hander's lone win this season came in his second start of the year when he defeated the Braves. This will be his fist career start against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets came tantalizingly close to his third complete game of the season Saturday, working 8 2/3 innings and allowing just one run on seven hits. An 11-pitch walk to Lance Berkman with nobody on in the ninth prompted manager Ned Yost to pull his ace after 122 pitches. The right-hander was frustrated with the decision, but he was still pleased with an outing that marked the fifth quality start by a Brewers pitcher in six outings.

home_pitcher_note: Reynolds struggled to find any rhythm in his last start and after five outings, the left-hander is still looking for his first big league win. Against the Dodgers, Reynolds allowed six runs, four earned on seven hits and three walks with one strikeout over five innings for the loss and his earliest exit this year. This will be his first career appearance against the Brewers and third start at home.
away_pitcher_note: Bush seems to have found at least a temporary answer to the struggles that have haunted him this season, delivering his second straight quality start Sunday in a Brewers victory. Bush worked seven innings and allowed four hits, with one fence-scraping home run in the first inning accounting for the only tally. The Brewers backed him with 10 runs worth of support, but Bush also helped himself by not walking anybody. He has one walk in his last three starts (19 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Francis pitched more to his 2007 form than the struggles of this year. The left-hander led the staff with 17 wins last season but had just one victory to his credit this year until his last start when he shut out the Dodgers over seven innings on four hits and two walks. He also struck out five. Francis is 2-2 in his career against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: After posting a 2.56 ERA in his five May starts, Suppan started June on a solid note, allowing three D-backs runs in seven innings of a no-decision on Monday at Miller Park. He has surrendered three runs in 15 innings of his last two starts, both Brewers wins. Suppan has had success against the Rockies; he's 5-1 against them with a 3.58 ERA in eight starts including 2-0 with a 4.34 ERA in three starts at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Cook was sharp in his last start, allowing a run over eight innings to pick up his eighth victory of the year. He also tied a season high with six strikeouts and helped the Rockies build a modest two-game winning streak after losing eight straight. Cook is 4-6 in his career against the Giants but was 2-0 against them last season.
away_pitcher_note: Misch threw a scoreless inning in Saturday's 6-0 rout of the Nationals and will rejoin the rotation for Tuesday's start in Colorado. The Giants skipped over Misch last time after he went 0-2 with a 6.39 ERA in six starts. He moved to the bullpen after that, but goes back to the starting rotation this time. The Giants recalled him from Triple-A Fresno on April 27.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez had a strong outing at Coors Field Friday, lasting six innings and one batter against the Brewers and giving up four runs on five hits and two walks, each of which led off innings and ended up scoring. Two of the five hits were back-to-back solo homers, but he was otherwise extremely effective, striking out six and inducing nine ground-ball outs, retiring 12 consecutive hitters between the first and fifth innings. He kept his fastball down and worked both sides of the plate, tempting hitters outside of the zone, then jamming them inside.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander turned in another domiant performance in Friday's 10-1 victory over Washington. He needed just 83 pitches to get through seven innings and didn't even give up a hit until the fourth, baffling the Nationals throughout. Lincecum now is on his second four-game winning streak of the season and has been one of the best pitchers in the National League in what's turning out to be a breakthrough year.

home_pitcher_note: After two straight poor outings, Reynolds held the Brewers to two runs and four hits while earning his first Major League win on Saturday. Reynolds, breaking several bats along the way with his sinker, came up with a key line-drive double play in the second inning and worked two outs to strand a runner at third in the fifth.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Sanchez blanked the Nationals in seven innings, giving up four hits. The left-hander never really got into trouble, but the Giants turned three double plays behind him to end innings. He has given the Giants five consecutive quality starts, going at least six innings and allowing two earned runs or less in those outings, and manager Bruce Bochy says the lefty's improved focus on the mound has made a big difference.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd continues to impress White Sox manager Ozzie Guillen. The right-hander threw seven strong innings Sunday against the Twins, allowing two runs on six hits and a walk. His nine strikeouts were a career high en route to his third straight win. After that start, Floyd said his strikeout numbers depend on the strength of his curveball, which is his primary out pitch. The one free pass he issued is the only one he's allowed during his current winning streak. He has not faced Colorado this season.
away_pitcher_note: Francis labored through a 32-pitch first inning when he gave up two walks, three hits and two runs on Sunday, and gave up a two-out run in the second. However, he pitched much better, and left with three runs and seven hits in six innings in losing to the Brewers, as his fastball command and ability to use his changeup increased. So in his last two starts, with the exception of Sunday's first two innings, he is slowly finding his form. The Rockies need that.

home_pitcher_note: Danks looked mortal Monday against the Twins, giving up four runs in a start for the first time since April 9. On the other hand, he made it through six innings -- something he hasn't done with any consistency this season. He walked three and struck out four and didn't factor in the decision. His results haven't wavered month-to-month, owning a 2-2 record in both April and May. He even allowed exactly 10 runs in each month.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies weren't sure who was going to start on Saturday after they optioned Glendon Rusch to Triple-A Colorado Springs last week. They ultimately decided on De La Rosa, who was moved to the bullpen after giving up seven runs on four hits in 3 1/3 innings against Philadelphia on May 27. He's made three relief appearances since the demotion, and has surrendered two earned runs on four hits in 4 2/3 innings. He pitched a perfect seventh inning on June 7.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander saw his four-game winning streak come to an end, not to mention the conclusion of a string of six starts without a loss, during Detroit's 6-4 victory on Tuesday night at Comerica Park. Contreras had not allowed more than two runs in a game since May 4, prior to giving up six runs on a season-high 13 hits over six-plus innings against the Tigers. Contreras walked one and struck out one. He has a 2-0 record with a 3.46 ERA lifetime against the Rockies, with one of those starts coming at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Cook became the third pitcher in Rockies history to win at least nine games before the All-Star break, and he has ample opportunity to break Shawn Chacon's 2003 club record of 11 W's before the break. In his last start, a win over the Giants, Cook threw 101 pitches in seven innings and might have gone deeper had he not gotten a couple of pitches up in the zone to lead to two runs in the eighth inning. Cook was especially strong early, when balls were either hit on the ground or became lazy flies, and finished with nine ground-ball outs.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez is coming off one of his best outings of the season. He tossed seven shutout innings, struck out three and gave up just four hits in a no-decision against San Francisco on Wednesday. The right-hander showed supreme control against the Giants, effectively mixing his fastball, curveball and changeup to fool San Francisco's hitters. Jimenez has just one win this season, and it came against the Braves on April 8, when he allowed three runs on six hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens is expected to start the Braves' makeup game against the Rockies. The game was originally scheduled for April 10 but was postponed because of snow. Jurrjens was scratched from his start on Wednesday against the Cubs after twisting his right ankle while walking down the stairs the night before. The 22-year-old right-hander allowed a season-high 11 hits in his last start, June 5 against the Marlins, but he got the win, his sixth of the season. He has given up four homers in his past three starts, after surrendering just one in his first 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Reynolds followed his first career win, against the Brewers, with his worst performance of the season against the Giants. Reynolds struggled to keep his sinker down in the strike zone, and the Giants tagged him for eight runs on 10 hits in 3 1/3 innings. Reynolds pitched into the fifth inning in each of his first six starts, and his ERA was 5.24 before Thursday's game against San Francisco. This will be Reynolds' first start against an American League team.
away_pitcher_note: It's fortunate for Byrd that the humidor is in use at Coors Field these days, because he's turned his share of ballparks into launching pads this year. Byrd served up his league-leading 17th homer of the season in a rough start against the Twins on Wednesday. Coming off an extraordinarily efficient outing against the Tigers, he was beaten up for six runs (five earned) on six hits with a walk and a strikeout in just three innings of work. He'll look to have better luck at Coors, where the fly-ball pitcher is 0-2 with a 9.82 ERA in five career appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Francis got through a clean first inning -- a problem for much of the year -- and pitched well for nearly all of his six-plus innings Friday against the White Sox at U.S. Cellular Field in his last start. However, four of the final six batters he faced reached, and he ended up with a no-decision. Still, Francis showed an effective two-seam fastball and continued his recovery from a slow start to the season.
away_pitcher_note: Laffey's last start against the Twins on Thursday wasn't the most efficient of outings, as he needed 101 pitches to get through six innings. But he was nonetheless effective, allowing just a run on five hits with a walk and four strikeouts. He got himself into some jams and some three-ball counts, but he remained confident in his sinker and it paid off. Laffey, who has been a key contributor to the Indians' injury-ravaged rotation, has never faced the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa is making his second straight start after he was demoted to the bullpen on May 28. De La Rosa has struggled with his command this season, but was extremely sharp in a spot start against the White Sox on June 14. He threw five shutout innings and struck out a career-high eight batters in the no-decision. In six career games against the Indians, De La Rosa is 1-3 with a 7.67 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Sowers once again showed an inability to put away hitters. He'd get ahead in the count, but he couldn't make the pitch that would turn a favorable count into an out. That ended up hurting him badly in his last outing, which a late Tribe rally turned into a no-decision. Sowers gave up nine hits and four runs in 4 2/3 innings. Having squandered a 3-0 lead, he left the ballgame trailing and with his pitch count at almost 100. That's not what the Indians need from him, particularly with the troubles of their bullpen. He will need to pitch deeper into the ballgame if he plans to stick in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Cook, the third pitcher in Rockies history to reach double figures in wins before the All-Star break, needs one more win to tie Shawn Chacon's club record, set in 2003. Cook labored the second time through the order while beating the White Sox on the road on Sunday. But the Mets have seen him at his best. Cook threw the Rockies' only complete game of he year against them at Coors on May 25, when he held them to one run on four hits in a 4-1 Rockies victory.
away_pitcher_note: Maine gave up a lot of long flyouts on Sunday -- and one ball escaped the park -- in 6 1/3 innings vs. the Rangers in the first game of a doubleheader. Despite allowing a season-high five earned runs on seven hits, Maine's only real gripe with his performance was an inability to induce key ground-ball outs. And he'll head into Coors having already pitched there once this season, throwing six innings and surrendering four runs -- three earned -- on three hits in a loss on May 25.

home_pitcher_note: Facing the only team he's beaten this season, Jimenez came into Monday's game against the Braves overanxious. He showed flashes of greatness, striking out seven hitters, but his control problems cost him the game. Jimenez gave up three runs (two earned), walked a season-high five batters and threw 110 pitches in five innings. Jimenez has improved of late, however, and was in the midst of a 12-inning scoreless streak before giving up all three runs to the Braves in the fifth inning. This will be Jimenez's first career start against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: In the second game of Sunday's doubleheader, in his third start since coming off the disabled list, Martinez went six innings and allowed only two runs to the hot-hitting Rangers. He worked with little more than a mid-80s fastball, but Martinez located almost everything, tossing 64 strikes on 92 pitches. He also did it on six-days rest, and if the rotation stays as is, Martinez will have five off-days before setting foot on the mound at Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: After giving up eight runs in 3 1/3 innings against the Giants on June 12, Reynolds worked all week with pitching coach Bob Apodaca to straighten out his mechanics. The extra work immediately payed off as Reynolds kept his sinkerball down and used his changeup to fool the Indians on Tuesday night. He gave up just one run on five hits in six innings against Cleveland and didn't surrender a walk for the first time in eight starts. Reynolds pitched against the Mets on May 23 and gave up four runs in six innings in the no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey's final line was ugly -- six runs in six innings -- but he pitched well for most of Monday's outing against the Angels. He had given up three runs through six innings, but then allowed three straight Angels to reach base to open the seventh. All three scored after he left the game, but the Mets hung on and Pelfrey won his first decision in over two months. His next start comes against the Rockies, a team that hit him for six runs over three innings in an abbreviated start last year.

home_pitcher_note: Bannister held the Cardinals to two runs in seven innings to go 2-0 with two no-decisions in June. Bannister gave up nine hits but walked none for the second straight game. The only extra-base hit, a double, came when a catchable fly ball was lost in the outfield. Bannister expended just 81 pitches (58 strikes) in his seven innings before being lifted for a pinch-hitter. He faced Colorado once last year, giving up three runs and five hits in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Francis, who is notorious for struggling early, finally appears to be the same pitcher who won 17 games last year and was named the Opening Day starter this year. Francis started the season 1-5, but is 2-1 with a 2.88 ERA in his past four outings since June 3. In his latest start, against Cleveland, Francis yielded two runs (one earned) on five hits to earn the win. The lean lefty will be making his third straight start against an American League Central team, and he's had success against the Royals in the past. Francis is 1-0 in two starts against Kansas City, having given up just three runs in 14 1/3 combined innings.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke stymied the Cardinals on two hits in seven innings on Thursday at St. Louis, with only a Rick Ankiel solo home run marring his line. He walked just one and struck out seven. Greinke had pitched seven shutout innings in his previous start at Arizona, failing to get a decision in what turned out to be a 10-inning, 1-0 loss. Greinke has held opponents to a .171 average with runners in scoring position and he and his catchers have not allowed a stolen base yet this season.
away_pitcher_note: This will be a homecoming for De La Rosa, who spent the past year-and-a-half with the Royals before he was traded to the Rockies earlier this season. After being banished to the bullpen May 28, De La Rosa has come back to pitch dominantly in his past two starts. He struck out what was then a career-high eight batters and didn't give up a run against the White Sox on June 14. In his next start against Cleveland, De La Rosa struck out ten batters and gave up three runs on four hits in six innings. This will be De La Rosa's first start against his former club.

home_pitcher_note: Hochevar ran into a command problem, one that always is troubling when it strikes, last Friday night against the Giants. His sinking fastball is wonderful when it's down in the strike zone because ground balls proliferate. When it's too far up in the zone, base hits proliferate. That was Hochevar's fate as he left in the fifth inning with the score 4-4. He had no decision in the loss but it was disappointing after he'd pitched a convincing victory over the D-backs in his previous game. This is his first shot at the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Cook has been the Rockies' best pitcher all season, but he proved Friday that even he's capable of bad games. Against the Mets, the 29-year-old righty gave up six runs on 12 hits in seven innings. His biggest problem was his inability to keep his sinkerball low, which allowed the Mets to score six runs after three innings. Carlos Delgado hit a two-run homer in the second, and Trot Nixon added a solo shot in the third. Cook settled down after that, however, and pitched effectively enough to remain the game until the seventh. This will be Cook's first game against the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: Bonine earned no decision for his trouble in his second Major League start last Friday at San Diego, but with seven innings of two-run ball, he had a better performance than the win he recorded in his debut. He has an even ratio of ground balls to fly balls, but he has taken advantage of the defense behind him to throw strikes and mix pitches. His knuckleball remains an X-factor in future starts, should he need it.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez had been pitching well, without run support or wins, for a month and a half. He was finally rewarded Saturday night, when he used his fastball and slider as out pitches and mixed in good off-speed stuff while holding the Mets to two hits over eight innings in a win at Coors field on Saturday night. Jimenez, who earned his first win since April 8, has a 1.35 ERA over his last 20 innings.

home_pitcher_note: All the early-season speculation over whether Verlander was pitching hurt has been put to rest by his arsenal of stuff over his past few outings. He had a season-high 10 strikeouts over 5 1/3 innings last Sunday at San Diego despite lacking a feel for his offspeed pitch. He hit 98 mph several times on the PETCO Park radar gun. He has dominated Interleague Play over his three full big league seasons, going 8-0 in nine regular-season starts against the National League.
away_pitcher_note: Old problems returned in Francis' last start, a loss at Kansas City on Monday. For one, he gave up four runs in the first inning. He had curbed that season-long problem in his two previous starts. Francis also struggled with the command of his fastball, and that's why manager Clint Hurdle thought he struggled. For the game, Francis lasted just 4 1/3 innings and gave up seven runs. In his last three starts, Francis is 1-1 and has given up 12 runs.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers had allowed just four earned runs over 36 innings in his previous five starts before the Cardinals charged him for five runs on nine hits over 5 1/3 innings, handing Rogers his first loss since May 15 and his first Interleague defeat since he joined the Tigers three years ago. He had allowed a lone run over his first 4 2/3 innings before a Brian Barton homer sent him laboring to finish the fifth before three hits chased him in the sixth. He'll try to start a new winning streak against a Rockies lineup that hits about 10 points against left-handers compared with right-handers this year.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Reynolds had no secondary pitches working but fount a way to last seven innings and hold the Mets to three runs in a 3-1 loss at Coors Field. It was a step forward to Reynolds, who adjusted by relying on his sinking fastball and showing just enough of a curveball to keep hitters honest. He is not a strikeout pitcher, but he has six against one walk in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa started off fine then got rattled in his last outing, a loss to Kansas City. His catcher, Yorvit Torrealba, thought he just lost control because he was overthrowing the ball. De La Rosa just called it a bad outing. He lasted just 4 2/3 innings and gave up four runs, two earned. It was a setback compared to his last two outings. In those, he struck out 18 batters and allowed just three runs.
away_pitcher_note: Maddux went into his last start on Wednesday against the Twins with eight consecutive starts without a victory, though that was more a function of the Padres inability to score enough runs for him than him struggling with his command or simply getting knocked around. That wasn't so much the case against the Twins as Maddux allowed six earned runs over his 5 2/3 innings -- he had allowed eight runs over his last six starts alone -- on seven hits, one being a two-run home run to Twins No. 7 hitter Brenden Harris, who hit one of two home runs in the ninth inning Tuesday off Trevor Hoffman. Maddux hadn't allowed more than five runs in a start this season since April 18, the day after the Padres played 22 innings against Colorado and needed innings from the 41-year-old.

home_pitcher_note: Cook has now dropped two straight decisions. Errors by his infielders and clutch hitting by the Royals contributed to his last loss, which came on Wednesday in Kansas City. He felt like most of his pitches were good and that he avoided throwing up in the strike zone. Cook lasted 5 1/3 innings and gave up four runs, three earned. It was better than his last outing. In that start, Cook took the loss after giving up six runs in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Banks, the waiver wire wonder, has emerged as one of the Padres' most dependable pitchers, though he was roughed up in his last start on June 26 against the Twins.
