Like Greg Maddux the day before, Banks was staked to an early 3-0 lead but couldn't make it stand up. He allowed a monster two-run home run to Justin Morneau in the fourth inning and was gone after 5 1/3 innings, having allowed four runs on seven hits. The four runs were the most that Banks has allowed in his five starts with the Padres since joining the team in May.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez will have that rare feeling of being happy to get back to Coors Field, where he held the Mets to two hits in eight innings in his last start there. Between then and now, Jimenez had an awful outing in Detroit, giving up four runs and throwing 104 pitches in just four innings. Jimenez had none of his secondary pitches until his final inning in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf ran into command issues almost from the start of his last outing on June 27 against the Mariners. Wolf allowed six of the first 11 batters to reach base, as he compiled five walks in 3 1/3 innings. Wolf needed 50 pitches to get through the first two innings alone against the Mariners. He has now walked nine batters in his last two starts and hasn't won since June 11. His ERA has climbed from 3.83 on June 11 to 4.13. He'll face the Rockies for the first time since April 15 when he allowed one hit over seven innings with nine strikeouts in earning his first victory with the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies placed lefty Jeff Francis on the 15-day disabled list on Wednesday with left shoulder inflammation and gave Redman his second chance this year. None of the candidates for the fifth starter spot distinguished himself this spring, so the Rockies went with Redman because he helped the club late last season. But Redman had uncommon problems throwing strikes. Now, after some success at Triple-A Colorado Springs (5-2, 4.64 ERA in nine starts), Redman returns.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing on Saturday against the D-backs, Miller was masterful through the first four innings, but a rough fifth and sixth ended his night on a sour note. After throwing four straight shutout innings while tossing just 41 pitches to start the game, Miller gave up six runs -- three earned -- in the next two and threw 49 pitches in the process. The 6-foot-6 lefty finished his night in a 5-1 game with two outs in the sixth inning, giving up five hits while striking out four and walking three on 90 pitches. Miller will be facing the Rockies for the first time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: In his last two games, both losses, Reynolds has experienced growth. Two starts ago, he lost to the Mets but lasted seven innings without his best stuff. In his last start, a 4-3 loss to the Tigers, he adjusted to a tight lineup by backing hitters off the plate with inside fastballs. He was charged with four runs in 5 2/3 innings, but two runs scored after he left the game.
away_pitcher_note: On Sunday afternoon against the Diamondbacks, Olsen had a solid outing but got little help from his offense in his ninth no-decision. The 24-year-old -- who came into the game with a 2.58 ERA in his last four starts, but an 0-2 record -- gave up just three runs on five hits while striking out four and walking two before leaving the game after seven innings and throwing 104 pitches. His opponent, Dan Haren, on the other hand, held the Marlins to just one run in seven innings. Florida eventually won on a walk-off single by Jorge Cantu.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa struggled with the command of his fastball and curveball Monday against the Padres. His inconsistency to find the plate put him behind in too many counts, and San Diego took advantage. De La Rosa gave up a season-high 11 hits and six runs in five innings in the no-decision. This was the second-straight shaky start for De La Rosa, who gave up four runs -- two earned -- in just 4 2/3 innings in a loss to Kansas City. De La Rosa is most effective when he uses his wicked slider to strikeout his opponents, but he has just seven strikeouts combined in his past two starts after striking out 10 batters against Cleveland on June 19 and eight batters at the White Sox on June 14.
away_pitcher_note: Working through the lineup a couple of times remains part of the learning curve for Tucker, the 21-year-old rookie right-hander. In his previous start, a no-decision against the Nationals, the hard-throwing former 2005 first-round pick got into trouble in the fifth inning, when he issued solo homers to Elijah Dukes and Dmitri Young. Tucker threw 101 pitches, and gave up six hits. He struck out six, but exited with his team trailing by a run. In his last two starts, Tucker has given up 11 runs in nine innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cook threw his first career shutout, vanquishing the Padres, 4-0, on Tuesday night. He didn't let a runner past second base and forced 15 outs on ground balls. Cook can dominate a game with his sinker, but against an aggressive Padres lineup he crossed up hitters with a four-seam fastball. He finished with four strikeouts and no walks. Cook will be making his fourth appearance against the Marlins. He is 1-1 with a 4.73 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander has been victimized by the long ball of late. He gave up two in his last outing, including a grand slam to Ronnie Belliard, in a loss to the Nationals. In his last five starts, Hendrickson has allowed nine home runs in a 24 1/3 inning span. Hendrickson has dropped five straight decisions. For his career, he is 2-1 with a 3.00 ERA in eight games at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: McClung called his last start, a no-decision at Arizona, "a dogfight." While D-backs starter Yusmeiro Petit retired all nine hitters he faced in the first three innings, McClung battled, facing 16 batters in the first three frames. He surrendered seven hits in that span and plunked two batters, but somehow limited Arizona to two runs. McClung settled in after the third and got the Brewers through 5 1/3 innings, allowing just those two runs on eight hits with one walk and six strikeouts and leaving the team in position to rally for a win. The Rockies are one of six Major League teams McClung has never faced.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez's act plays well in Denver, but it hasn't been a hit in any other city. Now he has a gig in Milwaukee. In his last start, Jimenez held the Padres to one run in 6 1/3 innings of an 8-1 victory, and has gone 3-2 with a 2.67 ERA at Coors Field. On the road, however, he is 0-6 with a 6.96 ERA. But his gameplan against the Padres -- attack inside with his fastball for strikes, or to back hitters off the plate in the early innings -- could work anywhere if he a) has his secondary pitches working, but b) doesn't rely too much on them.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia, the reigning American League Cy Young Award winner and arguably the best pitcher available on the midseason trade market, became a Brewer on Monday when the teams formally agreed to a swap that sent four prospects to Cleveland. Sabathia is a left-hander and will join right-hander Ben Sheets atop Milwaukee's rotation in a bid to end the franchise's 26-year postseason drought.
away_pitcher_note: Making his first big league start since May 6 and pitching on short rest, Redman gave the Rockies everything they could have hoped for against the Marlins. He allowed just two runs on six hits in six innings. Both his fastball and cutter were working, which enabled him to force ground balls that resulted in three double plays. Redman was sent to Triple-A Colorado Springs after pitching ineffectively the first month of the season, but he worked with Sky Sox pitching coach Chuck Kniffin to straighten out his delivery. Redman was called up Wednesday after Jeff Francis (3-7) went on the disabled list with inflammation in his left shoulder.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Sheets didn't have his best stuff, but still came away with a win as he worked in and out of trouble all afternoon to allow just one run over 5 2/3 innings pitched.  Sheets didn't seem to have the ability to put hitters away, causing his pitch count to swell and his outing to be shortened. Still, Sheets managed to keep the game in check and became the first Brewers pitcher to reach 10 wins this season.
away_pitcher_note: Rusch makes his first start for the Rockies since May 31 at Chicago, so when he takes the mound against the Brewers, both of his starts for the club will be against his former teams. Before rejoining the Rockies on Saturday and pitching a rough inning in relief against the Marlins, Rusch went 1-2 with a 4.61 ERA at Triple-A Colorado Springs while waiting for an opening in the rotation. He got his chance when the Rockies decided to send down right-handed prospect Greg Reynolds, who went 2-6 with a 6.71 ERA in 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Bush had one of his best starts of the season, working quickly through eight solid innings. He allowed just one run on four hits, striking out a season-high seven batters and walking none. Bush was lifted for a pinch-hitter in the bottom of the eighth inning, on his way to a no-decision as he left the game with the score tied at 1 after having thrown 100 pitches. The Brewers won the game on a walk-off hit by Prince Fielder, and both manager Ned Yost and Bush were happy with the performance.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa rebounded from two straight poor outings to earn the win against Florida on Saturday. Against the Marlins, De La Rosa gave up three runs on six hits in five innings. He retired the first batter in each of the first four innings, which allowed him to allude any serious trouble. De La Rosa is 2-1 with a 4.90 ERA since returning to the starting rotation on June 14.

home_pitcher_note: Perez pitched another gem against an above-.500 squad on Sunday, shutting out the Phillies over seven innings and limiting them to four hits. While he wouldn't be able to seal the win in the 12-inning test of endurance, his 110 pitches (71 for strikes) were just a few more steps in the right direction for Perez. In seven of his 10 starts vs. teams with a winning record this season, Perez has held those squads to two runs or less. In Perez's last appearance against the Rockies, he tossed five innings and surrendered four runs.
away_pitcher_note: Cook was selected to his first All-Star Game on Sunday, but he didn't pitch like one later that day against the Marlins. His sinker and cutter stayed up in the strike zone, and the Marlins tagged him for seven runs on 11 hits in 7 2/3 innings. This will mark Cook's third game against the Mets this season. He was nearly perfect in the first meeting, pitching a one-run complete game. The second matchup didn't go nearly as smoothly. Cook gave up six runs on 12 hits in seven innings for his fourth loss of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez made a modest effort toward regaining his old form in Monday's start, going 5 1/3 innings and allowing two earned runs to the first-place Phillies. His pitch count was high (105 throws), but manager Jerry Manuel said that this was just Martinez getting to the point where his pitches are moving better but just missing their spots. Martinez will now face the Rockies, who he won't have fond memories of after giving up six earned runs at Coors Field in 4 1/3 innings of work on June 21.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez, who has struggled mightily on the road this season, had a great outing in Milwaukee. The right-hander baffled the Brewers for seven scoreless innings, allowing just three hits and striking out seven. He struggled with his control early on, walking four batters in the first two innings, but worked quickly and was able to keep his pitch count down the rest of the way. Jimenez improved to 4-8 on the season and his ERA dropped to 4.21 with the performance.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey hit another milestone in Tuesday's start, as he didn't walk a single batter in seven shutout innings vs. the Giants. The 6-foot-7 righty has been mixing in both a two- and four-seam fastball to complement his heavy sinker. Because he threw 113 pitches (73 for strikes), manager Jerry Manuel said that Pelfrey will most likely not be allowed to exceed 100 pitches in his next start, which will come against the Rockies. In his last outing against Colorado on June 22, Pelfrey also didn't allow a run but lasted only 5 2/3 innings. He'll come into this start having won his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Redman didn't pitch a lights-out game in Milwaukee his last time out, but the lefty managed to keep the game within reach for the Rockies. He allowed four runs on five hits over five innings of work, walking just one. Redman allowed three of his four earned runs in the first inning, but then settled down to allow just one over the next four. But Redman was up against new Brewers lefty CC Sabathia, who allowed just three runs, and the Colorado bullpen couldn't hold Milwaukee close.

home_pitcher_note: The early part of the season was a rough education for Jimenez, who had never started the season in a rotation. But he has learned. In his last seven starts, Jimenez is 3-3 with a 2.28 ERA, with 35 strikeouts in 43 1/3 innings. Jimenez is 3-2 with a 2.67 ERA in nine starts at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Manager John Russell said Maholm will start the first game of the second half because the lefty has been the Pirates' most effective and efficient starter all season. Maholm showed why in his last start on July 10 against the Yankees. He made the Bronx Bombers look like duds in his eight innings, allowing only two runs on seven hits. He had complete control of the strike zone and seemed to drop every curveball and slider in for strikes. The 25-year-old southpaw is 1-1 with a 3.75 ERA against the Rockies in his career. Both decisions were at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: It's been a long time since July 9, the last time Rusch pitched. But it was worth remembering. Rusch, pitching against one of his former clubs, held the Brewers to one run and five hits in six innings for his first win since April 26. The Rockies are hoping Rusch, who began the year in the Padres bullpen, will provide some veteran stability to the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Snell's last outing against the Cardinals was encouraging. His stat line [five innings, five hits, four runs and six strikeouts] wasn't overwhelming, but his approach and variety of pitches were. Snell now believes he's primed to make a strong second-half run and it begins in Colorado, where he's 1-1 with a 4.72 ERA against the Rockies in his career.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had one of his worst outings of the season in his most recent start against the Brewers, giving up seven earned runs in just 3 2/3 innings. However, Mark Redman wasn't much better against the Mets three days later, surrendering five earned runs on eight hits in just 3 1/3 innings. With Kip Wells expected to start on Monday after being on the disabled list since April 29 with a blood clot in his throwing hand, manager Clint Hurdle decided to go with the younger arm in De La Rosa and move Redman to the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: With Phil Dumatrait on the disabled list and Tom Gorzelanny in the Minors, the Pirates have two rotation spots to fill coming out of the All-Star break. This is the first one. While no announcement has been made, the most likely candidate would seem to be Yoslan Herrera, who made his Major League debut on Saturday. It was a rocky one -- six runs on 11 hits in 4 1/3 innings. However, with the lack of Major League-ready options, Herrera will still most likely get a crack at improving those results.

home_pitcher_note: Cook reported feeling fine Tuesday night after throwing 40 pitches in three memorable shutout innings in the All-Star Game at Yankee Stadium, but stay tuned as to whether the Rockies throw him in this game or adjust his schedule. He sparkled in his last start before the break, holding the Mets to one run on six hits in six innings of a game the Rockies eventually lost because of missed opportunities on offense. In that one, Cook worked his sinker well, but also got three strikeouts because his four-seam fastball was accurate and hitters were not ready for it.
away_pitcher_note: Duke has given up 11 runs on 17 hits in his last two starts. He appeared to be in control against the Cardinals on July 11 with two outs in the third, but St. Louis put together a two-out rally, scoring four runs. It was the beginning of the end for Duke, who was pulled after six innings. The lefty is 2-2 with a 2.77 ERA against the Rockies in his career.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Wells' return to the Majors. He hasn't appeared in a big league game since April 28, when the blood clot in his right hand made it impossible for him to continue. Also, it's his first start since the Rockies' first game, when he held the Cardinals to one run and four hits in 5 1/3 innings in a no-decision that the Rockies eventually won. The Rockies need rotation leadership and are turning to Wells, who believed he should have been in the rotation when the season began.
away_pitcher_note: Eric Stults isn't overpowering, so his margin for error isn't great, as was demonstrated when he allowed first-inning back-to-back homers to the Marlins. But he made a quick adjustment and kept Florida off the scoreboard for the rest of his six-inning outing. He's already thrown a complete-game shutout, and that ERA is hard to overlook. When he keeps his off-speed stuff down, he can mow through a lineup efficiently.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez was shaky in the early innings against Pittsburgh, walking two, hitting another and throwing a wild pitch in the Bucs' three-run third inning. But he gathered his composure and slowed his mechanics to retire the final 13 batters he faced. The outing was a microcosm of Jimenez's season. After a slow start to 2008, Jimenez has pitched some of the best baseball in his short career during his past 10 starts. He hasn't surrendered more than four runs in any outing during that span, dropping his ERA from 4.85 to 4.20, and has picked up three of his four victories.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw will be promoted to make this start for the Dodgers, returning to the rotation after a three-start demotion to Double-A, where he went 2-0 with a 1.00 ERA. Kershaw, a rookie lefty, showed flashes of brilliance in his first tour with the Dodgers, but he also showed the wavering command of a 20-year-old. He has 24 walks in 38 2/3 Major League innings.

home_pitcher_note: Rusch, who spent most of the season pitching for Triple-A Colorado Springs, recorded his second consecutive win after giving up just two runs on six hits in 5 2/3 innings against the Pirates. Rusch stayed ahead in the count and used his curveball and changeup to keep Pittsburgh off balance. Rusch has made 10 starts against the Dodgers in his career, but he's 0-5 with a 14.21 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The All-Star break did Kuroda no good. After being spotted a three-run lead, he was battered by the Diamondbacks for six runs over the first 1 1/3 innings in his first start. The last time he pitched that ineffectively, he wound up on the disabled list with shoulder problems. Coming into the game, he had a 1.19 ERA in his three previous starts. He's 2-7 on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez was moved up one day in the rotation to fill in for Josh Fogg, who will be skipped after he was hit in the mouth with a ball during batting practice on Tuesday. Volquez often fell behind in the count and didn't have an easy inning in his last start against the Mets on Sunday. The 25-year-old All-Star pitched five innings, giving up four runs on eight hits with three walks and three strikeouts. He struggled at times to command the strike zone and even walked the pitcher as he threw 110 pitches in his five innings. It was his shortest outing in his past four starts, though he did not get a decision. Volquez is 5-1 in his past 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cook was ready to go after throwing just 40 pitches -- in the All-Star Game -- over the past nine days, and the extra juice caused him to overthrow in the first inning against the Pirates in his last start, on Sunday. He left his sinkerball up, and Pittsburgh tagged him for three runs on four hits during the inning. However, pitching coach Bob Apodaca got Cook to refocus and settle down, and he was soon back to his All-Star self. Cook gave up just one hit and no runs in his final six innings to earn the win. In four career starts against the Reds, Cook is 1-0 with a 7.11 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Though he did not get a decision, Bailey posted yet another solid performance against the Padres on Monday. The youngster threw 6 1/3 innings, giving up three runs on eight hits with two walks and two strikeouts. He threw 112 pitches and worked himself into and out of a one-out, bases-loaded jam. Bailey said he's changed "a few things" since he was recalled from Triple-A Louisville to replace the injured Aaron Harang, and it's paid off. In two games, he's lowered his ERA from 8.76 to 6.29. He was a victim of a blown save both times. Bailey moved up one day in the rotation after Josh Fogg was hit in the mouth with a ball during batting practice on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa was teetering on the brink of losing his rotation spot before turning in a gem against the Pirates, holding them to one run in seven innings and fanning seven. The difference was his composure. Relying on veteran catcher Yorvit Torrealba, De La Rosa pitched out of three spots in which he might have unraveled.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander received 30 stitches in his upper lip Tuesday after he was struck in the mouth by a ball during batting practice, but threw a 40-pitch bullpen session Friday and reported no problems. Fogg, who pitched for the National League champion Rockies last season, continued his solid return to the Reds' rotation when he pitched six innings and gave up two runs -- one earned -- on eight hits with a walk and a strikeout against the Mets on July 19. It was Fogg's first win since April 9. He continued to show progress with the command of the strike zone, particularly with his fastball -- an issue that plagued him earlier in the year. He threw just 82 pitches in the win with 51 going for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez said it was a dream come true after pitching his first complete game Tuesday against the Dodgers. Jimenez was nearly flawless, giving up one run on four hits and using his slider to induce 18 ground-ball outs. Jimenez has now tossed five consecutive quality starts and has four wins in four straight home starts since June 21. However, he is 1-7 on the road this season with a 5.82 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: For every step forward, Snell continues to take at least one back. After finally finishing six innings on July 18, Snell lasted just three in his last start. His efficiency is the area of greatest concern as it has been for most of the season. He needed 86 pitches to complete those three innings. He's also got to learn to slow his tempo on the mound. Snell faced Colorado two starts ago, lasting six innings and allowing three earned runs on six hits.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies called up De Los Santos from Triple-A Colorado Springs on Monday for his first Major League action since 2005 and his first start in the Majors since 2000. De Los Santos, 35, was 3-5 with a 4.92 ERA in 17 appearances for Colorado Springs, including 0-4, 6.62 as a starter.

home_pitcher_note: Herrera pick up his first Major League win in his third career appearances. After two horrendous starts, Herrera used his sinker early and often to get into tempo and stopped relying so heavily on his off-speed pitches like he had his previous time out. With the sinker moving and Herrera using both sides of the plate, he limited San Diego to six singles in six scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Rusch has won his past three starts and has become a vital part of the Rockies' recent resurgence. His bread-and-butter pitches -- his changeup and curveball -- weren't working against the Dodgers, but he made enough putouts to help the Rockies win. In five innings he gave up three runs on seven hits and walked two. Rusch was great against Pittsburgh on July 18, when he gave up just two runs on six hits in 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After getting off to a promising start this season, Duke is now winless since June 9. He allowed five runs on seven hits in six innings, though only two of those hits were hit on the nose. Regardless, Duke continues to have trouble keeping runners off base and is in a position where he's only pitched past the fifth once in his last six starts. Duke will be facing a Colorado team that he lost to in his first start after the break. Duke started off by retiring the first 10 hitters he face before the Rockies knocked him for nine runs and 10 hits in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: The reasons Cook is having a career year are simple: He's showing batters that he can throw strikes early in counts. That means they don't feel comfortable laying off his sinker, so they're pounding ground ball after ground ball. It happened again Friday night, when he went eight innings, threw 93 pitches and gave up just five hits in a 7-2 victory over the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: For the first time since May 2, 2007, Sanchez will be making a big league start. Last June, the 24-year-old underwent right shoulder surgery, and he has worked his way back ever since. He made five rehab assignment starts, including two for Double-A Carolina. In his last outing, the Venezuelan native worked seven innings. In five Minor League starts, he has thrown 28 innings. The highlight of Sanchez's career was his no-hitter against Arizona on Sept. 6, 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Suddenly able to handle runners on base, and able to spot his fastball for strikes and use his sinker to put hitters away, De La Rosa has held opponents to two runs in 12 2/3 innings while winning his last two starts. He held the Reds to two hits in 6 2/3 innings in his last start, a 5-1 Rockies victory. He still walked five in his last game, so there's room for improvement.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Volstad turned in a quality start at Chicago, even though he wasn't involved in the decision. The 21-year-old now will face the team he made his MLB debut against. On July 6 at Coors Field, Volstad threw two innings of scoreless relief, and he collected his first MLB win. This will be his third big league start. At Chicago, Volstad surrendered his first home run of the season -- either at the Minor League or big league levels. It came 19 1/3 innings into his MLB career. He also threw 91 innings at Double-A.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez has demonstrated tremendous aptitude over the course of his first full season. He started rough, but in July he went 5-1 with a 1.74 ERA. Jimenez throws four pitches effectively, and has learned how to adjust when one or more of them is not at its best on a particular day. At Cincinnati on Sunday, he wasn't able to keep his fastball down in the strike zone, but he still overpowered enough hitters for 12 flyball outs in six scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco was pretty much done in by one bad inning against the Mets on Monday. In the top of the second, Nolasco threw 18 pitches and gave up two runs on three straight hits to start the inning. Other than that, the 25-year-old righty was pretty much in control in the no-decision, allowing seven hits while striking out eight and walking none in six innings. Nolasco left after throwing 98 pitches -- 69 for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: De Los Santos was called up from Triple-A Colorado Springs to start Monday against the Pirates. He walked six in four-plus innings. Although he didn't get the loss in the 8-4 defeat, his start didn't help. Manager Clint Hurdle originally was lukewarm about starting him against the Marlins, but the Rockies did not obtain an experienced option at Thursday afternoon's non-waiver Trade Deadline

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Mets on Tuesday, Olsen kept his team in the game by giving up just two runs in 5 2/3 innings. Olsen started off the game on a bad note by giving up three straight doubles, but he was able to get out of the first inning with just one run and cruised in the next four frames. The 24-year-old went on to retire nine of the next 10 hitters he faced after the first inning, but was pulled in the sixth after scattering another run and throwing 24 pitches to six batters. He finished the night giving up six hits while walking two and striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: Rusch has been steady since joining the Rockies' rotation, and was in the lead on Tuesday against the Pirates when he was removed in an offensive substitution. The bullpen lost the game. Rusch gave up three runs on six hits, but didn't strike out any and walked two. The Rockies aren't looking for complete games from Rusch, but being efficient enough to throw six innings would be big.

home_pitcher_note: Cook has continued to push the Diamondbacks' Brandon Webb for most wins in the National League. As a sign of his maturity, Cook regained his composure after a fifth inning that saw him walk the first two batters and give up four runs, and lasted through the seventh inning of a 7-4 victory over the Pirates. Cook returns to Coors Field, where he is 6-3 with a 3.43 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Redding struggled through one of his worst performances of the season last Wednesday against Philadelphia. The veteran right-hander lasted just four-plus innings and couldn't get an out in a five-run fifth before being replaced by Steven Shell. Redding threw just 73 pitches -- 47 for strikes -- and fanned one batter in the outing.

home_pitcher_note: So, which guy shows up? Is it the one that gave up two runs in 12 2/3 innings in his first two starts of a 10-game road trip, or the one who gave up seven runs, five hits and four walks in 1 2/3 innings of a 12-2 loss at Florida in De La Rosa's last start? The Rockies badly need some semblance of consistent good pitching from him.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan recorded one of the worst outings of his career last Thursday when he surrendered eight runs -- six earned -- in just 5 2/3 innings against Philadelphia. The southpaw allowed nine hits and three walks, though he also struck out seven, his second-highest total of the season. Lannan threw 104 pitches, 66 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Francis last pitched in the Major Leagues on June 28, when he gave up five runs -- four earned -- and 11 hits in six innings of a 7-6 loss in Detroit. After resting and regaining his health, a three-start Minor League rehab assignment allowed him to regain fastball command and hone his breaking pitch and changeup. The Rockies need him to help transform them into a contender.
away_pitcher_note: Bergmann will start the second game of a doubleheader on Thursday after rain postponed Wednesday's matchup in Colorado. Bergmann was inconsistent in his last start. He allowed five runs on a bases-clearing three-run double and a two-run homer in ths second, but just one run in his other five innings in a 10-6 win over the Reds. He struck out two and walked three.

home_pitcher_note: Francis last pitched in the Majors on June 28, when he gave up five runs, four earned, and 11 hit sin six innings of a 7-6 loss at Detroit. Then he went on the disabled list with shoulder inflammation. After resting and regaining health, three-start Minor League rehab assignment allowed him to regain fastball command and hone his breaking pitch and changeup. The Rockies need him to help transform them into a contender.
away_pitcher_note: Perez posted one of his best outings of 2008 on Friday, when he went 7 1/3 innings and allowed just one run and three hits while striking out five. He threw 63 of his 102 pitches for strikes and got a standing ovation when he left the field in the eighth inning.

home_pitcher_note: In five starts since becoming a regular member of the Rockies' rotation, Rusch is 3-0 with a 3.67 ERA and the team is 4-1. In other words, he is doing exactly what a back-of-the-rotation starter should be doing -- keeping his club in games. In Sunday's 3-2 Rockies victory over the Marlins, Rusch's location was off at the start of the game, but he held the Marlins to two runs.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy, the reigning National League Cy Young Award winner, dropped his seventh game of the season, though he allowed just one run on five hits in seven innings during a 2-0 loss to the Giants at PETCO Park on Aug. 2. Peavy actually lowered his ERA -- from 2.67 to 2.59, striking out seven in his seven innings with no walks -- but he had nothing to show for it as the Padres fell to just 6-37 when scoring three or fewer runs this season.

home_pitcher_note: Cook had been practically infallible during his three-game winning streak from July 20-30, but he turned in one of his worst pitching performances of the season Monday against the Nationals. There wasn't any tilt depth to most of his pitches, and his trademark sinker stayed up in the zone. Cook, who had a two-run throwing error in the third, gave up seven runs -- four earned -- in 5 2/3 innings. It was his third-shortest outing of the season and tied his season high for runs allowed. Cook has been dominant against the Padres this season, going 2-0 with a 0.56 ERA in two games. He threw a complete-game shutout against them on July 1.
away_pitcher_note: The 42-year-old Maddux showed he wouldn't need 14 consecutive starts between victories, as was the case recently, as win No. 352 came rather easily, when he allowed one run in six innings in a victory over the Giants on Aug. 3. Maddux even had an RBI single, his first RBI in nearly two years. Maddux had good movement on his fastball, something he said he typically gets at PETCO Park but not so much elsewhere. He didn't walk a batter and hit one batter. He worked fast and got ahead of hitters. It was, really, vintage Maddux.

home_pitcher_note: Rockies manager Clint Hurdle announced before Friday's game that newly acquired pitcher Livan Hernandez would start in place of Jorge De La Rosa on Sunday. Hernandez went 10-8 with a 5.48 ERA in 23 starts with the Twins but was placed on waivers after Minnesota recalled Francisco Liriano. The Rockies acquired Hernandez because of his ability to eat innings and his familiarity with the National League West. He's 33-27 with a 3.95 ERA in 80 games against the Rockies' division rivals.
away_pitcher_note: Young, in his second start since a two-month stint on the disabled list with a facial injury, pitched 5 1/3 innings and allowed two earned runs to the Mets. He was a little gassed near the end, which was to be expected, so manager Bud Black pulled him after 98 pitches (55 for strikes). Young said he had good life on his fastball, while his off-speed pitches are "still coming along." Against Colorado, he's come around just fine, holding a 5-1 record vs. the Rockies with a 2.40 ERA in 56 career innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez picked a bad time to remind everyone he's still only in his first full Major League season. He dominated in July, going 5-1 with a 1.74 ERA, but against the Nationals he reverted back to the mistakes that plagued him earlier this season. He threw with plenty of velocity against Washington but couldn't find the plate, walking a season-high six batters in five innings. He also gave up six runs, the most he's surrendered since May 27. Jimenez said the problem was with his mechanics -- his left shoulder got too far ahead of the rest of his body when he went through his motion.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson was outstanding in his last outing against the Pirates, but the bad news for he and the D-backs was that Jeff Karstens was a little better. Johnson held Pittsburgh to just two runs over 7 1/3 innings and did not walk a batter while fanning seven. Karstens, though, carried a perfect game through 7 2/3 innings before winding up with a two-hit shutout. The loss snapped Johnson?s five-start winning streak and left him stranded at 293 career wins.

home_pitcher_note: Francis's return from shoulder inflammation started off sweet but quickly turned sour against the Nationals. He gave up just two hits in four innings before unraveling in the fifth and sixth, giving up five runs. Three of those runs came off two home runs by Lastings Milledge. Francis has now given up a team-high 19 homers this season. The lefty had great location with his fastball early, but it began to cut in on him as the game progressed, which allowed the Nationals to take advantage. Francis said he felt no pain in his shoulder after the game, but both his sinker and his four-seam fastball were thrown with noticeably less velocity than usual.
away_pitcher_note: Davis struggled again in his last outing against the Braves, lasting just 4 1/3 innings, giving up seven runs on nine hits, picking up the loss. It was Davis' second consecutive bad outing after taking a perfect game into the seventh inning in San Diego July 29. In his last two starts, Davis has lasted a combined six innings and has given up 12 earned runs in the last two games.

home_pitcher_note: Rusch is starting in place of Aaron Cook, who is resting an unspecified amount of time with general fatigue. That may turn out to be a good thing for the Rockies. Rusch has been Colorado's most consistent starter over the past few weeks, winning four straight decisions since July 9. In his most recent start, against the Padres, Rusch gave up two runs in six innings to beat his former club. The key to the 33-year-old's success has been his ability to manage games and throw strikes. In his past six starts, Rusch has issued just three walks compared to 20 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Haren lost his last start, which turned out to be a 5 1/3-inning debacle. He allowed six runs on 10 hits to the Braves, striking out five as he picked up the loss. Things started to unravel toward the end of his outing and afterward, as seven runs ended up scoring in the sixth inning. The $44 million man has struggled a bit recently. Despite winning four starts in a row, in his last two starts has given up a total of 10 runs in 11 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Redding struggled against Milwaukee last Saturday, allowing three home runs and five runs overall in just five innings. He struck out three, but got no offensive support as Washington got shut out for the second straight day in a 6-0 loss.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa was moved to the bullpen after the Rockies acquired Livan Hernandez last week. However, De La Rosa was re-inserted into the rotation when Aaron Cook was taken out for rest. De La Rosa's last appearance was in relief duty Aug. 9 against the Padres. The lefty was dominant, giving up no runs on just one hit and striking out three in 2 1/3 innings. He was equally impressive in his last start, on Aug. 5, against the Nationals. He surrendered two runs in seven innings and struck out six in the no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan was again stellar Sunday against Milwaukee. He went six innings, allowing just one run and striking out six. He did walk five batters, but he left with the score tied at 1-1. Late-inning offensive pushed the game past nine innings, where the Nationals lost 5-4. Lannan did lower his ERA to 3.40.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez couldn't have gotten off to a worse start as a Rockie. The former World Series MVP gave up four straight hits to open Sunday's game against the Padres, and all four came around to score. Hernandez retired the side in order in the second, but his inability to keep the ball down in the strike zone continued in the third, when he gave up five runs off two home runs in the inning. The 33-year-old was taken out after giving up nine runs on seven hits and walking four in 2 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Perez started for Washington on Tuesday and pitched six solid innings, giving up three runs on eight hits against the Mets. Most importantly, he gave most of the relievers a day off. Perez got off to a slow start as New York scored three runs in three innings against him. After that, he settled down and held the Mets scoreless the rest of the way.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies are hoping a few extra days of rest will help Cook, who has experienced tightness and pain in his back ever since throwing three innings in the All-Star Game. Cook went 11-6 with a 3.57 ERA in 20 starts before the break, but he is 3-2 with a 5.13 ERA since. The Rockies pulled him out of a scheduled start on Thursday and moved him to Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda has his act back together, having posted his third consecutive strong outing by pitching a two-hitter for seven innings against Philadelphia. Kuroda has overcome the mental block about getting full extension on his slider and the pitch is now as sharp as it was when he threw two shutouts. He made only 79 pitches against the Phillies and has a 1.21 ERA over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez labored through six innings Tuesday, throwing 108 pitches and giving up four runs on 11 hits against the D-backs. While he clearly didn't have his best stuff, Jimenez kept the Rockies in the game by striking out four and wiggling his way through several jams. The right-hander struggled in his last outing against Washington on Aug. 7. He gave up six runs on eight hits in five innings to take the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley allowed the Brewers three runs on four hits in the first two innings before shutting them down on one hit over the next five innings. He's won his last three decisions and eight of his last 10. Billingsley is 0-2 lifetime with a 6.46 ERA against the Rockies and hasn't faced them yet this year.
away_pitcher_note: Francis, in his second start since returning from missing time with a shoulder injury, displayed his old velocity and command in his most recent start, when he gave up three runs over six innings of a no-decision against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe's standout start against the tough Milwaukee lineup got lost in the late-inning back and forth, but he pitched well enough to deserve a 10th win. He allowed only one run over seven innings without a walk and as soon as manager Joe Torre gave the game to the bullpen, everything unraveled. Lowe hasn't been the most consistent as a Dodger, but he has been an innings-eater.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa's strong start against the Nationals on Friday -- when he went six innings, struck out seven and gave up three hits in a win -- and the fact he's been on more than off since the All-Star break, have earned him a chance to stay in the rotation and prove that he's viable there in the future.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez is making his third start with the Rockies. The veteran right-hander allowed six runs and 10 hits to the Nationals his last time out, but was able to pull out a victory and end a three-start losing steak. Hernandez is 5-5 with a 6.41 ERA, 29 strikeouts and 19 walks in his last 10 starts but has split his two decisions while allowing 15 runs since joining the Rockies on Aug. 10.
away_pitcher_note: Originally scheduled to pitch on Thursday, Harang will instead pitch on Friday due to neck spasms. In his last start, on Saturday night, the righty endured his second straight tough outing, giving up a career-high eight earned runs in 3 1/3 innings against the Cardinals. The righty allowed seven hits and three walks while throwing 78 pitches. Harang has yielded 16 earned runs in 7 1/3 frames over his last two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Cook, who long ago set a career high for victories, is in pursuit of a 20-win season. He has won four of his past six starts, though he hasn't gone long in any of his last three. After two losses in which he lasted 5 2/3 innings, Cook went five in his last start, allowing two runs on seven hits in a win against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez was masterful in blanking the Cardinals on just three hits over seven innings in his last start. He walked four and struck out four in a 97-pitch effort. After a relatively rough stretch following the All-Star break, Volquez has caught his second wind. He was solid for 6 1/3 innings and earned a 5-1 win over the Pirates on Tuesday. Working on two extra days of rest, he gave up one earned run and five hits, walking three and striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez earned his second victory of August and put a two-game losing streak to rest by allowing three runs over five innings against the Dodgers. Jimenez had struggled with his mechanics and had difficulty repeating his delivery. Jimenez was mostly sharp in his last start but needed to exit early after throwing 102 pitches and handed the ball to the bullpen, which tossed four scoreless.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the Cubs on Tuesday, Cueto pitched seven innings and gave up one earned run on four hits with two walks, two hit batsmen and five strikeouts, and he certainly deserved better than a 5-0 loss. He nicely evaded jams throughout the game, as he had runners in scoring position with fewer than two outs in the second through sixth innings. He also had a much more clean first inning in which he retired the side in order, which has been a sticking point in previous outings.

home_pitcher_note: Cain left his last start with a 5-2 lead, but Brian Wilson's first blown save since May 2 denied him the opportunity to square his record at .500 for the first time since April 2007. Nevertheless, Cain is on a roll. He has a 2.14 ERA in his last 10 starts and has allowed no more than one run in six of those outings. Cain, who made his Major League debut against Colorado on Aug. 29, 2005, is 6-3 with a 2.89 ERA against the Rockies
away_pitcher_note: Francis was the staff leader in victories last season and was fourth in the NL with 17 victories but he's posted just three this season. A problem for the left-hander has been fastball command. In his last start, Francis allowed three runs, one earned, on nine hits with four strikeouts for a no-decision against the Dodgers. Francis is 6-5 in his career against the Giants and 2-4 at AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: Palmer earned himself another start as the fill-in for injured left-hander Jonathan Sanchez. He worked six respectable innings against Florida last Thursday, allowing two runs and six hits in six innings while receiving the no-decision. Palmer received considerable defensive help, as the Giants turned two double plays (he started one of them) and threw out a runner at home. Still, it was a vast improvement over Palmer's Major League debut against Atlanta on Aug. 16, when he yielded six runs and seven hits in 2 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa pitched well in his last start, allowing two runs -- one earned -- on four hits and two walks while striking out four. But the left-hander took the loss as the Rockies could generate only one run. De La Rosa said he made just one mistake on the day, a curveball that Andre Ethier hit for a go-ahead single. De La Rosa allowed three runs -- two earned -- and four hits over 5 1/3 innings for a no-decision against the Giants earlier this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum's coming off an outstanding start in what is becoming an increasingly outstanding season. He lasted eight innings against San Diego last Friday, allowing four hits in a 5-0 Giants victory. Lincecum became the first Major Leaguer to reach 200 strikeouts and the first Giant to amass that many Ks in a season since Jason Schmidt had 251 in 2004. Lincecum's 1-1 with a 2.70 ERA in three starts this year against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez again struggled with his command in his last outing against the Reds. He kept balls up and Cincinnati tagged him for six runs on eight hits in 3 2/3 innings. Hernandez has given up at least six runs in all three starts with the Rockies, and he hasn't made it past the sixth inning in any of them.

home_pitcher_note: Hayhurst had an interesting Major League debut on Aug. 23 against the Giants at AT&T Park, allowing three runs in four innings. Hayhurst, recalled earlier that day from Triple-A Portland, was on a pitch count since most of his work this season in Portland had been in relief. But Hayhurst went only four innings against the Giants, allowing three runs on five hits with two walks and two strikeouts. He could make his next start or end up in the bullpen if the Padres decide Chris Young and/or Shawn Estes would be ready to come off the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Cook wasn't able to make it past the fifth inning for the third straight game Saturday against the Reds. He grinded through five innings, giving up four runs (three earned). Cook has been plagued by fatigue and back stiffness the past few weeks, but he said there were positive signs from his latest outing. Rather than missing up in the strike zone, like he had in his previous three outings, many of his pitches were too low, which resulted in less big hits. He also said it's an easier adjustment to fix.

home_pitcher_note: Geer makes his Major League debut against the Rockies. He spent the entire season with Triple-A Portland, going 8-9 with a 4.54 ERA in 28 games, including 27 starts, for the Beavers. Geer is one of a handful of young pitchers the Padres are excited about, and one the team wants to get a look at over the final month of the regular season.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez earned a no decision against Cincinnati after giving up three runs on four hits in six innings. He was sharp early, but an errant throw to first led to one run, and he gave up three walks and a home run in the sixth. Jimenez hasn't been pitching as well as he did in July, when he went 5-1 with a 1.74 ERA, but manager Clint Hurdle has been impressed with the way he's been able to get by without his best stuff. Jimenez is 2-2 with a 4.66 ERA in August.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy threw a season-high 121 pitches in his last start on Monday against Arizona and pitched well, though he earned a no-decision. Peavy allowed two runs on four hits over six innings with seven strikeouts. He lowered his ERA to 2.84 overall and 1.54 at home. He likely would have worked longer but the D-backs made him work. Peavy threw 36 pitches in the fourth inning alone, including nine to Chris Snyder, who eventually lined a two-run single into center field after fouling off five pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Francis finally got rewarded with a win in his third consecutive quality start, allowing two runs in seven innings against the Giants on Monday night. He was winless in his five previous starts, which included three no-decisions. He still has trouble with the first inning, though, as he gave up both runs in the first and now has a 9.23 ERA in the inning as opposed to a 4.28 ERA in all other innings combined.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa turned in a quality start in his last outing, also against the Giants. He gave up one earned run on five hits, walking three and striking out three. He's put together four consecutive quality starts and has won four of his last six decisions.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Sanchez's first start since leaving the disabled list. He missed three starts with a strained throwing shoulder and was replaced in the rotation by Matt Palmer. Sanchez didn't look at all like he was hurting in his last performance, as he allowed two runs and five hits in seven innings on Aug. 11 in a 3-1 loss at Houston. But before that he failed to work six innings in six consecutive starts. Sanchez has faced the Rockies three times this season, earning a win on June 12 despite yielding seven runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez earned himself another start after allowing two runs on five hits over 6 1/3 innings against the Giants on Wednesday night. He had given up 12 runs over 9 2/3 innings in his first two starts with the Rockies. He took a three-hitter into the seventh inning of that game before allowing back-to-back home runs. He had given up 31 runs over his previous five games overall.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum continued to strengthen his National League Cy Young Award credentials in his most recent outing, allowing one run in 7 2/3 innings as the Giants beat Colorado on Wednesday, 4-1. He also struck out 10 in that game, marking the seventh time this season he has done so. That matches the third-best total in the franchise's San Francisco history (since 1958). Jason Schmidt had nine double-digit strikeout games in 2004, Ray Sadecki recorded eight in 1968 and John "The Count" Montefusco had seven in 1975.

home_pitcher_note: Aaron Cook was solid in his last start, a victory over the San Diego Padres on Friday. His 95 pitches went over six innings as he allowed only two runs on five hits with two walks and three strikeouts. After pitching out of a first-inning jam and throwing a wild pitch that led to another run scoring in the second, the next four innings saw only one other run cross the plate on Cookʼs watch. He said he felt great as he continues to get back into prime physical shape after dealing with a back issue.
away_pitcher_note: Complaining of a "flat" changeup, Zito allowed eight runs (seven earned) and seven hits in 3 1/3 innings at Cincinnati in his most recent outing. He had thrived before that, winning back-to-back outings for the first time since the end of last season. The Giants are 9-9 in Zito's last 18 starts after losing in each of his first nine appearances. Somewhat remarkably, Zito has not faced Colorado this season. He was 1-1 with a 3.12 ERA against the Rockies in four starts against them last year.

home_pitcher_note: Ubaldo Jimenez struggled with his control in his last start, against the Padres on Aug. 30. When he did throw strikes, the Padres had difficulty producing, and Jimenez's inability to regain his rhythm in the fourth inning cost the Rockies the game. In that inning, Jimenez walked four batters and saw three runs cross the plate. He would eventually leave the inning after lasting only 3 2/3 innings, allowing six runs on two hits, while striking out two and walking five. Jimenez would later say that it was a mechanics issue that led to his struggles.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler answered a one-year contract extension offer from the Astros by earning his 10th win of the season against the Cardinals on Saturday. The righty gave up a three-run homer to Rick Ankiel in the first inning before settling in, allowing just four hits through the second through sixth innings. Now he'll start against Colorado for the first time this season after throwing three innings in relief against the Rockies, where he gave up three runs on five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Continuing a hard-luck season, Francis held the Padres to one run and six hits in seven innings on Sunday, but he left the game trailing. He finished with a no-decision in a 2-1 loss. But the good news is Francis struck out six and walked two, and the biggest hit against him came courtesy of a fielding misplay. Francis is 1-1 with a 1.93 ERA in two career starts against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt had his longest outing of the year in his last start, throwing 8 1/3 innings in a winning effort versus the Cubs. He is 5-1 with a 1.59 ERA over his last six games, allowing eight earned runs over 45 1/3 innings. Oswalt hasn't faced the Rockies this year. In his career, he's 5-1 with a 2.14 ERA over eight starts against Colorado, allowing 13 earned runs over 54 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: There's a long way for the Rockies to go to equal last year's magic, but if the pixie dust falls the way of the Purple Pinstripes, De La Rosa could be a huge part of the reason. De La Rosa is 3-1 in his last five starts, and pitching better each time. He showed tremendous change-of-pace on Monday while holding the Giants scoreless on four hits in a 4-0 Rockies victory.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is scheduled to pitch in the finale of the Astros' series with the Rockies, but that could change since he was pulled from his last start with a strained right oblique muscle. Rodriguez had thrown 5 2/3 scoreless innings, allowing seven hits, while striking out four on 93 pitches. After his last outing, manager Cecil Cooper expressed optimism the lefty would make his next scheduled start.

home_pitcher_note: While going 1-3 with a 7.39 ERA in his past six starts, Campillo has shown signs that he's tiring. The 29-year-old rookie right-hander had gone 3-1 with a 1.77 ERA in his last six starts. Knowing that he isn't a power pitcher, opponents have shown greater patience against Campillo's offspeed repertoire. This will be his first start against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Cook had one of his worst outings of the season in his last start against the Giants. The right-hander gave up six runs on 10 hits in just three innings. It was the shortest outing of the season for Cook, who had trouble keeping his sinker down in the strike zone. Cook had been battling fatigue and lower back stiffness in recent weeks, but he said he felt fine and that the poor start was due to bad execution.

home_pitcher_note: Parr enjoyed a successful Major League debut while tossing six scoreless innings against the Nationals on Thursday night. The 22-year-old right-hander, who doesn't possess overpowering stuff, was labeled as being "sneaky quick" by Braves manager Bobby Cox. Primarily a fastball pitcher, he has the ability to keep his pitches out of harm's way. While combining for 13 wins in the Minors this season, he surrendered just 13 homers.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez is 1-3 with a 10.13 ERA since joining the Rockies, but positives have arisen from his last two starts -- a loss and a no-decision against the Giants. He pitched into the seventh inning in the loss and the sixth inning in the other game, won by the Rockies. Hernandez was able to change speeds effectively and stay out of the middle of the plate in both games. The only problem is when he loses his effectiveness -- it goes quickly and manager Clint Hurdle has to be alert and have relief help ready.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has exceeded his innings total from any previous professional season by more than 30 frames, and he's starting to show some fatigue as he nears the end of his rookie season. Despite enduring early control problems on Friday against the Nationals, the right-hander allowed one run in five innings and won for the first time in five starts. An extra day of rest may prove beneficial as Jurrjens attempts to claim his second win of the season against the Rockies. He scattered eight hits in 7 2/3 scoreless innings at Coors Field on June 16.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Jimenez rebounded nicely against the Astros after giving up six runs to the Padres. Against Houston, the right-hander relied less on his breaking pitches and focused exclusively on pounding the strike zone with his fastball. The results were encouraging: He surrendered just three runs on five hits in six innings, and the Rockies won. Jimenez is 1-1 with a 4.09 ERA in two starts against the Braves this season.

home_pitcher_note: Francis pitched extremely well for the second straight outing, a good sign that the left shoulder troubles that plagued him earlier this season have completely subsided. Unfortunately for Francis, he went up against two aces -- Jake Peavy and Roy Oswalt -- and went 0-1 in the two games. The lefty made just one mistake against the Astros on Saturday, leaving a changeup up in the strike zone that was pounded for a two-run home run. However, Francis has given up just three runs on 13 hits in his past 13 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley threw another gem on Saturday against the D-backs, yielding four hits and a walk in 6 1/3 scoreless innings, striking out nine. Billingsley -- Los Angeles' leader in wins, ERA and strikeouts -- has now gone 11 straight outings without allowing more than three runs, a period in which he's 6-2 with a 2.48 ERA. The right-hander is 0-2 with an 8.76 ERA in three career outings (two starts) at Colorado, but he threw six innings of two-run ball on Aug. 20 against the Rockies at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had been dominant in his past three outings before Sunday, giving up just two runs in 19 innings. But he struggled with his command against the Astros, giving up four runs on six hits and walking four in 5 1/3 innings. De La Rosa surrendered just one run in six innings the last time he faced the Dodgers on Aug. 21.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Kershaw had a difficult start against the Diamondbacks. The left-hander pitched out of a bases-loaded jam in the first inning, but he couldn't protect a two-run lead while allowing home runs to Chris Snyder and Adam Dunn. Kershaw's pitch count soared, and he was lifted after four innings, even though he walked only one batter. This next start will be in Coors Field, where Kershaw was pounded for five runs on 10 hits in three innings by the Rockies on July 22.

home_pitcher_note: Cook has been stymied twice in his attempt to match Kevin Ritz (1996), Pedro Astacio (1999) and Jeff Francis (2007) for the club single-season record for victories (17). The first time, against the Giants, he lasted just three innings. The second time, he gave up three first-inning runs against the Braves, and four runs total before leaving too early for a decision. Cook said the Braves hit a couple of good pitches during the first, and he felt he was in a better place mechanically.
away_pitcher_note: After beating his former Padres teammates in Los Angeles, Maddux lost to them in San Diego, allowing four runs over six innings. The Dodgers were blanked, so Maddux had little chance, but he trailed almost from the start, allowing a two-run homer to Adrian Gonzalez in the first inning. Maddux is 1-3 since joining the Dodgers for the stretch run, with two of the losses coming against last-place teams (Washington was the other).

home_pitcher_note: Reynolds, the club's No. 1 pick in 2006, had 11 starts early in the season, but they came at a time when he had troubles with his delivery and wasn't in the strike zone consistently enough to stay in the Majors. But he pitched better at Coors Field, where the Rockies were 5-2 in his seven starts. Reynolds pitched well in a relief appearance against the Braves on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: LeBlanc was in line for his first Major League victory in his last start, on Tuesday against the Dodgers, allowing but one run over six innings -- on a solo home run to Manny Ramirez to start the sixth inning. But the Padres bullpen did not hold the lead. LeBlanc, a left-hander, had his nasty changeup moving and spotted his fastball well. He allowed five hits, two walks and had four strikeouts. He worked fast and smartly against a team that had defeated him six days earlier in his Major League debut.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez's last start, a no-decision against the Braves on Thursday night, is best described as mixed. He left after five innings with a lead, and he struck out six. But he also yielded five hits, walked four, hit a batter and threw 92 pitches. Deep into his first full season, Jimenez has had his moments but hasn't displayed consistency.
away_pitcher_note: Estes was roughed up in his second start since coming off the disabled list earlier this month. The veteran left-hander allowed three runs in the second inning of a loss to the Dodgers at PETCO Park on Wednesday. Estes allowed two home runs, a solo shot to James Loney and later a two-run shot to center field by Manny Ramirez. Estes left after five innings, having allowed five runs on six hits, with three walks and one strikeout. Estes is among the pitchers the Padres are evaluating over the final weeks of the regular season as they try to see who could join their rotation in 2009.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez was demoted from the starting rotation after giving up four runs in 4 1/3 innings last week against the Braves. However, he was forced to make a spot start Wednesday when Jeff Francis was shut down for the season. Francis missed all of July with shoulder inflammation, and he felt pain in the shoulder after his last two outings. Hernandez is 1-3 with a 9.85 ERA in six games with the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Geer might not be as highly-touted as fellow rookie pitcher Wade LeBlanc, though the right-hander is unbeaten after three starts and has a 3.18 ERA after limiting the Giants to two runs on nine hits in seven innings in his last start, Sept. 11 at PETCO Park. Geer allowed more hits than he would have liked but worked fast and didn't walk a batter as he finished with two strikeouts. He recorded 16 fly ball outs, including a few that center fielder Will Venable ran down near the fence in deep center field.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa pitched decently against the Dodgers, but one bad inning in the fourth did him in. He allowed three runs in the frame and three hits. All told, the left-hander gave up four runs on seven hits, struck out five and walked three in five innings. It was De La Rosa's first loss since Aug. 21, when he gave up two runs in six innings in Los Angeles.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer was lights-out in his last start on Sunday against the Reds at Chase Field, throwing six innings of two-hit, one-run ball. The rookie had nine strikeouts to three walks, but still is searching for his first Major League win, despite having a team-low ERA of 2.80 for starters. After just 14 big league appearances, Scherzer has never faced the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Cook pitched his best outing since the All-Star break on Sunday against the Dodgers, but he still fell short in his bid to tie the Rockies' single-season win record after Greg Maddux pitched equally well. Cook threw eight shutout innings while surrendering eight hits and striking out two. His location was much better than it had been in recent outings, and he kept his sinker low to induce 17 ground-ball outs.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the Giants, Davis pitched seven strong innings. He wasn't involved in the decision for the third consecutive game, but it may have been the best Davis had pitched in about two months, as he walked no batters and allowed only one unearned run on a dropped fly ball in the outfield. Davis has faced the Rockies only once this year, taking a no-decision on Aug. 13, when he threw five innings, allowing four runs (three earned) on six hits at Coors Field in a 6-5 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Reynolds didn't last long in his first start since July 4. The 6-foot-7 righty lasted just two innings plus five batters after giving up seven runs on nine hits Monday against the Padres. Reynolds was optioned to Triple-A Colorado Springs after giving up seven runs in 1 1/3 innings on Independence Day and spent his time there working on his location and mechanics. The work didn't pay off in Reynolds' return, and he was clearly frustrated after the game.
away_pitcher_note: It was back to basics in Haren's last start. After going four starts without a win, Haren tossed the first shutout of his career, limiting the Giants to just four hits. He tied a career high by striking out 12 batters. It took Haren 117 pitches to finish the Giants off after needing 99 to get through four innings in his last start. Haren admitted he had lost a bit of confidence in himself after being roughed up in recent starts, but he seemed to get it all back again. Haren is 2-0 with a 1.92 ERA in two starts against the Rockies this year.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old ace originally was scheduled to pitch Wednesday, but the Giants capitalized on Monday's scheduled off-day to juggle the rotation and give Lincecum an extra start, which will occur on the final day of the season against Los Angeles. Lincecum's six-decision winning streak ended in his last outing, a 3-2 loss at Arizona. Nevertheless, Lincecum pitched his second complete game in a row and walked none, only the third time in 31 starts he has managed that feat.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez got off to a shaky start Tuesday, giving up a two-run home run to Adrian Gonzalez in the first. He settled down after that, though, for one of his best outings of the season. Jimenez gave up two runs on three hits and struck out nine in seven innings. He relaxed after the first inning and focused on better command with his fastball and breaking pitches. Jimenez, who has 158 strikeouts, became just the fourth pitcher in Rockies history to whiff at least 150 batters in a single season.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez is coming off a sloppy 3 2/3-inning outing in which he allowed six runs and six hits at Arizona. That cliche about "making pitches when he had to" didn't apply to Sanchez, who could have escaped the second inning unscathed but allowed a double to opposing pitcher Brandon Webb with two outs, two on and an 0-2 count. Arizona proceeded to score five runs. Sanchez owns a 2-4 record at AT&T Park, but his home ERA (4.33) is superior to his road figure (5.02). He's 1-1 with a 5.25 ERA in four starts this season against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez struggled after the Rockies acquired him for a stretch run that never was, and lost his rotation spot. But he went back into the rotation when the Rockies decided to shut down Jeff Francis because of shoulder pain. Hernandez responded by pitching five scoreless innings and giving up three hits in a 1-0 victory over the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Despite starting the season 0-8, Zito has reached double figures in victories for the eighth consecutive season. A 4-1 surge in his last seven starts has helped Zito regain some equilibrium. Zito began throwing a slider earlier in the season and wasn't comfortable with it, but lately he has relied on it more, and it has made his other pitches more effective, particularly his changeup. Zito excelled in his only previous appearance against the Rockies, allowing two runs and four hits in eight innings on Sept. 3 at Coors Field in San Francisco's 9-2 triumph.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa was extremely sharp against the D-backs, giving up just one run on three hits in six innings to earn the win. He had problems with his command in the fourth inning, when he threw a wild pitch and walked two straight batters to load the bases, but Ian Stewart made a leaping catch at third to bail him out. Besides that -- and Adam Dunn's solo home run in the sixth -- De La Rosa had little trouble, striking out six in the outing.

home_pitcher_note: Haren will be making his final start of the 2008 regular season. The right-hander has gotten back on the winning track after a rough stretch at the end of August and beginning of September. In his last outing, he allowed three runs over six innings to the Rockies in Coors Field. All three of the runs scored on Garrett Atkins' fourth-inning homer. In his start before that, he tossed his first career shutout as the D-backs beat the Giants, 2-0.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies scratched the fatigued Aaron Cook (16-9, 3.96 ERA) and turned to Hirsh, who will be making his first Major League start this season and first since last Aug. 7, when he suffered a broken fibula when hit by a line drive from the Brewers' J.J. Hardy. This season, he suffered a rotator cuff sprain in Spring Training, spent most of the year at Triple-A Colorado Springs (4-4, 5.80 ERA), and made three relief appearances for the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Webb is looking to become the first pitcher to record 23 wins in a season since Curt Schilling and Barry Zito each did it in 2002. Webb has won his last three starts after being unsuccessful in three tries to pick up his 20th win. In his last outing against the Cardinals, Webb allowed two runs over seven innings of work and struck out Albert Pujols to end the seventh with a runner on and the D-backs clinging to a one-run lead.
away_pitcher_note: Rusch, starting because rookie Greg Reynolds had struggled mightily during his September callup, is making his first start since Aug. 14. Since his last start, Rusch has gone 0-1 with a 3.31 ERA in 13 relief appearances. In eight starts since joining the Rockies, Rusch is 4-2 with a 4.89 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson was roughed up in his last outing in St. Louis, allowing five runs in six innings, four of which came in the first inning. Unlike his previous five starts, where he ended up with five no-decisions despite posting a 3.22 ERA, Johnson was never in the game, thanks to the one bad inning. The Big Unit, who hasn't won since Aug. 12, said he hasn't been this frustrated on the mound since 2004.
away_pitcher_note: In a sense, Jimenez's first full season in the Majors is a success. Jimenez carried a 6.46 ERA in April and by the end of June was 2-8 with a 4.71 ERA. Thanks to strong work since then, Jimenez has become one of three Rockies pitchers to finish in double figures in wins. That's the first time that has happened since 2003, when Darren Oliver went 13-11, Jason Jennings went 12-13 and Shawn Chacon went 11-8.

home_pitcher_note: Webb is making his fourth consecutive Opening Day start and his first at Chase Field. The right-hander finished second in the balloting for the National League Cy Young Award last season. While he scuffled against the Rockies in 2007, Webb was 3-0 against them in 2008 with a 3.07 ERA. Fast starts are commonplace for Webb, who is 18-2 in the season's first month over his career. Last year he won his first nine starts of the year. Webb has no explanation for the hot starts, but it certainly is not due to good springs. This year he was 1-2 with a 5.82 ERA with his final outing coming in a Minor League game. Webb has also possessed a devastating sinker, but in recent years he has developed his curve and change into extremely effective pitches, particularly the change. Webb has been elected to three straight All-Star Games and has not allowed a hit in two innings during the Mid-Summer Classic. A workhorse, Webb has been on the disabled list just once in his  big league career and has thrown 208 innings or more in each of his five full seasons.
away_pitcher_note: Cook emerged to be an All-Star last season. He has always had an exceptional sinkerball, but last year he grew by being able to get more strikeouts (a career-high 96). His next step is becoming more effective against left-handed hitters, who hit .297 last year and have batted .299 against him in his career. Toward that end, he devoted much of his spring to perfecting a slider to work inside against them, and his sinker and changeup can be effective in getting weak contact. The Rockies also could use a repeat of the first month of last year, when Cook went 4-1 with a 2.41 ERA in six starts while the rest of the rotation pitched poorly. Cook has been competitive but doesn't have strong numbers against the D-backs -- 1-1 with a 5.19 ERA in three games last season and 5-4, 5.14 in 18 career appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Haren is starting his second season for the D-backs after coming over from Oakland in an eight-player deal in December 2007. The right-hander had an outstanding spring in which he worked on adding a cut fastball to his repertoire. Haren got off to a good start last April when he was 4-1. Against the Rockies in 2008 he was 3-0 with a 3.33 ERA. He was 11-4 last year at Chase Field.
away_pitcher_note: The second half of last season and this spring have been a charmed time for Jimenez. He went 8-3 with a 3.68 ERA in 14 starts after last year's All-Star break, signed a contract for four years and $10 million during the winter and starred for the Dominican Republic during the World Baseball Classic. During Spring Training, Jimenez showed the ability to get ground balls with his sinking fastball and his changeup, and used his four-seam fastball and curveball for strikeouts. The question is whether he has learned enough to be a steady pitcher during the season's early days. This spring, he worked on a habit of overthrowing when he's tired. If he can manage his energy better, he can become a top pitcher.

home_pitcher_note: Davis was limited to 146 innings last year, his lowest total since 2003, due to a battle with thyroid cancer. This spring, he was set back with some soreness in his left triceps, but by the end of the spring he seemed to be fine. Normally Davis is an innings-eating pitcher who compiles double-digit win totals. Prior to last year he had not won fewer than 11 games in four years. He had a 4.09 ERA in two cames against the Rockies in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Morales counts as the biggest success story of the Rockies' Spring Training, bigger even than the emergence of top outfield prospect Dexter Fowler. Last year, Morales was considered the best of the Rockies' prospects. He was called up late in 2007 and helped the club to its World Series appearance. But last year, when asked to begin the year in the starting rotation, he showed poor fastball command and an inconsistent delivery. He went to the Minors in late April and did not return. It wasn't until after the year that he informed the club that he had battled back issues since Spring Training. A healthy Morales showed better command this spring, and the Rockies believe he can be dominant when he has a good fastball and mixes in a changeup that's special. But one question lingers: Does he have the patience and knowledge of himself to adjust quickly when he gets out of kilter?

home_pitcher_note: After years as a junior rotation member on good teams, Marquis arrives as the oldest member of the Rockies' rotation and the one with the most Major League experience. Given the leeway that comes with such status, Marquis sacrificed his spring to work on some new delivery mechanics. He was seeking a stronger leg push and more power when his motion takes him to the plate. Well, his early-spring performances were awful and panic, or at least worry, ensued in the Purple Pinstripe Nation. But sometime before his final Cactus League start, Marquis had enough control of his actions that he no longer had to think about them, and he pitched well. This is the Rockies' home opener, and Marquis is 3-0 with a 2.51 ERA in five career starts at Coors in other uniforms.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels is scheduled to make his first start of the season in Coors Field after missing the home opener because he battled inflammation in his left elbow this spring. Obviously, it's an understatement to say how important Hamels is to the rotation. He earned World Series and NLCS MVP honors, establishing himself as one of the game's best big-game pitchers. Hamels enters every season thinking he could win a Cy Young award. There is no reason he cannot, but he must stay healthy to make that happen.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies have treated De La Rosa with the philosophy that if you build a pitcher, he can win. Other clubs saw De La Rosa as talented but gave up on him because his emotions took control on the mound. The Rockies put their performance enhancement coach, Ronn Svetich, on the case, and pitching coach Bob Apodaca showed De La Rosa confidence when he didn't have it in himself. The result was a 7-3 record and 3.08 ERA after last year's All-Sar break. Even more important, the Rockies inked De La Rosa into a rotation spot when it became clear that lefty Jeff Francis would not be healthy enough to pitch, and stayed with him as he worked through mechanics this spring. When De La Rosa's mid-90s fastball, changeup and slider are working, he is capable of high strikeout numbers. But he can struggle with runners on base.
