away_pitcher_note: Myers makes his second start of the season. For whatever reason, Myers has had pretty good success at Coors Field. He is 4-0 with a 3.67 ERA in five games.

home_pitcher_note: Cook lasted just 2 1/3 innings on Opening Day against the D-backs-- his shortest start since Aug. 7, 2004, when he left a game after two innings because of blood clots in his lungs. All that happened in Monday's opener was Cook didn't have his sinker and the ball was carrying. It was a bad combination. All spring, Cook worked on his slider and changeup to use when the sinker was not at his best, but he didn't count on it being that bad. Besides, his secondary pitches weren't working, either. It was a day when the teams combined for eight home runs, so the two Cook gave up didn't look as bad. Still, Cook will be looking to get the Phils to hit the bal on the ground. However, Cook has struggled against the Phillies -- he is 1-4, 6.14 ERA in seven career appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Right-hander Chan Ho Park makes his season debut as a Phillies starter after beating out left-hander J.A. Happ for the fifth spot in the rotation during spring training. Park signed with the Phillies in the offseason because the Phillies promised him a chance to earn that job. He wanted it so badly he bypassed playing with South Korea in the World Baseball Classic. He won it, and now he has to prove he deserves to keep it.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly will start in the Cubs' home opener, and he can only hope the wind is blowing in. Last Wednesday at Houston, he served up four home runs but still got the win as the Cubs scored four runs in each of the first two innings. The four dingers were the most off the lefty since he he gave up a career-high five on June 11, 2003, against Atlanta. Lilly did give up eight hits and wasn't too happy with his outing. He's still a little behind work-wise after participating in the World Baseball Classic. He was 7-5 with a 4.50 ERA in 15 home starts last season.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez dominated the strike zone on Tuesday at Arizona, striking out eight in seven innings and pitching out of a couple of jams in the Rockies' 3-0 victory. It was one of those nights when Jimenez felt his fastball, his split-finger pitch, his curve and his slider. A key to pitching at Wrigley, however, is adjusting to conditions. But Jimenez can handle that, since he does that at Coors Field, where there are nights when one or two of his pitches won't do what he intends. Jimenez made his first Major League start at Wrigley in the final game of the 2006, and is 0-1 with a 4.63 ERA in two starts there.

home_pitcher_note: Harden recorded his eighth career 10-strikeout game in his last start against the Brewers but did not get a decision. He was in line for the win, but Milwaukee rallied in the ninth. Harden gave up three hits over six innings and looked strong. The radar gun at Miller Park was registering mid 90s consistently with his pitches. He was 5-0 with a 1.79 ERA in 15 games at home last season. Harden has never faced the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: The opponent will be familiar. Marquis pitched for the Cubs in 2007-08 and went 23-18 in 63 games before the Rockies acquired him for right-handed reliever Luis Vizcaino. Marquis certainly earned the favor of his home fans Friday, when he held the Phillies to two runs on five hits in seven innings of the home opener, a 9-2 victory. A sinkerball pitcher, Marquis stayed low in the strike zone and forced 13 groundouts, which included three double plays.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf took the Dodgers into the eighth inning in Sunday's win against the Diamondbacks, even though he felt he was pitching without an effective fastball. In a very young rotation, Wolf is the one experienced enough to make a quick adjustment and win a game even without his full repertoire. Wolf had command of his curveball and kept hitters off-balance with pinpoint changeup command.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa mixed an effective fastball and changeup during the first two-plus innings of his initial start, a home loss to the Phillies on Saturday. But he couldn't put hitters away with his changeup, started falling behind in the count with two outs, and wound up giving up five runs and six hits in 4 2/3 innings. The Phillies also forced him to throw 99 pitches in that time.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley had gone back-to-back like a staff ace. After beating the Padres by allowing two runs over six innings, he was even better against the Giants, allowing one run over seven innings with 11 strikeouts. Catcher Russell Martin said Billingsley is now able to make in-game adjustments, like throwing the same pitch at slightly different speeds to keep hitters off balance, after being pretty much a total-effort thrower in his first two seasons.
away_pitcher_note: Cook rebounded from a poor outing on Opening Day at Arizona -- six runs in 2 1/3 innings -- to pitch well enough to win at home against the Phillies. Cook gave up three runs and seven hits, including a line drive off his backside, in six innings, but did not figure in the decision. He was forcing quick swings and keeping the ball down in the strike zone, inducing two double plays. Cook is 2-3 with a 2.89 ERA in eight career games at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: In his first Major League start, McDonald pitched two perfect innings, then imploded. He allowed a home run, walked the pitcher and wound up charged with five runs in 2 1/3 innings. McDonald, who showed remarkable composure during last year's playoffs, was as inconsistent against the Diamondbacks as he had been while compiling a 5.32 ERA in Spring Training. He
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez has got to love L.A. right about now. His history there isn't exactly great. He is 1-0 but with an 11.12 ERA in three starts at Dodger Stadium. However, on Sunday he'll just be happy he's anywhere but Chicago. Jimenez's pitching hand froze during the Cubs' home opener on Monday. He threw 104 pitches in 3 2/3 innings and gave up three runs, four hits and six walks. He could gain a feel only for his slider, but his fastball and split-finger pitch were taken out of the equation. Weather like that won't be a problem in Los Angeles.

home_pitcher_note: Garland has had two polar opposite outings with the D-backs. He won his first regular-season game when he held the Dodgers to three runs on five hits over seven innings. The right-hander had allowed just one run over 6 1/3 innings before giving up a two-run homer to Casey Blake in the seventh on a sinker that stayed up a little more than he would have liked. Garland, who was signed as a free agent in January, also drew a key walk during a five-run third inning rally. In his most recent outing, on Wednesday against the Cardinals, he allowed seven runs on seven hits over 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis has pitched the Rockies to wins over the Phillies and the Cubs. He went seven innings and gave up one run against the Cubs on Wednesday, and his best inning might have been his last. After running into trouble in the sixth, he pitched an efficient 1-2-3 seventh. Marquis has pitched well at all National League West venues but hasn't had the best of fortune at Chase Field. He is 0-3, but with a 3.60 ERA and .211 batting average against.

home_pitcher_note: Petit will get the starting nod on Tuesday in place of Brandon Webb, who is on the 15-day disabled list with stiffness in his right shoulder. Petit also took Webb's turn last time through the rotation. The right-hander cruised through the first three innings in that game before running into trouble in the fourth. Orlando Hudson homered and Russell Martin doubled home a pair to cap the inning. Those three runs were the only ones allowed by Petit in five innings. The Arizona bullpen, though, fell apart that night in an 11-2 D-backs loss.
away_pitcher_note: Morales makes his return from a stint in the Minor Leagues, where the Rockies temporarily kept Morales because they didn't need a fifth starter. The 23-year-old left-hander was sharp in his lone Major League start this season, allowing just one run on four hits against the Diamondbacks in the Rockies' third game of the year. In his career against Arizona, Morales is 1-1 with a 4.50 ERA in three starts. In his lone start at Colorado Springs, Morales threw six scoreless innings against Reno.

home_pitcher_note: Haren could easily be 3-0 right now instead of 0-3. The right-hander has allowed one run in two of his starts and just two in the other, yet has gotten little if any run support as Arizona has scored just one run total in the three games that he has started. His last start, on Friday against the Giants, was typical. He allowed just one run over six innings and did not walk a batter while fanning six, yet came away with a 2-0 loss. In a rare show of emotion, he slammed his helmet and bat when he was pinch-hit for in the top of the seventh inning. In 19 innings this year, Haren has allowed just 12 hits and walked three while striking out 17.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa pitched his way out of trouble for 5 1/3 scoreless innings against the Dodgers on Friday but was denied his first win of the season. De La Rosa allowed five hits and four walks but pitched out of several jams to keep the Dodgers scoreless. But the Dodgers came back for four runs in the seventh against the Rockies bullpen as De La Rosa was saddled with the no-decision. The left-hander is 1-1 with a 2.53 ERA in seven appearances against the Diamondbacks, who signed him as an amateur free agent in 1998.

home_pitcher_note: Cook struggled on Saturday afternoon at Dodger Stadium, giving up three home runs in a four-inning start. Manny Ramirez was responsible for two of the runs, the first a line drive to left-center field on a 3-2 pitch and the second a line drive down the left-field line. Cook gave up five runs on eight hits, capped when Andre Ethier pulled a three-run homer into right field in the fourth inning. Cook, Colorado's ace last season, had pitched into the sixth inning in two of his first three starts of 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Eric Stults did what a fifth (or is it sixth?) starter needs to do against the Giants. He pitched five innings, allowed two runs and gave his club a chance to win the game. One of the runs scored without a ball leaving the infield after Stults opened the second inning by issuing a walk. He scattered five hits and kept the ball in the park.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez struggled to maintain any consistency Sunday afternoon in Los Angeles. He was in trouble from the start and had only one inning where he faced the minimum. Jimenez has had two consecutive tough starts since his season debut in which he pitched seven scoreless innings and struck out eight. Against the Dodgers, he pitched 4 1/3 innings and gave up seven runs and seven hits. He walked four and struck out three.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald tossed 4 1/3 scoreless innings against the Rockies on Sunday, just three days after pitching a scoreless inning out of the bullpen. McDonald was denied his first win of the season because he didn't reach the five-inning threshold. McDonald pitched out of trouble as he allowed four hits and walked three while striking out two. The right-hander will make another start against the Rockies on Friday, but this time it will be at Coors Field, where he has never pitched.

home_pitcher_note: Twice in his last start, a loss to the D-backs at Chase Field, Marquis fell behind hitters and paid. He went 2-0 to Mark Reynolds and gave up a home run in the second inning, then went 1-0 against Miguel Montero in the fifth and gave up a three-run shot. Marquis' outing was plagued by the poor execution of his teammates, offensively and defensively.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw lasted just 4 1/3 innings in his last outing, surrendering eight hits and six earned runs in an 8-5 loss to Houston. Kershaw, who walked two and struck out three against the Astros, will be making his first appearance of the season against the Rockies. Kershaw has three starts vs. Colorado, going 1-2 with a 5.14 ERA, giving up 19 hits in 14 innings. He has 14 strikeouts while walking nine in those three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Many Rockies scouts believe Hammel could be an effective starter. After three bullpen appearances, the last two of which have been scoreless outings of two innings in length, Hammel will have a chance to prove them right. Left-hander Franklin Morales suffered a strained muscle in the shoulder on Tuesday leaving the Rockies with a hole in the rotation. Hammel pitched starter-type innings for the Rays in Spring Training and should be prepared.
away_pitcher_note: Young pitched a two-hitter over seven innings in his last start against the Giants, putting behind him a terrible start in his last outing, but he was shackled with a no-decision as the San Francisco Giants rallied to win it, 1-0, in the bottom of the 10th inning. "I felt good, but I walked too many guys and created a little trouble for myself," Young said. "I had decent command with the fastball. I didn't use the slider early, but it got better as I went along. I'm trying to make good pitches and that's the bottom line." Young walked four and struck out three in his third start in San Francisco, where he has never won and had given up 10 runs in his last 10 2/3 innings. Young retired 10 of the first 12 hitters he faced and was able to pitch himself out of a couple of jams.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa revealed his stellar side in his last start, a loss to the D-backs at Chase Field. He gave up two runs in 6 2/3 innings, but struck out six. Most of his strikeouts and his key double-play grounder against Chad Tracy came on his slider, which can be a tremendous put-away pitch when his fastball is working early in counts.
away_pitcher_note: With Shawn Hill going on the disabled list with elbow soreness, the Padres decided to push Josh Geer's start to Thursday and call up Gaudin to pitch on normal rest Tuesday. Gaudin was signed to a Minor League deal on April 12 after being released by the Cubs at the end of Spring Training. Chicago had used Gaudin as a reliever, so he needed a couple starts at Triple-A Portland to stretch out his arm. In two Minor League outings, he didn't give up a run over a combined 8 2/3 innings, striking out 10 and walking two. Manager Bud Black said Gaudin can go 90 to 100 pitches against the Rockies, whom he has faced twice in his career (7 IP, 3.86 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Cook moved closer to form Friday night against the Dodgers, finishing with a no-decision in a 6-5 loss. He gave up two runs on three hits and two walks in the first inning in a continuation of his less-than-scintillating early-season work. But he settled and gave up just one other run in six innings, striking out four and tying a career high with six walks. Facing the Padres should help, as he's 11-4 with a 2.74 ERA against San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Correia is still looking for his first victory as a Padre after losing a 3-1 lead in the sixth inning of a no-decision against the Pirates in his last start on Friday. Correia's pitches had some significant movement against the Pirates, which was good in that he allowed just three hits in five innings -- but was also bad since he hit a batter and walked four. In three starts this season, Correia has walked 10 batters in 16 innings. The Padres like his stuff but would like him to limit the walks and pitch better from the stretch with runners on base.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson followed up his best start of the season with his worst start in nearly a decade -- at least in terms of command. The seven walks he issued, in only 3 1/3 innings, Saturday in Arizona, were his most since he issued the same number of passes on July 25, 2000. Johnson may have been guilty of trying to overthrow in his emotional visiting debut in Chase Field, as he was consistently outside. He won't have the extra baggage in this latest quest for career win No. 297.
away_pitcher_note: After throwing seven innings of shutout ball in his first start, Jimenez has struggled with his mechanics and his command. He has been unable to finish five innings in his last three starts, giving up 16 earned runs in 12 innings.  Facing the Dodgers at Coors Field Saturday, Jimenez was erratic in his delivery and his pitches missed the target by a large margin.  When he found the strike zone, he hit too much of it, allowing L.A. to tee off with five consecutive hits in the four-run first.

home_pitcher_note: The senior member of the Giants' rotation (Cain broke in as a 20-year-old in 2005) will be out to sustain the best start of his career, never before having won his first two decisions. He was typically clutch in his last outing, allowing eight baserunners but only one run in seven innings at Arizona. It was his fourth quality start in as many outings this season. Cain has a way of putting pressure on his mound opponent: With a modest support of at least three runs, he is 28-6.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis had a couple big wins for Colorado in April, putting the breaks on a pair of three-game losing streaks. His last start was the longest by a Rockies starter this season, going 7 1/3 innings and yielding three runs on six hits and four walks while striking out five. His sinker is well-suited to Coors Field, where he improved to 5-0, but he is even better at AT&T park, where he has a 2.21 ERA over 36 2/3 innings. Marquis has been helping his team with his bat, hitting .500 (4-for-8) with three sacrifices, two runs and three RBIs.

home_pitcher_note: Zito maintained a 13-inning scoreless streak until yielding a two-run homer to the Dodgers' Casey Blake in his last start. Zito happened to record that streak at home. His previous best at AT&T Park was 11 innings spanning a pair of starts April 21-May 2, 2007. Zito's rigorous offseason conditioning program and improved concentration seem to have helped, as his fastball has approached 90 mph -- a sufficient complement to his off-speed pitches -- and he has avoided telltale lapses. For example, he retired the leadoff batter six times in seven innings against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start of the season, Hammel had an effective fastball and breaking ball for nearly three innings against the Padres on Monday. But he gave up a two-run triple with two down in the third, and wound up giving up five runs -- four earned -- in three innings. He threw 78 pitches, 45 for strikes. Hammel had competed for a rotation spot with the Rays before being traded to the Rockies just before the season started, and pitched in relief until Monday. He admitted fatiguing, but should have more stamina for his next start.

home_pitcher_note: Correia has thrown five or six innings and let up two or three runs in each of his first four starts of the season, but the Padres need him to find a way to solve his efficiency issues and go deeper into games.  All his runs came from two two-out homers at Coors Field on Wednesday. His changeup was his best pitch against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had one bad pitch, a changeup that Scott Hairston deposited for a two-run homer, in his last start, a no-decision in the Padres' 4-3 victory at Coors Field on Tuesday night. De La Rosa's fastball and slider have been sharp in his last two outings. He has six strikeouts in each of his last two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Geer got a no-decision in his last start on April 30 against the Dodgers, allowing four runs on seven hits in six innings, including a two-run home run to Orlando Hudson and a solo home run to Manny Ramirez. Mostly, though, the righty worked efficiently and got nine ground-ball outs, pitching to contact which, when he's going well, is what he does. Manager Bud Black noted that Geer maintained his poise and "battled" even after Hudson and Ramirez hit home runs. Geer needed 93 pitches to get through six innings, not nearly as efficient as he was in his first start since being recalled from Triple-A Portland when he used 86 pitches to get through seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies' ace performed like it in his last start, a home victory over the Padres. He carries a 12-4 with a 2.80 ERA in 21 career games, including 19 starts, against the Padres. He gave up home runs to Adrian Gonzalez and Henry Blanco in the last of his seven innings. Otherwise, he pitched scoreless ball. The Padres picked that game to rest vets David Eckstein and Scott Hairston, however, so it stands to reason the lineup facing Cook could be stronger. That might not be a bad idea, since Cook is 5-1 with a 1.69 ERA in seven appearances at PETCO.

home_pitcher_note: After three bad starts, Jimenez righted the ship by holding the Giants to three runs and five hits in seven innings. He struck out five, walked two and escaped some of the problems out of the stretch that have plagued him in his previous three outings. The biggest problem was he faced Randy Johnson when he was at his best. This start will be the same matchup, but it'll be at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson, the all-time leader in wins against the Rockies -- who are also the team he has defeated the most -- improved to 19-7 against them last Friday by pitching seven shutout innings. He allowed four hits, walked none and struck out nine but lamented his lack of consistency afterward, given the fact that he lasted only 3 1/3 innings and walked seven in his previous outing. In 12 lifetime starts at Coors Field, Johnson is 7-4 with a 3.50 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Can't blame the Giants for dreading this matchup. Marquis is 4-1 with a 1.98 ERA against them in eight games, seven starts. On Saturday, Marquis pitched a complete-game five-hitter, with only Pablo Sandoval's leadoff homer in the ninth preventing a shutout. Marquis used his usual sinker, but mixed in a cutter and a changeup while striking out four and walking one. Marquis has thrown at least seven innings in four of his five starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Cain's first four outings of the season were quality starts until last Saturday, when he allowed five runs in six innings as the Giants lost to the Rockies, 5-1. Cain surrendered three home runs that afternoon, including two to Ryan Spilborghs, the leadoff hitter. That was a recurring theme for Cain, who permitted the leadoff batter to reach safely in each inning but one. Though the Giants have improved their run support this year for Cain, they still have scored one run or fewer for him in 39 of his 109 starts -- 35.8 percent.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel, in his second start since moving from the bullpen, held the Giants scoreless and gave up six hits in six innings of Sunday afternoon's 1-0 loss. He showed a lively fastball, and as the game progressed his breaking pitches increased in their sharpness.
away_pitcher_note: Vicitimized by a grand slam and a solo home run in his last start, Nolasco watched his losing streak extend to three straight decisions. The 26-year-old threw a season-high 112 pitches in that loss to the Cubs at Wrigley Field. He yielded a grand slam to Derrek Lee and a solo shot to Mike Fontenot. Normally, Nolasco is good about keeping the ball in the park. He surrendered two in his previous five starts, and hadn't been taken deep in three successive outings. Nolasco is 2-0 against the Rockies, and he's 1-0 at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa left Monday night's game against the Padres at PETCO Park with a reasonable line -- five innings, three hits, three earned runs. But three other runs scored as a result of his throwing error, and the three earned runs came on a Scott Hairston home run that put him in position to lose (he wound up with a no-decision in a game the Rockies came back to win, 9-6). At least, he didn't unravel. He finished with three walks and three strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson was solid once again while making his first career start against the Reds on Monday, giving up two runs on eight hits while striking out six with no walks in 7 1/3 innings. The 25-year-old, who left after throwing 102 pitches -- 74 for strikes -- hasn't issued a walk in two starts this season. After getting out of a first-and-third, one-out jam in the top of the first, Johnson didn't put a runner in scoring position until the seventh inning and needed just 68 pitches to get through six. He then allowed Cincinnati to tie the game at 2 in the seventh after giving up three straight hits to start the inning. He's only pitched two scoreless innings of relief in his career against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: In his last three starts, Cook has regained the form that made him an All-Star Game participant in 2008. He demonstrated savvy in his last start, when he held the Padres to one run and five hits in eight innings on Tuesday night. That's a team he has beaten repeatedly because hitters feel compelled to pound his sinker into the turf. This time, they laid off, so Cook threw 20-25 breaking and off-speed pitches. However, Cook gave up seven earned runs in 7 1/3 innings in his only start against the Marlins last season and is 1-2 with a 6.10 ERA in four career games against them.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad wasn't as sharp as usual against the Reds on Tuesday, but he still pitched well enough to earn his fourth quality start. The 22-year-old right-hander gave up four runs -- three earned -- on seven hits while walking three and striking out five. But Volstad was pitching out of trouble all night, and he needed 97 pitches to get through his six frames. He also said he did a bad job of holding on baserunners as the first two runs came in after a stolen base. On Sunday, Volstad will be returning to Coors Field -- the place where he made his Major League debut on July 6, 2008, when he pitched two scoreless innings out of the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez had his best outing of the season, especially when put back-to-back with a quality seven-inning start in San Francisco in his previous start. He regained command of his fastball and used it with confidence on both sides of the plate, masterfully setting up a big curve that froze hitters consistently. He held the Giants scoreless for seven innings, finally giving up a run when he tried to pitch into the eighth and left with runners on second and third and nobody out.
away_pitcher_note: Paulino replaces Russ Ortiz, who was moved to the bullpen. Paulino was very successful in his three games as a starter this year, but not so much as a reliever. As a starter, he compiled a 2.55 ERA, allowing five earned runs over 17 2/3 innings. He allowed three runs over seven innings as a reliever, however, for a 21.00 ERA. Paulino has never faced the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis had only his second uneven outing of the season against the Giants Thursday, giving up seven runs (five earned) on eight hits over six plus innings. His command was good enough that he issued no walks, but his sinker wasn't at its best, and the Giants, seeing him for the second time in a week, were able to take advantage.  Marquis uncharacteristically hurt himself in the field, making errors on two bunt plays that each led to extended innings and an unearned run in each case.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton's defense didn't help him much during his last outing versus the Cubs, which resulted in two unearned runs of the five he allowed. Hampton did not face the Rockies last year. In his career, he's 9-3 with a 4.56 ERA over 21 games versus Colorado. At Coors Field, which he called home from 2001-02, he is 17-10 with a 5.79 ERA in 33 games.

home_pitcher_note: For the second time in three starts, Hammel was unable to pitch at least five innings. In his last start at home against the Marlins, the right-hander went 4 1/3 innings and he gave up six runs on eight hits to pick up the loss. Hammel has been Jekyll and Hyde this season. In three appearances at home, Hammel has a 10.80 ERA but has yet to allow an earned run in 10 innings on the road. Hammel has never faced the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez threw a gem in his last outing, lasting eight shutout innings against the Padres while yielding five hits. Rodriguez has been the Astros' most consistent starter by a landslide this year, producing quality outings in all but one of his starts. Rodriguez has a career 3-1 record and a 3.50 ERA over seven starts versus the Rockies. He's 2-1 with a 3.93 ERA at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm has not had great results in two out of his last three starts, which is a concern for Pittsburgh considering how consistent the left-hander has been over the past year. However, it was bloop hits on decent pitches that did him in his last time out, on Saturday at Citi Field. Usually depended on to finish at least six innings per start, a 42-pitch fourth inning in his last start did him in and forced him out after five. He allowed seven runs to the Mets, the most Maholm has given up since May 3, 2008. Maholm is 1-2 with a 5.00 ERA in three career starts against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: After struggling throughout his career against the Marlins, De La Rosa shined Saturday, when he went eight innings, recorded a career-high 12 strikeouts and allowed two runs on four hits. The left-hander commanded his fastball, a sharp slider and a solid changeup for his best outing of the season. But De La Rosa took the loss as he was outdueled by the Marlins' Josh Johnson. De La Rosa is 2-1 with a 4.97 ERA in six appearances against the Pirates, and 0-1 with a 10.80 ERA in three appearances at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Snell had an encouraging start his last time out, as his fastball velocity returned to the 94-96 mph range after lagging in his previous start. The right-hander seems to be over the effects of his 131-pitch start on April 29, and now all he needs is some run support. Snell has struggled with his walk total all season, but he issued just one across six innings in his last start. Snell is 2-2 with a 4.78 ERA in four appearances (five starts) against the Rockies in his career.
away_pitcher_note: On Sunday, Cook posted his fourth consecutive quality start -- defined as six or more innings and three or fewer runs -- by pitching six innings and giving up two runs (one earned) on four hits against the Marlins. The sinkerballer kept the ball down and forced 10 groundouts. In two career appearances -- one start -- at PNC Park, Cook is 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA. Last July 30, Cook gave up four runs in seven innings, inducing 16 ground-ball outs in a 7-4 victory over the Pirates at PNC Park.

home_pitcher_note: Duke pitched a gem in his last start, a 7-1 win over St. Louis on Tuesday. The lefty hurled eight innings, allowing one run on four hits, and notched five strikeouts. Duke was very efficient in tossing 104 pitches -- 67 were strikes. Duke has allowed more than one earned run in a game just twice in his first seven starts and is 2-2 lifetime against the Rockies, with 7.43 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Jimenez spooked the Astros by spending the early innings chucking fastballs, some of which were clocked as high as 99 mph. At times this pitch would buzz by a hitter's chin. More often than not, though, he threw strikes, and that's why he gave up one run on seven hits in seven innings, struck out four and forced 11 groundball outs. It's a minor roll for Jimenez, who has pitched seven innings in each of his last three starts and has held opponents to five runs. Jimenez has never pitched at PNC Park, but is 1-0 with a 2.57 ERA, eight strikeouts and two walks against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe was scheduled to pitch Sunday but was pushed back to Monday when the Braves' series finale with the D-backs was rained out and will be pitching on six days of rest. While winning his fourth consecutive start with seven solid innings against the Mets on Monday night, Lowe provided one of his best performances of the season. The 35-year-old sinkerballer held the Mets hitless through the first 3 2/3 innings and limited them to just one extra-base hit -- a seventh-inning leadoff double. He has allowed two earned runs or fewer in three of his past four starts. While with the Dodgers last season, Lowe went 2-1 with a 3.26 ERA against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: About the best that can be said for Marquis is he's not facing the Astros. Already having poor numbers against many of that team's best hitters, Marquis gave up 10 hits and nine runs in 3 2/3 innings in his last start, at Coors Field. The Braves were Marquis' original Major League club, but he hasn't fared that well at Turner Field -- 8-10 with a 4.53 ERA in 50 games.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens was pushed back a day after Sunday's rainout and will be pitching on six days of rest. Jurrjens' run of tough luck was extended on Tuesday, when he held the Mets scoreless until surrendering a two-run single with one out in the eighth inning. One inning later, the Mets tied the game, giving him a no-decision. Jurrjens has gone 1-2 with a 1.95 ERA during his past six starts. He was 2-1 with a 3.48 ERA in three starts against the Rockies last year.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Hammel pitched solidly for the first time at Coors Field by giving up four runs -- one earned -- on seven hits in 5 1/3 innings. However, he was the hard-luck loser. Hammel was able to locate his fastball and mix in some good sliders and curveballs against the Astros. Hammel has never faced the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez completed his second straight impressive outing in Friday night's 4-3 win over the D-backs, but ended up with a no-decision when Arizona tied the game in the ninth inning. He allowed just two earned runs and struck out 10 in seven innings. The strikeout total gave Vazquez 39 career games with double-digit strikeouts. Vazquez is winless in four starts at Turner Field this season. This will be Vazquez's first start against the Rockies since June 8, 2004, when he pitched for the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa has sizzled, striking out 22 in 15 innings over his last two starts. The only drawback was the Rockies haven't hit well behind him. They lost 3-1 at Coors against the Marlins in the first game, when he fanned a career-high 12 in eight innings. He struck out 10 in seven innings against the Pirates in his last start but left trailing, 1-0 (the Rockies won it, 3-1, with a ninth-inning comeback). De La Rosa has had consistently strong fastball command throughout the season. Against the Pirates, he had supreme confidence in his changeup. He has never pitched at Turner Field, and the only time he faced the Braves he struck out three and walked two in two scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: With Jo-Jo Reyes being moved to the bullpen, Medlen will attempt to continue the dominance he's shown while going 4-0 with a 1.07 ERA in the six starts he's made for Triple-A Gwinnett this year. Medlen hasn't started since May 11, but threw in relief on Saturday. The 23-year-old right-hander possesses a live fastball, an above-average changeup and the ability to consistently locate his slider. He began his rapid rise toward the Majors after joining Double-A Mississippi's rotation midway through the 2008 season.
away_pitcher_note: Cook had a wet and painful experience Saturday at Pittsburgh. He pitched a strong first inning but gave up four runs on four second-inning hits, and didn't return after a rain delay. To top it off, he received treatment for a sore back. the poor outing came after Cook had posted a 2.67 ERA in the previous four outings. No one expects Cook to miss a start with the back issue, but the Rockies are monitoring it.

home_pitcher_note: The learning curve that Tigers manager Jim Leyland has talked about all season is starting to take shape for Porcello. The right-hander has won his last three starts after a six-inning, one-run performance Saturday, which Leyland called the rookie's best outing of the year. During that time, Porcello has given up only two runs in 18 innings, while striking out 13 and walking seven batters. Seven starts into his career, the 20-year-old Porcello said he's learning how to utilize his breaking ball and not always try to blow his fastball past batters.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez's last start, Sunday against the Pirates, was less efficient than his recent work, but it's hard to argue with one run and seven strikeouts in six innings of work. It all was washed away when his bullpen and defense managed to give up 10 runs in the seventh inning. Nonetheless, the start was significant. Being tested because he didn't have his best fastball, Jimenez pitched off his secondary pitches and threw enough good fastballs in strikeout situations. He is 2-1 with a 2.00 ERA in his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: While the three starters ahead of him surge, Galarraga continues to struggle in the No. 4 spot in the Tigers' rotation. In his last start, on Sunday, he didn't make it through the first inning, giving up five runs and recording only two outs. He has now given up at least five runs in four straight starts. With Jeremy Bonderman scheduled to make his second rehab start for Triple-A Toledo on Thursday, a rotation shakeup could be down the road. But manager Jim Leyland hasn't set any timetable for Bonderman's return nor given any indication of when a change might happen.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis is coming off his best outing of the season, an eight-inning effort in which he allowed just one run on five hits against the Braves on Monday. In that outing, Marquis threw 71 pitches through the first four innings, and then settled in to throw just 32 through the last five. That lower pitch count was due in part to the four double plays he induced from Braves hitters using an effective sinker. Marquis hasn't faced Detroit since 2002, when he was pitching for Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: It's hard for the Tigers to know how Willis will perform in the start after a win, because he's never done so in a Tigers uniform. It took 17 months and nine starts, but Willis finally recorded his first win as a Tiger on Tuesday, when he one-hit the Rangers through 6 1/3 innings, striking out five and retiring 17 straight batters at one point. Teammates saw a newfound serenity to Willis, who spent the first month of the season on the DL with an anxiety disorder. Now the challenge will be finding some form of consistency.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel has pitched better on the road than at home this season, and it's quite possible his last start, a loss to the Braves, could have gone differently. Hammel went six innings and gave up six runs, but three were earned. No runs were in when second baseman Clint Barmes committed his second-inning error. Two of the subsequent hits that inning were of the infield variety. Hammel has no record but a 7.88 ERA, in four career games, one start, against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: For the most part, De La Rosa's poor record hasn't been his fault. He's had next to no run support. But that can't be said about Wednesday's performance against the Braves that left him screaming, and pounding and kicking the water cooler in the dugout. De La Rosa lost the strike zone early in the fourth inning, walking three of the first four batters and hitting the other. By time he was gone after 3 2/3, he had given up seven runs on five hits. Because he couldn't get fastballs over early in counts, hitters didn't have to offer at his slider. In his lone start against the Dodgers, he gave up 11 hits in 5 1/3 innings but managed to leave without a run charged to him.
away_pitcher_note: Stults was scratched from his most recent scheduled start Wednesday night because of a jammed thumb suffered making a defensive play in his previous start in Florida, when he was lifted after five innings in a no-decision. The Dodgers are 6-1 in Stults' starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cook was masterful in his second career shutout, a four-hitter at Turner Field on Thursday night. It was one of those nights when Cook and catcher Chris Iannetta could dispense with strategy and just rely on the sinker. The Braves finished with 20 groundouts, and all their hits were along the ground as well. It was a big development, since Cook lasted just 1 2/3 innings in his previous start and experienced back tightness. Cook went 0-1 and the Rockies lost back-to-back starts to the Dodgers in late April, but that was before a turnaround that has seen him throw "quality starts" (six or more innings, three or fewer earned runs) in four of his last five outings.
away_pitcher_note: Eric Milton is tentatively listed as the starter, returning to the rotation for a second start after being skipped because of a day off. In his first start, Milton struggled with his command, walking four in four innings, racking up 84 pitches and failing to protect two leads. It was his first Major League start in two years after a lengthy comeback from "Tommy John" surgery, so maybe there were more butterflies than he acknowledged. This will be an acid test at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez was solid, but not spectacular in his last start, a 4-3 loss at Detroit. He was hurt when catcher Chris Iannetta couldn't control a low breaking ball and a run scored. Jimenez has been consistently in the mid-to-upper 90s with his fastball. In his lone start against the Dodgers this season, he gave up eight hits and six runs in four innings.  Lifetime, he is 4-2 with a 7.07 ERA in nine games, eight starts, against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: After flirting with a no-hitter and pitching into the eighth inning in his previous start, Kershaw reverted to scuffling against the Angels in his last time out, allowing only one run but walking four in five innings. Kershaw's final line would've been worse had he not pitched out of four jams -- the only run he allowed scored on an infield single.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies' 10-game road trip treated Jason Marquis well, as he earned two more wins to raise his total to a team-leading six. In each of those starts, he made it into the eighth inning, giving up three total runs in 15 2/3 innings of work. He had strong command of his sinkerball in his most recent outing, as he gave up only two earned runs. He isn't scheduled to pitch in the series against the Dodgers, getting the start after an off day in the series opener against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Not only did Young earn a victory in his last start against the Cubs but he also had a pivotal two-run single that got the Padres on their way to a ninth consecutive victory. All told, Young allowed two runs in seven innings with no walks and four strikeouts. Young took a perfect game into fifth inning, retiring the first 14 hitters before he allowed a single to Mike Fontenot. "As a pitcher, once it gets into that fifth inning ... that's when you think about it," Padres manager Bud Black said of Young's flirtation with a no-hitter. "But you think about it real brief. He's been down that path before."

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies love Hammel's fastball and pitch mix but had questions about him after he showed the inability to escape jams in a couple of starts. But Hammel said he never lost confidence. It all came together for him Sunday against the Tigers, when he went six innings and gave up a run on six hits and three walks. He added four strikeouts, and made key pitches when necessary. Now he must conquer Coors Field, where he is 0-2 with a 7.63 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Geer turned in a strong effort in his last start, on May 23 against the Cubs. Geer allowed one run on five hits over 6 2/3 innings, recording seven strikeouts and no walks. Geer got a mix of ground-ball (seven) and fly-ball (six) outs and mixed his pitches well against a lineup that can be dangerous. Aside from a solo home run to Derrek Lee, Geer didn't allow much else. The outing was quite a turnaround for a pitcher who had allowed five runs in each of his past two appearances. Geer is 1-1 with a 2.00 ERA in three career starts against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Take away two innings and De La Rosa is on the same roll he's been on since his second start of the season. But in each of his last two starts, he's had an inning in which he's given up seven runs. When pitching well, De La Rosa throws early strikes with his fastball and uses his slider to complete strikeouts. Before giving up seven and recording just one out in the fourth inning Monday against the Dodgers, he had struck out six -- all on sliders.
away_pitcher_note: Gaudin had a rough five-run third inning in his last start on May 25 at Chase Field against the D-backs. After sailing through the first two innings, facing only six batters, Gaudin let up a leadoff homer to Chris Snyder, a triple to rival pitcher Doug Davis, two RBI singles and another run on a wild pitch. His line for 5 1/3 innings in the game was seven runs (all earned), five hits, five walks (one intentional) and six strikeouts with a homer, the wild pitch, a batter hit and a balk. Command is still an issue and something the Padres will want him to work on before his next start against the Rockies at Coors Field on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt was uncharacteristically wild toward the end of his last outing versus the Reds, walking in the tying run with a four-pitch walk to Jonny Gomes in his final inning. Oswalt, who took a no-decision in that game, was pitching with a bruised hand after fielding a grounder with his pitching hand. He continues to search for his second win of the season, in his 11th start. Oswalt won his only start versus Colorado in '08, pitching a complete game shutout. In his career, he's 6-1 with a 1.84 ERA over nine starts versus the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: For the most part, Cook pitched well Tuesday night. But a fourth inning that saw him walk two, then give up a three-run double to Casey Blake, left him with the decision in a 7-1 loss to the Dodgers. For Cook, not being able to locate one sinker where he wanted was the difference between a good outing and a poor one. Interestingly, Cook threw his first career shutout at Atlanta on May 21, but still has a 5.76 road ERA this season.

home_pitcher_note: Cecil Cooper guaranteed Paulino would receive another start regardless of the results of the right-hander's last outing, so Paulino will pitch against the Rockies in the second game of the four-game home set. Paulino allowed three home runs in a loss to the Reds his last time out, giving up five runs (four earned) on seven hits over six innings. Paulino last faced the Rockies on May 12 in Denver, allowing eight runs (seven earned) over four innings in a losing effort.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez sailed for much of six innings, but faltered with two down in the seventh and took the loss against the Dodgers on Wednesday at Coors Field. There was plenty to like, however. He went to a two-seam fastball and bordered on dominant. He didn't have 20 pitches in an inning until the seventh. It'll be just Jimenez's second start at Houston's Minute Maid Park (0-0, 4.76).

home_pitcher_note: Moehler was stellar in his most recent start, tossing his first complete game in almost nine years during a 6-0 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates Friday. Since being reinstated from the disabled list May 4, Moehler is 2-1 with a 3.90 ERA. He has not been too good against Colorado in his career (1-2, 6.85 ERA), nor at Minute Maid Park this season (0-2, 9.22 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: Right-hander Jason Marquis has been the Rockies best pitcher the first two months and he showed it in his last start against the Padres. Marquis relied on his sharp sinker for eight shutout innings, scattering six hits and striking out six to notch his seventh win. In his last start against the Astros, Marquis gave up nine runs in 3 2/3 innings, easily his worst performance this season.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez has struggled mightily over the course of his past two starts after being arguably the best starter in the National League through his first nine outings. He didn't get out of the fifth inning either May 25 at Cincinnati nor Saturday at Pittsburgh, being charged with a combined 11 runs (five earned) on 19 hits and five walks in 9 2/3 innings, losing each time. He had allowed only 12 earned runs in his first 63 innings this season, leading the NL in ERA before Saturday. Rodriguez is 4-1 with a 3.35 ERA in eight career starts against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel threw plenty of strikes in his last start against the Padres -- 48 of them in 65 pitches -- but he left a few pitches up in the strike zone and paid the price. In 3 2/3 innings of work, Hammel didn't have his fastball command and yielded a three-run home run, an RBI double and an RBI triple, but got a no-decision. Hammel's next start should be on the road, where he's been much more comfortable (1.64 road ERA vs. 8.53 home ERA).

home_pitcher_note: After three consecutive superb outings, Wainwright was merely pretty good his last time out, and that won't sit well with him. One of Wainwright's best attributes is his unwillingness to settle for anything short of outstanding. Wainwright has pitched at least seven innings in four consecutive starts, and after issuing 18 walks in his first five games, he has handed out only 10 free passes in his past six.
away_pitcher_note: Interim manager Jim Tracy said De La Rosa is as talented as any starter on the squad but that he lacks one attribute -- the ability to get out of trouble. That was lacking again in his last start as he allowed a three-run homer on a 0-2 fastball with two outs to Padres slugger Adrian Gonzalez. De La Rosa pitched five innings and gave up four runs, but it could have been worse if Gonzalez wasn't gunned down at the plate to end the fifth.

home_pitcher_note: Monday brought another frustrating start for Wellemeyer, who just can't seem to build any momentum. He has yet to string together three consecutive good starts, and that's discouraging not only to him but to a team that was hoping he'd build on an excellent 2008 season. He does seem to have conquered the early-innings problem he had in April and part of May. Now, he just needs to do a better job of keeping it together when things start to turn against him.
away_pitcher_note: In a 4-1 loss at Houston in his last start, Cook kept the Rockies close until the sixth inning, when Carlos Lee lined a sinker over the left-field wall for a big two-run homer. Cook's best inning may have been the fourth, when he gave up just one run with runners on first and third and no outs. All but one of the outs in play and many of the nine hits were on the ground.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro was scratched from his Tuesday start due to back spasms, but the Cardinals continue to hope that he'll miss only one appearance. That would put him on track to slot back into the rotation on Sunday at home against Colorado, and pitching at home tends to be a very good thing for Pineiro. He has a 2.05 ERA at Busch Stadium this year (5.45 on the road), and he's 9-3 with a 3.34 ERA at home since joining the Cardinals at the non-waiver Trade Deadline in 2007.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez went six innings in the Rockies' 3-2, 11-inning loss to the Astros on Tuesday night. It wasn't the easiest time on the mound, as Jimenez pitched around seven hits and four walks but forced 11 ground-ball outs. Included were two double plays. It wasn't the most efficient performance (112 pitches), but Jimenez's resourcefulness is one reason he is considered an up-and-coming star. The Cards know about him. Manager Tony La Russa was highly complimentary of him after he had a strong performance for the Dominican Republic against the Cards during a World Baseball Classic exhibition game.

home_pitcher_note: This would be Kyle Lohse's turn in the rotation, but Lohse was placed on the disabled list after he aggravated a right forearm injury on Wednesday night. Thompson will be almost exactly on turn, with five days' rest after he filled in for Joel Pineiro, who had back spasms. The Cardinals are 18-7 when Thompson starts a game.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis has to be happy not to be facing the Astros. In his start on Wednesday night, he gave up three first-inning runs, mostly on soft hits, settled down for five scoreless innings, then gave up two in the seventh. One run in the seventh was on a leadoff homer by Hunter Pence, who dominates Marquis (11-for-22). But the homer was a hanging slider that any good hitter should have a good chance at, and that's the kind of pitch Marquis was kicking himself for throwing. A onetime Cardinal, Marquis is 4-2 with a 3.99 ERA in eight games against the Cards but gave up five runs in 5 2/3 innings while losing his lone start against them last year.

home_pitcher_note: Looper will get an extra day of rest before this start, and he could use the time to cool off. Looper was upset with himself on Wednesday after he entered the fifth inning with a 9-1 lead and could not get out of it, allowing four Marlins runs before exiting with the bases loaded and the potential tying run stepping to the plate. Seth McClung preserved the lead, but Looper, who had allowed only one hit before that inning, was stuck with one of the most frustrating no-decisions of his career. "I don't know what happened," he said. "It's still such a big blur to me." He owns a 5.28 ERA in 19 games against the Rockies, but only two of those appearances were starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel matched his career high for innings in a smooth, seven-inning, four-hit performance against the Astros. He gave up two runs in the Rockies' 10-3 victory. Hammel simply kept his fastball and slider down, something he has done on the road, where he is 2-1 with a 1.86 ERA this season.

home_pitcher_note: Bush began Thursday's start in pain, when a ball off the bat of Florida's Hanley Ramirez came back to the mound and hit him in the pitching elbow in the top of the first inning. Despite the bruised elbow, Bush pitched six innings in a 4-3 loss, giving up all four runs on seven hits. Bush has faced the Rockies three times in his career, with a career record of 2-1 and an ERA of 2.50. In his last start against Colorado in 2008, Bush struck out a career-high 13 hitters in an 11-1 win at Miller Park. In eight innings, Bush held the Rockies to one run on three hits, walking none.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Cardinals, De La Rosa broke out of his three-game slump by pitching 6 2/3 innings, allowing three runs on seven hits with seven strikeouts and earning his first win of the season. His reward for a job well done is to face the Brewers in his next start, the organization he entered the Majors with. De La Rosa is a career 2-5 with an 8.47 ERA at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo pitched at least eight innings for the fourth time this season, allowing just two hits over eight frames against the Braves. He walked four in that game, but struck out six and kept Atlanta hitters off-balance all night. He spotted his fastball well and had the Braves flailing at his curveball. He hopes to erase the memory of his last outing against the Rockies, which came on Aug. 8, 2007. In that start, he lasted just 2 2/3 innings while allowing 11 earned runs on 12 hits.
away_pitcher_note: Cook was cookin' against the Cardinals in his last start as he threw eight innings and allowed only an earned run on four hits to pick up his fourth win. Cook's reliable sinker forced the Cardinals to record 15 outs via the groundball. Cook has not put together back-to-back quality starts since May 5 against the Padres and May 10 versus the Marlins. He's 4-2 with a 3.55 ERA lifetime against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez struck out a season-high nine in his last start, but not with the use of his blazing 98 mph fastball. Instead, he fooled Cardinals hitters with offspeed stuff early in counts in eight innings and allowed two runs on four hits for the win. Since May 1, Jimenez is 3-3 with a 2.63 ERA in eight starts. Jimenez will be looking for his first win in Interleague Play, where he's a career 0-3 with a 5.00 ERA, against the Mariners in his next start.
away_pitcher_note: It's difficult to tell by his record, but Washburn is having his best season since 2002, when he won 18 games for the Angels. Washburn is coming off another solid start, when he held the Twins to one run over six innings, striking out six and walking one. It was the eighth time in 11 starts the lefty has allowed two or fewer runs this season, but he has not won a game since April 21. Washburn is 1-0 with a 2.70 ERA in two career starts against the Rockies at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis held the Cardinals to two runs in 6 2/3 innings of efficient pitching while winning Monday at Busch Stadium as the Rockies completed a four-game sweep. Marquis has curried the favor of his fielders because of his penchant for aggressively attacking the bottom of the strike zone with his sinker and his slider. However, Marquis is more effective on the road than at Coors Field (3-2, 5.34 ERA), which is where he'll face the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: The hard-throwing right-hander unexpectedly makes his first start of the season, filling in for left-hander Erik Bedard, who was scratched because of slight inflammation in his left shoulder. Morrow, who started five games late last season, began this season as the closer, but lost the job in mid-May and had recently asked the team to re-convert him back to a starter. That was expected to occur at Triple-A Tacoma, not with the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel's excellence on the road continued on Tuesday. After allowing runs in each of the first two innings, the righty stuck around long enough to get a win by lasting six innings in Milwaukee, with nothing more allowed in a tight victory. He has walked just eight batters -- one intentionally as his lone free pass issued Tuesday -- in his last seven starts. He has fallen short of five complete innings in three of his four outings at Coors Field, however.
away_pitcher_note: The Mariners know what they'll get from Vargas on most occasions -- a decent enough effort, though unspectacular, that will keep them close. The right-hander needs to throw more first-pitch strikes and command his fastball inside with more efficiency, but he's been a nice find that's bolstered what's become a dependable rotation. The Mariners will closely watch how Vargas reacts to his first loss, a 3-1 setback in Baltimore on Tuesday. He didn't pitch that poorly, giving up three runs on seven hits over 5 2/3 innings. And Vargas was honest when he told reporters that he wasn't happy with his performance, demonstrating that he understands where he needs to improve.

home_pitcher_note: After two horrendous starts against the Milwaukee Brewers -- the team with which De La Rosa made his Major League debut -- the left-hander solved the Brew Crew on Wednesday, allowing two runs in six innings. Control was still an issue -- he walked four batters -- but he also struck out eight batters and notched a second straight win after his 0-6 start to the year. Like everyone else, De La Rosa was swept up in the rash of impressive starting pitching during Colorado's winning streak.
away_pitcher_note: Niemann got an extra day of rest before his start vs. Los Angeles and he'll receive another one before going against the Rockies. It didn't seem to help him much last time, as he labored against the Angels, throwing 91 pitches and walking three batters in 3 2/3 innings while allowing four runs on seven hits. He was throwing hard but his curveball didn't seem to have the same snap it has had over his previous four or five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cook ran the starters' winning streak to eight consecutive games with a solid outing Thursday in Milwaukee, allowing just one run despite seven hits in six-plus innings. He struck out a season-high seven batters and only ran into trouble when he loaded the bases on two singles and a walk in the seventh. After recording the first out of the game, Cook became the first pitcher to throw 1,000 career innings in a Rockies uniform. Tampa Bay has been unkind to Cook -- he has allowed 11 earned runs in 12 innings over two starts in his career against the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: It was another short outing for the rookie Price, who in four starts this season has yet to pitch into the seventh inning. The left-hander was erratic in 4 1/3 innings against Anaheim, walking six and throwing 105 pitches. But he was also dominant, striking out six and allowing only two hits and one run. It's that dichotomy that has been frustrating so far for Rays fans, who continue to wait for a breakthrough performance from Price and will hope the thin air in Colorado doesn't deter him.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez was working his fastball against the Mariners -- for better or for worse. It was bad in the beginning as his first eight pitches were fastballs and Russell Branyan smashed one for a home run. After giving up four runs in four innings, Jimenez regrouped and ended the game by tossing five scoreless innings for the complete-game win. The win was Jimenez's first in Interleague Play (1-3, 4.67 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: After being Tampa Bay's workhorse the first two months of the season, Garza has been unable to get past the sixth inning in his last two starts. He got hit hard in the first inning against Washington on Friday, giving up three runs on four hits, but eventually settled down and put zeroes on the board until exiting after 5 2/3 innings. He threw 116 pitches, though, and walked four, giving him six walks and seven strikeouts in his last two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis wasn't as dominant as he had shown all season against the Mariners in his last start, but he found a way. In seven innings, Marquis had only one 1-2-3 inning but through guts and guile, he found a way to escape unscathed in every inning but one. In all, Marquis surrendered just an earned run on seven hits but got the no-decision as the Rockies scored twice in the eighth for a 5-3 victory. Marquis' next start will be against the Pirates. He owns an 8-6 career record against the Bucs with a 3.83 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf earned his first win since May 18 in his last start. The right-hander threw six innings and gave up only one run on two hits against the Tigers. The last time Ohlendorf gave up just one run was May 13 against the Cardinals. Ohlendorf has yet to face the Rockies in his career. He is 2-3 with a 5.02 ERA in six road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel silenced all the naysayers with a win against the Mariners at Coors Field, a place he had yet to conquer. Hammel kept his fastball down in the zone in 5 1/3 innings, allowing just an earned run on five hits with no walks and a season-high six strikeouts. Four of the six strikeouts came on curveballs. Hammel's start was cut short because of a 55-minute rain delay in the sixth inning. In Hammel's only career appearance against the Pirates, he picked up the loss in relief by giving up a solo home run in 1 2/3 innings as a member of the Tampa Bay Rays in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Morton makes his first start since suffering from a strain in his left hamstring June 10 against the Braves. He lasted just one inning in that start, surrendering one hit and no runs on 13 pitches. It was his first start of the season. Morton has never pitched against Rockies, but he has been more impressive on the road than at home in his short career. Three of Morton's four career victories have come in opposing ballparks.

home_pitcher_note: After picking up his first wins of the season in consecutive stats to begin June, De La Rosa took a major step backward in his last outing. He gave up seven runs to the Rays in 2 1/3 innings, his shortest effort of 2009. De La Rosa had trouble with his command, leaving the ball up and over the middle of the plate, a dangerous way to pitch at Coors Field. The Rays pounced for five extra-base hits. De La Rosa pitched a gem at Pittsburgh on May 15, striking out 10 and walking none in seven innings of one-run ball. He owns a 3.66 ERA in seven career appearances (19 2/3 innings) against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm was rocked for eight runs on 14 hits in five innings in his most recent start. Despite getting ahead of each of the first nine hitters he faced, the lefty had problems getting the ball down consistently, which the Twins took advantage of. Maholm's results have been to both extremes this season. He's now allowed seven or more runs in three starts, but has allowed one or fewer six different times. Maholm pitched seven scoreless innings against the Rockies earlier this season. He is 1-2 with a 3.60 ERA in four career starts against Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Matched against Tim Lincecum, his teammate at Fresno in 2007, Palmer had a solid effort on Wednesday in San Francisco. Lasting 6 1/3 innings, he yielded three earned runs on six hits, walking two -- one intentional -- while striking out five hitters. Palmer maintained his unbeaten record when the Angels rallied in the eighth inning to take the lead against Lincecum. Palmer has excelled at Angel Stadium, going 4-0 in six appearances, five as a starter, with a 3.41 ERA. He lost to the Rockies last year while with the Giants, giving up four earned runs in 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cook went seven innings in his last start and won to tie Jason Jennings for the franchise lead in wins with 58. In the 5-3 victory over the Rays, Cook aggressively stayed in the zone against hitters who were hoping his sinker would dip low for balls, and he used the sinker effectively for grounders. He gave up consecutive homers for Carl Crawford and Evan Longoria on breaking balls, but didn't let anything hurt him for the rest of his time on the mound. Cook won his only career start at Angel Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: With Ervin Santana's right triceps tightness forcing him to the 15-day disabled list, O'Sullivan gets his second Major League start. The Angels are hoping he has the same command and poise he brought to the AT&T Park mound on Tuesday night when he held the Giants to one earned run on five hits and one walk across seven innings, striking out five hitters. He's not overpowering, but O'Sullivan, 21, is effective when he puts his fastball in good spots and keeps hitters off balance with a breaking ball and quality changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez is 3-0 with a 2.43 ERA and 23 strikeouts against 12 walks in his last four games. He's done it in myriad ways -- skating through traffic on the bases against the Astros on June 2 but giving up only one run in a no-decision, giving up four early runs but pitching a complete-game victory over the Mariners on June 12, and dominating for eight innings against the Cardinals on June 7 and against the Rays in his last start. He can pitch with his fastball  but also can adjust when hitters are too aggressive.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders fought his control early, walking home a run, and yielded a pair of homers while lasting 6 1/3 innings in a no-decision against the Dodgers on Friday night at home. He was touched for four earned runs on six hits and three walks, striking out four hitters. He has made it into the seventh inning in nine of his 14 starts. Saunders has never faced the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis held the Pirates to three runs and forced a whopping 20 groundball outs in a 7-3 victory at Coors Field on Friday night. Marquis actually has had better nights. None of his secondary pitches worked. Of course there is a difference between the lineups of the aggressive, experienced Angels and the less accomplished Pirates. But by being allowed to experiment this spring, rather than being forced into competition for a job, Marquis has learned and is better able to adjust to hitters or his own effectiveness level.

home_pitcher_note: Braden (5-6) threw seven innings, allowing two runs on six hits in a tough-luck loss to the Padres. He finished with one walk and six strikeouts. Braden got just one run of support from Oakland hitters, continuing a trend of poor run support for Braden this season. He has received one run or less of support in eight of his 15 starts. "I've always said my goal is: nine innings, no walks, no hits, no runs," Braden said. "We go from there. I'm not the guy to talk to about the guys who are swinging it."
away_pitcher_note: Hammel struggled when his team needed him most Saturday night in a Rockies victory over the Pirates. He gave up one run after the Rockies tied the game in the second, and three runs after his team had taken a two-run lead. But six of the eight hits off Hammel were singles. He struck out four and walked two. Hammel, who came to the Rockies from the Rays, is 2-1 with a 6.75 ERA against the Athletics. That includes one start and four relief appearances. He is 2-0 with a 2.70 ERA in three relief appearances, covering 6 2/3 innings, at McAfee Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill, 21, had one of the best outings of his rookie season on Monday against the visiting Giants, rolling through seven innings on 99 pitches while giving up one run -- a solo homer to Travis Ishikawa -- on four hits and a walk while striking out four. A sinkerball pitcher with a low-90s fastball, Cahill has been on a roll of late, allowing more than two earned runs once in seven starts since May 17. This will be his first career start against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa recovered from a messy start against the Rays to beat the Pirates on Sunday, but not without some trouble. He had a mechanical issue in the first inning, opening his front shoulder too quickly. Although he gave up one run, he faced seven batters and had to get the final two outs with the bases loaded. He wound up going 5 2/3 innings and giving up four runs, then turning it over to an effective bullpen. De La Rosa held the Pirates to one baserunner in the third through fifth innings. De La Rosa, who pitched for the Royals previously, is 2-1 with a 2.29 ERA in three starts against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: After surrendering four runs in his first two frames, Mazzaro rebounded to throw four scoreless innings before being removed in a 4-1 loss to the Giants on Tuesday. He allowed seven hits, walked two and struck out six on 105 pitches, but as he did on June 12, he had the misfortune of matching up with Tim Lincecum, who threw his second consecutive complete game against the A's. This will be Mazzaro's first career start against Colorado, and his sixth overall.
away_pitcher_note: Cook allowed one run over seven innings to earn his seventh win of the season and his 59th since joining the Rockies (a franchise record). He gave up only three hits and two walks, while recording four strikeouts. Rockies manager Jim Tracy said Cook's sinker against the Angels was "as heavy as I have seen it all season". Cook has one previous start against the Athletics, which resulted in a no-decision after he allowed one run over eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf got roughed up by the White Sox last time out. In only 3 1/3 innings, he allowed five runs and three homers, along with two walks, two wild pitches and a hit batter. The Dodgers had won seven of Wolf's eight previous starts and he came into the game having allowed only one run the previous 11 innings. It was his first start of the year lasting less than five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez pitched a solid seven innings against the Angels on Tuesday, giving up seven hits and four earned runs, yet he got the loss thanks to a timely two-run single by Bobby Abreu in the top of the eighth inning. It was the first loss of June for Jimenez, who had won three straight. Jimenez is 4-3 with a 6.84 ERA in 10 career games against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: For the second consecutive start, Billingsley was given a lead of at least three runs and couldn't protect it, missing out on becoming the first 10-game winner in the National League. This time, Billingsley allowed home runs to Paul Konerko and A.J. Pierzynski -- who hit a three-run shot -- and came away with another no-decision. He also walked four in the outing and has walked nine in his past 12 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis got lit up early and often against the Angels Wednesday, giving up seven earned runs in 31/3 innings of work. Going for a major league leading 10 wins, Marquis recorded the loss, moving to 9-5 with a 4.22 ERA. Marquis in 10 games against the Dodgers is 4-1 with a 2.19 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: On Friday against the Seattle Mariners, Kershaw displayed more control over his pitches than in many of his other starts this season. In six innings, Kershaw walked just one batter (tied for his lowest total of the year.) Kershaw rarely got behind batters, and his superb location helped him strike out eight Mariners on the night. Kershaw did give up runs in the fourth and sixth innings, but he never allowed Seattle to mount a prolonged rally. Kershaw is 2-3 with a 7.30 ERA in five career starts against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: The Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum played big Friday night, and Hammel took advantage, forcing nine outs in the air. Most of them were off the end of bats. Dodger Stadium plays big usually, but the ball tends to travel during day games, so it remains to be seen if Hammel will use the same approach and if it'll work the same. But everything, it seems, is working for Hammel during a stretch where he is 5-0 with a 3.40 ERA in seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa pitched six mostly smooth innings in his last start, a win at Oakland. Fans and professional observers alike sometimes hold their breaths whenever De La Rosa gets into a tough situation, mainly because there have been stretches when he would get tripped up by one bad inning. But he is 4-1 in his last five starts, mainly because he's been able to work through early problems.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer had won three straight before his last start, when he gave up four hits, walked three and gave up eight runs -- just three earned -- in 4 1/3 innings of a 12-8 loss to the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Cook is making a case for his second successive All-Star Game appearance. He is 5-0 with a 1.75 ERA in his past five starts, and his five wins in June led the National League. In going eight-plus innings and holding the Athletics to one run during a 3-1 victory on Sunday, Cook used his four-seam fastball against the left-handers in the lineup and had more fly-ball outs (10) than ground-ball outs (nine).This is the first time Cook will face the D-backs since Opening Day, when he gave up six runs and seven hits in a 2 1/3-inning pratfall at Chase Field.
away_pitcher_note: Petit, who has been on the 15-day disabled list since May 9 with a strained right shoulder, recently completed a rehab assignment with Triple-A Reno. In his last outing with the Aces, he pitched three innings and allowed three runs (two earned) and five hits. He was 0-1 with a 6.89 ERA in five starts for Reno. He takes the spot of Billy Buckner, who was sent down on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez had yet another solid outing in the Rockies' 4-2, 13-inning loss to the Dodgers on Monday night. He yielded one hit in the first four innings and went seven innings total, with two runs on five hits and four strikeouts. A few small executions issues tripped him, such as a poor pitchout and a balk that moved runners before he gave up a two-run single. Facing the D-backs should bring good memories. Jimenez threw seven scoreless innings against Arizona in his first start of the season, a 3-0 Rockies victory on April 7.
away_pitcher_note: Haren dominated the Reds is his last start on Tuesday. He pitched seven innings and only allowed one run on four hits while striking out nine. Haren also helped his own cause at the plate. He hit the first homer of his career and also doubled in the D-backs' 6-2 victory. He lowered his National League-leading ERA to 2.19 in the victory. Against the Rockies this season, Haren is 1-1 with a 0.64 ERA in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: The efficiency of Marquis' 3-0 shutout of the Dodgers on Tuesday night was stunning. He threw strikes on 66 of his 86 pitches, didn't walk anyone and held the Dodgers to two hits. He's had strong games pitching without his secondary pitches, like an 8 2/3-inning beating of the Pirates earlier in the season at Coors. But against the Dodgers, he had a cutter to go with the sinker. Marquis will meet the Nationals at Coors, where he is 4-2 with a 4.34 ERA this season.
away_pitcher_note: Through five innings against the Marlins on Tuesday, Stammen was on his game, giving up one unearned run on three hits and retiring eight of nine batters at one point. But sporting a 5-1 lead in the sixth, the 25-year-old rookie gave up a run on a wild pitch, then allowed a two-run homer to Hanley Ramirez to make it a one-run game. After that, a bullpen that came in with the most losses and highest ERA in the big leagues allowed the Marlins to take the lead and gave him a no-decision. Stammen finished having allowed four runs (three earned) on six hits with no walks and two strikeouts while throwing 73 pitches (47 strikes). This will be his first career appearance against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel has set career highs for innings pitched in a game in his last two starts -- 7 1/3 innings in a win over the Athletics, and an eight-inning complete game in a 1-0 loss to the Dodgers on Wednesday afternoon. Hammel's new two-seam fastball gives him a pitch low in the zone. He has had more flyballs than groundballs in the last two starts and that could be dangerous at Coors, but much of the contact has been weak.
away_pitcher_note: As has been the case since close to the start of June, Zimmermann was solid against the Marlins on Wednesday, but he didn't end up with a win to show for it. The 23-year-old rookie gave up just two runs on six hits with six strikeouts and one walk before leaving with 100 pitches under his belt through six innings -- right before a 19-minute rain delay. Zimmermann left with a 2-1 lead, but the Major Leagues' worst bullpen -- statistically -- allowed Florida to come back in an eventual loss. Zimmermann sports a 2.12 ERA since the start of June, but he only has one win. This will be his first career appearance against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa is riding a career-high three-game winning streak and arguably had his finest outing of the season as he threw eight shutout innings of four-hit ball with four walks and six strikeouts in a 5-0 win over the D-backs. Arizona didn't have a player reach second base until the sixth inning and had only three players overall accomplish such a feat. De La Rosa showed the tantalizing promise he always had as he had complete command of all four of pitches -- fastball, slider, curveball and change. In his last six starts, De La Rosa is 5-1 with a 4.67 ERA after beginning April and May winless.
away_pitcher_note: Detwiler started against the Braves on Friday and lasted 3 1/3 innings and gave up five runs on 10 hits. He said he had a good bullpen session before the game. By the time the game started, however, it was clear to Detwiler that he had a problem with his release point. Most of his pitches were up in the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: It just wasn't Cook's night in his last start against the D-backs. The sinkerballer left the game after getting his wind knocked out diving for a ground ball, and then lost a chance to get the win when the bullpen could not protect the lead.
