He gave up three runs, two earned, on nine hits in five-plus innings. Despite the unlucky performance, Cook has won his last five decisions and sports a 1.98 ERA in his last six starts. He will attempt, again, to win his sixth consecutive decision -- a personal and club record -- when he faces the Braves. On May 21, Cook pitched a four-hit shutout against the Braves at Turner Field.
away_pitcher_note: On Independence Day in Washington, D.C., Hanson was spectacular for the fourth straight outing. He pounded the plate, throwing over 70 percent strikes, giving up three hits and one walk in seven innings. The lone run -- ending his 26-inning scoreless streak -- came on a fastball down the middle to Adam Dunn, who crushed it deep into the upper deck for a solo homer. "I left it over the plate, and he let me know," Hanson said. The rookie did not earn a victory, as Atlanta's bullpen blew the game upon entering the game in the eighth.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez threw one bad pitch and it cost him in his last start, against the Diamondbacks. He threw 5 2/3 no-hit innings until serving up a three-run home run to Mark Reynolds to tie the game. Jimenez yielded another run in the seventh and took the loss. Expect the promising 25-year-old right-hander to pitch deep against the Braves, as he has thrown more than 100 pitches in all but one of his 17 starts this season. Jimenez has yet to face the Braves this season but is 1-2 with a 5.66 ERA in four career starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe has not been sharp in the past couple of weeks, even saying, "It seems like a struggle every time out," after his last start -- a loss to the Nationals. In that game, Lowe threw 5 1/3 innings, leaving the bases loaded for his relievers, who let only one inherited runner score. Lowe was tacked with four earned runs on 10 hits. His sinker often didn't sink out of the zone, and Lowe only had one strikeout during the start.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis collected his Major League best 11th win Monday night at Coors Field, throwing eight shutout innings to run his scoreless steak to 17. His sinker was in great form, helping to account for 13 groundball outs, and his slider was effective in key situations, including a bases-loaded, inning-ending double play to protect a 1-0 lead in the seventh inning. Opposing hitters are now 0-for-9 against Marquis with the bases loaded. The All-Star's final start Saturday before the break should leave him well-positioned to contribute at the Midsummer Classic in St. Louis, where he won 42 games over three seasons with the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: With just one win in his past seven starts, Jurrjens hasn't received the deserving compensation that reflects the 3.40 ERA he has posted during this span. During Monday night's loss to the Cubs, he surrendered four earned runs for just the third time this season and surrendered his third homer in a span of four starts. Known for his ability to keep pitches down in the zone, the 23-year-old right-hander has occasionally fought some early control issues that have proved damaging. One of his finest starts this year occurred on May 19, when he limited the Rockies to one run and three hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel had such poor fastball command Tuesday night against the Nationals that he never had a chance with his secondary pitches. Yet, he was able to smile about it. He gave up four runs on two homers, but the Rockies won the game late, 5-4. This occurred after he held the Dodgers to one run in a 1-0, complete-game loss, so it didn't shake his confidence. Hammel has faced the Braves once this year, but it wasn't fun. He gave up six runs, three earned, in six innings of an 8-1 loss at Turner Field.
away_pitcher_note: With Javier Vazquez scratched because of a lower abdominal strain, Medlen will be asked to pitch as many innings as possible during what should shape up to be a bullpen game.  Medlen hasn't started since May 31 and just two of the seven appearances he's made since then have consisted of at least three innings. The rookie hurler was 1-2 with a 6.28 ERA in three starts he made in May.

home_pitcher_note: Gaudin is coming off a strong outing on July 8 in Arizona, where he limited the D-backs to one run on three hits with four walks and seven strikeouts. He left with a 2-1 lead and received a no-decision in a game the Padres eventually lost when their bullpen lost the lead in the late innings. "Anytime you lose a ballgame you had a chance to win, whether it's because of a mental mistake or a physical mistake, it's frustrating," Gaudin said. "But you try to take the positives from it and go out tomorrow, not make those same mistakes and execute when you can." Gaudin actually has had a pretty good first half despite his 5.03 ERA. He's been hurt by command issues but when he's in the strike zone, he's been good.
away_pitcher_note: Cook comes out of the All-Star break looking get back on track after two average July starts. Against the Braves in his last start, Cook gave up five runs on nine hits in 5 2/3 innings without his best sinker. In the start before, he yielded three runs, two earned, in five innings before leaving with his wind knocked out. He has a 5.91 ERA in July after posting a 5-1 record with a 2.36 ERA in June.

home_pitcher_note: Geer struggled in his last start before the All-Star break, allowing six runs in 4 2/3 innings in a loss to the Giants on July 9. Once again, the long ball hurt him as he allowed a home run to Bengie Molina in the first inning and then consecutive home runs in the fifth inning to Travis Ishikawa and Juan Uribe. Geer has now allowed a National League-leading 22 home runs. "At this level, you've got to keep the ball down," Geer said. Geer has a good two-seam fastball that moves but when it's left up in the strike zone becomes far less effective than when he buries it low in the strike zone.
away_pitcher_note: There are only three words to describe Jimenez this season: hard-luck loser. The Rockies have scored three runs or less in 10 of Jimenez's 18 starts and the club has lost the last nine in those instances. Jimenez is 6-9 with a 3.81 ERA this season. In his last start before the All-Star break, he picked up the loss yielding two runs in six innings against the Braves. As talented as Jimenez is, he's been one pitch from possibly winning in each of his last four decisions -- three of which are losses.

home_pitcher_note: Correia, easily one of the highlights from the first half of the season, allowed three earned runs over 5 2/3 innings in his last start on July 12 against the Giants, faltering late after a strong start. Correia, who came to Spring Training on a Minor League contract, has won six games and been a plus for a staff ravaged by injuries. Against the Giants, his former team, Correia allowed eight hits, one walk and struck out three. Heading into the All-Star break, he led the Padres in innings and was tied with Jake Peavy in victories.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel had a rough outing in his last start as he lasted three innings and surrendered five runs on nine hits. He couldn't get out of jams and gave up runs in each inning he worked. In eight starts from May 24 - July 1, Hammel went 5-1 with a 3.47 ERA. However, in his last two starts leading up to the break, he's given up nine runs in 8 2/3 innings. Hammel will get the start ahead of Marquis in the rotation because of the Marquis' possibility to play in the All-Star game.

home_pitcher_note: Latos, a 6-foot-6, 225-pound right-hander, will make his Major League debut against the Rockies after being called up from Double-A San Antonio. Latos was 5-1 with a 1.91 ERA in nine starts at San Antonio after starting the season with a 3-0 record and a 0.36 ERA at Class A Fort Wayne. In 72 1/3 innings this season, Latos has 73 strikeouts while allowing 42 hits and 12 walks. He pitched a scoreless inning on July 12 in the XM All-Star Futures Game. The right-hander's fastball has been clocked in the mid-90s, and he has shown pinpoint control in the Minors. In his last start for San Antonio, on July 9, Latos pitched five perfect innings before being taken out due to pitch count.
away_pitcher_note: The All-Star sinkerballer pitched a great first inning in his last start but battled himself the rest of the way. A fine illustration of Marquis not being himself was that he had seven groundball outs and seven flyball outs. On the season, he has a 2.10-to-1 groundball to flyball ratio. He went six innings and gave up three runs on seven hits to pick up the loss in a 4-3 decision.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa pitched one shaky inning of relief for the Rockies on July 12 in their comeback win over the Braves. He allowed two runs on two hits. In his last start, De La Rosa tossed 6 1/3 innings July 8 in Colorado's 10-4 victory over Washington. He allowed three runs on five hits, walking three and striking out five. De La Rosa has won six of his last seven starts after a rocky 0-6 record with four no-decisions to start the season.
away_pitcher_note: The Marlins made Davis work his last time out, forcing the left-handeder to throw 99 pitches in a four-inning outing. Davis struck out seven but issued three walks and gave up five runs in the loss. The outing was Davis' shortest since pitching four innings against the Giants on June 10.

home_pitcher_note: Cook struck out eight to match a career high in his last start, when he tossed six innings en route to a dominating 10-1 Rockies win over the Padres. He allowed one run on eight hits and walked four. Cook described the game as "really weird" considering that he allowed more baserunners than usual for a quality start. "I pitched with a lot of guys on base, gave up a lot of hits, but the defense came up huge behind me, and I was able to get some strikeouts when I needed to," he said.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer, who is still seeking his first win since a victory against Texas on June 23, shined against the Padres, limiting the San Diego offense to two runs over seven innings while racking up nine strikeouts. The right-hander continues to show improvement on the mound and could develop into a staple of the D-backs' rotation in the future. He's pitched at least six innings in five of his last six outings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Jimenez struck out a season-high 10 batters in the Rockies' victory over the Padres. He tossed seven innings, allowing three runs on three hits. With the Rockies holding a 5-1 lead, he gave up two runs in the fifth inning that breathed some life into the struggling Padres' bats. "[Jimenez] is inches away from being a very special player, but we're not there yet." Rockies manager Jim Tracy said. "[He needs to] get to the point where the mindset is such that when you build a 5-1 lead, there's very little doubt as to where the game is headed. That's what we're working on."
away_pitcher_note: Garland pitched well enough to win in his last outing, but came away with a loss as the D-backs fell, 6-1, to the Cardinals at Busch Stadium. Garland allowed just two runs over six innings. Both of the runs came on homers by Albert Pujols. The first homer to Pujols came on the first pitch of the fourth inning while the second came on a 3-0 pitch when he was leading off the sixth. In his start just prior to the All-Star Break, Garland picked up his first win since May 19, a span of nine starts. He has pitched better than his numbers would indicate. A few outings in which he was really hammered has skewed his ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Saturday at San Diego, Hammel struck out seven in 5 1/3 innings and gave up one run. He didn't figure in the decision, a 3-1 Rockies loss. The most memorable part of that game, however, was Hammel hitting the Padres' Edgar Gonzalez in the head with a 93-mph fastball. The pitch was clearly an accident, and Hammel said being able to talk to Gonzalez on the phone after the incident has eased his mind. Hammel threw six scoreless innings in his only start against the Giants this season, but San Francisco won, 1-0, in 10 innings on May 3.
away_pitcher_note: Cain won his second successive decision in his most recent start against the Pirates. The right-hander tossed seven dominating innings, giving up just one run on five hits. Cain also struck out eight batters, his highest total since June 26. He has faced the Rockies twice this season, coming in back-to-back starts on May 2 and 7. His second start was the better of the two, as he threw six shutout innings while surrendering just one hit.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa bordered on dominant while holding the D-backs to one run and four hits in seven innings of a victory at Coors Field on Monday night. Using a new sinker taught to him by staff ace Aaron Cook, De La Rosa is pitching more efficiently than at any point in his career. With the Rockies having changed their rotation to keep Jason Marquis on normal rest, De La Rosa will be pitching on five days' rest.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez followed up his July 10 no-hitter against San Diego in respectable fashion. Inconsistent through most of the season, Sanchez allowed three runs and just four hits in six innings at Atlanta last Monday. He wasn't involved in the decision as the Braves scored eight late runs to prevail, 11-3. Despite lacking command of his offspeed pitches, Sanchez struck out eight Braves and walked one, reflecting the wicked stuff he typically takes to the mound under any circumstances.

home_pitcher_note: Cook pitched through traffic, giving up eight hits in 6 1/3 innings. He gave up four runs, the last of which came after he was relieved for matchup purposes. Overall, though, it was a strong outing. Two of the runs came when center fielder Dexter Fowler misplayed a Justin Upton line drive into a triple.
away_pitcher_note: Sadowski might need a strong effort to save his spot in the rotation. After impressing the Giants with six- and seven-inning shutout efforts in his first two starts, he pitched respectably in a July 8 loss to Florida (two earned runs and five hits allowed in five innings), but the 26-year-old rookie was hit hard by the Atlanta Braves last Tuesday as he yielded eight runs and eight hits in 3 2/3 innings. After walking four batters in 13 innings spanning his first two starts, Sadowski has issued seven free passes -- one intentionally -- over 8 2/3 innings in his last two outings.

home_pitcher_note: The old wildness returned last Tuesday for Perez, who walked six batters over six innings in a losing effort against the Nationals. Though Perez has unquestionably been more effective since returning from the disabled list earlier this month, he has issued a total of 17 free passes in his three starts -- a win, a loss and a no-decision. He also suffered through similar bouts of wildness in two starts against the Rockies last season, walking 14 batters in 11 innings. Perez has not beaten the Rockies since 2005.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez showed moxie on Wednesday in a no-decision against the D-backs. He went six innings and was hurt by one pitch -- a three-run homer by Miguel Montero -- even though he had no fastball command. Taking advantage of the D-backs' familiarity with him, and trying desperately to stay afloat, Jimenez pocketed his blazing fastball and used his breaking ball for the final three innings of the six he was on the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey had a nice bounce-back performance against the Nationals Wednesday, but it still resulted in a loss. He went seven innings deep and let up three runs, including a two-run homer to Josh Willingham off a slider which the big right-hander hung over the plate. Pelfrey was firing mid-90's on the gun, and mentioned after the game that he was "the Mike that hasn't been there for a while." Both manager Jerry Manuel and third baseman David Wright said that Pelfrey's stuff was some of the best they've seen from him.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis, tied with the Giants' Matt Cain for the National League lead in victories, was not healthy for his last start, but you'd have never known it. He went eight innings in a victory over the Padres on July 19, but a middle-finger blister that had been bothering him for more than a month caused him to alter his grip on his main two pitches, his sinker and his changeup. He was supposed to start Friday against Cain and the Giants, but was pushed back and will start in his hometown. After a bullpen session Sunday, Marquis reported that he could throw with his normal grip for the first time in two weeks.

home_pitcher_note: In easily his worst start of the month, Santana served up five runs on a career-high 12 hits and three walks last Friday in Houston, taking his eighth loss -- though only the third in which he did not submit a quality start. The Mets can only hope a reprieve will come at Citi Field, where Santana holds a 1.86 ERA this season, and where he has never failed to deliver a quality start. He will be making his first-ever start against the Rockies, one of only two teams he has never faced (the other being the Twins, his former employer for eight seasons).
away_pitcher_note: Hammel gave up three runs and seven hits in six mostly solid innings of a 3-1 loss to the Giants on Friday night. It was a step forward for Hammel, who had struggled with fleeting fastball command during home games. But this start is at the Mets' Citi Field, and Hammel is a beast on the road -- 4-2, 1.93 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Called upon to replace the disabled Fernando Nieve in the rotation, the 22-year-old Niese sparkled last Saturday in Houston, relying more on his high-80s fastball than his trademark curveball. He held the Astros to one run on four hits over seven innings, walking two and striking out three. Counting his previous seven starts with Triple-A Buffalo, Niese has now produced a 0.78 ERA over his last eight outings. His next start -- presumably, he has earned one -- will come against the Rockies, another team he has never faced.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa, who stated the year 0-6, leads all Major League pitchers with eight wins since June 1. In his last start, he went 7 1/3 innings and struck out seven, against no walks, in an 8-2 victory over the Giants. He threw just 96 pitches and could have had a complete game, but getting Rafael Betancourt and rookie Jhoulys Chacin (who made his Major League debut) was a priority.

home_pitcher_note: Lehr is 13-3 with a 3.31 ERA in Triple-A this season and was named earlier this week the International League's pitcher of the week. He began 2009 in the Phillies organization, but was traded in May and began his third stint with the Reds organization in less than two years. Since returning to Louisville, Lehr was 8-1 with a 2.51 ERA in 11 starts and one relief appearance. His previous big league stops were with the A's and Brewers and he had a combined 66 appearances, but no Major League starts. The right-hander's last game in the Majors came against the Reds with the Brewers on May 22, 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Cook breezed through the Giants' order his last time out on Sunday, needing only 77 pitches to complete seven innings. He allowed two runs on nine hits in picking up his 10th win of the season and seventh in a row. Cook is 2-0 with a 5.34 ERA in seven career appearances against the Reds. Both of those wins have occurred at Great American Ball Park, where he owns a 2.86 ERA. Cook has had some trouble in his limited exposure to the Reds' lineup. Jonny Gomes is 3-for-3 with two home runs off him, and Reds regulars own a .326 average against him in 43 at-bats.

home_pitcher_note: After he struggled over his two previous outings, Bailey returned to form in a 6-3 win over the Padres. Bailey allowed three earned runs on six hits in 7 1/3 innings. His only major mistakes came in the sixth when he gave up back-to-back homers which cut the lead to 5-3. Yet he received enough offensive support to earn his first victory since June 27. Bailey will look to continue his success against the Rockies, who he is 0-1 against in his career. He gave up four runs and 15 hits in a start against Colorado last season.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez did not receive a decision despite another solid outing last Monday against the Mets, allowing three runs on six hits in seven innings. It was the third straight start he had surrendered exactly three runs and the 17th consecutive time he had lasted at least six innings. Jimenez is 1-0 with a 1.50 ERA in two career starts against the Reds, including tossing six shutout innings in his lone career start at Great American Ballpark. The current Reds' roster owns only 18 total at-bats against Jimenez, with Joey Votto going 2-for-5 with a double off him. Jimenez is moving from his July -- historically his best month -- to August, where he has struggled to a 4-5 mark with a 5.05 ERA in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo exited Monday's game against the Padres with the fate of his hands. Yet he earned the loss when reliever Nick Masset allowed an inherited runner to score from third. Arroyo now has lost his last two starts after he had won his previous two outings. Arroyo gave up just three runs over 6 1/3 innings but was knocked around for nine hits. He will look to snap his losing streak against the Rockies who he is 1-2 against in his career with a 4.39 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: After having his start pushed back because of a blister on his right middle finger, Marquis said he felt fine even after taking the loss in a 4-0 defeat against the Mets on Tuesday. Marquis went six innings and allowed three runs -- two earned -- on seven hits, saying he could use his regular grip on his sinker for the first time in a few starts. Marquis owns a 6-3 mark with a 4.81 ERA in 14 career games (13 starts) against the Reds. He is 4-2 with a 4.42 ERA at Great American Ballpark. Edwin Encarnacion is 8-for-16 with two home runs in his career against Marquis.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer is 4-1 with a 3.30 ERA (11 earned runs in 30 innings) in July and 10-7 with a 5.32 ERA this season. In 6 2/3 scoreless innings Monday against the Diamondbacks at Chase Field, he allowed six hits and four walks and struck out five. That is encouraging as the Phillies enter August. They will need Moyer to keep pitching well to keep the strain off the bullpen, which will be needed come October -- assuming the Phillies hold onto their lead in the National League East.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel had the worst start of his career Thursday against the Mets, getting knocked out after just 1 1/3 innings and five runs. Hammel gave up five consecutive hits to start the second inning, and all five came around to score in a 7-0 loss. Hammel has appeared in one game against the Phillies in his career, allowing two runs on five hits in 2 2/3 innings in relief. He has never pitched at Citizens Bank Park. Raul Ibanez and Matt Stairs are the only Phillies with more than two at-bats against Hammel, and both have had success. Ibanez is 2-for-5 with a solo home run while Stairs is 5-for-8 with two home runs, a double and four RBIs.

home_pitcher_note: Happ survived the Trade Deadline. He had been rumored to be part of a trade that would bring Roy Halladay from Toronto, but the trade never materialized. Happ has been effective pitching out of rotation and bullpen this season. It remains to be seen where he will end up once Cliff Lee and Pedro Martinez both join the 25-man roster, but for the moment he remains a starter.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa won a franchise-record seventh consecutive start on Thursday against the Mets, giving up two runs on three hits in 6 1/3 innings. De La Rosa chipped in with a double, scoring the go-ahead run for the Rockies in the seventh inning. He'll look to extend his streak to eight wins against a Phillies' franchise that has given him problems in the past. De La Rosa is 0-2 with an 8.79 ERA in five career games against the Phillies, including three starts. He was lit up for seven runs (six earned) in 3 2/3 innings in his only career start at Citizens Bank Park. Shane Victorino is 3-for-6 off De La Rosa with a home run while Jimmy Rollins is 3-for-7.

home_pitcher_note: Lee couldn't have had a much better debut for the Phillies on Friday against the Giants at AT&T Park. He threw a complete game. He allowed one run, four hits and two walks in a 5-1 victory. He struck out six. Oh, he also went 2-for-4 with a double -- the first extra-base hit of his career. He worked efficiently and effectively, and made the Phillies feel pretty good about acquiring him July 29 from the Indians for prospects Carlos Carrasco, Lou Marson, Jason Donald and Jason Knapp.
away_pitcher_note: Cook was solid for most of his 6 2/3 innings in Friday night's Rockies victory over the Reds, but he didn't figure in the decision. His biggest problem, besides the consecutive home runs by Joey Votto and Brandon Phillips in the sixth, was the Rockies didn't find their offensive stride until late in the game. Cook gave up seven hits but forced 10 ground-ball outs. He'll need to keep the ball low against the dangerous Phillies at Citizens Bank Park, a similar bandbox to Great American Ball Park.

home_pitcher_note: Was the gun at Great American Ball Park a little off Saturday night? It clocked Jimenez as reaching 100 mph on multiple occasions. But that actually wasn't important. Jimenez and catcher Yorvit Torrealba realized the Reds were sitting on his fastball, no matter how hard he threw it. So Jimenez went eight innings and didn't let a runner past first base after the second inning. He struck out eight in a 6-2 Rockies victory. In his next start, Jimenez will face the Cubs at Coors Field, where he is 4-4 with a 3.99 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano had to come out of his last start after three innings because of back stiffness. He gave up two runs on three hits in the brief outing, his shortest of the season. He will be vying for his fourth straight win. On the road, Zambrano is 5-2 with a 3.17 ERA. The right-hander is winless in three starts at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis was cruising toward his 13th victory until he ran into problems in the seventh inning. With the Rockies leading 3-0 against the Reds last Sunday, Marquis gave up a double to Brandon Phillips, hit Scott Rolen with a pitch in the head and then allowed a three-run homer to Laynce Nix which tied the game. Marquis only scattered four hits on three runs and had been almost perfect before the seventh. Marquis will look to beat the Cubs, a team he pitched for last season. He beat them April 15 for his second win of the season when he pitched seven innings and gave up one run on five hits in a 5-2 win.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster threw six shutout innings in his last start against the Marlins but did not get a decision as Florida rallied for a walk-off win. The Cubs limited him to 97 pitches, but now, Lou Piniella says he'll turn Dempster loose. This was the right-hander's second start since coming off the disabled list and they were just being careful. Dempster did walk four. Coors Field has not been kind to Dempster, who is 0-2 with a 15.23 ERA in seven games there.

home_pitcher_note: After taking a beating to the tune of five runs and seven hits in 1 1/3 innings against the Mets on July 30, Hammel displayed improved fastball command and devastating off-speed pitches in a victory over the Phillies on Tuesday night. Hammel gave up three runs and seven hits in 6 2/3 innings. He struck out six, including Ryan Howard with the bases loaded in the third, and did not walk a batter. Going into the home start against the Cubs, Hammel's struggles at Coors Field are well-documented (1-3, 7.20 ERA). However, in his last home start, on July 24, Hammel held the Giants to three runs and seven hits in a respectable six innings of a loss.
away_pitcher_note: Wells is on cruise control. The rookie picked up his fourth straight win in his last outing against the Reds, giving up one run on six hits over 7 1/3 innings. He struck out five. Wells is the first Cubs rookie to win four straight since Kerry Wood did so April 30-May 17, 1998. Three Cubs pitchers have won five in a row, including the late Jeremi Gonzalez, who did so June 23-July 16, 1997.

home_pitcher_note: The Cubs are clearly contenders and have dangerous hitters in their lineup, but De La Rosa can take comfort and pleasure in the fact he's not facing the Phillies, who hit three home runs off him and scored seven runs in five innings on him Wednesday night at Citizens Bank Park. Nothing against the Cubs, but De La Rosa is 0-3 with a 9.78 ERA career against the Phils and 0-2 with a 15.12 ERA at Citizens Bank Park. He doesn't have a harrowing history, or much of any type of history, against the Cubs (1-0, 0.00 ERA in four relief appearances covering 6 1/3 innings).
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny made a great first impression in his Cubs debut. The lefty, acquired in a five-player deal with Pittsburgh on July 30, gave up one run on three hits over 7 1/3 innings against the Reds. Gorzelanny walked one, and cutting down on free passes is something he's been working on. He also helped himself with a RBI single but cautioned not to get too used to seeing him hit.

home_pitcher_note: The start became available because the Rockies are resting right-hander Aaron Cook, who is recovering from a hyperextended right big toe. He has been pushed to Saturday. Chacin, 21, called up from Double-A Tulsa on July 24, has pitched well in four relief appearances, including two innings on Saturday in his last appearance. Chacin showed a good fastball and changeup, plus beyond-his-years mound presence during Spring Training. He's also developed a slider that he has used at the Major League level. This will be his first regular-season start. The Rockies considered going with veteran Josh Fogg, but manager Jim Tracy said it was more important to have Fogg ready in case Chacin struggles. Chacin will be limited to around 75 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf left his last start with a one-run lead but was handed a no-decision as the Diamondbacks rallied late. Ohlendorf gave up just one run on four hits in six innings, with manager John Russell saying after the game that the next step for Ohlendorf is to get a little more efficient so he can pitch deeper into games. The righty has one start against the Rockies this season and took a defeat by giving up six runs on nine hits in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez won his third straight decision in his last start to even his record. He threw 6 2/3 innings and yielded two runs on four hits with six strikeouts to defeat the Cubs. However, he did issue five walks. Even with the command issues, Jimenez throws at least five pitches and he was able to control a two-seam fastball and, later, the curveball to cruise to victory. Jimenez has tossed at least six innings in 19 consecutive starts and has thrown more than 100 pitches in 21 of his 23 starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Hart's first start with the Pirates ended in a no-decision, though the right-hander pitched well enough to earn his new manager's praise afterward. Hart allowed three runs on nine hits in six innings. Pittsburgh is looking to Hart to stabilize a spot in the rotation that has been in shaky all season. He showcased solid fastball command with velocity in the 92-95 range in his last start. This will be Hart's first career start against the Rockies. He has pitched one inning of relief against Colorado and allowed two runs in it.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis has been stuck on 12 wins for nearly a month now, but of the three starts he's had for win No. 13, his last start was easily the worst. The first-time All-Star lacked sharpness as he surrendered five runs on eights with a season-high five walks to take the loss Saturday against the Cubs. Marquis had been pitching with a blister problem as recently as July 19 against the Padres. Coincidentally, that was when he picked up his 12th win. In his three starts since then, he's 0-2 with a 4.74 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm is now 0-2 in his last five starts after a no-decision in his last start, one in which Maholm allowed four runs in seven innings. Maholm has now allowed at least four runs in each of his last four starts. He was hurt by two home runs in his last start. It was the second time in his last four starts that Maholm had allowed two runs in a game. He is 1-3 with a 4.50 ERA in five career starts against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: It wasn't vintage Josh Johnson in his last start, but the 6-foot-7 right-hander was effective enough to collect his 11th win and 18th quality start in 23 overall outings this season. At Philadelphia, the 25-year-old ace gave up one run on four hits with six strikeouts and one walk. He was lifted after 85 pitches and 55 strikes, but he had some stressful innings. Three double plays helped Johnson get out of jams. The Marlins are 18-5 with the righty on the mound. On May 9 at Colorado, Johnson beat the Rockies, giving up one run in eight innings. Johnson has pitched 154 innings this year; his career high is 157, which came during his 2006 season as a rookie.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel hasn't been sharp lately, and he knows it. In his last start, on Sunday against the Cubs, Hammel gave up 11 hits and had only one 1-2-3 frame in his five-plus innings. Yet he picked up the victory, yielding just three runs -- all earned. In his his past seven starts, Hammel has a 6.48 ERA, though the Rockies have won four of those starts. Hammel's problem right now is that he can't throw his fastball on a downhill plane, thus the pitch is coming out of his hand flat. Therefore, hitters have been able to square up on him.

home_pitcher_note: VandenHurk had his share of baserunners against the Astros on Monday, but he got out of trouble most of the time and got the win after giving up just two runs. Still, the three walks and five hits put his pitch count at 97 after five innings, ending his start a bit early. VandenHurk, taking the No. 4 spot in the rotation with Anibal Sanchez on the disabled list and youngsters Andrew Miller and Sean West fighting inconsistency, has now given up no more than two runs in four of his five starts for Florida this year. He gave up two runs in 4 1/3 innings during his only career start against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Cook left his last start, a 3-1 loss to the Phillies, after five innings and 73 pitches with a hyperextended right big toe. The injury led to his being removed from a start Monday against the Pirates. He suffered it backing up third on Jimmy Rollins' triple. In that contest, Cook was toe-to-toe with the Phillies' Cliff Lee but threw two bad pitches -- one Paul Bako hit for his first homer of the season, the other the triple by Rollins. Cook is 1-1 with a 3.55 ERA in two starts at Florida.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad simply couldn't get out of the fifth inning in a no-decision against the Astros on Tuesday. In that frame, he gave up five runs, fired 35 pitches to nine batters and left before recording the final out. The 22-year-old finished giving up six runs on eight hits and three walks in 4 2/3 innings. Over his last two starts, he's gone a combined nine frames and given up 13 runs (10 earned). Volstad recorded his first career win against the Rockies and sports a 4.15 ERA in three career games (two starts) against them.
away_pitcher_note: Cook left his last start, a 3-1 loss to the Phillies, after five innings and 73 pitches with a hyperextended right big toe. The injury led to his being removed from a start Monday against the Pirates. He suffered it backing up third on Jimmy Rollins' triple. Cook is 1-1 with a 3.55 ERA in two starts at Florida.

Still, the three walks and five hits put his pitch count at 97 after five innings, ending his start a bit early.
