away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had poor arm-side command of his fastball early, but made pitches when they counted. Then he held the Cubs to one run on seven hits in 7 2/3 innings and struck out 11 during the Rockies' 11-5 victory at Coors Field. The fact De La Rosa could recognize overthrowing early and correct it before letting it ruin his outing is a sign of growth.

home_pitcher_note: Stammen had a solid outing against the Braves on Wednesday, but it wasn't enough to earn the victory. He went six innings and allowed just four hits on 79 pitches, but two of those hits were costly solo home runs. With the no-decision, Stammen remains winless in his last four starts. He turned in a brilliant outing against the Rockies on July 6 in Denver, going seven innings and allowing just one run on five hits. However, he took the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez didn't have fastball command early, but threw enough good ones and used his improving breaking pitches to keep the Pirates at bay. When his best fastball arrived, he dominated. Jimenez held the Pirates to three hits in eight scoreless innings of an 8-0 victory at Coors Field. Jimenez is 1-1 with a 4.76 ERA in three career games against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the Reds on Thursday, Balester pitched five innings and gave up five of the seven runs the Nationals surrendered. Four of the runs came on a pair of two-run homers by Jonny Gomes. The other was on a solo homer by Ryan Hanigan. One reason Balester has given up so many homers -- he has allowed nine in 24 innings -- is that his four-seam fastball has been too straight. Ironically, Balester said Thursday's start was the best his arm felt all season, but the box score tells a different story.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis' 13th win of the season against the Pirates Thursday marked a return to form for the All-Star pitcher and took him off a three-start schneid. He didn't have his best sinker working, but he was able to hold the Bucs to one run on three hits over seven innings. He worked ahead of hitters for much of the outing and benefited from excellent defensive play behind him. Marquis exploited the holes in the Pirates' swings, striking out six on the day, including three against cleanup hitter Garrett Jones.

home_pitcher_note: In fine form, Mock demonstrated the type of pitcher he is capable of becoming in his last start, on Friday night against the Reds. Mock pitched six strong innings as the Nationals won, 2-0, at Great American Ball Park. Mock dominated over the first four innings, striking out five batters, and he was able to get out of trouble in his final two frames.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel gave up only three runs in a loss to the Marlins on Friday, but constant trouble put his pitch count at 95 after just four innings and gave him a relatively short start. The 26-year-old put at least two runners on in each of his four frames and finished giving up six hits and four walks while throwing just 55 percent of his pitches for strikes. It was the sixth start this season in which Hammel pitched fewer than five innings. The South Carolina native did not talk to reporters after that start, as manager Jim Tracy said he took a flight out of Miami to deal with a death in his family. Tracy said Hammel knew about the matter before his start and that he was "OK to pitch." Hammel is scheduled to make his next start and will meet back with the team in Washington, D.C., on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Cook did not have a good outing in the opener of a doubleheader against the hot-hitting Marlins on August 16. The sinkerballer left pitches up in the zone and Florida's bats made him pay, scoring seven runs over 2 1/3 innings. Cook gave up two homers -- a solo shot to Hanley Ramirez and a three-run blast to Chris Coghlan -- and seemed to struggle with his command all day. Cook will look to bounce back against the Giants, against whom he is 1-0 with a 2.57 ERA this season.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez had one of his best games of the year in his last outing, limiting the Mets to two runs and four hits in seven innings while receiving no decision. Sanchez walked four, which usually means trouble for him, but he issued two of those free passes with two outs. The game marked only the third time that Sanchez worked at least seven innings this season. Sanchez faced Colorado on July 25, yielding five runs in five innings in an 8-2 loss.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, De La Rosa pitched 5 2/3 solid innings against a hot-hitting Marlins team to pick up his 11th win of the season. The left-hander allowed just one unearned run on seven hits while striking out three to improve to 8-1 over his past 10 starts. De La Rosa has had success against the Giants once this season, picking up a win and holding San Francisco to two runs over 7 1/3 innings on July 25.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez has won two of his three starts despite never having pitched more than five innings. In his last outing, at New York, he surrendered one run and five hits in five innings and owed a 3-1 lead before being removed for a pinch-hitter. Martinez lacks overpowering velocity but has shown that he possesses enough zip on his sinkerball to retire big league hitters. This will be Martinez's first appearance against Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: The young right-hander ran his August record to 4-0 with a brilliant start against Washington on Tuesday, allowing two runs on seven hits over eight innings and striking out five while walking just one. It marked the 21st time in a row in which he'd gone six or more innings, and after striking out Nationals cleanup hitter Adam Dunn three times, No. 4 hitters are 8-for-72 against him this season. He showed good control of his explosive fastball and recovered quickly from his lone hiccup in the second inning to cruise the rest of the way.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum had an uncharacteristic outing in his last start at Cincinnati, allowing five runs in six innings. He struck out two, reflecting his diminished velocity. But the National League's reigning Cy Young Award winner and Major League strikeout leader seemed unconcerned, since he has bounced back from similar outings previously. Oddly, Lincecum has not faced Colorado this year. He's 3-2 with a 4.40 ERA against the Rockies lifetime, including 2-0, 4.18 at Coors Field, where he earned his first big league victory on May 11, 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis continued to show why he was named to the 2009 National League All-Star team in his last start Aug. 19 against Washington, as he moved into a tie for the most victories in the NL with six-plus strong innings in a 5-4 win. He allowed three runs on nine hits, walking one while striking out one. He also helped his own cause at the plate, going 1-for-4 with a double and a run scored. Having allowed one run in seven innings in his previous start, Marquis' re-emergence after nearly a month between wins bodes well for Colorado's continued quest for the playoffs.
away_pitcher_note: Zito's ERA in seven starts since the All-Star break is 2.36 -- better than rotation mates Tim Lincecum (2.65), Matt Cain (2.53) and Jonathan Sanchez (3.54). He's only 3-2 personally in this span, but the Giants have won five of his seven outings. Zito pitched one of his better games of the season on May 3 against Colorado, yielding two hits and walking one in seven innings as the Giants proceeded to win, 1-0, in 10 innings. Among Rockies hitters, Todd Helton (.313, 5-for-16) has had fair success against Zito. But Zito has thrived against Brad Hawpe (.071, 1-for-14), Chris Iannetta (.100, 1-for-10), Clint Barmes (.154, 2-for-13), Garrett Atkins (.182, 4-for-22), Ryan Spilborghs (.188, 3-for-16) and Troy Tulowitzki (.211, 4-for-19).

home_pitcher_note: Hammel has struggled at Coors Field, where he's 2-3 with a 7.02 ERA, but hopes his continued fastball command will help him keep the Dodgers at bay in a critical series that could decide the outcome of the NL West. The right-hander has been trying to integrate a sinker into his repertoire to serve as a complementary pitch with mixed results -- when it's on, he gets grounders; when the sinker doesn't sink, he gets hit. So he's redoubled his efforts to command his four-seam fastball and throw it for first-pitch strikes. That strategy was successful Thursday in Washington, where Hammel allowed a run on three hits over seven innings, never allowing the Nationals to generate any sustained offense.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw had another wild inning last time out against the Cardinals and this time couldn't get out of it, running up his pitch count to 97 and bringing manager Joe Torre's hook after only 3 2/3 innings. He had four walks and a wild pitch. Despite an overpowering fastball, Kershaw is most effective when he pitches to contact and conserves his energy. Kershaw is winless in his past six starts and he's 2-2 with an 8.64 ERA at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: With Aaron Cook on the disabled list with a sore right shoulder, Josh Fogg gets his first start of the season in a critical game against the Dodgers. Fogg has been the long man out of the bullpen for the Rockies since coming up in late May, and he has allowed more than one earned run only one time in 20 appearances this season. Fogg is holding opposing hitters to a .186 average, the best mark among Rockies relievers. Nicknamed "The Dragon Slayer" for his big wins in the 2007 pennant race, Fogg was a non-roster invitee to camp this year and was 3-1 with a 5.80 ERA in eight starts for the Triple-A Sky Sox before being called up in May.
away_pitcher_note: Against the Cubs, Wolf pretty much repeated his performance in Arizona from five days earlier. He again fired a one-hitter through seven innings and was equally effective with the bat, doubling home both runs the Dodgers scored while he was in the game. Wolf's strikeouts were down from 10 to five, but he was more efficient, posting five 1-2-3 innings. The left-hander was lifted for a pinch-hitter after 88 pitches. He's 3-0 with a 1.99 ERA in his past three starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, De La Rosa lacked his put-away slider. He gave up a pair of two-run homers in six innings. He gave up six runs. But he earned a win in a 14-11 game with the Giants on Saturday night. That was a huge step for De La Rosa, who has pitched well more often than not since the latter part of last season but still must overcome a reputation for falling apart when things go wrong early. That certainly wasn't the case Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: He's not even on the 40-man roster yet, but Padilla is expected to be promoted to make his Dodgers debut in the series finale in Denver, replacing injured right-hander Hiroki Kuroda. Padilla hasn't pitched in a Major League game since Aug. 5, as a member of the Rangers. He's allowed six runs in nine innings at Coors Field over his career.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum, affectionately referred to as "The Freak," took a no-hitter into the sixth inning on Sunday against the Rockies, but he failed to closed the door. With the Giants leading, 2-1, he left Seth Smith a hanging changeup that was belted into the right-field seats for a two-run homer. However, the fact that he had an otherwise strong start without his best stuff speaks to how good the reigning National League Cy Young Award winner is. Lincecum is 0-1 in his past four starts and hasn't won since Aug. 1. He will get a chance at revenge on Friday, when the Rockies play at AT&T Park.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez rides a six-game winning streak into his rematch with Tim Lincecum in San Francisco on Friday. Jimenez upstaged Lincecum's no-hit bid at Coors Field on Sunday, throwing eight innings of six-hit ball, his two-run homer to Edgar Renteria standing as the righty's only mistake. He struck out nine and walked two, marking the 22nd consecutive start in which he has completed six innings or more. Jimenez has made nine starts in a row in which he has yielded three runs or fewer.

home_pitcher_note: Zito threw a mixed bag against the Rockies at Coors Field Monday, pitching six innings of three-hit ball without allowing an earned run. He did allow the tying run in the fifth inning, however, and though the run was unearned, Zito walked the leadoff man of the inning and two more, including walking Todd Helton with the bases loaded to tie the game.  He ended up walking six (one intentional) in a game that ultimately saw the Giants walk 13 while giving up 10 hits in 14 innings.  Despite the no-decision in the game the Giants went on to lose, Zito is 3-2 with a 2.08 ERA since the All-Star Break.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis  tried for a Major League-leading 15th win in his last start, but through no fault of his own, he failed to get the win. Marquis pitched eight innings and gave up just one earned run on six hits with five strikeouts against the Giants on Monday. A sinkerballer, he left the ball up to the first three hitters and allowed a run. He then was able to keep the ball down in the zone and left the game tied at 1. Marquis will get another crack against Barry Zito and the Giants Saturday at AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: Cain has gone winless in his last six starts, but don't let that fool you. He has a 2.72 ERA in this span, walking nine and allowing 36 hits in 46 1/3 innings. He's also 6-2 with a 2.28 ERA at home this season. Cain has pitched at least seven innings in all eight of his starts since the All-Star Game, hiking his season total to 177 1/3 innings and putting him just a few outings away from reaching the 200-inning level he covets so much. Cain's 2-1 with a 2.84 ERA in three starts against Colorado this year.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel has been on a roll his last two times out, pitching seven innings of three-hit, one-run ball in Washington and another seven innings of two-run ball in the Rockies extra-inning win against the Dodgers Tuesday.  It was his longest outing of the year at Coors Field, where he has made significant improvements his last three starts.  He has consistently performed better on the road this year, posting a 6-4 record and a 2.88 ERA away from Colorado.  He has one previous start in San Francisco this season, pitching six innings of shutout ball in a game the Rockies went on to lose 1-0 in May.  He has been aggressive in his approach to hitters in his recent starts, leaning on his four-seamer and mixing in his curve and cutter to good effect.

home_pitcher_note: With the Rockies off on Monday, left-hander Jorge De La Rosa will start Tuesday's opener against the Mets, followed by right-handers Ubaldo Jimenez and Jason Marquis. The next time the Rockies will need a starter is next Saturday at home against the D-backs. De La Rosa is 2-0 in seven career games against the Mets, including one start.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off back-to-back quality starts, Pelfrey served up 11 hits and walked five batters in last Wednesday's loss to the Marlins, spoiling his bid to win consecutive decisions for the first time since May 1 and 7. Instead, Pelfrey will begin September on a mission to finish the year with a winning record for the second straight season. That task begins against the Rockies, a team he blanked for 6 1/3 innings earlier this year, and against whom he holds a career 3-1 record and 2.35 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez is coming off two outstanding duels with Giants ace Tim Lincecum, the first a 4-2 victory at home and the second a 2-0 loss at AT&T Park. Jimenez's biggest regret was not spiking a curveball to Pablo Sandoval, who hit a home run. Jimenez is 1-1 with a 3.00 ERA in three starts against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Efficient until his final inning last Thursday, Redding produced his second straight strong outing since returning to the rotation. He struck out five Marlins and walked two, allowing five hits -- though three of them were solo home runs. Redding will look to cut down on the long balls while continuing this burst of success against the Rockies, a team he has faced only in relief this season. Last year, Redding was 1-1 with a 6.55 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis will again be looking to match his career high for wins when he faces the Mets at Coors Field. Marquis pitched decently on the road at San Francisco in his last start, but was done in by a lack of run support and a couple of soft hits that fell in during the Giants' biggest inning. Marquis is 6-4 with a 3.59 ERA at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Misch will make his second big league start since last season with the Giants. He had produced a 0-1 record and 2.89 ERA in 19 appearances (22 innings) in relief with the Mets this season before allowing one earned run in seven innings against the Cubs on Friday. He came with in eight outs of gaining his first big league victory -- in what was his 12th big league start. His has an 0-8 record, and his teams have lost each of his 12 starts. He and John Cummings of the 1993-94 Mariners are the only two big league pitchers who have begun their careers with 12 starts in which their respective teams have lost 12 times. Misch was a starter for most of this season in Triple-A with the Mets' Buffalo affiliate in the International League and the Giants' Fresno team in the Pacific Coast League. His Triple-A work this season includes 18 appearances, five of them starts, that produced a 4-2 record and 3.10 ERA in 52 1/3 innings. He has allowed three home runs in 81 1/3 (big leagues and Triple-A).

home_pitcher_note: Hammel was effective in his last outing, when he held the Giants to four hits and two runs in five innings. Manager Jim Tracy pulled him for Franklin Morales at the first sign of trouble, but Hammel has proved more often than not he's capable of beating such problems. Still he has to be better at home, where he is 2-3 with a 6.47 ERA in 12 games, 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Haren picked up the win in his last start against the Astros last Sunday at Chase Field. The right-hander allowed three runs on seven hits over six innings. In his last two starts, he has allowed five earned runs in 14 innings. Haren was dominant in the season's first half, compiling a 2.01 ERA in 18 starts. The second half has been a different story as he has a 4.50 ERA in nine starts. In three starts against the Rockies this year, he is 2-1 with a 0.90 ERA, and in those 20 innings, he has fanned 24 and walked just two.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies picked up Contreras from the White Sox, for pitching prospect Brandon Hynick, just before Monday's deadline for acquiring players to be eligible for a postseason roster. Contreras went 5-13 with a 5.42 ERA for the White Sox. But Contreras has big-game experience and will be facing NL hitters not familiar with him. Manager Jim Tracy said as long as Contreras spots his fastball properly, he can baffle hitters with his split-finger pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Davis did not get a decision in his last start, which came against the Dodgers last Monday at Dodger Stadium. The left-hander allowed three runs on five hits over six innings in a game the D-backs won, 5-3, in 10 innings. Davis has not won in his last four starts, though he has pitched poorly in only one of those games. In two starts against the Rockies this year, he is 0-2 with a 14.73 ERA. In a July 20 start at Coors Field he lasted just 2 1/3 innings -- his shortest outing of the year -- and gave up eight runs.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa couldn't command his fastball and had a hittable changeup in the first inning of his last start, at home against the Mets. But he grabbed control of his mechanics and gave the Mets absolutely nothing thereafter. De La Rosa held the Mets to no further scoring and four hits in six total innings.
away_pitcher_note: Petit has pitched well for the better part of the past two months. There had been speculation that he would lose his spot in the rotation, but over his last seven starts he has a 3.00 ERA. That number goes down to 1.54 if you remove one start in which he allowed seven runs in just four innings. Last time out against the Dodgers, Petit got a no-decision despite allowing just two earned runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Masterful performances are becoming the norm for Jimenez, who held the Mets to two runs in eight innings during the Rockies' 5-2 victory on Wednesday night. After giving up a solo shot to Jeff Francoeur on a first-pitch breaking ball in the fourth inning, Jimenez was as close to 100 percent as possible in terms of throwing quality pitches the rest of the night. Jimenez is 7-1 with a 2.44 ERA in his past 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last three starts, Bailey is 3-0 with a 1.69 ERA with four earned runs, eight walks and 19 strikeouts over 21 1/3 innings. During Wednesday's 5-3 win over the Pirates, he worked his third consecutive quality start as he pitched 6 1/3 innings with three earned runs and seven hits allowed. He walked three and set another career-high with eight strikeouts. Two of the runs crossed on solo home runs, and Bailey was successful at avoiding any big innings or scoring situations.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis has received little run support in his past three outings, and he couldn't avoid the big inning in his last two, both losses. Marquis is still looking to tie his career high in wins, 15, and he has a maximum of six starts left to try to eclipse the Rockies' record for wins in a season -- 17, shared by Kevin Ritz (1995), Pedro Astacio (1999) and Jeff Francis (2007).
away_pitcher_note: Maloney got his opportunity to start when Justin Lehr was skipped in the rotation because of a sore right groin. Maloney pitched for Double-A Carolina on Thursday, allowing three hits and a run in seven innings. The 25-year-old made four starts for the Reds earlier this year but spent most of the season with Triple-A Louisville. He was 9-9 with a 3.08 ERA in 23 starts for the Bats. Maloney had 130 strikeouts to 26 walks in 150 innings with Louisville.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel left his last start, on Friday night, with a 4-2 deficit against the D-Backs and starter Dan Haren. But he pitched around base traffic and a couple of defensive mistakes and showed composure. Hammel has pitched solidly in his last two starts and has shown that the playoff race isn't a problem for him. He experienced a taste of it last year with the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo turned in his eighth consecutive quality start in his last outing, limiting the Braves to one run and six hits in seven innings on Friday in Atlanta. He struck out four and walked three, throwing 99 pitches. The run came on a sixth-inning homer by Nate McLouth. Arroyo has pitched in bad luck at times during his streak of quality starts, going just 2-3. He has made 28 starts and he has gone at least six innings and allowed three or fewer runs in 18 of them. Arroyo had a no-decision in a start against Colorado on Aug. 2, allowing three runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Contreras is with a new team in a new league, but his success rate is easy to figure. When Contreras commands his fastball and gets ahead in the count, he's capable of nights like Saturday, when he won his Rockies debut by holding the D-backs to one run on eight hits in 6 2/3 innings. When he doesn't get early strikes, performances like those that led to a 5-13 record and 5.42 ERA with the White Sox can happen. Contreras believes a bullpen session with Rockies pitching coach Bob Apodaca before his debut start with the club might have unlocked some success.
away_pitcher_note: Wells has made three starts for Cincinnati and the Reds have won them all. After two no-decisions, he got his first win in the Majors as a starter since 2007 by beating Atlanta on Saturday. He allowed just one hit over six innings, although he struggled at times with his control. Wells walked four and hit a batter. He made 97 pitchers, with 46 of them balls and 51 strikes. Wells has allowed just three hits over 11 innings in his past two starts, walking eight. He began the 2008 season with Colorado before going on the DL with a blood clot and then being released in August.

home_pitcher_note: This spot would have normally gone to rookie Mat Latos, but the Padres have shut him down after he threw 123 innings this season. So the team will bump everyone back a day to get them extra rest and give this start to long reliever Mujica, who nearly got a spot start earlier this season before Clayton Richard arrived to take it. The team will, obviously, need some relief help, which could mean the Major League debut of left-hander Cesar Ramos, a possibility to follow Mujica to the mound.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa has more wins than any pitcher since June 1, so it could be said his turnaround is a complete one. But De La Rosa also has been spending time looking at film of his last start, a win but a rough performance. He lasted just five innings of a 13-5 victory over the D-backs. He gave up just two hits, but walked six. There were some pitches that were close, and he reacted to some calls in the fifth inning, but he said the real problem was he was slightly off-kilter. De La Rosa hasn't had the best of luck against the Padres this season -- 0-1, 5.06 ERA in three starts. Of course, all of those were in April and May, before he caught fire.

home_pitcher_note: Stauffer was very good in his last start against the Dodgers, on Sunday, allowing one earned run in 6 2/3 innings. He has gone 6 2/3 innings in each of last two starts after going five innings in each of his previous five. Against the Dodgers, Stauffer got 11 ground-ball outs and walked one. "Stauffer has been pretty steady since he joined the rotation," Padres manager Bud Black said.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers began the year in standout fashion at Double-A Tulsa, going 8-2 with a 2.48 ERA in 15 starts, with 83 strikeouts against 19 walks in 94 1/3 innings. His numbers were not nearly as impressive in 12 games, including 11 starts, at Triple-A Colorado Springs. There were five extremely bad games in which he gave up 31 earned runs in 20 2/3 innings. The rest were decent or better. Rogers, 24, played shortstop for three years in the Rockies' chain before moving to the mound in 2006.

home_pitcher_note: Richard had a rough time in his last start against the Giants on Monday, allowing six runs on eight hits over four innings, including five runs in the third inning, when Juan Uribe and Edgar Renteria hit consecutive home runs. "The pitches that were hit hard were fastballs. I left some over the plate and they made the most of them," Richard said. "Really, it was just a couple of mistakes." Richard didn't have much in the way of secondary pitches against the Giants and couldn't bury his sinker nearly enough to avoid trouble.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis held the Reds to one run and four hits in 7 1/3 innings and matched a season high with seven strikeouts in a 3-1 victory on Tuesday night. In the victory, Marquis' signature sinker was not consistent, but he had extreme downward tilt on the slider and he faced Reds hitters who couldn't make the adjustment. The Padres haven't had much luck with him, either. He is 2-0 with a 0.56 ERA in two starts against them this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum was scratched last Tuesday with back spasms in his lower left side. But he recovered relatively quickly and resumed throwing Friday. The prolonged rest might actually help Lincecum, who was leading the National League with 200 1/3 innings pitched at the time of his injury. Lincecum last faced Colorado on Aug. 28 and excelled, allowing four hits in eight shutout innings at AT&T Park.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel has become the guy who can't get a decision. But more often than not these days he is keeping the team in games against talented opposing starters. His last start was arguably his best of the year. He held the Reds to one hit going into the eighth, and finished with three hits and two runs against in 7 1/3 innings. Using his four-seam fastball to get ahead of hitters, Hammel matched a career high with eight strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: After recording a 1.92 ERA in his first nine starts following the All-Star break, Zito has yielded five runs in nine innings over his last two outings. He still has a winning record (4-3) in the second half. He owns a microscopic 0.42 ERA in three starts against the Rockies this year, having permitted them one earned run and 13 hits in 21 1/3 innings. Zito is 5-5 with a 3.80 ERA in 14 starts at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez pitched through a left hamstring strain for the final half of his six innings in his last start, a no-decision in the Rockies' 4-3 victory over the Reds. Jimenez threw a bullpen session on Thursday and reported feeling good enough to pitch on his regular turn, Saturday against the Padres. However, manager Jim Tracy moved him so that he'll have more rest and face the Giants. Down the road, the move puts Jimenez in position to start the first game of the final series of the year, on the road against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Cain has a long history with the Rockies. He faced them in his Major League debut on Aug. 29, 2005, and has faced them 17 times, more than he has confronted any other team except San Diego (also 17). The Giants have won three of Cain's four starts against Colorado this year; his personal record in those games is 2-1. His last outing against the Rockies was a no-decision on Aug. 30 in which he surrendered four runs in six innings and yielded back-to-back homers to Todd Helton and Troy Tulowitzki.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had one blemish in his start on Friday in San Diego, issuing a bases-loaded walk to Oscar Salazar in the first inning, but he allowed little else. The left-hander gave up five hits over seven innings and collected eight strikeouts while walking four batters. He did not factor into the decision as the club rallied in the ninth to earn a comeback win. De La Rosa was bumped up two days and takes the place of Jose Contreras, who is nursing a strained quadriceps, but will make the start on normal rest.

home_pitcher_note: Mulvey's first Major League start did not go as he'd hoped. The right-hander allowed six runs on 11 hits in just four innings against the Brewers at Chase Field. Mulvey is taking the place of Yusmeiro Petit in the rotation likely for the rest of the season. The club wants to get a look at the right-hander acquired in the deal that sent Jon Rauch to the Twins. Mulvey is no stranger to being traded. A second-round pick by the Mets in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft, he was dealt to the Twins as part of the Johan Santana deal. Mulvey, who was 5-8 with a 3.93 ERA in 24 starts for Triple-A Rochester this year and has appeared in two games in relief for the D-backs since joining the team on Sept. 1. He made his big league debut on July 20 with the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis faltered against a team he had handled well this season when he allowed five runs to San Diego on Sunday as the Rockies fell 6-3 in the series finale.  In his previous two starts against the Padres, Marquis yielded just one run over 16 innings, but San Diego touched him for three runs in the decisive sixth after he walked Everth Cabrera with the bases loaded, one of three unintentional walks in the inning.  After having his start bumped up one day but still pitching on normal rest, Marquis faces an Arizona team that scored six runs against him in a loss on April 20.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer was on track to win his 10th game last time out against the Brewers, but the bullpen could not come through for him. The right-hander allowed one run on three hits over six innings and left with a 2-1 lead. The Brewers scored four runs against the bullpen in the seventh and went on to win 5-3. Scherzer did not have his best slider but did have a better feel for his changeup as the game went along. Not getting a lot of first-pitch strikes caused Scherzer's pitch count to rise early and prevented him from pitching deeper into the game.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel has been the Rockies' hard-luck starter. Most of the time, he's pitched well and helped the Rockies win but wasn't figuring in many decisions. In his last start, however, he got the bad luck of facing the Giants with a motivated Tim Lincecum on the mound. He gave up three runs in a second inning that featured two soft singles and yielded four runs today, but that was way too many against Lincecum. Hammel still needs two wins to give the Rockies five starters in double figures this season.

home_pitcher_note: Haren went eight strong innings in beating the Padres, 4-2. It was his 30th start of the season. He allowed five hits, three of which came in the fourth inning when he gave up the only two runs. He walked one and struck out four and got 11 ground-ball outs. He retired the last eight batters he faced. Haren has the best strikeout-to-walk ratio in the Majors. This will be his third start against the Giants. He lost a 2-0 game on April 17 in which he gave up one run in six innings and he got a no-decision in a 5-4 loss to the Giants on Aug. 25. He has had five straight quality starts, but has just two wins to show for it along with three no-decisions and one loss.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies went into Jimenez's last start, Tuesday at San Francisco, hoping he would prove once and for all that he's an ace. But Jimenez gave up seven runs, six earned, in 2 2/3 innings -- by far his worst start of the season. Who knows what would have happened had third baseman Garrett Atkins not flubbed a grounder and negated a possible inning-ending double play? Still, Jimenez searched for fastball command and didn't find it until it was too late. Now Jimenez faces the D-backs, a familiar opponent that hacks at his fastball. He'll have to read swings quickly and adjust accordingly.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa shut down the Giants on three hits in eight scoreless innings while pitching the best game of his career. In the sixth inning, De La Rosa faced men at second and third, then struck out the top three hitters in the Giants' order. He finished with a fanning of Pablo Sandoval after an eight-pitch at-bat. De La Rosa has gone 15-3 after an 0-6 start.
away_pitcher_note: Mujica is scheduled to make his third start after pitching in 63 games as a reliver. In his last start, on Sept. 16 against the D-backs, Mujica tossed 4 2/3 innings and allowed two runs on six hits as San Diego won, 6-5. He recorded five strikeouts and did not issue a walk.

home_pitcher_note: The good news is Marquis seems to have corrected the mechanical problems that had been bothering him last month. But he's hurting himself with his pitch selection. In his last start, Friday against the D-backs, he did Brandon Allen a favor by giving him a slider -- when fastballs were working. Allen knocked it for a key home run, and Marquis finished with a no-decision in a game the Rockies lost. Marquis lost his previous game to the Padres, with pitch selection being a problem on multiple occasions.
away_pitcher_note: Entering Stauffer's last start, the Padres had won each of his previous four outings. After allowing only one run in six-plus innings during each of his past three games, Stauffer allowed three runs on four hits and four walks in three innings during a 5-1 loss to the Pirates on Friday. He just didn't have it, as he labored through a 40-pitch first inning.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel has a shot to join Jorge De La Rosa, Ubaldo Jimenez, Jason Marquis and Aaron Cook as Rockies starters to post a double-digit win total this season. Hammel should have done it before now, considering his mostly solid work. He earned the elusive ninth win Saturday at Arizona. He held the D-backs to three runs and four hits in seven innings. The game was close until the late innings, when the Rockies pulled away for a 10-4 victory.
away_pitcher_note: Richard will be making his 11th start since being acquired from the Chicago White Sox. In his last start, Richard and Pittsburgh right-hander Ross Ohlendorf hooked up for a tight pitchers' duel, but neither was around for the decision in a 2-1 San Diego victory at PNC Park on Saturday. Richard pitched six innings and allowed one unearned run on four hits in the start.

home_pitcher_note: It'll be Cook's first appearance since Aug. 21, when he left a start against the Giants early with soreness in his right shoulder. Manager Jim Tracy said Cook will be watched closely and kept at a pitch count of 60-70. Tracy said there is also a chance right-hander Jose Contreras (1-0, 1.86 in two starts with the Rockies, after 5-13, 5.42 with the White Sox) can pitch in relief. Cook will be looking to re-establish himself as a starter for the Rockies' likely playoff trip.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter won't take anything off over his final two starts, but he's pretty much tuning up at this point. He's on schedule to start the Cardinals' playoff opener, so the most important things are to stay sharp and to stay healthy. There's little question about the first, as he pitched eight shutout innings his last time out. And so far, there's been no question about the second since May. He's also in the running for what would be his second Cy Young Award.

home_pitcher_note: After his worst start of the season against the Giants, Jimenez returned Sunday to shut down the D-backs. He gave up four hits and two walks in the first two innings, but just one run. After that, he gave up just two more hits, and he left the mound with eight strikeouts in seven innings. Like many ace-type performers, Jimenez is looking like a pitcher opponents must get to early or risk being dominated.
away_pitcher_note: This is Wainwright in a nutshell: he pitched seven strong innings his last time out, struck out 10, allowed two earned runs -- and was frustrated with his performance. That's because his teammates gave him a lead, and he didn't bring it home. Never mind that he was good enough to win on most other nights. That's the competitive nature that teammates love in Wainwright, and it should serve him well in a tough environment in Denver.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had one of his worst outings of the year Tuesday against the Padres, but it was made palatable by the fact that the Rockies ultimately won the game, making them 20-11 in games he's started.  De La Rosa had trouble throwing strikes, lasting only 2 1/3 innings while giving up six runs on six hits and three walks.  He had trouble executing a "put-away" pitch after getting ahead of hitters in the first inning, getting two outs on five pitches to open the game, then yielding a walk, a single, and a triple to fall behind.  In the third inning, he struggled to get the ball over the plate early in counts, and ultimately let his frustration get the best of him.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse is coming off his most encouraging start in six weeks, and not a day too soon. He'll try to follow it up in another tough place for pitchers, Coors Field. Lohse now has two starts left to state his case for a place in the Cardinals' playoff rotation. The irony, of course, is that he can't afford to think in those terms. He has to make sure he's healthy and his mechanics are in order, and hope the rest works out.

home_pitcher_note: Whether it's pitch selection, mechanics or plain old execution, Marquis is struggling these days. He has a 6.49 ERA in his last six starts, during which the Rockies are 1-5, and has given up five earned runs in four of those. Before his last start, when he gave up six runs (five earned) in 4 2/3 innings against the Padres, manager Jim Tracy said Marquis was over analyzing, anticipating adjustments by hitters. The manager wants him to get back to the sinker that was responsible for his success through three-quarters of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Whomever starts this game will also get the Brewers' season finale, and an off-day could allow manager Ken Macha to shuffle the rotation to make Jeff Suppan the choice. But Narveson may have pitched his way into that honor with 5 2/3 outstanding innings against the Cubs on Wednesday, allowing only three hits, including a solo homer to opposing starter Jeff Samardzija. Narveson is trying to make his case for a job next season, and the Brewers may want to take the opportunity to see him as much as possible.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel saw another strong start go for naught Thursday, as he lasted 6 1/3 innings and yielded two runs on six hits, striking out six while walking none. The Rockies bullpen let in the tying run in the seventh and eventually lost the game when the go-ahead runs scored in the eighth. It was Hammel's fifth no-decision in his last seven starts, and his fifth quality outing in the span. He's gone at least six innings in his last five starts, and in 10 of his last 11 starts, he's allowed three runs or less, earning his stripes as one of the club's most dependable starters in the second half of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan has been much better on the road this season (4-3, 3.56 ERA in 13 starts) than at Miller Park, and he's 3-0 with a 3.75 ERA in four career starts at Coors Field. He had another poor start at home on Thursday, when he surrendered seven earned runs and a season-high 12 hits in a loss to the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Any fears that five weeks off because of a shoulder injury would make Cook ineffective proved unwarranted. Cook held the Cardinals scoreless on four hits in five innings (76 pitches) Friday night. He also forced 12 groundball outs. It was one of those games when Cook could stay with his sinker almost exclusively. He'll be asked to throw more pitches, and it will be a test if he has to adjust. But the Rockies are counting on Cook in the season's final days and, they hope, in the playoffs.
away_pitcher_note: Parra missed three starts with a stiff neck but looked no worse for the wear on Friday, when he worked seven innings and limited the Phillies to two runs, one of them unearned and the other earned only because of a scoring change. Ryan Howard's two-run single was originally ruled an error on Brewers first baseman Prince Fielder and one RBI, but it was later switched to a base hit. Parra matched his season high with eight strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf will probably get this start, which would put him in line to start Game 1 of the playoffs. Wolf pitched the club's postseason clincher in Pittsburgh and was in position to win after allowing two runs in 6 1/3 innings, but the bullpen let it get away for his 16th no-decision. Still, he's been the most consistent starter on the staff this year and a workhorse with 209 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez pitched seven strong innings against Adam Wainwright and the Cardinals Saturday night, taking a tie game into his final inning on the hill before yielding a leadoff solo homer that proved to be the Cardinals winning run in their division-clinching victory. He struggled in the first inning, yielding three runs on two walks and two soft hits, and he is working to be more effective out of the gate.  He allowed four runs on six hits and three walks, and once he found his fastball command he retired 10 of 11 batters faced after the first inning, and 16-of-20 into the seventh. His seven strikeouts came at big moments. He struck out the side in the fourth, which allowed the Rockies to tie the game in the bottom of the inning.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw made a decent return to the rotation Sunday after missing three weeks with a separation of his non-throwing shoulder, but he'll need to get deeper than four innings to convince the staff he's ready for prime-time playoff responsibilities. He seems healthy enough, but he struggled with command of his slider against the Pirates. Pitch count is always the key for him.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies needed De La Rosa on Sunday. Although he wasn't sharp and faced nearly constant traffic in five innings, he finished with eight strikeouts and made enough pitches at key times -- pitching out of bases-loaded situations twice -- to win. He needs one more victory to match the club record of 17, held by Jeff Francis (2007), Pedro Astacio (1999) and Kevin Ritz (1995).

home_pitcher_note: Dodgers manager Joe Torre announced on Friday that Padilla would start the season finale for the Dodgers. Padilla's start against the Rockies probably will be an audition for what kind of role he'll have on the Dodgers postseason staff. If Padilla struggles, he could be relegated to the bullpen for the NLDS, while a good outing could make him a viable option at starter. Padilla's two most recent starts for the Dodgers didn't go well. He gave up four runs on eight hits in five innings on Sept. 18 against the Giants, and he gave up four more runs in five innings on Sept. 24 against the Nationals. On Wednesday in San Diego, Padilla threw two scoreless innings of relief.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis wasn't quite dominant Tuesday night at Coors Field, but he battled his way out of jams and held on for six quality innings of two run ball, leaving with a lead after scattering six hits and four walks. Fourteen of his 18 outs came on groundballs, a great indication that his sinker was in fine form.  He used it with more and more confidence in the game, going to it early in counts and challenging hitters with it.  He felt as comfortable as he's felt in some time, bringing some fine-tuned mechanics and a rejuvenated mental approach to the game. He faced big bases-loaded jams, walking in one run but getting groundout double plays in each case to escape or minimize the damage and set up the Rockies for a critical win.

home_pitcher_note: Lee, the reigning American League Cy Young Award winner, went 7-4 with a 3.39 ERA in the 12 starts he made after the Phillies acquired him from the Indians on July 29. The 31-year-old southpaw registered nine strikeouts and limited the Rockies to one run over seven innings on Aug. 6.
away_pitcher_note: On Friday night, with the Rockies still in position to win the National League West, Jimenez turned in a gem, holding the Dodgers to one run and two hits in six innings of a 4-3 victory. After the All-Star break this season, Jimenez went 9-3 with a 3.08 ERA. He's capable of going into the 120-pitch range and still being effective. In two career regular-season starts, Jimenez is 0-1 with an 8.10 ERA. But in Game 2 of the 2007 NLDS at Citizen Bank Park, Jimenez shut the Phils down -- 6 1/3 innings, one run, three hits. Although he didn't figure in the decision, the Rockies won.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed three hits, three runs and two walks in three innings Saturday against the Marlins. Hamels finished the season 10-11 with a 4.32 ERA, and is 0-2 with a 7.02 ERA in his last three starts. But Hamels proved himself to be a big-game pitcher last postseason, when he went 4-0 with a 1.80 ERA in five starts to earn World Series and NL Championship Series MVP honors. "Now I have to put it together, but this is the time where everything really matters and really counts," Hamels said.
away_pitcher_note: Cook has held opponents to one run in 13 innings in two starts after missing five weeks with a sore shoulder. Both of those games were at Coors Field, where an effective sinker is a great weapon. That's perfect preparation for Citizens Bank Park and its bandbox-tight dimensions. Last time Cook pitched at Citizens Bank Park, he gave up three runs on seven hits in five innings and had to leave because he aggravated a turf-toe problem. He is 1-1 with a 3.75 ERA in two starts at CBP.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel battled inconsistency early in the season but turned into a threat to win against high-quality lineups when he decided to eliminate a sinker and go with his four-seam fastball. The sinker was a good idea, considering that balls hit in the air at Coors Field can be dangerous. However, he didn't control it as well as the four-seamer, so he went with what was working for him. Of late, Hammel has been efficient in early innings. That was the improvement he needed to make to last longer in games. There is one red flag, though, as the Rockies head into Game 3. he was 3-3 with a 5.63 ERA in 16 regular-season starts at Coors Field, as opposed to 7-5, 3.13 on the road. Nonetheless, his strong second-half performance led manager Jim Tracy to pick him over Jason Marquis for the start.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez went 5-1 with a 3.63 ERA in nine starts for the Phillies. He is 2-3 with a 4.31 ERA in 10 career appearances against the Rockies. The 37-year-old right-hander is 6-2 with a 3.40 ERA in 13 postseason games, 11 of them starts. That includes a 4-0 record and 2.84 ERA in Division Series games. He last pitched in the postseason in Game 3 of the 2004 World Series, throwing seven shutout innings in Boston's 4-1 win over the Cardinals. Martinez has pitched once since Sept. 19, going four innings against the Astros on Sept. 30. He allowed three runs on six hits.

away_pitcher_note: The Game 3 start that was originally supposed to go to Pedro Martinez is now Happ's, after the originally scheduled game for Saturday was bumped back to Sunday due to wintry conditions in Colorado. Happ, who will be making his first postseason start, was struck on the left leg with a line drive during a seventh-inning relief appearance during Game 2 on Thursday.  The rookie left-hander threw just four pitches during the outing and has since said that his leg isn't bothering him.  One of the leading candidates to be named the National League's Rookie of the Year, Happ went 10-4 with a 2.99 ERA in the 23 starts that he made this year.  He tossed a four-hit shutout against the Rockies on Aug. 5 at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez was strong for nearly four innings in Game 1, until he started missing up in the zone and over the plate. He gave up five runs in five innings and took a 5-1 loss. It's possible that if the Rockies had made the most of their chances in the first two innings, he'd have been in better position. But Jimenez did not pitch to his regular-season standards, when he went six innings in 29 of his 33 starts. He was 8-5 with a 3.4 ERA in 15 starts at Coors Field this season.
away_pitcher_note: While making his first career postseason appearance in Game 1 at Citizens Bank Park on Wednesday afternoon, Lee fell one out shy of completing a shutout.  The reigning American League Cy Young Award winner also limited the Rockies to one run and six hits in seven innings on Aug. 6.   Now Lee will be asked to conquer the challenge that will be presented as he pitches in Coors Field for the first time in his career. During Wednesday's dominant effort, the 31-year-old left-hander had retired 16 straight batters before surrendering a two-out seventh-inning double. The frigid conditions that were present this weekend are supposed to disappear before Monday, when game-time temperature is projected to be in the low 50s.

home_pitcher_note: Fister, the Mariners' No. 5 starter, is making his fourth and final start of Spring Training.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa, who won 16 games during the 2009 season, has allowed six runs -- five earned -- over 25 innings this spring.

home_pitcher_note: Last year, Brewers manager Ken Macha held his young right-hander for Game 2 of the regular season. This time, Macha figures that the 24-year-old Gallardo is ready for the bright lights of Opening Day. He was the obvious choice after going 13-12 with a 3.73 ERA and 204 strikeouts in 30 starts last season before the Brewers shut him down. It was the fifth 200-plus strikeout season in club history, and Gallardo ranked third in the National League with a .219 opponents' batting average.  The Brewers would love to see Gallardo get off to another hot start; he was the team's pitcher of the month last April after beginning the season 3-1 with a 2.86 ERA in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Last season, as Jimenez's arsenal of power pitches and competitive spirit grew, manager Jim Tracy recognized him as a potential staff ace. Jimenez struck out 158 against 85 walks last year. His task this year will be to increase his efficiency and go beyond the 218 innings he tallied last year. Jimenez's experience against the Brewers is scant -- 1-0, 2.77 ERA in two starts. His one start at Miller Park was stellar, however. He went seven scoreless innings, gave up three hits, struck out seven and walked five for the win in the Rockies' 4-3 victory on July 7, 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf's Brewers debut will come against a team he's handled well in his career. He was 1-1 with a 2.96 ERA against Colorado last season for the Dodgers and, in 14 career starts, Wolf is 5-3 with a 4.02 ERA against Colorado. The Brewers signed Wolf during baseball's Winter Meetings to a three-year contract and hope he'll provide a left-handed foil to right-handed ace Yovani Gallardo atop the starting rotation. Gallardo led the Brewers last season with 17 quality starts (six or more innings with three or fewer earned runs). Wolf put together 24 such starts, tying Cliff Lee for the most of any left-hander in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: This start originally belonged to Jeff Francis, but the Rockies transferred the left-hander to the 15-day disabled list on Saturday morning due to shoulder soreness, making room for Smith in the rotation. Smith, who had been lined up for a spot in the Rockies' bullpen, pitched admirably during Cactus League play, striking out 18 batters and walking six over 18 innings in which he surrendered just three runs.

home_pitcher_note: Davis returns to Milwaukee after a three-year stint with the Arizona Diamondbacks. He resuscitated his career with the Brewers from 2003-06, and Milwaukee GM Doug Melvin was interested in a reunion because of Davis' durability. He's topped 200 innings in four of the past six seasons and made at least 33 starts in five of those six. The exception was 2008, when Davis underwent treatment for thyroid cancer. He is 19-14 with a 3.37 ERA in 58 career starts at Miller Park and has limited opponents to a .229 average there.
away_pitcher_note: When Cook and the Brewers last saw one another, it was a happy occasion. Cook pitched eight innings and held the Brewers to four hits and one run in eight innings of a 9-2 victory at Coors Field last Oct. 1, as the Rockies clinched a playoff berth. Cook went through a brief crisis when he lost the release point on his sinking fastball, but one afternoon on a Minor League field he regained his form and all was fine in Rockies Nation. Cook is 6-2 with a 3.02 ERA in 10 career games (nine starts) against the Brewers, and 2-1 with a 3.00 ERA in five starts at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: The 29-year-old left-hander gets the start in Colorado's home opener, facing a Padres team against which he is 0-2 with a 5.94 ERA in his career. Last year at Coors Field, De La Rosa was 10-6 with a 5.21 ERA in 19 games, 18 of them starts. San Diego slugger Adrian Gonzalez is 4-for-15 lifetime vs. De La Rosa, with one home run and five strikeouts. Padres outfielder Scott Hairston is 4-for-7 with two homers and six RBIs.
away_pitcher_note: Richard, the former University of Michigan quarterback, got off to a rough start in spring, as he struggled with fastball command. But he pitched better as spring wore on and showed the same promise the team saw from him when he won five games after being acquired in July in the deal for Jake Peavy. Richard, when he's pitching well, gets a lot of ground balls. Walks can be a concern for him but he's working to cut those down. He's been  working on using his curveball more which would be a nice compliment to his fastball that has a sinking action to it.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel went 10-8 with a 4.33 ERA last year, his first full season in a starting rotation after bouncing between starting and relief work with the Rays. Hammel attacked the strike zone and had an effective fastball and curve early in Spring Training. His numbers were inflated by some bad innings toward the end of camp, but his early Cactus League work served as evidence of what's possible. Hammel had four no-decisions and a 5.79 ERA in five starts against the Padres last season.
away_pitcher_note: Scouts in Spring Training raved about Latos as a pitcher who potentially has the best stuff on the staff. Latos, who is 22, won four games in his Major League debut with the Padres last season after making the jump from low Single-A. He has electric stuff and had an ERA under 2.00 for most of the spring. The Padres have cleaned up a few things with his mechanics to streamline his delivery. He's taken well to everything the team has asked him to do. Latos is using a curveball more and, even though he throws in the mid-90s, doesn't mind pitching to contact.  The Padres will again monitor his innings. He'll likely stay in the 150-160 innings range.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez displayed a fastball that ranged from 96 to 99 mph and had an effective breaking ball in his first start, a 5-3 road victory over the Brewers. Jimenez struck out six and gave up eight hits and one walk against the Brewers, never looking as if he was descending into trouble. Last season, Jimenez made 33 starts but somehow his turn left him with just one start against the Padres (1-0, 3.86 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: Garland needed 86 pitches to get through four innings in an Opening Day loss to the D-backs. He allowed six runs, though only two were earned as the Padres defense committed two errors behind him early in the game. Garland struggled with his curveball, allowing a home run over the wall to Mark Reynolds on one and then an inside-the-park home run to Stephen Drew on another. All told, Garland allowed five hits and two walks with four strikeouts against one of two teams he pitched for in 2009 (the Dodgers being the other).

home_pitcher_note: In his first start since Sept. 27, 2008, while pitching for the Athletics, Smith, who missed last season with various nagging ailments, gave up five runs on four hits (two of them homers) in five innings of a 7-5 road loss to the Brewers. with the exception of three pitches (resulting in two homers and a double), Smith did a reasonable job of hitting his locations, considering how long he had been inactive.
away_pitcher_note: Maine was responsible for one of the two poor starts during the first turn of the Mets rotation. Pitching with a diminished fastball, he needed 92 pitches to achieve 15 outs against the Marlins. And by the point he had thrown his last final pitch, he had allowed eight hits, including two home runs. Maine attributed his performance to poor location of his fastball, but others saw a lack of velocity. He hasn't faced them since June 20, 2008 when he beat them at Coors Field. None of the Rockies have had much exposure to Maine. Todd Helton and Miguel Olivo have eight at-bats each. As was the case last season, Maine was more effective against left-handed hitters than he was against right-handed in his first start.

home_pitcher_note: Cook gave up five runs, four earned, in 5 1/3 innings in a loss to the Brewers in the final game of the season-opening, three-game set. Cook had his sinker working early and threw some effective curveballs. His biggest issue as the game progressed was he got ahead of hitters early in counts but allowed them to extend at-bats. More consistency would put him deeper in games. Cook did not face the Mets last season.
away_pitcher_note: Moved to the third spot in the rotation -- the Mets didn't want John Maine and Ollie Perez next to each other for fear of overworking the bullpen -- Niese responded with a pretty good performance. He appeared quite comfortable as he completed six innings, allowing eight hits, two walks and three runs. The Rockies are one of the eight teams Niese has faced in his brief career. They beat him in the second game of a double header at Citi Field July 30, scoring four runs in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa started 2010 with a dominant one-hit, nine-strikeout performance over seven innings Friday in the home opener, a 9-0 victory over the Padres. De La Rosa is one of those pitchers who, when he's on, you start speaking in whispered tones when the zero in the hit column lasts awhile. All nine strikeouts were on changeups, but pitching coach Bob Apodaca noted, "They were all set up by something early, whether the slider early or definitely fastballs. He was ahead in the count the vast majority of the game." De La Rosa is 3-0 with a 3.71 ERA in eight career games, but just two starts, against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: In his season debut against Washington, Pelfrey displayed all the reasons why the Mets still believe in him (two runs on four hits in six innings) and all the reasons why they remain so frustrated with him (four walks). In the end, it was a victory for Pelfrey -- albeit against a second-rate offense. He'll face a greater test against the Rockies, who battered him for seven runs in four innings in his last trip to Coors Field last September. Pelfrey is 3-2 in five career starts against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe proved to be an escape artist on Saturday night, when he issued a career-high seven walks and still allowed just one run in six innings against the Giants.  The veteran sinkerballer has won his first two starts despite the fact that he hasn't shown the same consistent command that he possessed during Spring Training, when he displayed the delivery that he refined during the offseason. While opponents have compiled a .380 on-base percentage against him through two starts, they have also been limited to a .225 batting average. During his last nine starts last year, the veteran hurler allowed opponents to compile a .366 batting average and .413 on-base percentage. He is 3-1 with a 1.59 ERA in his past four starts against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel had one bad inning in which he gave up four runs Saturday night, but he pitched seven innings and received a no-decision in the Rockies' 5-4, 14-inning loss to the Padres at Coors Field. That inning featured a momentary loss of fastball command, but his fastball and slider worked the rest of the time. Hammel threw strikes on 60 of his 100 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Kawakami experienced some seventh-inning misfortunes while constructing one of the better starts of his career during Sunday's season debut against the Giants. The Japanese hurler was perfect through the first three innings and held a 2-1 lead before Mark DeRosa's two-out, sixth-inning single led to a throwing error that plated a pair of runs. Utilizing his two-seam fastball to induce 11 ground outs, Kawakami needed just 65 pitches to complete the six-inning effort. Last year, high pitch counts led him to pitch into the seventh inning in just six of his 25 starts.  Kawakami, who has posted a 3.40 ERA in his past 22 starts, will be making his first career appearance against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez faces a high standard in each outing. He went six innings and gave up two runs, one earned, in Sunday's 4-2 victory over the Padres at home, but the question is could he have gone farther. Actually, Jimenez was in shape to pitch deeper in the game until losing his location to several batters in the sixth. Still, Jimenez, who reached 100 mph early in the game, proved that he's hard to beat, even when he's not at his most efficient. He has 13 strikeouts in 12 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off the worst start of his young career, Jurrjens will look to rebound and also prove that the drop in velocity that he displayed on Monday in San Diego wasn't a sign that he's still experiencing problems with the right shoulder that plagued him at the beginning of Spring Training. While allowing a career-high eight earned runs in 3 1/3 innings against the Padres, Jurrjens struggled to command a fastball that was routinely clocked around 87-88 mph, 3-4 mph lower than normal. The 24-year-old right-hander, who had allowed two earned runs or less in 27 of his previous 35 starts, has since thrown a pain-free bullpen session. Jurrjens went 2-0 with a 2.08 ERA in two starts against the Rockies last year.
away_pitcher_note: Smith pitched his best game in over a year to win the series opener against the Mets in Coors Field Tuesday.  Having spent all of 2009 in the Rockies' Minor League system after coming to Colorado in the Matt Holiday trade, Smith earned his first win since his 2008 rookie campaign with the A's. He allowed six hits and two walks over seven innings while striking out eight, and raised his game from "competitive" in his first start of the season to "dominant" in the follow-up.  He was aggressive in the strike zone and he was able to locate all of his pitches, enabling him to execute his game plan and build a foundation for his next start.

home_pitcher_note: Last Wednesday, the Nats gave Stammen a 3-0 lead off starter Kyle Kendrick after one inning, but the Phils would come right back and take a 4-3 lead. Ryan Howard highlighted the scoring with a two-run single. Stammen gave up seven runs in the game and lasted 1 1/3 innings. Stammen didn't have any excuse for his disappointing outing. But he continues to have problems with his breaking pitches. He couldn't get them to work in his last start against Philadelphia at Nationals Park.

Olsen started for the Nationals on Thursday and kept them in the ballgame against the Phillies. He was solid during the first five innings, allowing just one run. But things started to unravel in the sixth. With the game tied at 1 and a runner on first with two outs, Olsen had problems throwing strikes. Olsen walked Jayson Werth and Raul Ibanez to load the bases. Juan Castro came to the plate and singled to right to drive in Placido Polanco and Werth. Olsen left the game in favor of Tyler Clippard. After Carlos Ruiz was walked intentionally, Clippard walked Greg Dobbs to force home Ibanez and make it a 4-1 game. Olsen pitched 5 2/3 innings and gave up four runs on five hits.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching one of the best games of his career in Colorado's home opener, a seven-inning, one-hit shutout, De La Rosa had one of his worst outings in almost a year Thursday, falling to the Mets, 5-0.  His 17-3 record since June 1, 2009, entering Thursday's game was a product, in part, of his pinpoint command.  His command was elusive, to say the least, against the Mets. He walked five and threw two wild pitches, all contributing to run-scoring rallies.  While yielding eight hits and five runs (four earned) over six innings, De La Rosa kept the game from getting out of hand, bailing his team out of jams while minimizing the damage on a day when none of his pitches were working for him.

home_pitcher_note: On Friday, Lannan had his best start of the season, pitching seven innings and giving up two runs on seven hits, but didn't figure in the decision in a 5-3 victory over the Brewers. Lannan gave up a solo homer to Casey McGehee in the second and an RBI single to Corey Hart in the fifth, but nothing else.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel had no fastball command and no secondary pitches in his last start. The result was a seven-run, eight-hit effort in 1 2/3 innings against the Braves. As a result, a decent offensive performance went to waste and the Rockies lost, 9-5. But he can rebound. Last year, Hammel gave up five runs and seven hits in 1 1/3 innings against the Mets, then beat the Phillies in his next start.

home_pitcher_note: On Saturday, Hernandez taught the Brewers about the science of pitching. The 35-year-old right-hander handcuffed the Brewers by changing speeds and location. He moved the ball in and out, up and down, but kept it mostly down. Hernandez threw very slow and then much faster, or fast and then much slower. He threw a four-hit shutout as the Nationals stretched their winning streak to three with an 8-0 victory over the Brewers. It was Hernandez's first shutout since 2004, the eighth of his career and his 48th complete game. Hernandez struck out only three and walked two while facing just 33 batters in the nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: How does the right-hander follow up on his last start? Jimenez threw the first no-hitter of his career and the first in team history in a 4-0 victory in Atlanta. He threw a career-high 128 pitches and became the fourth Dominican-born player to toss a no-hitter in the Major Leagues. Jimenez did it despite some control troubles that caused him to walk six. But he struck out seven and set down the final 12 batters he faced to finish the job. And just for fun, guess what he did the next morning? He ran six miles to run off some of his leftover energy. Colorado manager Jim Tracy said he just loves Jimenez's work ethic and how much the right-hander wants to get better.

home_pitcher_note: While Smith's ERA has steadily decreased in his first three 2010 starts, he's still struggling to find any semblance of consistency. His most recent outing, Sunday at Atlanta, is a perfect example. The five hits he allowed are acceptable, though it means he was pitching out of trouble. The seven walks he issued only exacerbated his problems, finally catching up and forcing the left-hander to exit after 5 1/3 innings. Through 17 1/3 innings on the season, 18 strikeouts aren't sufficient to offset 15 hits and 11 walks allowed. For a command pitcher who relies heavily on a plus changeup to compensate for a high-80s fastball and a middling curve, anything less than pinpoint control puts him at a serious disadvantage.
away_pitcher_note: One first-pitch fastball with two outs in the ninth inning stood in Nolasco's way of a shutout last Saturday at Philadelphia. While Jayson Werth delivered a home run, Nolasco still finished with his fourth career shutout. Nolasco became the first Marlin to go the distance since he did on Aug. 18, 2009 at Houston. Of his 109 pitches, 71 were strikes. Nolasco had previously gone as deep as six innings this year. The right-hander has struck out 13 and walked seven this season in 20 2/3 innings.
