home_pitcher_note: In order for Cook to be successful, the right-hander needs to pound the strike zone with a heavy sinker, get hitters to chase it and induce groundouts. When that doesn't happen -- and it hasn't happened consistently enough in 2010 -- Cook struggles. That's what occurred in his last outing Monday at Washington. Cook was tagged for five runs on seven hits in three innings, walking four and forcing manager Jim Tracy to go to his bullpen earlier than he wanted. Cook has won 27 games in since 2008, so he knows how to go deep into games in a pitch-efficient manner. The Rockies need him to regain his ability to be an innings-eating anchor to their rotation.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching in 50-degree temperatures in Philadelphia last Sunday, Robertson said: "This is my kind of weather." Formerly with the Tigers, Robertson is used to pitching in the cold. He likely will have some more in his start at Colorado. The lefty comes off an efficient outing, working 6 1/3 shutout innings at a tough place to pitch -- Citizens Bank Park. Coors Field will present another challenge. Robertson has shown craftiness, like he did in his last start, working around four walks.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa helped his own cause in a 10-4 victory over the Nationals on Tuesday night. His three-run double proved to be the big hit in an eight-run inning. That gave the Rockies an early 10-0 lead. He helped again later with a double and finished 2-for-3 with those three RBIs. But De La Rosa had a tough time despite the early lead, needing 118 pitches to make his way through five-plus innings. The left-hander battled some control problems, striking out six but walking four to improve his record to 2-1 on the season. He gave up four runs on seven hits to Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad has worked at least six innings in all three of his starts. Completing seven has been a challenge. The 23-year-old's best outing was a 6 2/3-inning effort in a win over the Reds. He tossed a career-most 117 pitches that day. His last time out, he was not involved in the decision against the Astros. He gave up three runs on five hits. Volstad has pitched to contact all year. He has eight strikeouts and seven walks in 19 innings. Volstad made his MLB debut in 2008 at Colorado, picking up the win in relief.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel is still looking for his first win in his fourth start of the season, but he had a quality start in Washington on Wednesday, pitching well and leaving with the game tied after seven innings.  Hammel allowed four runs (three earned) on eight hits and a walk while striking out six.  He struggled to get first-pitch strikes in the first four innings, but improved over his last three, throwing breaking balls for strikes early in the count to compliment his fastball.  His fastball showed signs of the command he'd been missing in his previous starts, and he explained that he was pitching on a better plane with better direction as he went deeper in the game.  Though the bullpen took the loss, his seven innings helped give his relievers some necessary rest.
away_pitcher_note: Haren had a strange night in his last start. On the mound, the performance was less than stellar as he allowed seven runs on nine hits in six innings against the Cardinals at Chase Field. At the plate, however, it was a different story. Haren went 4-for-4 and helped lead an offensive explosion that resulted in a 9-7 Arizona victory. Four of the seven runs he allowed came via a pair of homers by Ryan Ludwick and one by Albert Pujols. After allowing three runs in the fourth, Haren was able to retire the Cards in order in the fifth and sixth innings. Haren was dominant in his Opening Day start against the Padres and was in line for a win in his outing against the Dodgers before L.A. rallied against the Arizona bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez kept the momentum going after his no-hitter in Atlanta, throwing 7 1/3 innings of shutout ball in Washington to run his scoreless streak to 16 1/3 innings, while becoming the first pitcher in 17 years to follow a no-hitter with a scoreless outing.  The Rockies ace was dominant, holding the Nationals to five hits and two walks while striking out five.  He had his best ground-ball ratio of the season, recording 15 of his 22 outs through grounders, and he only allowed three men as far as second base during the entire outing.  He made good use of his offspeed pitches, throwing his changeup and slider for strikes in fastball counts.  He is making his second start of the season at Coors Field, having given up a season-high two runs against the Padres on April 11, and his career 3.40 ERA at home is the lowest mark for any starter with 150 innings or more at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson struggled early against the Cardinals in his last start as he allowed three first-inning runs. Then in the second inning, he was involved in a bench-clearing incident when his mound opponent Chris Carpenter was unhappy about being hit by a Jackson pitch. After the three-run first, Jackson settled down and managed to allow just one more run while getting through eight innings. He left with the score tied, but the Cards managed five runs in the ninth against the Arizona bullpen to secure the win. Jackson was acquired by Arizona in a three-team trade during the Winter Meetings that sent Max Scherzer and Daniel Schlereth to the Tigers. The D-backs are his third team in three years. He pitched for Tampa Bay in 2008 before being dealt to the Tigers before last year. Jackson throws a fastball, curve, slider and change.

home_pitcher_note: Smith had a solid outing to open a Coors Field doubleheader on Saturday, holding the Marlins to four runs on eight hits and a walk over five innings while suffering the loss. He gave up a pair of solo home runs on well-executed fastballs, but was hurt more by a hit batsman who came around to score and a mistake pitch to Dan Uggla that turned into a double and later a run. Smith effectively minimized the damage throughout the game, avoiding the big inning and keeping the Rockies in the game, despite a lack of offensive support. It was a credible effort, and Smith has been effective in filling Jeff Francis' spot in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Benson has pitched well in his two starts for the D-backs after being called up from Triple-A Reno. The right-hander was signed to a Minor League deal on March 17. He made one start at Reno and pitched well enough to get the call when the D-backs needed a fifth starter. Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey were the candidates that Benson beat out for the spot. In his last time out, he held the Phillies to three runs (two earned) over six-plus innings. His first start for the D-backs came against the Padres at PETCO Park. He pitched out of bases-loaded jams in the first and second innings and managed to last six frames and allow just two runs. Last season, he appeared in eight games (two starts) for the Rangers, going 1-1 with an 8.46 ERA. Benson missed the entire 2007 season after undergoing right shoulder and elbow surgery. In one appearance for Reno this year, he allowed two unearned runs in five innings, pitching in 40-degree weather. Benson was the first overall pick by the Pirates in the 1996 First-Year Player Draft.

home_pitcher_note: Zito is off to the best start of his career. Skeptics warned before his most recent outing that he wasn't amassing many strikeouts (nine in 19 1/3 innings), often an ominous sign for a pitcher. Then he struck out 10 in eight innings against St. Louis, marking his second double-digit strikeout performance as a Giant. Zito has been especially tough on the Rockies, compiling a 4-2 record with a 1.98 ERA against them in 11 lifetime starts, including 2-0 with a 0.95 ERA last year.
away_pitcher_note: Aaron Cook rebounded from a rough start to his season to notch his first win in style, going the distance in an 8-1 victory over the Marlins to secure a split in a Coors Field doubleheader.  Boasting what he called his best sinker in two years, Cook recorded 15 ground-ball outs while scattering five hits and two walks over nine innings. He had complete control of the strike zone, executing first-pitch strikes and first-pitch outs, efficiently working through 111 pitches and saving the bullpen on an early season twin bill. The "vintage Aaron Cook" outing earned him his all-time best 32nd win at Coors Field, surpassing Jason Jennings for the most wins in one of baseball's most challenging parks for pitchers.

home_pitcher_note: After opening the season with three consecutive quality starts, Cain lapsed slightly last Sunday against St. Louis, yielding two runs and six hits in five innings as the Giants lost, 2-0. There was no shame in Cain's game, considering that one of the runs he yielded was on an Albert Pujols homer. Cain, who made his Major League debut against Colorado on Aug. 29, 2005, has faced the Rockies 18 times, more than any other club except San Diego (19). He's 8-6 with a 3.31 ERA lifetime against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: As expected, Rogers was recalled from Triple-A to make the start on Saturday. He last pitched on Sunday in Reno for the Colorado Springs Sky Sox. He was stretched out to 75 pitches, finishing five innings and allowing five hits and one earned run. The good news is that he walked one. He pitched one-hit ball over five innings in his previous start against Las Vegas. He'll be making his second career start and his fifth Major League appearance.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez has put up some eye-popping statistics, including strikeouts per nine innings (12.22) and opponents' batting average (.167). Left-handed batters are 0-for-14 off him. Before his most recent outing, in which he worked five innings against Philadelphia, he recorded back-to-back double-digit strikeout games for the first time in his career -- April 14 against Pittsburgh and April 20 against San Diego. Sanchez is 2-3 with a 6.85 ERA in 15 career appearances against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Recalled on Tuesday, Chacin got the jitters out with a strong ninth inning in the Rockies' 12-1 victory over the D-backs at Coors Field. He struck out two and pitched around an error. Considered the Rockies' closest-to-the-Majors pitching prospect, Chacin has stellar secondary pitches. The question heading into the season was whether he could command the fastball at a Major League level. After going 3-0 with a 1.69 ERA in four starts at Triple-A Colorado Springs, Chacin gets his chance.

home_pitcher_note: Correia struggled in the early going against the Marlins on Wednesday, but he settled in to get his fourth consecutive win. In the first two innings, Correia threw 35 pitches and gave up three runs. In his next three frames, however, he gave up just a solo homer to Jorge Cantu and not much else, finishing his five-inning outing with four runs on eight hits and one walk while striking out four and throwing 93 pitches (59 for strikes). For his career against the Rockies, the 29-year-old is 2-3 with a 4.29 ERA in 25 games (eight starts).
away_pitcher_note: The Cy Young Award talk has begun, although it is early. But Jimenez has a no-hitter and five stellar starts to his credit to open the season. The fastball has been a consistent 95-97 mph, which several of them reaching 99 and the magic century mark. However, it's the location of the pitches and the fact he can mix several offspeed and breaking pitches that has him one of the best in the NL at this point.

home_pitcher_note: LeBlanc tossed 6 1/3 shutout innings and had three hits in the Padres' 9-0 victory over the Brewers on Thursday. LeBlanc, promoted from Triple-A Portland on April 18 after pitcher Chris Young was placed on the disabled list with a strained right shoulder, had his third consecutive strong start since his being recalled. Balancing his plus-changeup with good fastball command, the left-hander allowed a few hard-hit balls early in the game but avoided any collateral damage. He allowed eight hits with no walks and six strikeouts while lowering his ERA to 0.52. "It starts with good use of the fastball," Padres manager Bud Black said. "We're seeing early-count strikes and keeping them off-balance."
away_pitcher_note: There's no easy way to sugarcoat Smith's last outing: it was terrible. The Rockies need him to get right since their starting rotation is currently struggling. Smith pitched well in a home victory over the New York Mets on April 13, but hasn't been the same since. He's given up 10 runs on 12 hits in his last 10 innings. He's already allowed six home runs over his five starts and walked 15. He'll be making his first career appearance against the San Diego Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Richard won his first game of the season Friday, throwing six scoreless innings in a 3-0 victory over the Brewers. Richard also struck out a career-high-tying eight and now has a 3.00 ERA, 23 strikeouts and 13 walks in 30 innings. Richard allowed three runs on seven hits on April 9 in Colorado in the Padres' 7-0 loss to the Rockies. He was the last Padre starter to earn a victory this season.
away_pitcher_note: Cook has been extremely effective in his two home starts this season, but hasn't yet been able to translate that into any kind of road success. At Coors Field, he owns a 2.40 ERA and a .177 batting average against. He's lost all three of his starts on the road, with an 8.79 ERA and a .344 batting average against. He's been slightly more effective on the road than at home through the course of his career. Fortunately he's pitching at San Diego, where he's 6-1 with a 1.60 ERA in nine career starts. His 13 wins against the Padres are his most against any team. If there's a chance to start a nice productive streak, this would be it for Cook.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda started the year fourth on the rotation depth chart but he's become the de facto ace. He showed why again on Sunday with eight dominant innings against the Pirates, pitching efficiently with a large lead. Unlike the other Dodgers starters, Kuroda is crafty enough to thrive even when he doesn't have all of his pitches working. And he doesn't cause his own problems, throwing enough strikes to post a strikeout-to-walk ratio  of better than 3-to-1. This is the Kuroda the Dodgers thought they were signing, but his first two seasons were marred by injuries. He is 0-2 with a 7.00 ERA in three career starts against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers wasn't terrible in his first start of the season, but he wasn't efficient either. The Rockies were hoping to get more than four innings out of their rookie, but with his pitch count at 92, he was finished. He gave up five runs on five hits and four walks. He struck out two. Rockies manager Jim Tracy said Rogers would get another start just so he doesn't feel like the team is losing any confidence in him. He's got great stuff and he started the year with the Rockies as a reliever. Once he understands his starting role, Rogers should be quite effective. He'll be making his first career appearance at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Charlie Haeger's move to the bullpen was never exactly official, but that's the flexibility manager Joe Torre has with a knuckleballer. Haeger threw four innings of one-run ball Tuesday out of the 'pen, just his second relief appearance of the season and his first since his pseudo-demotion. It was enough to impress Torre to return Haeger to the fifth-starter's role he had out of Spring Training -- at least for one start. Haeger, 0-3 with a 6.56 ERA, has had trouble controlling his floater: he has 23 strikeouts to 17 walks, and a 1.84 WHIP in 23 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin, 22, made nine appearances for the Rockies last season and displayed secondary pitches that were comparable to those of some of baseball's top pitchers. However, one start against the Pirates unmasked the fact that when called up, he didn't have location or command of his fastball. But on Sunday, after being called up because of injuries to the rotation, Chacin showed what he can do when he's spotting his fastball. He held the Giants to one hit and struck out nine in seven scoreless innings. With consistent fastball command, he could emerge as a Rookie of the Year candidate.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw did not seem rattled after he managed just four outs and allowed seven earned runs in a start against the Brewers on Tuesday. Kershaw saw his ERA jump by nearly two runs to 4.99 ERA. His strikeout rate is good: 36 in 30 2/3 innings, but he's struggling to locate, with 24 walks. He hasn't fared well against the Rockies, who have a .260 batting average against him. Only the Phillies (.269), and, after Tuesday, the Brewers (.279) have hit him at a better clip in the NL.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez celebrated the May 3 announcement that he was the NL Pitcher of the Month of April by slamming the door shut on the Padres with a career-high 13 strikeouts and one run against in seven innings of a 5-2 victory. Knowing the Padres wanted to take pitches, Jimenez pounded them with high-velocity strikes early and often. Now comes another test for Jimenez. He is 2-1 but with a 7.53 ERA in six starts at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Smith left Tuesday night's game with a 2-1 lead over the Padres, but he lasted just five innings. Five walks and 95 pitches suggested an inefficiency that more often than not will lead to trouble. Smith at times has shown a knack for making the pitch that will get him out of a tough inning, but getting ahead of hitters with quality strikes remains his assignment.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick may have saved his spot in the rotation --- or in the big leagues --- with his performance against St. Louis, a seven-inning gem, in which he allowed only six hits, no walks, no runs and three strikeouts. It's been feast or famine this season for Kendrick, who had another great start against Atlanta on April 20 but has been hit hard in his other four starts before Wednesday. The sinkerball pitcher must keep the ball down in order to be successful. If it's sailing up even a little bit, it could be a very long night.

home_pitcher_note: Cook seemed to be in control of Wednesday's game against the Padres until giving up four runs in the fourth inning. For most of his time on the mound, he was forcing weak contact and getting ground balls. However, he elevated three key pitches, and those were the hits that drove in four runs. Manager Jim Tracy acknowledged after the game that Cook has been inconsistent, but he expects him to go on one of his patented streaks of success at some point.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay continues to churn out wins for the Phillies, which is exactly why they brought him to Philadelphia in December. Halladay has done it all, until Tuesday. He pitches at Coors Field in Denver for the first time in his career. That is noteworthy because Coors can be a difficult place to pitch, but also because Halladay grew up in Colorado. If Ubaldo Jimenez can pitch successfully in Colorado, why can't Halladay?

Hammel made some adjustments after his pulled groin put him out of commission, realizing his stride may have been a bit long. More importantly, from his perspective, he recaptured the mental approach that led to his success in 2009, when he won 10 games for the Rockies and posted a staff best 3.17 strikeout-to-walk ratio.  Hammel has been haunted by the big inning this season -- topping out with a seven-run second inning in Atlanta in April -- but he is returning to the rotation with new focus and rejuvenated energy.
away_pitcher_note: What can Moyer possibly do for an encore? He became the oldest pitcher in baseball history to throw a shutout, at 47 years, 170 days old, when he twirled a two-hitter Friday against the Braves at Citizens Bank Park. Moyer has his work cut out for him. He is 0-2 with a 9.00 ERA in two regular-season appearances in Colorado, although he allowed one earned run in six innings in Game 3 of the 2007 National League Division Series at Coors Field.

Lannan may be on a pitch limit against the Rockies on Thursday. Manager Jim Riggleman said the team wouldn't want him to throw more than 100 pitches. It will be Lannan's first start since May 2 against the Marlins. He missed a start against Florida on Saturday because of left-elbow discomfort. Lannan threw a bullpen session on Monday without having any problems with his left elbow. He threw between 60 and 65 pitches. The team's trainers and pitching coach Steve McCatty were on hand to make sure Lannan was able to throw his full repertoire of pitches -- curveball, slider, fastball and changeup.

Jimenez could have prevented the run had he properly fielded a hard smash back to the mound on the play that drove home the winning run. Still, Jimenez has 49 strikeouts against 20 walks while being consistently dominant.

Even though Hernandez got stuck with a no-decision, he gave up just one run on five hits in seven innings as Washington beat Florida, 3-2. Hernandez's ERA actually went up despite giving up just the one run in seven innings. That's how effective he's been all season long. Hernandez rarely throws faster than the mid-80's, but he constantly keeps batters off-balance.

There were mechanical issues with finishing off pitches. It's reminiscent of Hammel's start to 2009, but by midseason he had corrected himself. The Rockies hope the corrections happen earlier this year.
away_pitcher_note: Atilano had the third strong outing of his young career, and it proved to be enough for his third win of the season. At first it looked as though Atilano was going to have a long night. In the first inning, the Mets had the bases loaded with one out. It didn't help that Atilano had a hard time gripping the ball because of the cold weather, but he managed to get out of the inning by striking out David Wright and Ike Davis. That marked the second time this season Atilano was able to get out of a bases-loaded jam. The first was against the Cubs in Wrigley Field. Atilano would go on to pitch 5 1/3 innings, allowing five hits, striking out a career-high five batters and walking two.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies have held off on announcing pitching plans. The fact Sunday is open could mean the Rockies intend to activate their former No. 1 pitcher, left-hander Jeff Francis, from the disabled list. He won 17 games and two in the playoffs in 2007, but his 2008 was marred by shoulder problems and he missed 2009 with shoulder surgery. Francis was supposed to begin the year in the rotation, but tightness set in just before Opening Day. However, Francis threw seven scoreless innings in his last rehab start for Double-A Tulsa and feels fully healthy.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen wasn't as effective against the Mets  on Tuesday as he was against the Braves on May 6, when he took a no-hitter into the eighth inning against the Marlins. Olsen lasted 5 1/3 innings and gave up two runs on nine hits, striking out two and walking one. The next day, Olsen apologized to Nationals manager Jim Riggleman on Wednesday morning for showing his emotions after being taken out of the game in the sixth inning Tuesday night. Olsen told the skipper that he didn't realize the television camera was panning on him as he was walking off the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Wells showed he's a quick learner. On May 6 against the Pirates, he gave up seven runs over two innings. In his last start Tuesday against the Marlins, Wells notched his fourth quality start, going eight innings. He joked that he was happy to get an at-bat. He's made only one start against the Rockies and lost. He's also fared better on the road, compiling a 3.86 ERA compared to 5.31 at home.
away_pitcher_note: Cook has not pitched with the expected consistency through his first seven starts, but he is coming off a positive effort. Cook held the Phillies to three runs in six innings and kept the Rockies close in a matchup with Phils ace Roy Halladay. The Rockies won in extra innings. Although Cook has been able to fight his way through rough times with a four-seam fastball and a breaking pitch, he needs to get on a good streak with his sinker.

home_pitcher_note: Silva is on a roll. The right-hander notched his fifth quality start in his last outing against the Marlins. The last time he began a season this well was 2004 when he opened 5-0 with the Twins. The Cubs are 6-1 when Silva starts. The key? "He throws a lot of strikes," catcher Geovany Soto said.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching scoreless ball for his first 15 1/3 innings this season, Chacin gave up six runs in five innings against the Nationals on Thursday night. Five of the runs came on two Ryan Zimmerman home runs, and each of those came on poorly located sliders. In the fifth, he couldn't put the inning away with two outs. It was not the best day for Chacin, but for the most part he stayed in the strike zone and didn't become flustered when things went wrong.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino was rocked for eight hits and seven earned runs in 4 2/3 innings and issued four walks and two wild pitches in his previous start Friday in San Francisco. The Astros have lost in 14 of Paulino's past 15 starts since July 3, 2009. Paulino, who has received poor run support this year, is 5-18 since joining the Majors in 2007. He's 0-1 with an 8.10 ERA in two career starts against the Rockies, both of which came last season. Paulino has pitched much better at Minute Maid in his career, going 2-10 with a 4.91 ERA in 21 games (17 starts).
away_pitcher_note: Smith gracefully accepted reassignment to the bullpen last week, but before he makes his first appearance as a reliever, he's got one more task to attend to: Another start. Thanks to Colorado's rotation being thrown off by Friday's rainout and subsequent doubleheader on Saturday against Washington, manager Jim Tracy announced Smith would start this game at Houston. Smith has started seven games for Colorado this season and has a 1-2 record and a 6.35 ERA. In his last start, on May 10, the lefty went 5 2/3 innings against San Diego, allowing eight hits and four earned runs, while striking out six and walking four. Wednesday will mark his first career appearance against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt has lost three consecutive decisions in his previous four starts despite pitching well. He held the Giants to six hits and two runs and struck out seven batters in eight innings Saturday in San Francisco but was outdueled by Tim Lincecum for the second time this year. In his five losses this year, the Astros have scored four runs in the 33 innings he's been on the mound. He's dominated the Rockies in his career, going 7-1 with a 1.78 ERA in 10 starts. Oswalt faced the Rockies once last year and held them to six hits and one run and struck out eight batters in seven innings to get a win. He's five wins away from tying Joe Niekro's club record of 144.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez offered another brilliant outing against the Nationals on Saturday, silencing their bats for eight innings while yielding two runs on seven hits and a walk and striking out five. He paid for a couple mistakes, including hanging a split-finger fastball to Adam Dunn, who sent it 442 feet into the third deck at Coors Field for the first home run Jimenez has given up all season. He was efficient with his pitches, throwing 115, including 70 for strikes, and kept a tight game in hand, only trailing after giving up a first-inning run, then shutting down the Nats until the Dunn solo shot. Jimenez set the tone for the Rockies to sweep their first doubleheader since September 2007, a game into their 21-of-22 win stretch that catapulted the club to its first World Series appearance.

home_pitcher_note: Lately, Bannister has focused on getting more ground balls as opposed to pop flies. Shifting his focus obviously worked during his last start against the Chicago White Sox last Sunday, when he got 10 ground ball outs. Bannister will look for more of the same as he takes on the Colorado Rockies for the third time in his career Friday, May 21 at Kauffman Stadium. Bannister picked up his second win of the season against the White Sox, moving one game closer to .500 at 2-3. Bannister is 1-0 with a 2.25 ERA in 12 innings against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start back from 18 days on the disabled list with a pulled groin, Hammel threw his second quality start of the season and his best overall performance, earning his first victory. He won the second game of a doubleheader with the Nats, helping the Rockies sweep a doubleheader for the first time since their 21-of-22 win stretch in the fall of 2007 to propel them into their only World Series appearance. Hammel reclaimed the approach that had been successful for him in 2009, challenging hitters by being aggressive in the strike zone. His restored fastball command allowed him to pitch with confidence, holding the Nats to three runs on six hits over seven innings while striking out seven and walking none.

Francis was stellar in his return to the Rockies rotation after losing a year and a half to shoulder surgery. He made his season debut against the Nationals on Sunday, and held them to one run in seven innings.  He scattered seven hits, three of which never left the infield, and settled down after yielding a first-inning run on a sacrifice fly. Francis had all his pitches working for him, showing good fastball command and using his curve and his changeup to get back into counts when he fell behind. He was completely unpredictable against a baffled Washington lineup. He threw 106 pitches, 67 for strikes, and walked two while fanning six.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke will take the mound for the Royals as they wrap up a three-game Interleague series against the Colorado Rockies. Greinke saw his last start go for naught as the Royals fell to the Orioles in 10 innings at Camden Yards. Greinke worked seven innings, gave up just two runs, four hits and a walk with six strikeouts, and still, his second win of the season eluded him. Lack of run support continues to plague the reigning Cy Young Award winner as the Royals have averaged just 2.9 runs per game through his first nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Quietly, Cook is beginning to turn the corner. Cook held the Cubs to two runs, one earned, in seven innings of his last start, which resulted in an extra-innings loss for the Rockies. In his last two games, both no-decisions, Cook has forced 24 ground-ball outs in 13 innings.
