Still, Jimenez has 49 strikeouts against 20 walks while being consistently dominant.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez was "less than his best," according to his manager and himself following his May 20 start against the San Francisco Giants at Chase Field. He allowed six earned runs on 10 hits over five innings, most significantly coughing up a 5-2 lead immediately after he was afforded it. Lopez said his pregame bullpen session portended anything but positive results, and that's just how it shook out. That's not to say confidence has been lost in Arizona's No. 4 starter. Entering his previous start, he had pitched at least seven innings in three consecutive outings and was sporting a 3.81 ERA. Lopez, who made 14 starts for the Rockies in 2007, last faced them in August '09, when, as a member of the Phillies, he allowed two runs in two innings of relief.

home_pitcher_note: You know how baseball is. Numbers measure players and in the final analysis do so accurately. But there's more to them than meets the box score sometimes. Yes, Hammel gave up five runs and six hits in 6 2/3 innings of a loss to the Royals on Friday night. But he had no run support until he left the game, three runs came on two pitches to the same batter (Jose Guillen), and two other runs came after he left. To last that long while pitching through a sore groin -- a situation that has to be watched -- represented a positive for Hammel.
away_pitcher_note: To put it bluntly, Haren hasn't been himself. In his most recent start, kicking off Interleague Play on Friday against the Toronto Blue Jays, the D-backs ace allowed four solo home runs over eight frames. He struck out eight. Haren said afterward he made a concerted effort to mix in a greater portion of four-seam fastballs and pound the inner half of the plate to discourage opposing batters from sitting on his cutter, his best pitch of late. While his results were better against the Jays, Haren is 10 starts into his 2010 season and his ERA is still near five. The All-Star right-hander will look to right his campaign against the Colorado Rockies. Haren last faced the Rockies on April 26: He allowed just two runs (both earned) on five hits over eight innings to record the win.

home_pitcher_note: Francis, after missing last season because of shoulder surgery and having to delay his start to this season while the recovery continued, has had all three of his pitches working in his two starts. When that occurs, it's possible for Francis to achieve what he did in 2007, when he won 17 games and two in the playoffs. A fastball that reaches the low 90s enhances his curve and changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Monasterios makes his first start since May 1, when he allowed one run in four innings of a 5-1 win. He gets the call because Ramon Ortiz allowed eight runs in two starts that lasted a total of 7 1/3 innings. The rookie keeps batters off-balance with a quality changeup, but manager Joe Torre is likely to keep him on a short leash because his arm isn't stretched out. Additionally, because of his lack of experience (only three games above Class-A coming into this season) he's been kept out of most pressure situations whenever possible. He's pitched only five innings since May 8.

home_pitcher_note: What started so good on Sunday ended not so good. Cook held the Royals scoreless for the first four innings but gave up four runs and didn't escape the fifth. The Rockies, who had given Cook a 9-0 lead, still won, 11-7, but Cook didn't get a decision. Cook finished that game with four walks in 4 1/3 innings, and has 25 walks and 25 strikeouts in 50 2/3 innings. The wildness is uncharacteristic.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda has been a quality-start machine for the Dodgers this year, even though the most recent one was a loss to Detroit. Even in that, after allowing three runs in the first inning, he help the Tigers scoreless over the next five innings. He's walked only one batter in each of the last three starts after an uncharacteristic five-walk wild spell against these Rockies. In his only previous Coors Field start, he was pushed around for five runs in six innings. In four career starts against the Rockies, Kuroda is 0-2 with a 6.94 ERA. Kuroda's turn in the rotation should have come up Friday, but manager Joe Torre wanted to give him an extra day of rest.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin continued to pitch well against the National League West on Tuesday, this time holding the D-backs to four hits and two runs in six innings. He'll be facing the Dodgers on Sunday for the second time, having pitched 7 1/3 scoreless innings against Los Angeles on May 8 for his second win of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw's three-game win streak was snapped in Chicago, even though he didn't allow an earned run. That made it four consecutive quality starts, during which his ERA is 0.64 with 27 strikeouts in 28 1/3 innings and he's 1-1 with a 2.28 ERA on the road this year. In his most recent start, the Cubs made him work, fouling off enough pitches to run up his pitch count to triple figures after only six innings. But aside from a disastrous start against Milwaukee that lasted only four outs, he's shown the ability this year to control the damage, a very good trait at Coors Field, where he's 2-2 with a 6.92 ERA. The Dodgers have scored 10 runs in his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum has allowed 11 runs in his last 9 2/3 innings after giving up 11 in his first 56 innings. He's losing command of the strike zone too, walking five in each of his past three starts. A blister problem that crept up during Spring Training may be affecting him more than he's willing to let on. The Washington Nationals took advantage of his wildness in scoring three runs on one hit in one inning during his last start. Two walks, a hit batter and three stolen bases in the fifth resulted in Lincecum's worst start since Sept. 23, 2008, against the Rockies, when he allowed six runs on six hits and five walks over 4 1/3 innings. He's 5-3 in 11 starts with a 3.52 ERA against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez improved upon his big league-leading numbers with his ninth win of the season on Wednesday night as he lowered his ERA to 0.88. He beat the D-backs for the second time this year and has not allowed a run in 17 innings. He'll be facing the Giants for the first time Monday, the only remaining team in the National League West yet to face Jimenez this season.

home_pitcher_note: Zito earned a no-decision in his last outing against Washington, allowing four runs (three earned) on seven hits in 6 1/3 innings. He also walked five. The lefty got off to a rocky start -- giving up a solo home run in the first and second innings -- but settled down until leaving with the bases loaded in the seventh. Zito is 5-2 with a 2.00 ERA in 12 career starts against the Rockies. Zito beat Colorado earlier this season on April 20, allowing two runs on five hits while striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel put together his best outing of the season against the D-backs on Thursday in an 8-2 win at Coors Field to help the Rockies clinch their first series sweep of the season. He matched a career high of eight strikeouts and also allowed fewer than three runs for the first time this season.

home_pitcher_note: A pitcher who has struggled to get run support throughout his career, Cain has proven he only needs a few runs to get the job done. He got one in the top of first inning in his last start and promptly went to work, throwing a one-hit shutout in a 4-0 win over Arizona. Cain also struck out a season-high nine batters, walking zero. In his last start against Colorado on May 1, Cain dazzled, tossing eight innings of one-hit ball and striking out eight to earn his first victory of the season. The right-hander is 9-6 with a 3.09 ERA in 19 career starts against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Francis was solid through five innings Friday against the Dodgers before allowing four runs in the sixth and taking the loss in his third start since returning from season-ending surgery in 2009. In eight career starts at AT&T Park, the lefty is 3-4 with a 5.86 ERA and one shutout.

home_pitcher_note: The D-backs have not named a starter for this game. With an off-day Thursday, they could skip the fifth spot in the rotation and start Ian Kennedy on regular rest. If it's not Kennedy, it could be Dontrelle Willis, whom the D-backs acquired on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Cook held the Dodgers to three runs, one earned, in 6 1/3 innings on Saturday night at Coors Field. But that was at Coors. Cook carries an 0-3 record and 7.04 ERA on the road into his start at Chase Field, but believes he's pitching with more control. In his career, he has a 4.18 road ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Willis will be making his D-backs debut. The left-hander was acquired along with cash from the Tigers on Tuesday for right-hander Billy Buckner. Willis appeared in nine games for the Tigers, eight of them starts, and was 1-2 with a 4.98 ERA. Willis, 28, won a job in Detroit's rotation this spring and had quality starts in three of his first four outings. But he struggled in May, going 0-1 with a 6.52 ERA, and the Tigers elected to remove him from the roster to make room for Max Scherzer. Command became a serious issue for Willis in 2008, and he spent much of the season on the disabled list with forearm and knee injuries. He started last season on the DL with what the club called an anxiety disorder.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin racked up six strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings against the Dodgers on Sunday, but his four runs allowed were too much to overcome. Chacin will be facing the D-backs for the second time in two weeks, after beating them on May 25.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez will oppose Jimenez for the second time in three starts. With Thursday's off day, the D-backs are giving Lopez an extra day after he was taxed hard in his last outing against the Dodgers. Lopez went eight innings and threw 115 pitches. He allowed four runs (only two of which were unearned thanks to a pair of errors by second baseman Kelly Johnson). Lopez suffered a 7-3 loss to Jimenez on May 26 at Coors Field. While not overpowering, Lopez has a good feel for pitching and manages a game well. He came to Spring Training as a non-roster invitee and pitched his way into the No. 4 spot in the rotation, besting Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey. The right-hander has battled arm troubles since being the ace of the Orioles' staff earlier in the decade. He throws a fastball, cutter, curveball, slider and change. Lopez appeared in seven games (five starts) for the Phillies last year and also started 18 games for Triple-A Lehigh Valley.
away_pitcher_note: With a four-hit shutout of the Giants on Monday, Jimenez became the fourth pitcher in Rockies history to reach 10 wins before the All-Star break. Shawn Chacon (2003), Aaron Cook (2008) and Jason Marquis (2009) had 11 before the break in their big years and Kevin Ritz won 10 before recess in 1996. But Jimenez needed just two months of the season to do his damage. In the victory over the Giants, Jimenez, who dominated the D-backs with the fastball in his last meeting with them on May 26, threw 79 fastballs, but also 14 curves, 16 sliders and 16 changeup/split-finger pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel held the Giants to one run, an Andres Torres home run, in 6 2/3 innings on Tuesday night in a game the Rockies eventually won, 2-1, in 11 innings. It was a breakthrough for Hammel, who stayed composed in a tight pitching contest with the Giants' Barry Zito. Despite his success, Hammel didn't have complete fastball command. If he can gain a handle on all his pitches and show consistency, a hot streak could be on the horizon.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez struck out a season-high eight batters in five innings of a 5-1 win over Washington on Wednesday at home to snap his three-game losing streak. Rodriguez has allowed three earned runs or fewer in seven of his 11 starts. He's 3-1 in  with a 3.55 ERA in five career starts at Coors Field, beating the Rockies there last by holding them to two earned runs in seven innings. Overall, he's 4-2 with a 4.31 ERA in nine career starts against the Rockies. Rodriguez is 21-35 with a 5.24 ERA in 77 career games on the road.

home_pitcher_note: With each passing start, Francis shoves into the past any concerns about the shoulder problems that cost him last season. For the most part, he has provided reminders that he was the Rockies' No. 1 pitcher when they went to the 2007 World Series. But he gave up three two-out runs and four overall in 5 2/3 innings of a loss to the Giants in his last start, after starting the game with four stellar innings. So he needs to be a little more consistent.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler is making his third start of the year after working out of the bullpen to begin the season. He worked 5 2/3 innings against the Nationals on Thursday in Houston, allowing five hits, two runs, one walk and striking out three batters. Moehler is 1-2 with a 6.67 ERA in eight games (four starts) in his career against the Rockies. He's pitched in two games in his career (both starts) at Coors Field and is 0-2 with a 9.58 ERA. He hasn't pitched at Coors Field since 2008. Moehler is 37-55 with a 5.07 ERA on the road in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Cook gave up three runs and four hits in his last start, a no-decision at Arizona. He learned early, when Justin Upton homered in the first, that his sinker wasn't at its best, but he used his curve and four-seamer and spotted his sinker where it wouldn't hurt him. He left the game in position to win. The best news, though, is Cook is pitching at Coors Field, where he is 2-0 with a 2.63 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Paulino earned his first win of the season in his most recent start Thursday, beating the Cubs, 3-1, at Minute Maid Park. He went eight innings and gave up five hits and one run and struck out seven batters for his first win since his final start of the 2009 season. He has allowed one run in his past 21 innings in three starts. He faced the Rockies twice last year, going 0-1 with an 8.10 ERA. He's 0-1 with a 6.19 ERA in three career starts against the Rockies, including 0-1 with a 15.75 ERA in his only start at Coors Field. He's 3-9 with a 7.10 ERA in 16 career games (12 starts) on the road this year.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin struck out a career-high nine in 5 2/3 innings, but fell to the D-backs in his last start. Chacin is looking similar to a young Ubaldo Jimenez. He has impressive stuff, but, like Jimenez before this season, there is early-inning inefficiency. He needed 38 pitches to go two innings and 57 to go three.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt is coming off a start in which he allowed a season-high nine hits and six runs in an 8-5 loss to the Cubs at home. He's thrown at least six innings in 11 of his 12 starts, but at 3-8 has tied for his most losses before the All-Star break in his career. His 283 starts are the third-most in club history, and his 140 wins are the second-most in club history, trailing only Joe Niekro (144). Oswalt is 7-2 with a 1.88 ERA in 11 career starts against the Rockies and has never lost at Coors Field (3-0, 2.17 ERA in four starts). He threw a one-hit shutout against the Rockies in Colorado in his previous start against them in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez saw his scoreless innings streak end at 33 innings when the D-backs' Conor Jackson homered for two runs on Sunday on a 3-1 changeup. But here's something interesting: Jimenez, who struck out eight, gave up six hits. Just one, by the D-backs' Kelly Johnson, came on a fastball. As long as Jimenez's best pitch is unhittable, he's difficult to beat, but it should be a good matchup with the power-hitting Jays.
summary: 2010-06-11 - Toronto Blue Jays @ Colorado Rockies (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Hammel turned in his best outing of the season on Monday, striking out three and not allowing a run in 7 1/3 innings in Colorado's 5-1 win against the Astros. He is 3-1 with a 3.00 ERA in his last five starts.

The Rockies lost Francis' last start, 4-3, to the Astros, but Francis didn't figure in the decision though he pitched well enough to win -- two runs in seven innings, with seven hits, one strikeout, 14 groundouts. Many of the hits came when Francis missed high with the fastball, but a changeup that has been accurate all season bailed him out of numerous jams.
away_pitcher_note: Litsch will be making his season debut after coming off the 60-day disabled list after recovering from Tommy John surgery. The 25-year-old right-hander takes the rotation spot of Brian Tallet, who was moved into the bullpen following his last outing on Tuesday, when he gave up five runs on six hits in four innings of a 9-0 loss to the Rays. Litsch will be trying to duplicate the stuff he showed in 2008 when he went 5-2 with a 1.92 ERA in nine starts after returning from a stint in the Minors in the middle of the summer. He finished the year 8-7 with a 4.46 ERA in 20 games (19 starts). Last year, Litsch made only two starts before being placed on the disabled list April 14 with a right forearm strain and then underwent the reconstructive surgery on June 12. This will be Litsch's first career appearance against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing against Kansas City Wednesday, Pavano proved again he can pitch deep into a ballgame. He lasted eight innings for the fourth time this season. Pavano struggled with his command early in the game, giving up his only two runs in the third inning. However, he said he settled down after that and was able to pitch the way he had planned. This is not the first time the right-hander has struggled with his command early on, saying he can link it back through the past couple games. His two runs against Kansas City came off two four-pitch walks, something that is uncharacteristic of Pavano. He has walked only 13 batters this season. In his 12 starts this season, he has given up more than two runs in a game only four times.
away_pitcher_note: Cook held the Astros to two runs in seven strong innings in his last start, but the team's offensive woes led to a 6-2 loss at Coors Field. Cook has gone to his slider out of necessity because the sinker hasn't been as effective, but he used both effectively and forced 16 groundouts against the Astros. Cook is 0-3 with a 6.81 road ERA, but he held the D-backs to three runs in five innings and left his last road start with a 6-3 lead.

home_pitcher_note: Baker had a rough outing against Kansas City Thursday. He gave up back-to-back home runs early and finished his five-inning stint with five earned runs against him. That was his first loss since May 19 against Boston and was only the second time he lost at home this season, the first coming on April 22 against Cleveland. The right-hander has given up four home runs in his last two starts after giving up only seven in his first 11 starts. He has given up five or more runs only four times this season. Baker couldn't keep the ball down in the zone against Kansas City and the Royals took advantage of that. He has gone 3-4 in his last 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin struck out eight in six innings against the Astros on Thursday. He pitched well early, but Rockies manager Jim Tracy said the young righty allowed Houston too many chances.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano had a remarkable outing against Atlanta on Friday. He had a season-best 11 strikeouts, the most he's thrown since he threw a career-best 12 against Detroit on July 28, 2006. He had seven strikeouts in a row from the third to the fifth innings, which tied a Twins' best which was set by Jim Merritt on July 21, 1966, against Washington. He struck out hot-hitting Jason Heyward three times in that game and struck out two other batters multiple times. He improved to 87 strikeouts on the season after throwing double-digit strikeouts for the third time this season. Liriano didn't walk a batter in that game, also the third time he has done that this season. The left-hander is undefeated in Interleague Play in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez struggled a bit in the rain and cold during a rain-shortened 5-3 win against the Blue Jays in his last appearance. He still earned the win, his big league-best 12th of the season, and struck out six in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel was excellent for the third straight time in his outing on Saturday against the Blue Jays, striking out six batters in eight innings and allowing just three hits for a 1-0 win. In his last two starts, he's pitched shutout ball in 15 1/3 innings of work. Hammel has not allowed more than two runs in an appearance since May 21 and is 4-1 in six starts since returning from the disabled list on May 15.
away_pitcher_note: According to manager Ken Macha, the Brewers "pitched well enough to win" on Saturday night against the Rangers, and among those pitching was Parra. The lefty tossed six strong innings, giving up three runs, which earned him his first quality start of the season. Parra took the loss, however, despite striking out eight batters, which would have been a career high if he hadn't just recorded 10 strikeouts in his previous start in St. Louis. After giving up five runs in 11 1/3 innings over his previous two starts, Parra seems to be coming around for the Brewers and establishing himself as a legitimate option within the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Francis threw his fourth straight quality start on Sunday against the Blue Jays to help the Rockies complete a three-game sweep. It was his second win of the season, as he allowed two earned runs in seven complete innings. In five career starts against the Brewers, Francis is 2-3 with a 7.76 ERA
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo struck out 10 batters against his hometown Rangers last weekend, but his string of quality starts ended at three. He allowed four runs on six hits and four walks in six innings and saw his ERA bump up a bit to a still-respectable 2.66. He has a 2.01 ERA in his last 12 starts. Gallardo matched up against Ubaldo Jimenez and the Rockies on Opening Day and took the loss after allowing four runs, three earned, on seven hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Here's a statement that, even with the humidor making Coors Field play bigger than ever, it's hard to imagine saying: Cook returns to the safety of Coors Field. He is 2-0 with a 2.62 ERA there, as opposed to 0-4, 7.38 on the road. Why? Maybe that question could be tackled before his following start, which will be at Anaheim. For now, why not enjoy his work at Coors?
away_pitcher_note: Wolf had a long chat with pitching coach Rick Peterson in the days leading up to his last start and it apparently paid off. Wolf, who tied his troubles to mindset rather than mechanics, tossed seven strong innings and didn't allow any Angels hits outside of a trio of consecutive hits in a two-run second inning. Wolf composed himself and retired Erick Aybar to end the threat and went on to finish an outing that helped ease the pain of a loss to the Cubs five days earlier in which he surrendered five home runs. Wolf beat the Rockies on April 6 in his Brewers debut but wasn't thrilled with the outing after allowing four runs on nine hits.

home_pitcher_note: In the first game of a series that's a rematch of the 2007 World Series (won by the Red Sox in a sweep), Chacin enters with rough numbers (1-3, 6.17 ERA) at Coors Field. Chacin had no fastball command in his last outing but worked through five innings and held the Twins to two runs, but the Rockies' offense did little and the game was a 2-1 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Lester in his last start against the D-backs continued like he has for much of the season, pitching seven solid innings for the Sox, allowing only four hits and two runs. He also walked only three and struck out seven. The two runs came in the second inning off of a two-run home run by Justin Upton. After that inning, Lester recorded all seven of his strikeouts and blanked the D-backs in the next five. With the win, Lester moved to 8-2 on the year with a 3.13 ERA. Just like his last start against the D-backs, this will be the lefty's first career start against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez continued his dominance in his outing against the Twins on Thursday. He pitched eight innings and gave up only one run, which came in the last inning of his outing. The Twins got eight hits off the ace, but Jimenez got them to hit into four double plays to end innings. He had four strikeouts and two walks in that start. With the Rockies on the verge of getting swept by the Twins, Jimenez snapped that chance, making his record 10-0 when the Rockies lose the game prior to his start. Jimenez faced Boston in Game 2 of the 2007 World Series in his first full season in the big leagues. He gave up two runs and five walks in 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: While nothing was easy for Lackey in his previous start, against the D-backs, like he has done much of the season, the righty kept his team in the game and found a way to win, moving his record to 8-3 with a 4.53 ERA. Lackey gave up three earned runs and eight hits, while striking out five in six innings. Throughout the night though, Lackey continued to struggle with his fastball command and kept his pitch count high almost every inning. Lackey will next face the Colorado Rockies, a team he one start against with a career record of 1-0 and a 3.38 ERA.

home_pitcher_note:
In Colorado's 2-0 win against the Brewers on Friday, Hammel extended his scoreless-innings streak to 25 1/3 in his third straight start of seven or more complete innings without allowing a run. Hammel is 3-0 with a 0.31 ERA in the month of June and, though not racking up the strikeouts in his recent outings, has been the beneficiary of timely Colorado hitting and excellent defense.
Hammel, who pitched for Tampa Bay for parts of three seasons, is 0-2 in his career against the Red Sox with a 5.50 ERA in eight appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Making his return to the starting rotation Thursday against the Colorado Rockies after spending time on the disabled list with a right forearm strain, Matsuzaka is hoping to pick up right where he left off in his last start against the Cleveland Indians back on June 7. He pitched eight strong innings, giving up four hits and no runs, while striking out five. Sox manager Terry Francona said going into the start that Matsuzaka is "feeling really good and checked out fine." The righty is 6-4 in Interleague Play with a 4.01 ERA, but he has never faced the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver strengthened his case for an All-Star Game berth with seven shutout innings against the Cubs on Saturday at Wrigley Field, holding them to two singles and no walks while striking out 11, one shy of his career high. Seizing the Major League strikeout lead from the Giants' Tim Lincecum with 107, Weaver unleashed 109 pitches, 74 in the strike zone. Only five balls left the infield. Weaver went with his fastball and breaking ball until mid-game when catcher Bobby Wilson started calling for a few changeups. Facing the Rockies for the first time, Weaver is 2-1 in six starts at home with a 1.85 ERA this season, striking out 44 in 39 innings.
away_pitcher_note:
Though he didn't earn a decision, Francis pitched well enough to keep the Brewers at bay for the Rockies to come back for an 8-7 win on Saturday at Coors Field. He allowed four runs (three
earned) in 6 1/3 innings for his third consecutive quality start. In one career start against the Angels, Francis went 6 2/3 innings while striking out four and allowing nine hits and two runs without a decision.

home_pitcher_note: Two consecutive rocky outings have Saunders in search of a groove again after he'd appeared to have straightened things out. He lasted only 2 2/3 innings, matching his season worst, at Wrigley Field on Sunday, yielding eight runs (five earned) on nine hits and two walks. Shoddy defense didn't help, but he never found his command and has surrendered 11 earned runs in 8 1/3 innings of his past two starts. He won his only career start against the Rockies, holding them to one run in six innings, but has struggled mightily at home. He's 1-6 with a 6.75 ERA in eight outings at Angel Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Cook's starts on the road and at home have been nearly polar opposites. He'll be on the road against the Angels on Saturday and he is 0-4 with a 7.38 ERA away from Coors Field. His last start, a no-decision against the Brewers at home, consisted of one earned run and three hits in seven full innings. Against the Angels, Cook is 2-0 with a 2.57 ERA in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Santana was in trouble most of the night on Tuesday but was resourceful in escaping, holding the Dodgers to three runs across seven innings and claiming the win with a late rally. Snapping a two-game losing streak during which he'd surrendered 10 earned runs in 10 innings, Santana yielded eight hits and two walks, striking out six men. The Dodgers were 2-for-9 against him with runners in scoring position, testimony to his toughness under pressure. Santana has faced the Rockies once, giving up two earned runs in seven innings but getting no decision.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin pitched out of a bases-loaded jam in the third inning on Tuesday and held the Red Sox to no runs and four hits, with five strikeouts and five walks, in 6 2/3 innings for his second win at Coors Field. Against the Angels, he'll be facing a lineup similar to the one he faced in a recent loss to the Twins, when he went five innings and gave up two runs but faced constant traffic. The Angels will try to work him into fastball counts and not give him a chance to get to his formidable secondary pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Correia walked five in 5 1/3 innings in earning a no-decision in his last start against the Rays. Coming off a start where he allowed five runs in five innings to the Blue Jays, Correia did walk five and allow two runs against Tampa Bay. But he felt like his curveball, a pitch he threw more than usual, helped offset his occasional lack of fastball command, helping keep a dangerous Rays lineup off-balance. "I've been pretty confident with all of my pitches ... it's just mixing them up better," he said. "I didn't throw a lot of first-pitch strikes, but [the walks] weren't costly."
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez was bailed out of the worst outing of his otherwise stellar season with an 8-6 comeback win against the Red Sox on Wednesday at Fenway Park when Jason Giambi and Ian Stewart hit ninth-inning homers. It was the first no-decision of Jimenez's 2010 campaign. After going home with dizziness the night before, Jimenez surrendered 10 hits, a homer and six runs while striking out five. The hits and runs totals were both season highs. The Rockies ace is 2-0 against San Diego this season, allowing three runs in 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: LeBlanc, who entered his last start against the Rays with a 2.88 ERA, had a tough time against the Rays' lineup. "Overall, he just wasn't repeating his pitches," Padres manager Bud Black said. "His ball-to-strike ratio isn't where it needs to be."
away_pitcher_note: Hammel accomplished the third-longest scoreless streak, 28 1/3 innings, before the fourth inning of his last start, at home against the Red Sox. But Dustin Pedroia led off that inning with the first of his three homers in the game. Hammel gave up four runs in that inning.

home_pitcher_note: Richard tossed six shutout innings in his last start against the Marlins, lowering his ERA to 2.75. He walked four but got help from two inning-ending double play balls. Richard said the Marlins made him "work for it." It was Richard's first victory since May 22 in Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: Francis was solid against the Angels on Friday when he allowed three runs on seven hits over 6 1/3 innings but was still saddled with a no-decision. He's struggled against the Padres with a 5-10 record and 5.15 ERA in 18 career outings against the division rivals.

home_pitcher_note: Cook was victimized by just one bad pitch on Saturday against the Angels, when he allowed a first-inning grand slam to Hideki Matsui before settling down to a throw a complete game. His sinker was on, as he recorded 17 ground-ball outs.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start of 2010, Bumgarner allowed two homers en route to earning the loss for his first career decision. After giving up a three-run homer in the top of the second, Bumgarner settled down and allowed only two hits the rest of the way, pitching seven full innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin struck out a career-high 12 batters in six innings on Sunday but was plagued by a three-run homer by Mike Napoli after an error by third baseman Ian Stewart in a 5-3 loss to the Angels. In all, he allowed five runs, two earned, over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum's last start was his shortest outing since Opening Day 2009, as the right-hander lasted only three innings against the Red Sox. In those three innings, Lincecum threw 79 pitches and walked three batters, allowing four runs on five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Somehow it's fitting that Jimenez throw on a fireworks night, although there have been unexpected pyrotechnics in his last two starts. He has given up 10 runs in 11 2/3 innings. In both, he has started strong but fallen behind hitters in the middle innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing against the Dodgers, Zito pitched six innings, giving up two runs on two hits while earning a no-decision. He experienced trouble in the third inning, when he gave up both his runs a sacrifice fly and RBI double.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel held the Padres to three runs in 6 1/3 innings, and no runs until the seventh, in his last start. He overcame a bad start against the Red Sox in his previous outing and has posted a 1.83 ERA in his past six starts by concentrating on first-pitch strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Cain once again failed to beat the Dodgers in his last outing, taking the loss after giving up four runs on seven hits to fall to 0-8 all-time vs. L.A. In Cain's last start against Colorado on June 2, he held the Rockies to one run on four hits in eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Francis had one of the worst games of his career Wednesday against the Padres (8 ER, 7 H, 3 IP) because he lost the ability to throw inside to right-handed hitters, throw srikes at all on the outside of the plate or sink his changeup. He believes it's an aberration.
away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals have yet to announce a Tuesday starter, but after Hawksworth threw a bullpen on Saturday, he's the guess. It could be Hawksworth, and it could be Jeff Suppan. Whichever one doesn't get the nod on Tuesday likely won't start until the weekend.

home_pitcher_note: Cook is 7-for-7 in quality starts this year for the Rockies at Coors Field, where he'll meet the Cardinals. He has a 3-0 record in Denver, while posting an 0-5 mark on the road. In a 7-3 win against the Giants on Thursday, he allowed three runs in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia rebounded beautifully from a rough start when he last pitched, but the thin air of Denver will be a new challenge for him. He's been solid on the road but not as good as he's been in St. Louis (1.20 home ERA, 2.92 road).

home_pitcher_note: After his historic start, Jimenez has been ordinary -- 17 runs in 17 2/3 innings but without lost -- in his last three outings. Falling behind early and walking four led to a seven-run third against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter didn't look like himself last time out, but he and the team insisted he was physically fine. The question came up because five days earlier, he was hit in the right forearm by a line drive. Carpenter is undaunted by Coors Field, with a 0.63 ERA in two starts there.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa makes his first start for the Rockies since being placed on the disabled list on April 27. Since June of last year, the left-hander is 19-4. In three rehab starts for Triple-A Colorado Springs, he was 1-2 with a 5.52 ERA, striking out 15 and walking four.
away_pitcher_note: Correia put together arguably his best outing of the season on Saturday against the Astros, tossing seven shutout innings in a no-decision. He allowed five hits, struck out four batters and walked two. He is 0-2 against the Rockies so far this season with a 7.36 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel held the Giants scoreless for the first seven innings on Sunday, but gave up two homers (one inside the park) and left with a no-decision. Still, Hammel struck out eight and walked one, against seven hits. Hammel beat the Padres on June 29 at PETCO Park.
away_pitcher_note: LeBlanc allowed one earned run on three hits in 6 2/3 innings on Sunday against the Astros, but got the no-decision. Despite allowing three earned runs or less in three of his last four starts, LeBlanc does not have a win during that span. His last victory came on June 12.

home_pitcher_note: Francis has struggled in his last two outings, combining for 13 runs in seven innings. He was spared a decision in Colorado's wild 12-9 comeback win Tuesday, but was roughed up by the Padres on June 30 to the tune of eight earned runs in three frames.
away_pitcher_note: Richard is coming off arguably his worst outing of the season, a 6-5 loss to Washington on Tuesday.  In that matchup, he allowed five runs on nine hits in six innings. In five career starts against the Rockies, he is 1-1 with a 3.90 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo will open the Reds' second half having won four of his past five starts. His last outing against the Mets was one of his best of the season, as he allowed one run in eight innings and walked none. He's lost just twice since April 23.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel remained unbeaten since May 21 when he allowed just two runs in 6 1/3 innings against the Padres on July 10 in a 4-2 win. He's 6-0 with three no-decisions since losing to the Royals more than seven weeks ago.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez will make his long-awaited return to the rotation after Tommy John surgery. He has not started for the Reds since June 1, 2009, because of the injury. In six rehab starts, Volquez went a combined 4-0 with a 1.45 ERA at Triple-A Louisville and Class A Lynchburg.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa struggled with his command early in counts in his first start since returning from a middle finger injury suffered in April. He surrendered seven runs (five earned) in 4 1/3 innings, throwing 95 pitches on July 9 against the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Wood has made three career starts, yet he almost had a perfect game to his name. He pitched eight perfect innings before allowing a ninth-inning single his last time out against the Phillies. The Reds went on to lose, 1-0, in 11, and Wood has yet to record a win or loss.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies' second straight walk-off rally got Cook off the hook for what would have been his first loss of the season at Coors Field on Wednesday against the Cardinals. The right-hander allowed five runs and 10 hits in five innings, leaving with a 5-0 deficit.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez posted 10 quality starts in 17 starts in the first half, and his seven wins are his most since he was 10-3 as a rookie in 2006. Sanchez has thrown 103 1/3 innings, and he's struck out 71 with 39 walks. This will be Sanchez's 18th start, which will be a career high.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez appeared to right the ship in his last start, holding the Cardinals to three hits and one run in a 4-2 win on July 8. Working ahead efficiently, he threw 93 pitches in eight innings. He had allowed 17 runs in 17 2/3 innings in three previous starts combined.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty opened the year as the No. 3 starter. He gets the fifth start of the second half, and second this year vs. the Rockies. He lost on April 24 at Coors, giving up five runs in four innings. For the most part, Robertson gives five or six innings per start.
away_pitcher_note: Francis earned a no-decision in the Rockies' 9-7 loss to the Padres on Sunday, but confessed his command to both sides of the plate has not been where he'd like to see it. The lefty has not won since June 13, taking one loss in that span.

home_pitcher_note: It's been a pretty daunting stretch for Nolasco. In his last three starts, he has drawn Tim Hudson, Dan Haren and Stephen Strasburg. He did win two of those before losing to Strasburg and the Nationals, which snapped a string of four straight victories.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel struck out a career-high 10 and went seven strong innings in his last start, but took a 3-2 loss to the Reds. Hammel was bailed out of trouble by a home run-saving catch by center fielder Dexter Fowler in the fifth, but in general handled himself well.

home_pitcher_note: Make the string 12 starts and counting. That is how many consecutive starts Johnson has gone without allowing more than two earned runs. The MLB leader in ERA, JJ has given up one earned run in 20 innings in July. This season, he has 130 strikeouts in 128 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In two starts since returning from a left middle finger injury, De La Rosa has struggled to find his fastball command. In his last outing, a loss to the Reds, he also shied away from breaking pitches. The Rockies need for him to regain form.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay allowed five earned runs in six innings vs. the Cubs last time out after surrendering just one run over 18 combined innings in his previous two starts. Look for a rebound Friday at home, where he's posted a 1.87 ERA in 11 starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Cook threw seven scoreless innings in his last start, at Cincinnati, his first road win. He retired 11 of the final 12 batters he faced. Cook returns to Citizens Bank Park, where he pitched the Rockies to their only victory in last year's 3-1 NLDS loss to the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies optioned Kendrick to Triple-A Lehigh Valley on Tuesday, indicating they had something planned to improve their rotation. But after Jamie Moyer injured his left elbow on Tuesday, putting his season in jeopardy, the Phillies will go with Kendrick.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez was hurt by an error, then gave up a three-run homer on a split-finger when a fastball might have been better in his last start. Only a late rally (the Rockies ultimately lost) saved him from his second loss. Jimenez has given up five homers in his last seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: It has been a long road back for Happ, who has not pitched since April because of a left elbow injury. Still not where the Phillies wanted him to be after rehab in the Minors, the Phillies optioned him to Triple-A Lehigh Valley. He returns because of Moyer's injury.
away_pitcher_note: Francis spotted his fastball inside, used his fastball and curve outside, and mixed in his dangerous changeup while throwing seven scoreless innings in a win over the Marlins Tuesday. It was a major bounce-back for Francis, who had an 8.03 ERA in his previous five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton is 2-1 with a 4.79 ERA in his previous seven starts. In four of those starts, he has allowed three earned runs in seven or more innings. He has shown improvement, but Blanton is still looking for that truly impressive performance.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel left his last start wanting two innings back in a 5-2 loss in Florida. Two runs came with two down in the first and three came on a homer with two down in the second. It comes down to the consistency with which he gets ahead of batters and locates his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: After giving up 10 hits and 14 runs (11 earned) in his first two starts after returning from a left middle finger injury, De La Rosa found his form against the Marlins on Thursday. De La Rosa gave up two runs on three hits and struck out eight in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Duke gave the Bucs his second consecutive strong start since returning from the DL with a strained flexor pronator, going six innings and giving up just three runs on six hits for his first win since out-dueling Roy Halladay on May 18 and giving a taxed bullpen a rest.

home_pitcher_note: Cook was hit hard by the Phillies on Friday, giving up five runs on nine hits while walking three in 4 1/3 innings. The 31-year-old has a 5.67 ERA in eight career games (five starts) against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf followed his worst start of the season by tossing his fourth quality start in his past five outings, fanning six Brewers over six frames Thursday. His only mistake was a Prince Fielder solo homer, and it was the difference in a 3-2 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez will try to rebound after what was one of his poorer outings in what has otherwise been a magical season. On Saturday against the Phillies, the righty lasted just two innings, surrendering six earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: A four-run second inning handed Maholm the loss Friday vs. the Padres. Maholm has been mired in a good-start, bad-start routine going back to June 23 at Texas. Two of his last six outings have lasted fewer than four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Francis pitched five strong innings before exiting for a rain delay on Sunday against the Phillies, striking out six and giving up two runs in a 4-3 loss. He's started five games against the Cubs, notching an 8.77 ERA without a decision.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster notched a quality start in his last outing but also served up a game-tying home run to Albert Pujols. Dempster is 2-0 with a 2.08 ERA in two starts vs. NL West teams.

home_pitcher_note: After an extended stretch without a loss, Hammel has taken defeats in his last three outings. He's given up 12 earned runs in 19 2/3 innings over that span but is 1-0 with a 5.40 ERA in one career start against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Since returning to the rotation, Gorzelanny is 4-0 with a 2.83 ERA in five starts. The lefty has fared better on the road, posting a 2.25 ERA in 10 games (six starts).

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa gave up two first-inning runs, but wound up holding the Pirates to three runs and six hits in seven innings. He struck out eight and has fanned 16 in 13 innings over his last two starts, although he lost both.
away_pitcher_note: Silva picked up the win in his last start against the Astros, an improved outing after not being able to go past the second inning in his previous two games.

home_pitcher_note: Cook suffered his first home loss of the year on Wednesday against the Pirates, surrendering five earned runs and six hits in 2 1/3 innings. He's taken two losses in a row, allowing 10 combined earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Sanchez pitched six solid innings before being unable to record an out in the seventh, coming out after giving up a pinch-hit, three-run homer. In six-plus innings, Sanchez allowed five runs on seven hits, striking out seven.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez appeared to regain his early season form on Thursday against the Pirates in a 9-3 win to help Colorado snap an eight-game losing streak. He allowed just one first-inning run, while striking out six and scattering four hits.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner took the loss in his last outing against Florida, when the Giants were one-hit by Florida's Anibal Sanchez. Despite the loss, Bumgarner went six innings, giving up three runs on six hits, to earn his fifth quality start in seven outings.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates acquired McDonald on July 31 and inserted him into the rotation. McDonald started in Triple-A this season, but made only one start with LA this year. He has pitched just 2 2/3 innings since July 19, which could affect how deep he can go.
away_pitcher_note: Francis' solid outing on July 30 was lost in a 17-2 win against the Cub, but he recorded one of his most efficient outings of the year. The lefty needed just 88 pitches to work through six innings, allowing two runs for the win.

home_pitcher_note: Duke wasn't hit all that hard in his last start, but the Cardinals found enough holes to chase him after five innings. Duke has given up at least six earned runs in five different starts this year. He is the first Pirates pitcher to lose 10 games.
away_pitcher_note:
Hammel had a particularly efficient start spoiled by a three-run homer allowed by a reliever on Saturday against the Cubs. Hammel needed just
83 pitches for 7 1/3 innings, taking the no-decision while striking out five and walking none.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf labored through his last start, needing 95 pitches to finish just the first four innings. Though he limited the damage (three runs), Ohlendorf walked four and went to a three-ball count eight times to the first 18 hitters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa earned his first win since returning from the disabled list in early July in an 8-7 win against the Cubs on Sunday. De La Rosa struck out five and allowed three runs in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm leads the club with seven wins, having snapped a two-game losing skid in his last outing. Maholm has been up-and-down lately, though his most recent start was an encouraging six-inning step in the right direction.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers had two big relief performances for the Rockies in early July before going to Triple-A Colorado Springs to stretch out as a starter. With Aaron Cook on the disabled list with a sprained right big toe, Rogers gets his shot.

home_pitcher_note: Though the Mets considered skipping Pelfrey's rotation spot, they opted instead to tinker with his mechanics and keep him on turn. The team feels that if Pelfrey keeps his arm speed consistent, he can beat the Rockies for the second time this season.
away_pitcher_note: After a few hiccups after the All-Star break, Jimenez has returned to dominance. He struck out nine, allowed one run and earned his second win in a row on Aug. 4 against the streaking Giants to match the franchise record for wins in a year (17).

home_pitcher_note: Neither five walks nor a rocky start doomed Niese on Friday in Philadelphia. Instead, it was a bullpen collapse than prevented Niese from recording his eighth victory. He will try again vs. a Rockies lineup that tagged him for five runs in April.
away_pitcher_note: Francis paid for two poorly located breaking balls, which went for home runs by Garrett Jones and Ronny Cedeno, in a 5-1 loss to the Pirates. But Francis has 23 strikeouts and two walks over his last four starts and has generally pitched well.

home_pitcher_note: Though he could not complete a frenzied eighth inning, Santana nonetheless fired 7 1/3 shutout innings last Saturday against the Phillies. He has not faced the Rockies since blanking them in similar fashion over seven innings of a game last July.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel held the Pirates to three runs on three hits in six innings while earning a 6-3 victory on Friday night. Hammel yielded a three-run Pedro Alvarez homer in the sixth, but otherwise dominated with his fastball and changeup.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa is on a nice run lately, having converted three quality starts in his last four outings and posting a 3.60 ERA in that span. For his career against the Brewers, his former team, the 29-year-old has a 9.19 ERA in four games (three starts).
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo wasn't sharp in his last start -- he allowed four runs on eight hits in his first four innings -- but he didn't have to be. The Brewers have scored 29 runs in Gallardo's past two starts, an 18-1 win at Chicago and an 11-6 win vs. the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers was workmanlike in his first start in the rotation since replacing the injured Aaron Cook. He tallied three strikeouts and eight hits in six innings, taking the winning decision in the Rockies' victory over the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson missed the Rockies when the Brewers went through Denver in June but faced them twice in relief in April. He was born in Englewood, Colo., a suburb of Denver, and allowed three runs in five innings of his only career start at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez continues his quest for an 18th win of the year, which would be a franchise record for wins in a season. He gave the Rockies a great shot but took the loss in a 1-0 defeat to the Mets on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Parra allowed only one D-backs run Tuesday but needed 106 pitches for 5 1/3 frames. He has worked five, 5 1/3 or 5 2/3 innings in eight of his past nine starts and has yet to deliver more than six innings all season. That means work for the bullpen

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw gave another quality start in his last appearance, but all anybody will remember from that game is the seven-run lead the Dodgers blew and the demotion of Jonathan Broxton afterward as closer. Nonetheless, it was a fine rebound effort.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin is expected to start in place of Jeff Francis. Chacin showed promise in his first stint with the Rockies this year, posting a 5-8 mark with a 4.04 ERA. He split time between the rotation and the bullpen but has an excellent arsenal.

home_pitcher_note: In five of his losses, the Dodgers have been shut out. He suffered a 1-0 loss to the Braves on a Brooks Conrad homer to center. He has a lower ERA than his other two big league seasons, but already has more losses than either of the other two years.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel threw seven innings on Thursday in his most recent turn, but he ceded eight hits and four runs in a loss to the Mets. He's thrown at least six innings in eight of his past 10 starts, but his ERA has risen from 4.31 to 4.42.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly is the left-handed Vicente Padilla, a stretch-run acquisition that so far is unbeaten in three starts as a Dodger. He finally walked a batter against the Braves, snapping a string of 16 1/3 walkless innings since being acquired.
away_pitcher_note: As has become custom, De La Rosa gave the Rockies a good chance to win on Aug. 13 against the Brewers. He allowed three runs on three doubles in the sixth after five spotless innings and hasn't allowed more than three runs in a start since July 17.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy appeared to be back on track after his Saturday start in Washington. He yielded just two runs in seven innings and struck out seven. It was his first quality outing in nine tries. He's faced Colorado twice already this season and is 0-1.
away_pitcher_note: In both starts filling in for the injured Aaron Cook, Rogers has given the Rockies a good opportunity to win. He's 1-0 with a no-decision, combining for seven earned runs in 11 2/3 innings during the stint.

home_pitcher_note: Mr. Consistent has yielded three runs or fewer and gone at least five innings in each of his first nine MLB starts, though he has just three wins to show for it. The rookie right-hander will be making his debut against a loaded Rockies lineup.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez was, again, denied his franchise- and big league-best 18th win of the year when Clint Barmes missed a popup and Huston Street blew a save in the ninth on Sunday. He struck out 10, his second-highest strikeout total of the year.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson deserved his fourth straight win Tuesday against the Reds, but he didn't get it. He held the NL's top offense to three runs in seven innings and struck out a career-high 10 but picked up his first loss in an Arizona uniform.
away_pitcher_note: Called up from Triple-A Tuesday to face the Dodgers, Chacin was sharp for three innings, struggled to get out of the fourth and ultimately allowed five runs. He is 1-1 with a 3.55 ERA in three appearances against Arizona this season.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel limited the Dodgers to two runs on four hits in six IP Wednesday before leaving with the game tied, 2-2. Hammel next faces Atlanta at home. In his one start vs. the Braves this season in Atlanta, Hammel gave up seven earned runs in 1 2/3 IP.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson has gone 5-0 with a 0.82 ERA in his past six starts. His recent dominance could be halted when he returns to Coors Field. He has allowed 13 earned runs and 19 hits in the nine innings that have encompassed his two career starts in Denver.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had another strong outing his last time out, giving up two runs on five hits in seven innings against the Dodgers. It just wasn't enough and his teammates could not solve Ted Lilly.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe has posted a 5.66 ERA in nine career starts at Coors Field. The veteran sinkerballer's finest effort there came on July 10, 2009, when he limited the Rockies to one earned run and four hits over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ubaldo Jimenez has taken Rogers under his wing and it's paying off. In his last outing, Rogers had a career outing, giving up one run on six hits in 6 1/3 innings against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has seen the Braves win eight of the 10 games he's started since returning from the disabled list. He has gone 2-0 with a 2.30 ERA, despite allowing opponents to compile a .307 on-base percentage in four starts this month.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez will make his fourth attempt at setting the club's single-season franchise record with 18 wins. He struggled with fastball command and gave up three runs in six innings for the loss against Arizona in his last start.
away_pitcher_note:
Kershaw hasn't notched a perfect first inning all season, and it came back to bite the Dodgers on Sunday in a 5-2 loss to the Reds.
Kershaw finished with 11 strikeouts, one away from a season-high, but he walked five and let up five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin was excellent his last time out, throwing 7 2/3 innings for the 1-0 victory against the D-backs. He struck out nine and walked just one for his sixth victory of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley didn't make it through six innings in his last start, but let up just three runs and struck out seven. He hasn't allowed more than two runs in a start in more than a month. With his calf still bothering him, he was pushed back two days.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel, still searching for just his second victory since July 10, pitched a solid outing against the Braves his last time out. He has not given up more than four runs in a start since a July 21 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly, who has been placed on waivers by the Dodgers, will try to continue his stretch of sensational pitching with his new club. Lilly has won all five of his Dodgers starts, posting a 1.83 ERA in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez has been almost incapable of thriving in back-to-back starts. But his inconsistency might bode well for him against Colorado, since he yielded five runs and six hits while walking three in 4 1/3 innings against Cincinnati.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa threw one of his best outings of the season, striking out seven and allowing just two runs against the Braves on Aug. 24. The southpaw appears to be regaining the dominant form of late last season.

home_pitcher_note: There has been a pronounced difference between Bumgarner's performance at AT&T Park and away from it. The 21-year-old rookie is 0-2 with a 6.04 ERA in five home starts, compared to 5-2, 2.62 in seven road outings.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers was lit up in his worst start of the season when he gave up eight hits and seven earned runs in 1 2/3 innings against the Braves on Aug. 25. A nine-run comeback got him off the hook.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum probably has never been so happy to see a month end. He lost all five of his August starts, posting a 7.82 ERA. He'll face Ubaldo Jimenez, to whom he lost, 4-0, on May 31. Lincecum's career record in August is 4-6 with a 3.70 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: For the fourth straight start, Jimenez was denied what would be his big league-best 18th win of the year on Aug. 27, which would also break the franchise record for wins in a season. He's allowed 10 earned runs in his last 28 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin has been stellar his last two outings, striking out 16 and allowing just one run in a combined 14 2/3 innings. The only time he faced the Padres this season was out of the bullpen, giving up two runs and two hits in 1 1/3 innings on July 11.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton seems to have turned around his season. He is 3-1 with a 3.41 ERA in nine starts since the All-Star break. He allowed just two runs in his last 13 innings over two starts, which is what the Phillies are looking for from their No. 4 starter.

home_pitcher_note: Luebke will be making his MLB debut. The Padres' first-round pick in 2007 is 10-1 with a 2.68 ERA and 88 strikeouts in 114 innings between two Minors stops in '10. If he pitches well He has the opportunity to remain in the San Diego rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Cook (4-8, 5.34 ERA), who has been out 3 1/2 weeks with a hyperextended right big toe, was scheduled to return Thursday vs. the Phils in a makeup game at Coors Field. But the Rockies reconsidered after noting Cook's 6-1 record at PETCO Park.

home_pitcher_note: Two RBIs from Shane Victorino are what ultimately cost Garland in Saturday's start vs. the Phils, but two leadoff at-bats by Jayson Werth are the ones he'd like to have back. Garland hit Werth with a pitch and walked him, and Werth scored twice.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel threw three innings of no-hit ball against the Dodgers before allowing seven hits and two runs in the following 2 1/3 innings. He still came away with his first career victory against Los Angeles, his first win since Aug. 6.

home_pitcher_note: Richard allowed one run in the first six innings of his last start, vs. the Phillies, before yielding a two-run homer to Mike Sweeney, which put the game away. He allowed four runs (two earned), as two of his own throwing errors led to the loss.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa fanned nine and held the Giants to four hits in his last start. Although he left with a 1-0 deficit, his work made a late comeback possible in a game the Rockies won, 2-1.

home_pitcher_note: In his last five starts, Jimenez has a solid 3.00 ERA, with 35 strikeouts to 12 walks and just one homer. Certainly, that's good enough for something, right? But he is 0-4, and the Rockies are 14-4. By any measure, he should have 20 win.
away_pitcher_note: In his career against the Rockies, Harang is 4-2 with a 3.00 ERA in six starts. He hasn't faced Colorado since getting a win with six scoreless innings on Aug. 22, 2008.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie has been on a hot streak for the Rockies, surrendering just two earned runs in his last 20 innings pitched, spanning three starts. In that time, he's 2-0 with 19 strikeouts. He's struck out five in 3 2/3 career innings against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Since his last start, Cueto has been dealing with a personal crisis. A death in the family required him to go home to the Dominican Republic. He planned to do his running and throwing while down there.

home_pitcher_note: Cook returned from a month on the disabled list to beat the Padres. He threw 6 1/3 solid innings and kept his sinker down until the seventh. He next faces the Reds, whom he shut out for seven innings on July 18.

home_pitcher_note: With two consecutive strong starts, Jimenez appears closer to the form he displayed during a Cy Young-caliber 2010. He allowed just two hits in eight innings during his last start, earning the tough-luck loser tag.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook tossed eight shutout innings in his last start against the Royals. Since a string of four rough starts to begin the year, he has a 2.78 ERA over his past six starts.

away_pitcher_note: Garcia allowed three runs in five-plus innings in his last start vs. the Royals on a day with conditions that favored hitters. The lefty hasn't allowed more than three earned runs in any of his 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin has looked like a top-tier starter for much of 2011, but he struggled against the D-backs on Tuesday, giving up five runs in seven innings. Expectations have raised for Chacin after a season-ending injury to Jorge De La Rosa.

away_pitcher_note: After two consecutive improved starts, Jimenez took a step back on Friday when he was hit hard by the Cardinals. He gave up six runs on a career-high 12 hits, as he took his seventh straight losing decision dating back to Sept. 22 at Arizona.

away_pitcher_note: Nicasio, displaying a mid-90s fastball and a fearlessness that impressed the Rockies' brass throughout his Minor League career, held the Cardinals to one unearned run in seven innings in his Major League debut -- a win last Saturday.

away_pitcher_note: Chacin was plagued by a rocky start in his last outing, giving up three runs on four hits in the first inning against the Cardinals. The right-hander has pitched well in his career against the Dodgers, posting a 4-3 record with a 2.40 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong will be pleased to return to AT&T Park, where he has allowed one earned run in 23 2/3 innings spanning four appearances (three starts). That's a remarkable 0.38 ERA. Yet Vogelsong is only 1-1 at home due to insufficient run support.

away_pitcher_note: Jimenez shook off two months of frustration by shutting out the Dodgers on four hits in his last start. He has thrown complete games in his last two road starts and has given up nine hits in his four road starts.

away_pitcher_note: Cook has been out with a broken right ring finger that he suffered in Spring Training. But he makes his return to action at PETCO Park, where he is 7-1 with a 2.21 ERA in 11 career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin has more or less assumed No. 2 duties since the loss of lefty Jorge De la Rosa for the season because of Tommy John surgery. Chacin beat the Giants, 2-1, in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley was a hero with his bat instead of his arm in Cincinnati with a home run and a double, raising his average to .304. Pitching-wise, he battled through five innings, allowing four runs, but got a win despite his lack of command.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel struggled with walks and his inability to put away hitters with two strikes in his loss at Dodger Stadium on May 30, but bounced back by not allowing a hit for the first 5 2/3 innings in San Francisco in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly deserved a better fate in Philadelphia, holding the Phils to only two runs over six innings in his fourth consecutive quality start. In 25 starts since being traded to the Dodgers last year, he hasn't allowed more than two walks in any start.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez was outstanding during the Rockies' last road trip, shutting out the Dodgers, 3-0, and giving up just two runs in a strong but luckless outing against the Padres. Jimenez, however, has struggled at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had an adventurous debut start in Philadelphia, walking five of the first 11 batters he faced. But he limited the damage to only one run and made it to five innings to qualify for a victory.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin turned in one of the best performances of his young career against the Dodgers on Friday, giving up just three hits in eight shutout innings, while striking out nine against three walks.

away_pitcher_note: The way Verlander is pitching, every start feels like a chance at another no-hitter. This time it's the Rockies' turn to try to hit his stuff after he two-hit the Indians on Tuesday in Detroit. He's 12-2 in Interleague Play.

away_pitcher_note: Hammel earned his first win since April 30 on Friday, despite giving up six runs over 6 1/3 innings. In six games (two starts) against the Indians, Hammel is 0-2 with a 6.27 ERA, with 19 strikeouts over 18 2/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Cook is still searching for his first win of the season after coming of the 60-day DL on June 8. He gave up four runs on eight hits over six innings in a loss to the Tigers on Sunday.

away_pitcher_note: Chacin took a no-decision in the Rockies' win over the Indians on Tuesday despite surrendering just one run on two hits in 6 2/3 innings. He struggled with command, though, walking six.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel battled through five walks and lasted six innings in his last start, a loss at Cleveland. It was a one-run game, and a run scored on his balk, when he forgot what pitch he was supposed to throw mid-windup.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd is coming off one of his worst outings of the season, in which he allowed six runs over five-plus innings in a loss against the Cubs. He carried a one-run lead into the fifth but failed to retire a batter while giving up four runs.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez is back in form after a slow spring, winning consecutive games for the first time since August. He allowed two runs on four hits and four walks while striking out seven Yanks in seven innings Friday and has a 3.66 ERA over his last 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Despite a rain-shortened no-decision in his last outing, Buehrle is still 10-0 with a 1.88 ERA in his last 14 Interleague starts. Also, his 25 wins during Interleague Play are the most all time.

home_pitcher_note: Cook has struggled a bit in his first four starts since opening the season on the DL. He has gone 5 2/3-six innings in each start. His trademark sinker has been slow to return in the early innings.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy will make his scheduled start despite pitching four innings of relief on Saturday against Washington. Peavy allowed just one hit while striking out seven and picking up the win in his first Major League relief appearance.

away_pitcher_note: Hochevar picked up his fifth win last Sunday against the Cubs, although he was pulled after 5 2/3 innings. It was his shortest outing since May 30 and the 88 pitches were the fewest he's thrown all year.

away_pitcher_note: Jimenez fanned nine, but went just 5 1/3 innings, mainly because the Braves had success fouling off pitches and extending at-bats. Jimenez gave up three runs (two earned). Since June 1, he hasn't given up more than three earned runs in any start.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann will make the last start of the first half before the Nats cut down his workload after the All-Star Break. Zimmermann has a 160-inning limit in his first full season since undergoing Tommy John surgery, but has the best ERA on the team.

away_pitcher_note: Narveson's first half was strikingly similar to his 2010 season, with an ERA (4.75) and strikeouts per nine innings (7.8) that rank slightly better than last year. He's won four of his last five decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin has dropped his last three starts, but it's hard to fault his performance in Washington on Sunday. He struck out four and held the Nationals to one run and four hits in seven innings, but received no run support.
away_pitcher_note: What a weird first half for Greinke. He's 7-3 with four double-digit strikeout games and the team is 9-4 when he starts, but he also has a 5.45 ERA. Greinke is hoping the results begin matching how he feels on the mound.

away_pitcher_note: The Brewers haven't been very good on the road, but Marcum has. He owns a 2.26 ERA in nine starts away from Miller Park and has gone 3-2, quite a feat considering the team has only 16 road wins all year.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel held the Nationals to two runs and five hits in 6 1/3 innings of his last start, a victory at Washington. He is looking to improve at home, where he is 3-6 with a 4.92 ERA in 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe struggled in his last start against the Phillies, allowing four early runs on 10 hits in six frames. But he can be encouraged by his career second-half numbers. He went 5-0 last September and is 76-48 with a 3.66 ERA lifetime in the second half.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez gave up two runs and teetered in the early innings, before finding perplexing Milwaukee with his split-finger pitch and his slider in a Rockies win. The Braves, however, elevated Jimenez's pitch count while beating him in Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Beachy allowed two runs in six innings in his last start against the Phillies, taking a no-decision against Roy Halladay. Beachy, who has never faced the Rockies, has allowed more than three runs in just two of his 12 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio made great strides on Friday, throwing seven scoreless innings of four-hit ball to earn the win. He induced 13 groundball outs and struck out four. His fastball command was excellent, and his slider was effective when behind in the count.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Hudson limited the Nationals to one run in seven innings while striking out seven. He's 4-0 in his last five starts, and one of those wins came July 7 against Colorado, when he allowed three runs in 7 1/3 innings in a 6-3 victory.

away_pitcher_note: Hanson lost for the first time in seven starts his last time out, as he allowed a season-high five runs in 5 1/3 innings in a loss to the Nationals. He last faced the Rockies on July 4 and earned the win after allowing just one run in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson pitched his second complete game of the season on Sunday against the Dodgers, allowing one run on five hits while striking out three and walking none. He allowed three runs on six hits in a loss to the Rockies on April 2.
away_pitcher_note: The struggling right-hander is still in search of his first win in 2011 after giving up three runs on eight hits in 4 2/3 innings in a loss to the Brewers on Sunday.

away_pitcher_note: Hammel has been a self-described enigma for much of this season, following solid outings with shaky ones. He lost to the D-backs on May 25 despite giving up just two unearned runs in seven innings.

away_pitcher_note: Jimenez has firmly put talk of his slow start to rest, going 6-3 with a 2.85 ERA in his last 10 starts. He has 63 strikeouts against 15 walks in that span.
