away_pitcher_note: Chacin has not won since June 15. He lost his fourth straight decision on Thursday after giving up five runs on four hits and a career-high seven walks over 4 2/3 innings against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda has been the subject of some trade speculation recently, but that hasn't affected his performance. He has six quality starts in his last seven outings. Run support has been lacking, though, as his 3.19 ERA has produced just a 6-12 record.
away_pitcher_note: Cook earned his first win since last season on Friday against the D-backs. He threw six innings, allowing four runs on eight hits, while striking out two and walking one. He has a 6-7 career record with a 4.09 ERA in 17 starts against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Stauffer saw his streak of consecutive quality starts end at eight as he struggled with execution and fastball command. He allowed five runs and walked four on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings in a loss to the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel said he felt good in his last start, a lopsided loss at Arizona. The numbers said otherwise -- 12 hits and eight runs in 5 2/3 innings. He did strike out a season-high seven, but he'll need to avoid the key walks and mistake pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Harang has reestablished himself this season. The righty hasn't lost a start since May 2 and is 4-0 in his last six starts. Harang threw six innings on Monday and gave up four runs on eight hits but still picked up a win over the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez had thrown well, posting a 2.58 ERA over 10 starts, before giving up five runs and eight hits in five innings of a loss at Arizona on Sunday. However, Jimenez struck out eight that day, and he says his confidence is intact.

home_pitcher_note: LeBlanc is 0-2 with a 5.12 ERA in three starts with the Padres this season, and he'll fill in for Dustin Moseley who dislocated his shoulder his last time out. With Triple-A Tucson LeBlanc is 5-0 with a 2.29 ERA in his last eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio's splits are troublesome. He is 4-0 with a 1.58 ERA in six starts at Coors Field but 0-3 with an 8.75 ERA in five starts away from home. Nicasio will be hoping to help the Rockies end a 14-game Sunday losing streak.

home_pitcher_note: After a bad stretch in which he had almost as many walks as strikeouts, Chacin threw a strong six innings with three runs, one earned, at Dodger Stadium in his last start. A poor offensive performance, however, left him with a loss.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels pitched well in Wednesday's 2-1 loss to the Giants at Citizens Bank Park, but he got no run support. He allowed six hits, two runs and one walk and struck out six in 7 2/3 innings. He is hoping for some help from the offense Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Cook took two wins during the Rockies' last road trip, a difficult swing through the National League West. In his last start, Cook threw seven scoreless innings and forced 13 groundouts against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick is likely making his last start in the rotation because Roy Oswalt is expected to return after two rehab outings. He's been above serviceable in Oswalt's absence and has allowed three earned runs or fewer in seven of his 10 starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Prior to his last start, Hammel had given up 12 earned runs in 10 2/3 innings pitched. But the right-hander rebounded on Friday, throwing 6 2/3 innings and allowing two runs on five hits in a 3-2 victory against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay benefited from a rout in his last start, tossing 98 pitches in seven scoreless innings of a 10-3 victory against the Pirates. He allowed one hit with five strikeouts, becoming the NL's first 13-game winner.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers entered his last appearance in the second inning -- just after Ubaldo Jimenez was traded -- in a starter's mind-set. Jim Tracy said Rogers was better than expected, as the righty threw five innings and allowed one run on one hit.
away_pitcher_note: The 25-year-old already has 20 career starts to his name, but only one this season after making his past five appearances out of the bullpen. Detwiler prepared like a starter over that time, throwing regular bullpen sessions as a long reliever.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio pitched a strong seven innings against the Padres in his last start, but didn't come up with the win after Colorado's bullpen collapsed. In the start, Nicasio allowed one earned run on five hits, while striking out a career-high 10 batters.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann turned in six shutout frames but took a no-decision against the Mets on Sunday, giving up seven hits and a walk while punching out six batters.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin earned a hard-luck no-decision after throwing 7 1/3 innings of one-run ball against the Phillies on Monday. He is 0-2 with a 5.25 ERA in two career starts against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez pitched six solid innings on Monday, allowing one run on six hits. It was the antithesis of his last two starts in which he allowed 12 runs in 11 2/3 innings without much of a sinker, his bread-and-butter pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Cook left his last start against the Phillies on Tuesday with muscle spasms in his neck, but he doesn't expect to miss his turn on Sunday. Cook is looking for his first win at Coors Field, where he is 0-4.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan notched his eighth win of the season on Tuesday. He lasted 6 2/3 innings, allowed three runs on nine hits and struck out a season-high eight batters. Once he was given the lead, Lannan was able to cruise until he left the game.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey is looking to build off his previous start, in which he tossed eight innings of one-run ball, walking three and fanning four. The 25-year-old has given up two runs or fewer in three of his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel will be happy to start on the road after giving up six runs in his last three home starts. The right-hander has tossed at least seven innings in all three of his starts against Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: Willis has allowed three earned runs or fewer in all five of his starts. In four of the five, he gave up two.  The last time he took the hill, the 29-year-old threw six innings, giving up two runs on eight hits with a walk and two strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers has pitched well while filling the rotation spot vacated by Ubaldo Jimenez. He has given up just two runs over his last 10 2/3 innings of work, displaying better command of his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Leake threw six innings, giving up three runs on six hits with three walks in a loss to the Cubs. He picked up his third loss in his last four games; however, he has recorded a quality start in each of those games.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood, a 14-year veteran, opted out of the Red Sox's organization after pitching well at Triple-A Pawtucket because the parent club didn't have an opening. Millwood steps into the rotation because of the severe neck injury to Juan Nicasio.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto is coming off his shortest start of the season. He lasted just 3 2/3 innings, giving up five runs on seven hits with a walk and two strikeouts in a loss to the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin earned his first win since June 15 on Saturday night, surrendering three runs on five hits and five walks over five innings. He struck out four while pitching through cramps in his pitching hand.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse returns after seven days' rest, and it's an open question as to what he'll have. He's been inconsistent lately, not getting deep into games. Lohse insists he's healthy, but he still needs to perform.
away_pitcher_note: Cook turned in one of his best starts of the year on Sunday, allowing two runs on four hits over 6 2/3 innings. He walked three and struck out four, the only damage coming on Jonny Gomes' two-run homer.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia comes back home, but he does so against a team that hammered him in Denver earlier this year. Still, that 1.56 home ERA is hard to ignore, and it's reasonable to think Garcia turns in a strong game.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel's last start was indicative of his disjointed season. He came back after a rain delay and wound up giving up six runs on four hits, including two homers, in a no-decision against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson's fourth start as a Cardinal comes under the lights on ESPN against a team that has drilled him. Jackson's lifetime numbers vs. Colorado are remarkable: a 17.28 ERA in five starts, only three of those in Denver.
away_pitcher_note: In his last three appearances, including two starts, Rogers is 3-0 with a 2.16 ERA. At times he has faced traffic on the bases, but has made big pitches to escape difficult situations.

home_pitcher_note: In his first Major League start this season, Millwood gave up three solo home runs, but was otherwise excellent in seven innings against the Reds in a 3-2 loss. Millwood struck out six with no walks.
away_pitcher_note: Hensley earned a no-decision in his last start after giving up three runs over 5 2/3 innings to the Braves. He left trailing, 3-0. The righty allowed eight hits, walked four and struck out four. He is 4-2 with a 4.53 ERA against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin's last start resulted in his second complete game of the season, when he held the Reds to two runs and six hits and tied a career high with nine strikeouts but absorbed a 2-1 loss at Great American Ball Park.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez, who remains winless over his past 11 starts in a career-long skid, went a season-low 1 2/3 innings in a loss to the Braves. He allowed five runs on seven hits, throwing 59 pitches. He is 2-0 with a 1.74 ERA lifetime against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Cook forced 14 ground-ball outs and looked good until he was done in by a five-run sixth inning, with much of the damage coming on less-than-solid contact against the Cardinals in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco is closing in on a number of franchise records. He has a chance to become the all-time strikeout leader. With 755, he is second to Dontrelle Willis, who has 757. Nolasco limited the Giants to one run in eight innings in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Hammel bounced back from two subpar outings by limiting the Cardinals to one run on five hits over 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda has been a tough-luck pitcher this year, but he blanked Houston over seven innings in his most recent start, on Sunday. He scattered five singles and a walk to win for the second time in three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers has shown improvement since coming off the DL on July 25, but he hit a bump in the road against the Cardinals on Sunday, when he was hurt by a career-high seven walks.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly has lost his last three starts despite having a 1.71 ERA in that span. The Dodgers scored only three runs in those games, including a 3-0 loss at Milwaukee on Monday night, when the offense hit into a triple play and four double plays.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood has given up five home runs in his first two starts with the Rockies, but Rockies manager Jim Tracy has been impressed with the veteran's ability to limit damage.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley had a strong outing against a tough Brewers lineup in his last start, allowing only one run in seven innings. He's struggled at Coors Field, though. In seven games (six starts} he is 1-5 with a 7.88 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin's Achilles' heel, his fastball command, eluded him on Tuesday against the Marlins, as he lasted just four innings after giving up five runs on eight hits and three walks.
away_pitcher_note: Myers will try again to break his career-long six-game losing streak. He hasn't won a game in more than two months -- June 17 in Los Angeles -- despite posting a 4.32 ERA in his past six starts.

home_pitcher_note: A key figure in the Ubaldo Jimenez trade, White will make his Rockies debut. He was 1-0 with a 3.60 ERA over three starts with Cleveland in his rookie season.
away_pitcher_note: Norris is 1-0 with a 2.25 ERA in his past two starts, including seven scoreless innings on Aug. 12 at Dodger Stadium. He's among the NL leaders with 8.6 strikeouts per nine innings, and he's allowed 143 hits in 153 innings pitched.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander is coming off a strong outing against the Marlins on Wednesday, when he gave up three runs over 7 2/3 innings, all the damage coming on a pair of home runs with the Rockies leading big in the eighth.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez threw eight scoreless innings Friday against the Giants, striking out eight and allowing five hits. He has won at least nine games in each of his seven Major League seasons. The Astros are 11-12 in his 23 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly is scheduled to make this start, even though he came out of his most recent start Saturday night in Colorado in the fifth inning with a stiff neck. Lilly allowed the Rockies runs in the first three innings, including a homer to Todd Helton.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers will make his second consecutive start against the Dodgers. On Saturday, he battled his way to a solid outing -- four runs over six innings -- after running into trouble in the first inning.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley faces the Rockies again after one of the stranger recent starts. At Coors Field, he allowed a first-inning two-run homer to Todd Helton, a seventh-inning two-run homer to Seth Smith, and pitched hitless ball in between.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood has proven to be a valuable innings-eater since joining the Rockies on Aug. 10. He has thrown 20 innings in three starts, walking just three batters.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander has impressed in his first four big league starts, allowing just five earned runs in his 22 innings pitched. He'll only get two or three starts, however, because of an innings limit that will move him to the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin earned his 10th win on Tuesday despite scattering 11 hits over seven one-run innings. The right-hander issued just one walk and benefited from three double plays.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson nearly finished his third game of the season his last time out, pitching 8 2/3 innings of two-run baseball in a win over the Nats on Wednesday. He struck out six, walked none and went at least eight innings for the third time in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: White, a key piece of the Ubaldo Jimenez trade, is looking for his first Rockies win after allowing five runs in six innings in his Colorado debut vs. the Astros on Tuesday. He didn't factor in the decision.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander bounced back nicely from a rough debut, when he allowed five runs on seven hits over four innings against the Braves on Aug. 20. In his second start, he blanked the Nationals over six innings, striking out four and walking four.
away_pitcher_note: Cook gave up five earned runs on 11 hits in a no-decision Aug. 24 against Houston. Cook is 6-4 with a 5.48 ERA in 23 career appearances (21 starts) against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter cashed in his third consecutive solid start on Friday against the Padres, pitching six scoreless innings, allowing six hits, striking out four and walking none in a win. The rookie is 5-0 when he doesn't issue a walk.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers seemed headed for victory in his last start against the Dodgers but a bad inning that included a disputed balk call ruined things. Rogers still seeks consistency.

home_pitcher_note: Harang failed in his first attempt to win his 13th game of the season, allowing two earned runs in six innings against the D-backs on Saturday. His eight strikeouts tied a season high, set back on April 15 against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood has struck out 15 against four walks in his four starts, but has given up six home runs. Pitching at PETCO Park, where the ball doesn't travel, could help.

home_pitcher_note: Luebke wasn't sharp in his last start against the D-backs, as he allowed two home runs, three earned runs and three walks in 5 1/3 innings. He's allowed five home runs in two starts against Arizona this season.
away_pitcher_note: White has struggled with command issues but has been able to fight through those in his two starts since joining the Rockies. He also is rounding into form after a long absence due to a finger injury.

home_pitcher_note: Latos saw his string of 11 consecutive outings allowing three runs or fewer end in his last start, when he allowed four runs in six innings to the Dodgers. He allowed six hits, four walks and had five strikeouts in the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Struggling after missing much of the season with a finger injury, Cook has to be happy to be back at PETCO Park, where in his career he is 7-1 with a 2.39 ERA in 12 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Imagine how good his numbers would look if not for an 18.00 ERA in the first inning this year. Rogers bounced back over the next five innings in his previous start, limiting the D-backs to one run over those frames.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie left-hander picked up his second consecutive win in three big league starts on Tuesday against the Rockies, pitching six innings, allowing two runs on nine hits while striking out three and walking one.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel had been removed from the rotation last month because of his year-long inconsistency. He is back because the Rockies are trying to monitor the innings of second-year RHP Jhoulys Chacin.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter has won his last two starts and has pitched well in his last five. His last start was against the Rox, and he allowed two runs on five hits over six innings. Collmenter allowed five runs in 4 1/3 innings at Coors Field earlier this year.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood threw seven scoreless innings in his last start, a win at PETCO Park over the Padres, and has been solid since joining the Rockies' rotation last month.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders suffered the loss in his last start against the Giants. The left-hander was under the weather and allowed four runs (three earned) over 5 1/3 innings. Saunders has a 5.05 ERA in six starts since the end of July.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin will make his first start since Aug. 28 after suffering through a fever and tonsil inflammation last week. He lost despite tossing a complete game against the Reds on Aug. 11.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey tied a season-low with three innings pitched, as the Reds were beaten, 6-4, by the Cardinals at Busch Stadium on Saturday. Of his six hits allowed for five runs, he had four of the hitters in either 0-2 or 1-2 counts.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander earned his first Rockies win his last time out against the Padres, but he's allowed at least four runs in each of his three starts with Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo took a line drive off of his left leg during his start but recovered to pitch well for eight innings at St. Louis on Sunday. The liner left a huge welt on his leg, which required treatment. Arroyo was optimistic that he would be OK.

home_pitcher_note: Pomeranz, a key piece of the trade that sent Ubaldo Jimenez to the Indians, will make his highly anticipated Rockies debut in Sunday's finale with the Cincinnati Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez will make his first start since July 5 after spending two months at Triple-A Louisville to work on his wayward fastball command.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke was outdueled by Chris Carpenter last week in St. Louis, marking only the seventh time in 24 games that the Brewers lost a Greinke start. He has a 2.96 ERA in 12 home starts vs. 5.04 in 12 starts on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers has struggled as he tries to audition for a spot in next season's rotation. He surrendered six runs on eight hits and five walks over 5 1/3 innings in a loss to the D-backs on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum is the rare Brewer who does better on the road than at Miller Park, where his ERA is nearly two runs higher (4.15). The Brewers have lost three of Marcum's four Miller Park starts since the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood hit his third career home run against the D-backs on Wednesday, but he also took the loss after surrendering four runs on 10 hits over 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin gave up three runs in 5 1/3 innings in a loss Friday night to the Reds. He made it through five innings, then his command deserted him, and a leadoff walk paved the way for a three-run sixth.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong allowed three runs in eight innings Saturday but lost his fifth straight, 3-0, to the Dodgers. He put up a quality start but took the loss, a recurring theme. He has received three total runs of support during his current losing streak.

home_pitcher_note: White has an 8.18 ERA and has given up nine home runs in just four starts with the Rockies -- including five in his start on Saturday against the Reds -- but he's managed two wins.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner ran up his pitch count to 101 through five innings but picked up his fourth straight win, striking out eight batters while giving up one run on three hits and three walks (one intentional) in an 8-1 victory over the Dodgers on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: The player to be named in the Ubaldo Jimenez trade with the Indians, Pomeranz threw five shutout innings in his first career start, a 4-1 victory over the Reds on Monday night. The Giants are dead last in scoring in the National League.
away_pitcher_note: Despite not recording a strikeout in his most recent outing last Monday against San Diego, Surkamp said that he made a mechanical adjustment that improved his fastball command. Surkamp has allowed just one homer in 16 2/3 innings as a Giant.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers made an adjustment in his delivery before his last start and limited the Brewers to one run -- a homer by Prince Fielder -- over six innings. It was a big improvement from his previous four starts, when he allowed four earned runs each time.
away_pitcher_note: In many ways, this has been Cain's finest year. His ERA is his lowest for a full season as is his WHIP (walks and hits per inning). His strikeout-to-walk ratio is his best and he has allowed just nine home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood continues his audition for a spot in the 2012 rotation when he makes his eighth start since joining the team in mid-August. So far, he's been solid, pitching at least six innings in five starts and into the sixth in the other two.
away_pitcher_note: Padres manager Bud Black called Luebke's start Tuesday a learning experience, but it wasn't a bad outing. He gave up two runs on 10 hits while striking out eight over six innings. Luebke has five or more strikeouts in nine of his last 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin looked like a possible All-Star in the first two months, but he started to struggle in June and now looks fatigued. The Rockies, nonetheless, want him to bounce back in his final two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Latos picked up his 18th quality start of the season Wednesday but fell victim to two solo home runs by Carlos Beltran. The right-hander took the loss after allowing three runs on seven hits and a walk while striking out eight over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: The winningest pitcher in franchise history, Cook is unlikely to return next year. So the Rockies, who are hoping to send him off with one last win, are giving him the home finale.
away_pitcher_note: Bass gets a spot start for Tim Stauffer, who suffered a forearm strain during his last start on Sept. 16. Bass made his first career start and also earned his first victory at Coors Field on June 13, allowing one run on five hits in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Sosa has lost his Past three starts despite posting two quality starts in that span. Sosa, making his ninth Major League start, has given the Astros five quality starts in his Past six, going 2-3 with a 3.71 ERA during span.
away_pitcher_note: White has struggled to keep the ball in the yard since joining the Rockies' rotation in August. The right-hander has surrendered 11 home runs in five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Myers has been terrific in his Past four starts, going 3-0 with a 1.19 ERA. He's allowed 19 hits in that span and struck out 22 batters, but most importantly is the fact he's allowed only one home run in 30 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The key component in the Ubaldo Jimenez trade has shown promise in his first two Major League starts, surrendering two runs over 10 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Happ has pitched well since he was forced to go to the Minor Leagues in August and work out some kinks. In his five starts since returning from Triple-A Oklahoma City, he's 2-1 with a 2.40 ERA. He hasn't faced Colorado this year.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel earned one final start after surrendering just one run over seven innings during a start against the D-backs on Sept. 6.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell will take the spot of Bud Norris, who has been shut down for the season with biceps tendinitis. Harrell tossed 5 1/3 scoreless innings on Sept. 2 against the Brewers, but he didn't get a decision.
away_pitcher_note: Kevin Millwood will fill in for Jhoulys Chacin in the finale against the Astros. It is the ninth start of the year for Millwood, who was roughed up in his last outing on Sept. 19, giving up seven runs in just 3 1/3 innings against the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Though Vogelsong has a better ERA at home (2.29) than on the road (3.57), his AT&T Park record is a mere 6-6, compared to 6-1 away from home. His three victories over Colorado are his most against any team this season.
away_pitcher_note: Rebounding from a recent slump, Chacin gave up two runs, one earned on six hits in his last outing, but the Rockies gave him no run support in a loss to San Diego. He has had no run support three times this season.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner needs 2 1/3 innings to reach 200 for the season. He would join Matt Cain (2007), Mike McCormick (1959-61) and John D'Acquisto (1974) as the only starters in the Giants' San Francisco era to pitch that many innings at age 22 or younger.
away_pitcher_note: White gave up five runs and was hit hard in his last outing, a loss to the Astros on Thursday. Putting his pitches in quality strike zone locations has been a problem for White, who joined the Rockies in the Ubaldo Jimenez trade.

home_pitcher_note: Surkamp replaces Matt Cain, who the Giants felt had thrown enough this season, in the 2011 season finale. Surkamp will be trying to strengthen his candidacy for the No. 5 spot in next year's starting rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz, part of the Rockies' bounty from the Indians in the Ubaldo Jimenez deal, had an ERA below 2.00 before struggling Friday night at Minute Maid Park against the Astros. Pomeranz pitched well against the Giants in a previous start.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell was ruled out of contention for the rotation in mid-March, but pitched his way back into the mix. Claimed off waivers by the Astros last year, Harrell went 0-2 with a 3.46 ERA in six games (two starts) for Houston.
away_pitcher_note: The 49-year-old Moyer made an inspiring comeback from elbow surgery in 2010 while he was with the Phillies. Moyer signed a Minor League contract during the winter and went 2-1 with a 2.50 ERA in Cactus League action. His arm and body were fine.

home_pitcher_note: Norris is beginning his third full season in the Major Leagues and is eager to establish himself. He was inconsistent last year with the Astros, going 6-11 with a 3.77 ERA in 31 starts with 176 strikeouts in 186 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio, 25, was going through the normal rookie highs and lows before the Nationals' Ian Desmond hit a line drive off Nicasio's head that resulted in a broken neck. Nicasio won a job and became a heartwarming story with a fine spring performance.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin, 24, held opponents to a .231 batting average, and his ERA last year was third lowest in club history. The Rox believe he can become a star if he achieves pitch efficiency. He went 1-2 with a 3.38 ERA in three starts vs. the Giants in 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie's veteran poise made the difference in his seven-inning winning effort against the Astros in Friday night's season opener. Guthrie gave up consecutive home runs in the fourth, but held serve. This will be his first career appearance at Coors.
away_pitcher_note: In 10 career starts at Coors Field, Lincecum has reached double figures in strikeouts just once -- last April 18, when he allowed one run and three hits in 7 2/3 innings as the Giants triumphed, 8-1. Colorado also was the site of Lincecum's first Major League victory on May 11, 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer gave up two home runs and four runs (three earned) in five innings. Three errors in the fourth inning drove up Moyer's pitch count. He missed with some close pitches in the first inning for balls, but was competitive.
away_pitcher_note: Though Bumgarner's career is clearly on the upswing, his lifetime numbers are intriguing. He currently owns a 20-20 career record, including 9-9 at home and 11-11 on the road. His day-night splits are almost as balanced. Bumgarner is 7-8 in day games and 13-12 under the lights.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio struck out four and held Houston to one run and five hits over seven innings, but he didn't get a decision in his return from injury Sunday. He relied on his fastball and can really be effective if he works in his slider at the right times.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson got the win against the Giants last Saturday when he allowed four runs in 6 2/3 innings. The outing took a turn with two outs in the seventh when he allowed a two-run homer to Brett Pill. He was 1-2 with a 3.72 ERA against the Rockies in 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin threw 90 pitches and issued five walks in four innings of his initial 2012 start, a 7-0 loss to the Giants in the home opener. A mechanical issue of his body getting ahead of his arm arose and robbed him of arm-side command.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter suffered through a tough spring and his woes continued into his first regular-season start. He allowed six runs (five earned) in three innings last Sunday against the Giants. The D-backs think Collmenter may have been pressing.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies had Pomeranz throw four innings for Double-A Tulsa on Tuesday as a tuneup. He didn't give up a run, although he had problems controlling the movement of his fastball. The Rockies will be careful with Pomeranz, a rookie, all season.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill had an odd start in his first outing with the D-backs on Tuesday night. He walked six, but he managed to allow just one run over six innings and none of the walks wound up scoring. Cahill said he "had no idea" where the ball was going.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start at Coors Field, Guthrie had a 6-0 lead over the Giants and Tim Lincecum but gave up consecutive home runs to start the fourth and didn't last the inning as the Giants took a lead. His team bailed him out, however, and won, 17-8.
away_pitcher_note: Luebke got off to an bad start against Arizona in his last outing, walking four in a 43-pitch first inning. He settled down thereafter, striking out five and allowing four hits. After the first, he needed 40 pitches to get the next 12 outs.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer was hurt by a sixth-inning Dexter Fowler error and suffered a 4-2 loss to the Giants in his last start. Moyer threw 29 pitches in the first inning but went 5 1/3 and kept the Rockies close. The team has committed five errors in his two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bass, filling in for an injured Dustin Moseley, allowed one run on three hits on 4 1/3 innings against the D-backs on Thursday. He threw 88 pitches after being pegged to throw up to 90. Bass struck out five and walked two.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio's home debut was nothing like his season debut, when the held the Astros to one run in seven innings. Pitching at Coors for the first time since suffering a broken neck last Aug. 5, Nicasio gave up six runs and walked five in 2 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Richard retired the first six hitters he faced in his last start before allowing eight runs over the next two innings. Granted, four of those runs were unearned but Richard allowed six hits, including a two-run home run to Matt Kemp and four walks.

home_pitcher_note: Showing that his shoulder was healthy, Marcum threw 105 pitches in a hard-luck 2-1 loss to the Braves on Saturday in Atlanta. He allowed just three hits and had six strikeouts to two walks over seven innings in his second straight quality start.
away_pitcher_note: After a walk-filled meltdown in a home-opening loss to the Giants, Chacin corrected some delivery flaws in his last start. He held the D-backs to one run and four hits in four innings, but a rain delay ended his start.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada moves from the bullpen to pitch in place of injured lefty Chris Narveson. Estrada made seven Brewers starts last season with a 3.70 ERA in those games. He should be good for about 75 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz was consistently behind in counts in his debut, allowing five runs in 4 1/3 innings. He couldn't establish three pitches for strikes, avoiding his changeup as the D-backs laid off his curveball.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo fixed a rhythm issue and has turned in two encouraging starts since a clunker against the Cardinals on Opening Day. In his last two outings, he's allowed only three runs and 12 hits in 14 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie took the mound suffering from a sore throat -- strep was going around the clubhouse -- and gave up six runs and nine hits in seven innings of a 7-1 loss to the Padres at Coors Field. He settled down after being hit hard early.

home_pitcher_note: Correia was scratched from his start Saturday, but he insists his left side is fine. In his last outing on April 14 in a 4-1 victory over the Giants, he allowed one run on three hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer tossed seven innings Tuesday, allowing just two unearned runs on six hits to pick up his first win of the season. At 49 years of age, he became the oldest pitcher in Major League history to record a victory.

home_pitcher_note: Correia was scratched from his start Saturday, but he insists his left side is fine. In his last outing on April 14 in a 4-1 victory over the Giants, he allowed one run on three hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer tossed seven innings Tuesday, allowing just two unearned runs on six hits to pick up his first win of the season. At 49 years of age, he became the oldest pitcher in Major League history to record a victory.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald was removed after allowing one run and three hits in four innings on Wednesday against the Diamondbacks.
away_pitcher_note: In his second start at Coors Field since suffering a broken neck and fractured skull last Aug. 5, Nicasio picked up his first win of the year Wednesday. The right-hander tossed 6 1/3 innings, allowing four runs on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: Charlie Morton pitched well in a losing effort against the Cardinals on Friday, allowing just one earned run on four hits in five innings of work. He struck out six and walked three, though he needed 93 pitches to get through his five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Dominant through five innings on Friday vs. the Brewers, a rough sixth kept Chacin from getting his first win of the season. The right-hander retired the first 10 batters he faced, and allowed three runs on four hits over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough first outing of the season, Pomeranz held the Brewers to two runs on two hits and three outs in five innings, with six strikeouts, in his last start. The rookie left that game with a 3-2 lead, but the bullpen didn't hold it.
away_pitcher_note: The Mets are expected to promote Schwinden to start Friday's series opener against Colorado. Schwinden, 25 years old, has gone 2-2 with a 2.05 ERA in his first four starts for Triple-A Buffalo.

home_pitcher_note: Moscoso will start in place of Jeremy Guthrie, who went on the DL after a freaky bike accident. Moscoso went 1-3 with a 7.91 ERA in four Triple-A starts. He allowed 18 runs (17 earned) on 35 hits and four walks in 19 1/3 innings while fanning 19.
away_pitcher_note: Gee followed one of the best starts of his career with one of the worst, allowing seven runs and 12 hits -- including two homers and a triple -- to the Giants in 6 2/3 frames Monday at Citi Field. The righty has never faced the Rockies in 35 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer, the oldest player in baseball, has been the Rockies' best pitcher -- the only one to go at least five innings in each of his starts. Moyer held the Pirates to one run and six hits in six innings in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: In his sharpest start of the season, Santana fanned 11 Fish in 6 2/3 frames of one-run ball. That came after the shortest outing of his career, a four-out start in Atlanta. Santana will look for consistency at Coors Field, where he's never pitched.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio allowed one earned run over 6 1/3 innings in Wednesday's no-decision vs. the Pirates, scattering nine hits while walking one and striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: Harang fouled a pitch off the top of his left foot and the more it swelled, the worse he pitched against the Braves. X-rays were negative, but the Dodgers will be watching him closely to see if there are any lingering effects on that landing leg.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin allowed five earned runs on eight hits and two walks in Wednesday's Game 2 loss to the Pirates, fanning five batters over five shaky innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly has been superb through three starts, allowing just two earned runs through a combined 20 innings. He was a perfect 3-0 with a 2.66 ERA in four starts last year against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Pomeranz left Friday's game against the Mets with left forearm tightness after four innings but said he is fine and is not expected to miss any time.
away_pitcher_note: The reigning NL Cy Young winner has earned a victory in each of his past two outings after starting the year with three straight no-decisions. He tossed a season-best eight innings on Friday against the Nats.

home_pitcher_note: Moscoso was called up to pitch for Jeremy Guthrie on 24 hours notice. He had mixed results, pitching well to get good counts and early outs, but he yielded six runs on nine hits and a walk in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a strong five-inning effort in his season debut, Hudson will attempt to conquer Coors Field, where he is 0-2 with a 7.77 ERA in four starts. He surrendered just two runs in a seven-inning effort there last year, however.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer had a gutty performance Sunday, throwing five innings and 109 pitches, yielding four runs on 11 hits and two walks.  He stymied hitters and minimized damage after a three-run first.
away_pitcher_note: Minor surrendered two homers and a career-high seven runs against a struggling Pirates offense on Monday. He had allowed a total of four earned runs in his previous three starts, combined. This is his first career start against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio gave up two runs on nine hits -- one a Matt Kemp homer -- and struck out four in a win against the Dodgers on Monday night. He relied on his fastball, but to keep from becoming predictable, he used it on both sides of the plate.
away_pitcher_note: Beachy has worked into the seventh inning in four straight starts and allowed two earned runs or fewer in each of his five starts. Opponents are hitting .193 against him. He lasted 4 2/3 innings in his only Coors Field start.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez lowered his ERA to 2.92 with seven shutout innings against the Brewers in his last start. He's taken to a few mechanical refinements by pitching coach Darren Balsley to improve his command. He's still looking for his first Padres win.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz went a career-high 6 2/3 innings in his last start, a no-decision the Rockies eventually won vs. the Dodgers, by displaying outstanding fastball movement. He was especially effective with his developing cutter that shattered several bats.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan picked up his first Major League win since Oct. 3, 2010, when he tossed five shutout innings against the Brewers in his last start as a fill-in for an injured Cory Luebke. The 37-year-old allowed four hits with two walks and two strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note:
White struggled with the home run ball during a brief trial last year, allowing 12 in 36 1/3 innings, but a finger injury earlier in the year might have affected him. White honed his slider and used an effective changeup at Triple-A
Colorado Springs.

home_pitcher_note: It was a strange outing for Bass last time out. He allowed five runs in the first inning and then one run over his next five, finishing with seven strikeouts. He also got his first two big league hits, including a three-run triple.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies' top Draft pick in 2008, Friedrich has battled injuries throughout his career. However, working out with the Phillies' Cliff Lee during the winter helped him with conditioning and taught him to develop a more consistent downhill plane.

home_pitcher_note: Capuano might be the Dodgers' most pleasant surprise of the season. Signed to be the fifth starter, he leads the club in wins, crediting a new breaking ball he uses against right-handers.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer cruised for four innings against Atlanta, allowing one unearned run on 51 pitches. He gave up five runs on six hits in the fifth and sixth.The third time through the lineup was rough as the Braves found their timing.

home_pitcher_note: Harang's most recent quality start was overlooked in the tumult of the Dodgers' walk-off loss in Chicago, but he was able to pitch out of multiple jams and keep his team in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio had a setback after his six-inning, two-run win over the Dodgers. He gave up six runs in five-plus innings in a loss to the Braves. He struggled with fastball command and hung some breaking balls that hurt him.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly is pitching through a sore oblique with quality start after quality start. At 4-0, he's off to the best start of his career and is 7-0 with a 1.03 ERA going back to last season.
away_pitcher_note: White demonstrated smoother mechanics and a more explosive sinker and slider in a loss on Tuesday to the Padres, his first game since being called up from Triple-A Colorado Springs. White works in another pitcher's park.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong bested Dodgers ace Clayton Kershaw to record his first victory of the season last Tuesday. Vogelsong lasted at least six innings in 19 of his 28 starts last year but is 5-for-5 in that category this season.
away_pitcher_note: After a nervous first inning, Friedrich struck out seven and gave up two runs (one earned), while beating the Padres on Wednesday afternoon in his Major League debut. Friedrich was fearless with his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum excelled early in his previous start, striking out five of the first eight Dodgers he faced to finish with eight strikeouts in five innings. Lincecum has fared much better at home (3.79 ERA) than on the road (8.15).
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie, set to pitch for the first time since April 22, is coming off a right shoulder injury that he sustained in a bicycle accident. Guthrie has stayed out of the middle of the plate and stayed down in the zone in his two road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer's last couple of starts have taken a disturbing trend. He has been competent to good through the first four innings, but he hasn't pitched beyond five innings and has given up big innings.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin will be making his fourth Major League start. He picked up the win in his last start against the Giants, allowing one run on three hits over seven innings. Corbin had his contract selected from Double-A Mobile on April 30.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Nicasio struck out nine and held the Dodgers to one run in seven innings at Dodger Stadium. However, the Rockies didn't hit and lost, 2-1. He will have to rebound from his last start at Coors, a 7-2 loss to the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill walked the first batter he faced on four pitches, hit two batters in a row in the sixth and then gave up a two-run double to Giants starter Matt Cain in his last start. He struggled with command and the Giants made him pay for it.

home_pitcher_note: After pitching well for 6 1/3 innings at San Diego in his first start since being called up from Triple-A Colorado Springs, White faltered badly in the fifth against the Dodgers on Sunday. He wound up giving up six runs in 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood returns to face a Rockies team that he pitched nine games for at the end of last season. He's coming off his best start -- and first win -- of 2012 with seven innings of three-hit, one-run ball at Yankee Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Friedrich dominated the Giants on Monday, striking out 10 over seven innings while allowing one run on six hits and a walk, but he didn't factor into the decision.
away_pitcher_note: Vargas is coming off his first subpar outing of the year when his changeup went AWOL as the Red Sox got him for five runs and seven hits in a six-inning stint. He pitched twice at Coors Field while with the Mets and was 0-2 with an 18.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie gave up one run on four hits, walked four and struck out four in 5 1/3 innings in a no-decision against the Giants on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Beavan is coming off the two shortest starts of his career, a three-inning outing when he took a line drive off his elbow, followed by four innings in Boston when the Sox forced him to throw 93 pitches. He's walked just six batters in seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: For a change, Buehrle got plenty of run support in an 8-4 victory at Atlanta on Wednesday. He failed to register a quality start for just the second time in eight outings, allowing four earned runs on six hits. Buehrle struck out four and walked one.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer held the D-backs to just one run through 6 1/3 innings Wednesday on six hits and two walks with five strikeouts. With this start at the new Marlins Park, Moyer, 49, will make an appearance in the 50th ballpark of his Major League career.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco has lost his past two starts after winning his first four decisions. He allowed four runs in four innings vs. the Braves on Thursday after surrendering six runs to the Mets in 4 2/3 innings in his previous outing.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio walked five and lasted just 4 2/3 innings in his last start, a no-decision in a 9-7 loss to the D-backs. Nicasio was affected by a bruised right hip suffered on a first-inning line drive, but has recovered after receiving treatment.

home_pitcher_note: In his last four starts, Zambrano has been brilliant. He gave up two runs in seven innings in his last outing, a win at Cleveland, where he walked five. In his last four starts, Zambrano has an 0.90 ERA (three earned runs in 30 innings).
away_pitcher_note: White pitched well for seven innings, giving up three runs, two earned, with seven strikeouts and no walks against the Mariners on Friday night. But he was the hard-luck loser as the M's Kevin Millwood threw a two-hit shutout.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto is still off to the best start of his career and continues to pitch efficiently and induce ground-ball outs. Already on the leaderboard in overall ERA, he also has a 1.42 ERA when pitching at Great American Ball Park.
away_pitcher_note: Friedrich had two lights-out road performances after being called up from Triple-A Colorado Springs but struggled Saturday, giving up nine hits, four walks and eight runs to the Mariners at Coors Field. He's back on the road but in a tough park.

home_pitcher_note: Leake is on a roll with two strong starts in a row. He credits being more aggressive and attacking hitters to his recent resurgence. He worked a season-high eight innings on Monday vs. Atlanta for his first victory of 2012.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie gave up three homers and six runs in six innings against the Mariners in a loss Sunday. This will be Guthrie's fourth start on the road where he is 2-0 with a 1.86 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In Tuesday's win over the Braves, Latos worked seven innings for the first time since April 24 and had velocities of 95 mph in his final inning. He threw 116 pitches in the game, but avoided the laboriously long innings that have often cut him short.
away_pitcher_note: The 49-year-old Moyer had his worst outing of the season in Miami, going 3 2/3 innings and giving up six runs and nine hits on 100 pitches, including a fourth-inning slam to Giancarlo Stanton. The lefty also walked four and fanned five.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio struggled against the Marlins, admitting he felt tired through the first three innings. That fatigue cost him, as he lasted just five innings and gave up six runs (five earned) on nine hits while walking three and striking out six in a loss.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez spun a seven-inning gem on Wednesday, striking out five and holding the Cubs to one run on eight hits without issuing a walk to earn his fourth win.

home_pitcher_note: White didn't have his best stuff against the Marlins, but it was good enough to help end the Rockies' six-game skid and get his first win since September. He tossed six innings and gave up four runs on eight hits while surrendering just one walk.

The rookie southpaw has six-plus strikeouts in three of four career starts. He cruised through the first three innings against the Reds in his last start, but labored afterward. He has walked one or fewer hitters in three of his four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell threw 94 pitches on Friday night in Los Angeles, but not one was a swing and a miss. No matter. Harrell, who prefers to pitch to contact, worked 7 1/3 innings, recording 17 ground-ball outs and allowing just one run.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie has allowed multiple home runs in four of seven starts this season, including five in his last two outings. He has allowed six earned runs in three of his starts, but did fan five Reds on Saturday while walking just one -- a season low.
away_pitcher_note: Norris has been brilliant in May, allowing just four earned runs in five starts, but his last outing was easily his worst of the month. Without his best breaking stuff, Norris lasted just 4 2/3 innings against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Outman will be the spot-starter, tasked with throwing about 50 pitches in order to get stretched out for more opportunities down the road. He's 8-7 as a starter, with a 3.78 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Capuano earned the win Sunday against Houston, allowing only one run in seven innings. In six appearances, the lefty has a 2.94 ERA at Coors Field, the third-lowest in the stadium's history for pitchers with five starts.

home_pitcher_note: On the heels of two encouraging starts, Nicasio regressed against Houston, giving up five earned runs on nine hits to pick up the no-decision in the Rockies' win on Monday. His command of his fastball and secondary pitches is still inconsistent.
away_pitcher_note: Harang took his first loss in nearly a month on Monday against the Brewers. He lasted five innings, giving up three runs, only one of which was earned. A questionable call at first base in the sixth led to trouble for the big right-hander.

home_pitcher_note: White, a First-round Draft pick in 2009, suffered the worst start of his young career against the Astros, allowing career-highs in hits (10) and home runs (3), and tying a high with six runs allowed. White was lucky to depart with the no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Eovaldi was outdueled by another rookie, the Brewers' Michael Fiers, in his first start of the year Tuesday. Despite the loss, the highly touted prospect showed promise in seven innings, surrendering two runs on four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders took the loss in his last start against the Giants though he deserved a better fate. Saunders allowed one run over 5 1/3 innings as the D-backs fell, 3-1. This will be his first start against the Rockies this year.
away_pitcher_note: Friedrich had his ups and downs in a 13-5 win over Houston, surrendering four runs in the third inning but also striking out six. He averages 6.4 strikeouts per contest.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy threw a career-high 122 pitches in beating the Giants in his last start. He allowed one run on five hits over 7 1/3 innings to earn the win. It snapped a five-start losing streak. This will be his first start against the Rockies in 2012.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie lived up to his innings-eater reputation against the Astros on May 31, pitching a full seven, though he did give up five earned runs. Guthrie's better on the road, where he has a 2-1 record and 2.22 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Miley pitched better than his numbers indicated last time out against the Padres. He allowed three hits and one run through seven innings before the Padres scored six runs in the eighth. Miley began year in the 'pen before joining the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Outman had a pitch count of 50 in his first start, but the former reliever expects that to be around 70 as he continues to stretch his arm out. Against the Dodgers on Friday, Outman went 3 1/3 scoreless innings, striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: White turned in his best game as a Rockie on Sunday against the Dodgers, going 6 2/3 innings and giving up two runs on a career-low two hits. In 2011, White held the Angels -- who have since made some nice additions -- to three runs.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson is 2-0 over his last three starts, during which he's given up just one run while striking out 17 in 20 innings (good for a 0.45 ERA). He has never faced the Rockies, but is 3-5 with a 4.10 ERA against the National League in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Francis returns to the Rockies, the team he led to the 2007 World Series. He is coming off some encouraging outings for the Reds' Triple-A club in Louisville; his last outing was a complete-game shutout. He went 2-0 against the Angels last year.
away_pitcher_note: Haren gave up two runs in a no-decision against the Rangers on Sunday, but was mighty inefficient, throwing 104 pitches while giving up seven hits and two walks in five innings. He has a 3.80 ERA in seven career starts at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Friedrich dominated the D-backs in Monday's win, allowing just four hits and two walks with four punchouts across seven scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Santana's struggles reached a new level against the Mariners on Monday, when he gave up seven runs on eight hits and six walks in 4 2/3 innings. He has given up 16 runs and walked 14 batters over his last three starts, which span 14 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie struck out four but was roughed up for seven runs on 11 hits and two walks in just 3 1/3 innings in a losing effort last Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Colon was masterful his last time out against the Rangers, keeping baseball's best offense off the board over eight innings. His effort helped shut out the Rangers for the first time all season, and Colon snapped a two-start losing streak as well.

home_pitcher_note: Outman gave up five runs and seven hits in just three innings in his last start, a loss at Arizona, when he was held to 55 pitches. Outman, working with about 90 pitches, will see if he is stretched out enough to be effective vs. his former team.
away_pitcher_note: Milone will have to be cautious in the hitter-friendly confines of Coors Field, having given up nine homers on the road, where he's 2-4 with a 6.35 ERA, compared to one at home. He gave up four runs on nine hits in five innings in Arizona on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: White was effective for six innings Friday vs. the Angels, except for two pitches -- a fastball and a slider that Torii Hunter hit for a pair of two-run homers. In his last 12 2/3 innings, the only runs off White have come on three two-run homers.
away_pitcher_note: Parker was roughed up by the D-backs in a loss on Saturday, striking out four but allowing six runs on eight hits and five walks in five innings. He had held opponents to one run over his previous 21 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers used Monday's off-day to push back Crosby's start a few days, slotting him back home, where his two previous starts have taken place. He beat Cleveland with 5 1/3 innings of three-run ball June 7, but has had off-and-on trouble with walks.
away_pitcher_note: Francis' return to the Rockies, after spending last year with the Royals and beginning this year in Triple-A with the Reds, saw him allow eight runs in 3 1/3 innings in a loss to the Angels. Last year, Francis was 0-2 against Detroit with a 2.21 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Fister will be activated from the disabled list to return once again from the left side strain that has bothered him for most of the season. He had four quality starts in May before the Red Sox hit him for six runs on 11 hits in five innings May 28.
away_pitcher_note: Friedrich was hit hard in his second loss Sunday vs. the Angels, giving up nine runs (eight earned) on 10 hits and three walks with five strikeouts in four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer allowed three earned runs Tuesday against the Cubs for the third time in his last four starts. Unlike those two previous times, he left with a no-decision rather than a win.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie, who has given up 19 runs in his past three starts, is running out of chances to prove he can be an effective member of the Rockies rotation. He is much better away from Coors Field, though, with a 4.23 road ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels has blown two three-run leads and nearly blew a six-run lead in his last three starts, including Wednesday's 9-8 victory over the Twins at Target Field. Hamels has a 6.08 ERA in his last four starts, so he is hoping for a rebound.
away_pitcher_note: Outman was in position to win his last start, when he battled through his team's sloppy defense and gave up five runs and six hits in five innings of the Rockies' eventual 10-8 loss to the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton's 9.91 ERA from May 19-June 13 was the worst in baseball, but he pitched his second complete game of the season on Thursday in a 6-1 victory over the Twins at Target Field. He hopes to build off that success against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: White developed a finger blister early in his last start and was pulled after giving up four runs, two earned, and seven hits in four innings of an 8-2 home loss to the Athletics. White said he is fine. He'll have to trim walks (five the last game).

home_pitcher_note: Worley was a hard-luck loser his last time out, getting no runs of support over seven innings. The 24-year-old dropped to 3-3 on the year but lowered his ERA to 2.80 -- tops in the rotation. This will be his first career start against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: After being rocked for 10 hits and eight runs in his Rockies season debut, Francis gutted out five innings and gave up four runs Friday night in Detroit. He did not get a decision, but the game ended a losing streak at eight.

home_pitcher_note: After making four Minor League starts, Oswalt is set for his Rangers debut. He gave up two runs in six innings while picking up a win in his last start with Triple-A Round Rock. Oswalt is 8-2 with a 1.94 ERA in 12 career starts vs. the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Friedrich heads into this game with a 2.10 ERA on the road, but there is a sign of trouble. In his last two starts, losses at home against the Angels and on the road against the Tigers, he did not have good location on his curveball or changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis has won each of his last two starts, posting quality starts in his last four outings and going 2-2 with a 1.76 ERA this month. He is 3-0 with a 1.13 ERA in Interleague Play this year and will make his first career appearance vs. the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Outman was the first to pitch after manager Jim Tracy implemented his four-man rotation, so he will be pitching on just three days' rest. He reached his pitch count in just 4 1/3 innings in his last start, surrendering four runs on five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison tied the AL lead with his ninth win in his last start, giving up six hits and one run in a 2-1 win over the Padres. He is 5-0 with a 1.82 ERA in his last seven starts and 2-0 with a 0.40 ERA in three Interleague starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: White's command was erratic in his last start against Philadelphia. The young right-hander gave up five runs on five hits in just 3 2/3 innings, leading manager Jim Tracy to describe his starter's performance as just "so-so."

home_pitcher_note: Francis' performance against the Phillies pleased his manager, as the veteran left-hander was efficient through five innings and surrendered just one run, which came on a first-inning solo home run off the bat of Jimmy Rollins.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg threw 111 pitches in his last start on Wednesday against the Rays, the second-most of the season. He was once again dominant, though, striking out 10 while walking two and allowing two earned runs on five hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: It's back home for Friedrich, where he is 1-2 with a 12.60 ERA. Friedrich hasn't won a game since June 4 -- with a 75-pitch limit, the streak may not snap -- and has since yielded 14 earned runs in 15 home innings, with a .339 average against.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez took a while to get going in his last start Thursday night against the Rays, throwing 50 pitches through two innings. He settled down eventually, holding Tampa Bay to two earned runs on seven hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cabrera, 24, led the Minors last year with 174 strikeouts at two Class A stops, and has fanned 82 in 91 innings at Double-A Tulsa this year. The Rockies decided not to restore Jeremy Guthrie to the rotation or recall Drew Pomeranz from Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann has been the recipient of only 3.3 runs of support per start, second fewest among Nats starters. Friday vs. the O's, he struggled with command but allowed only two runs on eight hits in 7 IP. Of course, he only received one run of support.

home_pitcher_note: Outman was painfully close to his first win on Saturday, but exited with two out in the fifth -- then was charged with five earned, insult to injury after holding the Rangers to one run through four. The 92 pitches were the most he's thrown all year.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson took a perfect game into the fifth inning of his last start on Saturday vs. the Orioles, though his pitch count rose quickly not long after. He allowed one run on four hits in 6 1/3 innings, striking out five batters while walking just one.

away_pitcher_note: Volquez had one of his strongest starts of the season last time out, going 6 2/3 scoreless innings against the Mariners. He threw 115 pitches, a season high. The right-hander hasn't given up a homer in his last three outings.

home_pitcher_note: The key figure in the Ubaldo Jimenez trade with the Indians last summer, Pomeranz has been retooling his motion and regaining velocity on his fastball for nine starts at Triple-A Colorado Springs. Sunday's game will be his return to the bigs.
away_pitcher_note: Wells went five innings on Tuesday, giving up five runs (two earned), striking out two and walking two. The right-hander threw 100 pitches, 60 for strikes, in his first Major League appearance since 2009.

away_pitcher_note: Outman struggled with a big lead for his second consecutive start, squandering a seven-run lead in a five-run third inning, his last. After retiring the game's first six batters, he lost his command and allowed five hits and a walk in the third.

home_pitcher_note: Kelly registered his second straight quality start, and manager Mike Matheny called it Kelly's best outing. He pitched six innings of two-run ball in Miami, but didn't factor into the decision.
away_pitcher_note: Francis has fashioned a 1.69 ERA in his last three starts and the Rockies have won his last four. He is mixing his 86-88 mph fastball with a slow curve that sometimes comes in at 68 mph. His last start he went six shutout innings with 82 pitches.

away_pitcher_note: Guthrie started on Opening Day and beat the Astros, but times have been tough since. This will be his 12th start of the season and his first since giving up four runs -- three earned -- on eight hits in three innings in a loss at Detroit on June 17.

away_pitcher_note: Friedrich held the Padres to one run and five hits, and struck out five against zero walks at Coors Field in his last start before the bullpen blew his lead. Friedrich has improved his efficiency while pitching in a four-man rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg had difficulty pitching in record Atlanta temperatures in his last start, laboring through three innings and leaving with heat-related issues. It's supposed to be hot again Friday in Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz regained velocity and downward power on his fastball during nine starts at Triple-A Colorado Springs, and he held the Padres to one unearned run in six innings on Sunday afternoon in his return.

home_pitcher_note: The All-Star kept the Braves at bay in his last start and was good enough to earn his third straight win. Gonzalez has only ever faced the Rockies a mile above sea level in Denver.
away_pitcher_note: Francis limited the Cardinals to two runs in five innings while throwing 77 pitches on Tuesday night. The Rockies have won the last five games started by Francis, who has made the four-starter, pitch-limit system work for him.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann continues to quietly put together an excellent season. He struck out seven Giants in a rain-shortened six innings on Tuesday, dropping his season ERA to 2.70, best in the Nats' rotation.

away_pitcher_note: Lee downplayed its importance to reporters, but he picked up his first win of the season in his 14th start of 2012 on July 4 against the Mets at Citi Field. Lee is hoping for a much better second half than first half, which was a big disappointment.

home_pitcher_note: In each of his two starts since rejoining the rotation, Guthrie has allowed just two runs on six hits over six innings. His last start was on Sunday, the last game before the All-Star break.

home_pitcher_note: Pomeranz held the Nationals scoreless on one hit in 6 1/3 innings in his last start while earning his first win. He has held opponents to one unearned run in two starts since being recalled from Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: Could this be one of Hamels' last starts for the Phillies? They could trade him before the July 31 Trade Deadline if the Phillies decide to be sellers. That's a definite possibility with the way they played in the first half.

home_pitcher_note: Francis pitched well in his last start on a blistering day at Washington, but he saw the two runners who were on base when he departed score because of sloppy defense, taking the loss. He has been the team's most consistent starter.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens had his best outing since being on the disabled list for two months on July 5, pitching eight scoreless innings, allowing four hits and walking just one batter. He also registered a season-high eight strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Friedrich outdueled Cliff Lee in his last start, giving up one run in six innings against the Phillies. The win, his first since early June, gave him more than any Rockies pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard is winless in his last five starts, recording four losses and a no-decision since June 8. He gave up four or more runs in each of his last three outings, including when he went just 3 2/3 innings on July 6.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie has struggled mightily at Coors Field this year, with a 9.23 ERA and 12 homers given up. In his last home start, against the Phillies, he gave up four runs in 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald struggled in his last outing, going just 4 2/3 innings and matching a season high with five walks. He surrendered four earned runs on eight hits and struck out two batters after striking out 10 in his prior start.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis got off to a rough start his last time out, allowing a first-inning run to the Dodgers. He settled down thereafter, allowing one more run over the next five innings. Marquis walked three (two intentionally) and struck out two.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz gave up five runs in five innings in his last start against the Phillies, but he'll be glad to face the Padres. In his last outing against them on July 1, he allowed just one unearned run in six innings, while yielding two hits.

home_pitcher_note: Wells struggled through 4 1/3 innings in his last outing, a loss to the Astros. Wells yielded two runs, walked five and accumulated several 3-2 counts. The outing was his shortest of four starts with the Padres this season.
away_pitcher_note: Francis held the Pirates to one run in five innings, but didn't get the win as the game was decided in the bottom of the ninth. Francis has a 2.57 ERA in his last four games, including a three-hit outing against the Padres June 29.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf was strong in six innings of work Tuesday night against the Astros, scattering six hits and striking out six while giving up just one earned run. It was his longest outing of the year in seven appearances, three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Friedrich was done in by a bad fifth inning against the Pirates, walking two, giving up four hits and tossing a wild pitch, resulting in a four-run frame. The good news: he was brilliant last time at Chase Field, throwing seven scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy tied his season high, tossing eight innings Wednesday in Cincinnati. He allowed just one run on eight hits and threw first-pitch strikes to 23 of the 33 batters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez arrived in a trade with the Royals for righty Jeremy Guthrie on Friday. After struggling in the American League, Sanchez returns to the NL West, where he was productive with the Giants 2006-11.

away_pitcher_note: In his big league debut on June 27, the 24-year-old lefty gave up seven runs (five earned) in 2 1/3 innings against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill continued his first-inning struggles in his most recent outing, against the Astros, despite earning the win. In surrendering two early runs, the 24-year-old increased his season total in the opening frame to 16 earned runs over 19 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Francis gave up five runs in five innings in his last start, at San Diego, but left the game with the lead, although he didn't figure in the decision. Francis had given up three or fewer runs his previous six starts.

home_pitcher_note: After suffering left arm soreness during his last start Friday night in San Diego, Pomeranz missed his scheduled outing Tuesday but will return to the mound Friday night. He allowed seven runs in three innings against the Padres in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo notched a win after allowing two earned runs on five hits and two walks with six strikeouts over six innings against the Brewers on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Over his past six starts, Friedrich's outings have alternated between good and bad. In his three stellar starts, he tossed 16 combined innings and gave up just four runs. On the other hand, in the poor outings he surrendered 15 runs over 13 1/3.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto went seven innings against the Brewers on Sunday, giving up eight hits and one earned run, striking out nine and walking one in a win.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez's Rockies debut didn't go well, the lefty allowed five earned runs over four innings and took the loss against the D-backs, 6-3. Sunday will be his first home game for his new team after being traded last week by Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Latos sprained his left ankle during his start against the Astros on Monday, but should be ready to start Sunday. The right-hander gave up two runs on eight hits in five innings, throwing 95 pitches and earning his eighth win.

home_pitcher_note: Francis was sharp in a win against Arizona on July 25, yielding two runs on five hits in six innings. In his 10 starts, Francis has given up more than three runs just three times.

home_pitcher_note: Pomeranz pitched well in his start against the Reds but was done in by a two-run fourth inning and an offense that offered no help -- the fourth time in 10 starts he has received zero run support.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook ran into some trouble in his last start -- a four-run fifth inning by Los Angeles -- but bounced back for his second straight win and third straight start of at least seven innings. He owns a 3.19 ERA in nine starts on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: White struggled with efficiency in his stint with the Rockies earlier this season, but Colorado hopes White can repeat his work in his last two starts at Triple-A Colorado Springs -- one run, eight hits and 10 strikeouts over 15 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn allowed a season-high six runs on Friday vs. the Cubs after giving up only one run in his first 13 innings out of the All-Star break. Lynn wasn't too critical of his location, citing pitch selection as the bigger culprit.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez was shelled in his first home start, leaving the game after allowing six runs -- two homers -- in 4 1/3 innings. Sanchez will face his former team for the first time since being traded to the Royals for Melky Cabrera in November.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong extended his streak to 16 straight quality starts in his last outing, giving up two runs (one earned) in six innings against the Dodgers. He lowered his season ERA to 2.22, the lowest among qualified pitchers as of that start.

home_pitcher_note: Francis endured his toughest start since his season debut on June 9, giving up five runs in four innings in a loss to the Cardinals, including four runs to the first four batters of the game. It was the lefty's first loss since July 7.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner allowed two runs in six innings last Monday and has struck out 26 batters in his last three starts. He is 2-2 with a 2.84 ERA in four career starts at Coors Field and earned a win there April 12 after allowing one run in 7 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Capuano had as much trouble with the Arizona lineup as Aaron Harang, allowing home runs to Paul Goldschmidt and Miguel Montero. He's lost five of his last six decisions and there is concern he's tiring.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz pitched without his best stuff against the Cardinals Thursday, giving up three runs in his first two innings before settling down for two more effective innings.  His erratic control raised his pitch count and forced an early exit.

home_pitcher_note: After containing the Cardinals in St. Louis, Harang was roughed up at home by the D-backs, with Paul Goldschmidt and Chris Johnson slugging home runs.  He's lost three of his last five decisions.
away_pitcher_note: White was strong in his first start since his recall from Triple-A. He shut out the Cards for five innings, while recording 12 ground balls, thanks to a new changeup and reclaimed control and consistency. White yielded two runs in the sixth.
