away_pitcher_note: After a six-game stretch when he only once yielded as many as three runs, Francis is now in a four-game stretch of giving up five or six. He had a good curve against the Giants on Saturday, but left too many balls up in the zone, lasting just 3 2/3.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum allowed two earned runs over 13 innings in his last two starts, having back-to-back quality starts for the third time this year. Prior to his last two outings, Lincecum was 1-3 in his previous five with an ERA of 6.84.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood was effective with a live fastball and good breaking ball when he was in the strike zone Sunday, but he wasn't in the zone enough, walking four and allowing three runs (one earned) in 3 1/3 innings before hitting Colorado's 75-pitch target.

home_pitcher_note: Cain was spurned late in his last start, allowing a three-run sixth inning to St. Louis to lose back-to-back starts for just the second time this year. He also went less than six innings in two consecutive outings for the first time this year.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz kept the Dodgers' bats in check during his last start, holding them to just three hits in four innings. Getting timely outs when he needed it, the left-hander also struck out seven and walked three.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Zito finished an out shy of going seven innings for the third time in his last five starts and didn't walk a batter for the second time this year. He allowed two runs for his third quality start in his last five outings.
away_pitcher_note: In two starts since making his return to the Rockies' rotation, White has allowed just two runs in 9 1/3 innings. He pitched four innings of one-hit ball against the Dodgers in his last time out, though he did equal a season high with five walks.

home_pitcher_note: Francis is 0-3 with a 10.80 ERA, allowing 19 hits and four home runs in 11 2/3 innings in his last three starts. He gave up an early three-run homer to LA's Matt Kemp in his last start, but pitched better before being removed due to the pitch limit.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers threw six perfect innings on Tuesday against the Reds before giving up a hit in the seventh. He surrendered three hits and one run in eight innings, extending his streak of allowing two runs or fewer to nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Getting ahead of hitters more often than in his previous Major League work, Chatwood threw five scoreless innings in the Rockies' 3-0 shutout of the Giants on Friday night. He still could reach a higher efficiency level, however.
away_pitcher_note: Although Wolf didn't earn the win on Wednesday, he did snap a two-start losing streak by throwing six innings and allowing just two runs on six hits. It marked the first time the Brewers won with Wolf starting since July 17.

home_pitcher_note: Moscoso was called up from Triple-A to start in place of lefty Drew Pomeranz, who is battling soreness in his chest. Moscoso has to break a bad habit of falling behind hitters at the Major League level to be effective.
away_pitcher_note: Twice in his three starts, Rogers has been in line for his first Major League win and lost it to a John Axford blown save. Rogers' last outing in Houston was impressive nonetheless, including a career-high eight strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: White didn't figure in the decision Sunday at San Francisco. He gave up three runs on seven hits in four innings, but pitched better than that. A botched rundown helped set up two of the three first-inning runs the Giants scored.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco was far from his best against the Dodgers, yet he still managed to get his first win since July 6 and snap a streak of losses in five straight starts. He threw five innings and scattered nine hits and one walk, but surrendered just two runs.

home_pitcher_note: After slumping for three starts, Francis was effective for five innings in a win over the Brewers at Coors Field on Monday night. Francis baffled the Brewers' hitters with his changeup and his cut fastball.
away_pitcher_note: LeBlanc was effective in his last start. The problem was, he was matched against a guy flirting with a no-hitter. Chris Capuano allowed two hits in eight innings, and LeBlanc yielded one run in seven in a loss to the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood showed an explosive fastball and did a good job of getting ahead in the count in pitching six innings in a win against the Brewers on Tuesday night. Chatwood has won his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Eovaldi labored and struggled with command, walking three and allowing eight hits over five innings in a loss to the Phils on Monday. He allowed three runs, two of which were earned. He is 0-2 with a 6.52 ERA in two career starts vs. Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Pomeranz was skipped for his last start after yielding four runs on six hits in four innings in San Francisco. Though his offspeed pitches were effective, he struggled to keep the ball down and is still working on repeating his delivery.
away_pitcher_note: Despite taking a tough-luck loss, JJ stayed hot. In eight innings he allowed just one run -- a solo shot to lead off the game -- on three hits while fanning seven. Over his last five starts he has a 1.60 ERA and has held opponents to a .161 average.

home_pitcher_note: Though the Mets have moved to a six-man rotation, Dickey will continue to start every fifth game as the others slot around him. That puts him in line to pitch Monday against the Rockies, after giving up a season-high three home runs to the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: White was effective against the Marlins, but lack of command and confidence with a strong sinker had the rookie running himself out of the game with 74 pitches in four innings. He gave up two runs on three hits and three walks (one intentional).

away_pitcher_note: Chacin threw seven innings of one-run ball in a Triple-A rehab start Thursday, improving to 1-1 with a 2.63 ERA in two Sky Sox starts. On the DL since May 6, he'll rejoin the Rockies' rotation in New York.

away_pitcher_note: After allowing a run in the first inning against the Marlins, Francis went 3 1/3 more frames without a ball leaving the infield. He pitched well, but a curveball that just missed its location resulted in a three-run shot in his fifth and final frame.

home_pitcher_note: Rookie right-hander Collin McHugh will take the place of Johan Santana, who was shut down for lower back inflammation. McHugh went 2-2 with a 2.45 ERA, 52 strikeouts and 19 walks over his final nine outings for Triple-A Buffalo.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood was roughed up for six runs in the first 1 2/3 innings against the Marlins when he was up in the zone, but after identifying the issue, he was able to relax, make adjustments, settle in and follow with 2 1/3 effective innings.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija is coming off a loss to the Reds in which he gave up four runs over five innings. He will be happy to be back at Wrigley, where he's 4-3 with a 3.36 ERA in 10 starts. This has been a tough month: He's 1-3 with a 4.07 ERA in August.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz battled through four innings and 76 pitches without good command Sunday, his fifth straight start of four innings or more.  He allowed just two runs (one earned) on three hits and four walks (one intentional) while striking out three.

home_pitcher_note: Raley is coming off his first Major League win, holding the Reds to four runs over 5 1/3 innings on Saturday. He posted a quality start in his only outing at Wrigley Field on Aug. 12.
away_pitcher_note: White gave up one run on just three hits to the Mets on Monday, but a 29-pitch first inning led to his departure after just four innings and 83 pitches. White has lowered his season ERA by nearly a point since rejoining the Rockies on Aug. 2.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa hasn't given up a run in his past two starts, victories over the Yankees and Cardinals. His scoreless streak is 14 innings -- three shy of his career best during a 16-win season in 2009.

away_pitcher_note: Lincecum bounced back after a pair of rough outings to throw seven innings of two-run ball vs. the Braves in his last start. The righty, who struck out seven to earn his third win of the season, has struck out at least six in five straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio's last start showed greater efficiency than previous ones. He went six innings for the first time since April 3, but the Cubs touched him up for five runs and five extra-base hits in the first two innings.

home_pitcher_note: Garland, whose experience helped the Rockies in the early going, has lost his last three starts. He wasn't shelled in any of them, and in two of them, the opposing starter pitched well.
away_pitcher_note: Perhaps one of the biggest untold stories this season, Corbin has begun 2013 by tossing at least six innings and allowing two runs or fewer in each of his first eight starts. His ERA ranks third in Majors behind only Matt Harvey and Clayton Kershaw.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin squandered a 6-0 lead vs. the Giants, allowing eight runs on nine hits in 5 1/3 innings.  He lost his aggressiveness and command in a five-run fourth, walking in a run and yielding a two-out RBI single to the pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy got back in the win column in his last start as he allowed three runs over five innings against the Braves. It was his first win since Opening Day. Kennedy is 0-1 against the Rockies this year with a 4.50 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After not yielding a hit in the first 6 2/3 innings against the Cards in his previous start, De La Rosa gave up four in the first two innings to the Giants and five overall. But he won, and will strive for better location this time.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill has been on a roll over his past five starts, compiling a 1.36 ERA to go with a 3-1 record. The only blemish for him has been his inability to be consistent with his command as he's walked 16 batters in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum has allowed six runs, tying a personal season high, in each of his previous outings this year against Colorado. He has made 25 career starts against Colorado, more than any other opponent.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood, in his second callup from Triple-A Colorado Springs, held the Giants to one run in 5 2/3 innings in a win Saturday. He has given up three or fewer runs in nine of his 11 career starts against NL West foes.

away_pitcher_note: Nicasio relied heavily on his fastball and found his secondary stuff was more effective than in previous outings Sunday afternoon, when he threw six innings during a 5-0 victory over the Giants at Coors Field.

away_pitcher_note: Garland has dropped four of his last five starts. His last outing saw him yield five runs on 11 hits against the D-backs. Some were grounders that found holes, but there was also some solid contact on pitches up in the zone.

home_pitcher_note: Norris shut out the Royals through six innings in his last outing, but he tweaked a lingering back issue that could have him questionable for Monday. Norris is 3-1 with a 1.93 ERA in six home starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin has had an eventful last two starts. He blew a six-run lead against the Giants, then took a shutout into the seventh only to give up four and end up with a no-decision against the D-backs. Still, flashes are there.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles lowered his ERA by more than a run and earned the win with six innings of one-run ball against the Royals last time out. Right-handers are batting .327 against him in 2013.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa battled through constant traffic for 5 1/3 innings, but struck out five, forced eight ground balls and gave up just one run in a 4-1 victory over the D-backs. He threw a season-high 103 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Chatwood handled the Giants for the second straight time, this time going six innings in a 5-0 win. Chatwood has expertly mixed his fastball and curve since being promoted from Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard escaped a rough first inning his last time out against the A's and stood in line for the win until the Astros blew a late 5-3 lead. Bedard has an 8.83 ERA in five road starts this year.

away_pitcher_note: The Astros' most consistent starting pitcher a year ago, Harrell has been hit or miss this season. Recently, it's been more miss than hit. He's 0-3 with a 7.90 ERA in his past three starts and lasted just 1 2/3 innings Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: After a strong April, Garland has slumped. He ran into bad luck with a couple of defensive mishaps with two outs in his last start, a loss at San Francisco, but gave up five runs, two earned, on seven hits and four walks in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw was charged with four earned runs over seven innings in his last outing against the Cardinals, ending a streak of 22 consecutive starts in which he allowed three earned runs or fewer. He's 3-3 with a 5.91 ERA in 10 career starts at Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin tossed seven innings and allowed two runs in his last start against the Astros, throwing only 82 pitches. Chacin has logged at least five innings in all of his previous starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke has been unable to record an out in the fifth inning in each of his last two outings, both against former teams. The right-hander is 1-1 with a 6.75 ERA in three starts since returning from a broken left collarbone.

away_pitcher_note: With Hyun-Jin Ryu scratched because of a bruised left foot, Magill was recalled from Triple-A Albuquerque to make the start. He has four starts for the Dodgers this year, all no-decisions, all games the Dodgers eventually lost.

away_pitcher_note: Chatwood proved his 3-0 mark in 2013 was more than a fluke with a career-high 10 strikeouts against the Astros on Wednesday. In six innings, he gave up just two earned runs and walked one.

away_pitcher_note: Nicasio had a 3-1 lead through five innings Friday vs. the Astros, but was fighting without the stuff he had his previous two starts. Four hits and four runs in the sixth doomed him to a loss. It was his first bad inning in the last 22.

home_pitcher_note: Villarreal is making a spot start for Johnny Cueto, who was placed on the 15-day DL, retroactive to Saturday, with a strained right shoulder.
away_pitcher_note: Garland hasn't won since May 4. The numbers were dicey in the last start -- five runs, seven hits in five innings of a no-decision against the Dodgers -- but many of the hits were grounders that found holes.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin took a-no decision in his last start against the Dodgers after giving up five earned runs, nine hits and two walks in six innings. He also struck out two, but his ERA grew to 4.26 as he remained without a win since April 19.
away_pitcher_note: Cashner had won his past three decisions before losing to the Mariners in his last start. He still pitched six innings and threw a career-high 105 pitches, allowing seven hits -- including three solo home runs -- and four runs.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa will try to improve to 6-0 since May 7 after the Dodgers scored two runs on him in seven innings. He has given up two runs or fewer in his last three starts and his 3.10 ERA is lowest among Rockies starters.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez smacked a three-run blast for his first career home run in his last start against Toronto. He didn't have the same success on the mound, struggling with his breaking ball as he allowed four runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Healed from a left groin strain, Francis was activated from the 15-day DL to make the start. Through eight starts this season -- the most recent a six-inning, one-run outing against the Cubs on May 14 -- Francis is 2-3 with a 6.00 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The Padres most reliable pitcher for much of the season, Stults has been especially efficient over his last four starts, averaging less than 13 pitches per inning. Not coincidentally, he's lowered his ERA by almost a point during that time.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio was hurt by balls that skittered down the third-base line, but pitched out of trouble for six innings, giving up five hits and three runs against the Reds on Tuesday night in a no-decision. He forced 11 groundouts.
away_pitcher_note: Staked to leads of 3-0 and 5-2 his last time out, Richard struggled thereafter, allowing two home runs and six runs on five hits in 4 1/3 innings against the Dodgers. He's now allowed 12 home runs in 38 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin surrendered five earned runs, walked two and struck out four over 5 1/3 innings to collect his fifth straight no-decision on Thursday. He pitched three scoreless innings before the Padres' four-run fourth.
away_pitcher_note: Haren's inconsistent season continued in a 10-1 loss to the Mets on Wednesday. He gave up seven hits and five earned runs, including three homers, over just four innings. After the game, he said, "I feel like I'm letting down the team."

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had his roughest outing since May 17 on Friday, giving up four runs on 11 hits and striking out five in five innings. He got a no-decision, making him 5-0 in his last seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf will make his first Major League start this year Wednesday. In 12 starts with Triple-A Syracuse, the right-hander is 4-5 with a 4.27 ERA. He has given up two runs or less in his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: He returned after one rehab start and struggled for four innings in a loss to the Padres on Saturday. With RHP Roy Oswalt almost ready and RHP Tyler Chatwood recovered from soreness, Francis is pitching for his spot.
away_pitcher_note: Ross Detwiler's last start for the Nationals came May 15, when an oblique strain knocked him out after three innings. In a rehab start with Class A Potomac Saturday, he surrendered one run in 3 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio carried a perfect game into the sixth inning against the Padres Sunday, giving up four hits and two earned runs. Working the bottom of the zone, he notched seven strikeouts and walked one.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick did not have his best stuff, but he battled and gave the Phillies a chance to win Friday in Milwaukee. He allowed eight hits, three runs, one walk and struck out six in six innings against the Brewers at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Right-hander Tyler Chatwood, who hasn't pitched since suffering inflammation of tissue in the right triceps and elbow area during his last start on June 3, is slated to start Saturday against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Pettibone allowed four hits, six runs (four earned), two walks and struck out four in 5 1/3 innings in a loss to Milwaukee on Sunday. He has a 4.96 ERA (nine earned runs in 16 1/3 innings) over his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: His form hasn't quite returned since he suffered a back strain on April 19, but he got his first win since then on Tuesday, when he held the Nationals to two runs in five innings. It took 93 pitches, as he tries to regain sharpness.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed two runs on seven hits and struck out five in six innings in a loss to Minnesota on Tuesday. Hamels got a no-decision to avoid his 10th loss of the season, but it was hardly any consolation to him.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson pitched with a blister on his right middle finger during his last start against Texas. He remained in the game but struggled with his command and lasted only five innings -- three runs on five hits -- because of a high pitch count.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa pitched through a cut on his middle finger two starts ago. In his last start, he checked out fine health-wise, but labored, giving up three runs on four hits and three walks in 5 1/3 innings of a loss to the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers threw a season-high seven innings in his most recent start, vs. Texas. He allowed just one run and continues to impress after transitioning from the 'pen in May. He continues to build his arm strength and is no longer on a strict pitch count.
away_pitcher_note: Francis, a Canadian who won his only career start at Rogers Centre, bordered on stellar in his last start, when he held the Nationals to two runs and five hits in six innings of a no-decision on Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle has turned his season around after a slow start to the year. He has six quality starts over his past seven outings while posting a 2.54 ERA. That has lowered his ERA to 4.66, which is a far cry from the 7.02 mark it was in early May.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio has had well-documented issues after early innings. He hasn't pitched in the seventh this year. Against the Nationals on Friday, he took a five-run lead into the sixth, gave up three runs and watched the team lose.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Indians, Zimmermann couldn't take advantage of a 5-0 lead. He pitched five innings and allowed six runs on eight hits. Everything he threw was up in the zone. He wasn't getting ahead of hitters.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt, long a contender for Cy Young Awards, signed with the Rockies on May 3. Unlike last year, when he signed late with the Rangers, he stayed long enough in the Minors (3-2, 2.16 at Double-A Tulsa) to find his form.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg made his first start since May 31 because of a strained lat muscle and he was solid, going five innings and allowing a run on one hit. He was on a pitch count and threw 82 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood has never faced the Nationals but is 2-1 with a 0.56 ERA in three road starts this season. Against the Phillies in his last game, Chatwood gave up seven hits but just two runs in five innings in the 4-1 win.

home_pitcher_note: On Monday, Haren pitched six innings and allowed four runs on seven hits in a no-decision vs. the Phillies. Haren will face the Rockies for the second time this season. The first time, Haren allowed five runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Slowed by a back injury early, Chacin returned to form in his last start by holding the Phillies to two runs and six hits in 8 2/3 innings. He's looking like he did in his first five starts (1.52 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Detwiler was solid during the first five innings against the Phillies, allowing a run on three hits. But things started to unravel for Detwiler in the sixth and he lost his fifth game of the season.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa didn't give up a hit until the sixth and held the Blue Jays to one hit in seven innings in his last start. He might have gone longer if not for a bruise on his left thumb that made his final four innings uncomfortable.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster has been a model of consistency in June. He's recorded a quality start in each of his four outings during the month, posting a 3.48 ERA. He surrendered three runs over six innings in his last outing vs. the Rays, but took the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio hasn't pitched deep into games, but he was competitive in his last outing, a loss at Toronto. Nicasio went five innings, throwing 97 pitches, and gave up four hits and four runs, but just two were earned.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander continues to look strong in his comeback from Tommy John surgery. In Lackey's last outing, he gave up two runs over seven innings against the Tigers, leaving with a lead but getting a no-decision when Andrew Bailey blew the save.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt pitched better than his ERA shows. He struck out 11 -- one shy of a career high he established during his rookie year -- in just five innings in his first Major League start of 2013. The Nationals scored four runs on nine hits.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood lost his last start at Washington but pitched well. He gave up just four hits -- three of them soft ones -- in six innings, struck out four and forced 11 ground-ball outs against two fly balls. He hasn't allowed a homer this year.
away_pitcher_note: Outside of Matt Harvey, Hefner has been the Mets' most consistent pitcher since late April. Over his last 11 starts, he is 2-4 with a 3.22 ERA, 54 strikeouts and 16 walks, delivering quality starts in eight of those outings.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin threw seven scoreless innings with five hits and three strikeouts while beating the Nationals in his last start. Chacin has a 1.74 ERA while winning his last three starts. He's fully recovered form an early back injury.
away_pitcher_note: Zito starts away from AT&T Park, and in such games he is 0-4 with an 11.28 ERA in 2013. He's handled Coors Field well in his career, posting a 3.70 ERA in nine starts. He allowed five runs on 11 hits in 5 2/3 innings there in May.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa earned his sixth win in the last seven decisions by hold the Nationals to two runs and seven hits in six innings on Sunday. De La Rosa struck out four and pitched around three walks, and threw 95 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: After losing at AT&T Park for the first time since April 7, Cain takes the mound at Coors Field, where he is 6-3 with a 4.50 ERA in his career. He allowed six runs in 6 1/3 innings at Colorado on May 16.

home_pitcher_note: Pomeranz, the headline prospect the Rockies received from the Indians for pitcher Ubaldo Jimenez in 2011, was 8-1 with a 4.50 ERA in Triple-A. He earned the promotion with two strong performances in hitters' parks.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner threw 111 pitches in each of his last two outings and topped that figure on three other occasions. In his last start against Colorado, on May 17, Bumgarner squandered a 4-0 lead and allowed a season-high nine runs (seven earned).

home_pitcher_note: In his first two starts since joining the club, Oswalt has displayed good fastball velocity and movement but must add overall sharpness and location. It's his first Rockies start at Coors Field, where he has a 2.25 career ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw fired eight innings of two-run ball in his last outing to beat the Giants for his first win in over a month. The left-hander allowed three runs over seven innings at Coors Field on May 31 in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Despite struggling with location all evening, Chatwood went six strong innings, allowing only one earned run and walking three in a no-decision. Ten of his 18 outs came on ground balls in a 3-2 loss to the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke has gone at least seven innings in four of his last five starts after not pitching deep into games for the season's first two months. He's faced the Rockies once this year, allowing four runs on nine hits in 5 1/3 innings at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin held the Giants scoreless for eight innings, and has gone at least eight in his last two starts at Coors Field. Against the Giants, he forced 11 ground-ball outs and threw an economical 95 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Capuano was hit hard his last time out, charged with seven runs on 10 hits in 3 2/3 innings against the Phillies. Before that start, he had thrown 11 scoreless innings since coming off the disabled list.

home_pitcher_note: Skaggs will be called up from Triple-A Reno to make the start in place of Trevor Cahill, who was placed on the disabled list with a bruised hip. This will be Skaggs' fourth big league start this season.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa left Saturday's start against the Giants before the seventh with a bruised left thumb but should be OK. He's dealt with the injury the last three starts but hasn't given up more than two runs in any of them.

home_pitcher_note: Miley did not pitch poorly in his last start against the Mets, but he wasn't very efficient. He fell behind hitters and pitched his way into jams, forcing him to last just 5 2/3 scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Giants ran up Pomeranz's pitch count early and hit two homers -- Buster Posey on a decent pitch, Hunter Pence on a poor one -- to chase him after 4 1/3 innings in his season debut on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin suffered his first defeat of the year in his last start against the Mets. The D-backs are 15-2 in games he has started. After picking up nine wins in his first 11 starts, Corbin is winless in his past six.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt said he was too reliant on his fastball, and it showed in a 8-0 loss to the Dodgers. Oswalt allowed nine hits and five runs in as many innings, striking out five in his third start since returning to the big leagues.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez didn't get a win on his 30th birthday, though he pitched very well in a no-decision against the Red Sox at Fenway Park. He allowed one run on seven hits in six innings, with one walk and six strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood ran into the hot-hitting Dodgers in his last start and struggled, giving up season highs for runs (six), earned runs (five) and hits (11). He also gave up two homers in five innings of what turned out to be a loss.

home_pitcher_note: Stults dropped his second consecutive decision the last time out against the Red Sox, allowing four runs in 4 1/3 innings. He's allowed nine earned runs in his last eight innings. He hasn't won a game since June 14.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin was not as dominant against the Dodgers on Thursday as he had been over his last two starts. He allowed four earned runs, nine hits and three walks in 5 2/3 innings while striking out four, nabbing his fifth straight win.

home_pitcher_note: Cashner worked a 1-2-3 first inning his last time out against the Nationals and allowed five runs on four hits, two walks and a hit batsman in the second inning. He was gone after two-plus innings, his shortest start of 2013.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa gave up four extra-base hits among the seven total he gave up in 5 1/3 innings against the D-backs, but he pitched well -- five strikeouts against no walks, and just three runs -- in the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Capuano lost his spot in the rotation when they acquired Ricky Nolasco from the Marlins on Saturday. But with rookie Stephen Fife battling a right shoulder injury, Capuano will get his first start in seven days.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz was 8-1 at Triple-A Colorado Springs, but in two starts since his callup, he's lasted 4 1/3 and 4 innings, respectively. Working often from behind in the count, Pomeranz has surrendered three home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw tossed eight innings of one-run ball to beat the Giants in his last outing on Sunday. The left-hander has gone at least eight innings in each of his past three starts and won all of them. He's 5-3 with a 1.60 ERA in 10 starts at home.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio returns from making two starts at Triple-A Colorado Springs -- one shortened to three innings because of rain, the other consisting of eight scoreless innings -- looking to overcome his tentativeness in key situations.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke fired seven scoreless innings to beat the D-backs his last time out, striking out seven and allowing two hits. He's won each of his past four starts. Greinke is unbeaten in six starts at Dodger Stadium this year.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood didn't give up a hit until the fourth. He stumbled a bit after being hit in the shin by a batted ball in the sixth, but he held the Padres to two runs and five hits in 6 2/3 innings. He's 3-1 with a 1.26 ERA in five road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco makes his first start at Dodger Stadium as a member of the home team. Acquired in a trade with the Marlins last weekend, Nolasco threw seven innings of one-run ball to beat the D-backs on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin was not as sharp as some of his outings, but was effective in his last start, when he went six innings and gave up one run on five hits and struck out four in a loss at San Diego. The Rockies removed him after 97 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa will try to keep a surprising run of dominance from the starting staff going beyond the All-Star break, as Colorado's starters boast a 2.23 ERA over their last eight games.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija needed the All-Star break. He is coming off his worst outing of the year July 10 when he gave up four home runs over 4 2/3 innings vs. the Angels. The Opening Day starter, he's given up 14 runs over 10 2/3 innings in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio looked like a new man in his first start back from Triple-A, allowing just three hits in a season-high seven innings. Notching his first win since mid-May, he struck out three in the 3-0 win over the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Villanueva did exactly what the Cubs needed in his last start against the Cardinals, lasting six innings and keeping the game close. But he took the loss in a one-run decision. It was his second start since returning to the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood closed out the first half with his best start this year, needing only 98 pitches to pitch a one-run complete game. Chatwood, one of the Rockies' most reliable young arms, gave up four hits and struck out four.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson finished the first half strong, throwing seven shutout innings against the Cardinals on July 11. He held them to three hits, did not walk a batter and struck out five. He's admitted the first half was "crazy" and also inconsistent.

home_pitcher_note: Pomeranz is being called up to make his fourth start with the Rockies this season. He is 8-2 with a 4.65 ERA in 16 Minor League starts this year but has struggled with his command in the Majors, issuing 14 walks over 12 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler aims to regain the success he enjoyed when he recorded three quality starts in his first four starts. He has only one quality start in his previous six, his first MLB win on June 20 against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin is eyeing a seventh win in eight straight starts after a six-inning, one-run outing in a 3-1 victory over the Dodgers. The righty struck out six and walked three, needing 94 pitches to make it through the sixth.
away_pitcher_note: Fernandez did not have his best stuff in his most recent start, but the All-Star battled and kept the Marlins in the game, giving up only one run in six innings for his team-leading 11th quality start.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa earned a no-decision Friday, giving up just one run over six innings, the victim of limited run support. De La Rosa struck out four and walked three, his critical mistake a solo homer to Alfonso Soriano.
away_pitcher_note: Turner had effectively kept the ball in the park in his eight starts before the All-Star break. He gave up just one home run in 54 innings. But in his last start at Milwaukee, he allowed two solo shots in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio won consecutive starts for the first time in his career. He labored through the first inning his last time out against the Cubs, but after his teammates gave him a lead, he remained aggressive, allowing one run in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Eovaldi had pitched at least six innings in each of his first five starts this year. That streak ended at Milwaukee in his first outing after the All-Star break. He was tagged for six runs on 10 hits in four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood labored early but held the Cubs to two runs and seven hits in six innings of a 4-3 victory on Sunday at Coors Field. The home run he gave up to Anthony Rizzo was just the third he has yielded in 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old Peralta has dazzled over his last four starts, posting a 0.31 ERA (one earned run allowed) in 29 1/3 innings. The Brewers have won all four of those games, and manager Ron Roenicke seems to think his young pitcher is settling in.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh, with solid Triple-A numbers pitching in high altitude in both Las Vegas and Colorado Springs, moves into the rotation to replace Drew Pomeranz, who was ineffective before suffering left shoulder soreness.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny will make his fifth start for the Brewers against a team he has a career 8.64 ERA against in four starts and six relief appearances. He had allowed one earned run in his first three starts but gave up five in 5 2/3 innings in his last one.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin was hit on the inner thigh by a line drive in his last start, a loss to the Marlins, but still managed to give up just three runs in seven innings. He pitched well enough to win, but didn't because of his team's offensive slump.
away_pitcher_note: Hand's last start was cut short when he was hit by a 97 mph fastball on his right hand. X-rays were negative and there was only some swelling and soreness to work through for the righty. This will be his fifth start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Back from Tommy John elbow reconstructive surgery, Beachy will be making his first start since June 16, 2012. Beachy will take Tim Hudson's place in the rotation after posting a 2.50 ERA in his last four rehab starts.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa said he struggled with command early but you wouldn't know by the numbers -- no runs, five hits, five strikeouts, one walk in a win over the Marlins on Wednesday. A chronic thumb bruise flared on a bunt, but he said it won't affect him.

home_pitcher_note: Wood has made just three starts, two at the big league level, since being promoted to Atlanta in late May. He showed some rust against the Mets on Thursday as he surrendered eight hits (all singles) in 4 1/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Chacin gave up three runs Sunday before finishing with three scoreless innings in his seventh quality start in eight outings. Chacin went seven innings, giving up eight hits and striking out four.

away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa struggled with his location throughout a loss to the Braves on Monday night, when he gave up eight runs, five earned, and 10 hits in five innings. He said his chronic thumb issues had no bearing on his performance.

away_pitcher_note: Before Tuesday night at Atlanta, Nicasio had given up one run in 19 innings over three starts. But he gave up six runs and six hits in the fourth inning, and eight runs and 10 hits in four innings overall in the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Though not as sharp as in his 2013 debut, Mejia still mustered a quality start (six innings, three runs) his last time out in Miami. As long as he continues pitching well, Mejia will remain a member of the Mets' rotation.
away_pitcher_note: The hard-throwing Bettis was jittery in his debut at Atlanta and gave up a two-run homer to Justin Upton, his second big league batter. He settled down, but must throw more strikes to make his 96-mph fastball effective.

home_pitcher_note: Harvey's ERA against the Marlins is 3.52. His ERA against everyone else is 1.97. Luckily for Harvey, he will be facing someone else in his next start -- the Rockies, who mustered only one run off him in six innings last year.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin battled after taking a line drive off his arm in the fifth inning of his last start, limiting the Pirates to a run in eight innings. He allowed six hits and struck out three with no walks. He said the injury should not affect his next start.

home_pitcher_note: Gee continued his midseason turnaround against the Royals, allowing one run on three hits in seven innings. He keeps hitters off-balance with solid command and a mix of speeds on his pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Manship, 28, was summoned from Triple-A to start in place of an injured Tyler Chatwood. He has a 6.20 ERA in 41 Major League games, all with the Twins, from 2009-12. He made 17 starts for Colorado Springs and was 6-8 with a 4.85 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa finished with four innings and three runs against, but a high pitch count and a lack of command led to a loss at Pittsburgh last Saturday -- his second straight short start in which his pitches missed frequently.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano seeks to stay hot in his introduction to a park unkind to pitchers. Liriano has gone seven-plus innings, allowing one run or none, in four of his last five starts. He did match his season high of five walks last time out.

away_pitcher_note: Locke will be closely watched after allowing 27 hits in 16 1/3 innings in his last three starts. A problem has been slowing down his pace when in trouble. He is more effective working quickly, which puts hitters on the defensive.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin pitched well in his last start against the Mets, allowing only two runs on seven hits over seven innings. He had a sharp sinker and slider and pitched better as the game wore on. He's allowed three runs or fewer in each of his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez allowed two runs on six hits in six innings against the Orioles on Tuesday. Still, his curveball was very good. He'll need it against the Rockies, a team he's allowed 23 earned runs to in four starts in 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Manship gave up two runs in a respectable five innings in his first start of the season, a loss to the Mets. Manship took a red-eye flight from Colorado Springs to New York for that outing. He should be rested this time.
away_pitcher_note: Stults has tamed the Rockies' lineup twice this season, allowing 11 hits and two runs in 16 innings. That said, pitching on the road (4.64 ERA) has proved much tougher than doing so at pitcher-friendly Petco Park (2.37).

home_pitcher_note: In his last start Friday at Coors Field, De La Rosa yielded six hits in the first inning-plus against the Pirates, but he found his changeup and slider and made it through five innings with one run scored for the win.
away_pitcher_note: Cashner struggled to locate his fastball in his last start, giving up five runs (three earned) on seven hits and four walks vs. the Reds on Friday. That snapped a three-game win streak for Cashner, who is 0-1 in two starts against Colorado this year.

home_pitcher_note: After winning all three of his decisions in July, Chen is 0-2 in his first two August outings. The southpaw allowed three runs on five hits over six innings his last time out against the Giants, but he only received one run of support.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio gave up three runs in 5 2/3 innings against the Pirates at home Saturday. He succeeded with an off-speed, backdoor slider -- a pitch that got him in trouble earlier this year -- mixed with his hard slider and fastball.

away_pitcher_note: Bettis needed just 80 pitches to throw six innings against the Pirates on Sunday, and he would have had a chance to go longer or win if not for an offensive substitution. It was the most efficient of his three Major League starts.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman took a no-decision on Monday night in Arizona, allowing a run on four hits over 5 1/3 innings. The righty also struck out eight.
away_pitcher_note: On a rainy night at Coors Field, Chacin efficiently used 100 pitches over eight innings to hold the Padres to one run and five hits, with six strikeouts against two walks. It was his seventh straight quality start.

home_pitcher_note: Martin allowed six hits, three runs, two walks and struck out six in five innings last Tuesday against the Braves. Martin fell behind 14 of 23 hitters, but he avoided major trouble with his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Manship was handed a three-run lead but blew it in the second inning of his last start, a home loss to the Padres. Manship had mechanical issues and gave up six runs in three innings before correcting them.

home_pitcher_note: Cloyd starts in place of left-hander John Lannan, who just landed on the disabled list because of a recurring knee injury that seems likely to end his season. Cloyd is 4-1 with a 1.33 ERA in his last seven starts in Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa allowed just two runs over seven innings Wednesday, rescued from a sixth-inning jam by his catcher to preserve another strong start. He struck out seven and improved to 6-0 with a 1.58 ERA in day games.

home_pitcher_note: Lee had his best outing of the second half Friday against the Dodgers. He went eight innings for the first time since June 24 and surrendered three runs. Lee got no help from his offense, though, and he hasn't won since July 5.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio fought traffic in the early innings of his last start, but he made key pitches and held the Orioles to two runs in six innings, despite walking four. In his last two starts, he hasn't been sharp but has been effective.

home_pitcher_note: The righty got four double plays to help him escape danger in his last start on Saturday against the Dodgers. Kendrick allowed two runs in six innings, but the Phillies were held scoreless for his 10th loss.
away_pitcher_note: After three mostly competitive starts, Bettis turned in a clunker Saturday night at Baltimore, when he gave up seven hits and four walks in 2 2/3 innings of a loss. But six of the eight runs against him were unearned.

home_pitcher_note: Koehler struggled with command in a no-decision against the Giants, allowing three runs on seven hits with four walks and four strikeouts in five-plus innings. The right-hander is 3-3 in his last six decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching after learning of the death of his grandmother in Venezuela, Chacin gave up more runs (three) than in any road game this year in a loss at Baltimore. He still struck out five in 5 2/3 innings and kept the game close.

home_pitcher_note: Since June 1, Fernandez has arguably been the best pitcher in the National League. He is 7-2 with a 1.63 ERA and 105 strikeouts in that span. He is now at 145 2/3 innings and will be shut down at about 170.
away_pitcher_note: In three starts, Manship has allowed 13 runs in 15 innings for a 7.80 ERA and an 0-3 record. Against the Phillies on Aug. 19, he allowed five runs in five innings and coincidentally has gone five innings in each start.

home_pitcher_note: Command has become an issue for Turner, who has walked 11 (two intentional) with no strikeouts in 10 innings in his last two starts, both no-decisions. Turner has lost three straight decisions since he beat Atlanta on July 10.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa earned his third straight win Tuesday against the Phillies, when he overcame a three-run third inning by retiring 11 straight hitters. De La Rosa threw 100 pitches, 60 strikes, in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio had a no-decision in his last outing against the Phillies. The right-hander allowed two runs (one earned) in 5 2/3 innings. He's 1-0 with a 3.12 ERA in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Zito hopes to regain the magic he spun on April 9 of last year, when he delivered the Giants' first win of the season with a four-hit shutout at Coors Field. Zito's woes on the road, where he's 0-7 with a 9.45 ERA, have been well-documented.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis took a no-decision in his last outing at Philadelphia, giving up a run on six hits and a walk with five strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings. The rookie will be making his sixth career start.
away_pitcher_note: Petit, who has appeared in 73 Major League games in parts of six seasons, was recalled when Matt Cain was placed on the DL on Friday. Petit pitched in one game this year, in July. He also made a start for the Giants last year.

home_pitcher_note: For the sixth time in seven starts, Chacin pitched through the seventh inning in a 3-2 win over the Marlins. The righty allowed two runs off only four hits, walking four and striking out five for his 12th win.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner recorded a 0.952 WHIP before the All-Star break and 1.261 since. Yet his first-half ERA was 3.02 in 19 starts, compared to 2.35 in seven second-half outings.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa battled a lingering thumb injury through all five innings of a 4-3 win over Miami on Sunday. De La Rosa surrendered three runs and walked three while striking out three more for his staff-leading 14th win.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo is on a roll with four straight quality starts and has already surpassed his win total of 12 from 2012. He hasn't allowed a walk in any of his last four outings, for a streak of 29 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio showed promising growth Monday, escaping several jams in a 6-1 win. He threw six shutout innings and allowed four hits, striking out nine and walking two in his third scoreless outing since returning to the Majors on July 12.
away_pitcher_note: Reynolds will be returning to Denver to face a Rockies team that made him the No. 2 overall Draft pick in 2006. His career in Colorado ended in 2011 after injuries and subpar performances.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood is set to start his first big league game in a month. He showed little rust Tuesday in a rehab game with Triple-A Colorado Springs, allowing one run and five hits over 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Leake has a 6.75 ERA over his last three starts, allowing a homer in each. What's been troubling is he's let opponents come back after having sizable early leads. On Monday, with a 4-0 lead, he allowed a three-run homer to Matt Holliday in the third.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis settled down after allowing three runs in the first inning of a 5-3 loss to the Giants. Bettis is still searching for his first win after allowing nine hits and four runs in six innings while striking out two.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw continues his quest for a second Cy Young Award. He had a 1.01 ERA in August after being the pitcher of the month for July. He pitched a shutout at Coors Field July 2.

home_pitcher_note: Jhoulys Chacin was utterly dominant against the Giants Wednesday, not allowing a hit for 6 2/3 innings. He allowed just one hit in seven innings, striking out nine with a fastball, curveball and slider and walking two.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco has thrown eight scoreless innings in back-to-back starts with 17 strikeouts and one walk. He's 3-2 with a 5.45 ERA in his career at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Bothered by a nagging bruise on his left thumb, Jorge De La Rosa battled through six innings in a 9-6 win over the Reds. He allowed three runs off eight hits, striking out three in win No. 15, one short of his career high.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez gets a pretty tough test in his starting debut. He has an 8.39 career ERA at Coors Field. But the Dodgers apparently promised him a quick trial.

home_pitcher_note: Smith struggled in six games this season (11.37 ERA) with the Padres but was very good in Triple-A (5-1, 3.39). Smith feels he's in a better place to succeed this time around, and won't try to blow the ball by hitters.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio struggled with his fastball command from the start in an 8-3 loss to the Reds on Saturday. He allowed six runs in 4 1/3 innings and struck out four, but Wilton Lopez could not get him out of trouble in the fifth.

home_pitcher_note: Ross continues to shine since moving back into the rotation on July 23. He's 3-3 but has a 2.45 ERA in eight starts. He struck out 10 and walked one in five innings last time out against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood is in line to make his next start, despite taking a line drive off his throwing hand Sunday. He tried to stay in the game after the injury, serving up a two-run homer, the only runs he allowed in two innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy has generally pitched well since he was acquired from the D-backs on July 31, especially at Petco Park, where he's 3-1 with a 3.09 ERA in four starts since the deal. Opponents are hitting .230 off him in those starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis couldn't escape a fifth-inning jam and paid the price, allowing eight hits and five runs in a 10-8 loss to the Dodgers. Bettis struck out four and walked one and is still in search of his first Major League win.

home_pitcher_note: With a 5-6 AT&T Park record, Lincecum has a chance to pull even at home for the first time since early June, when he owned a 3-3 mark. Lincecum's home WHIP is 1.193, compared to 1.500 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin settled down as the game progressed, but still picked up his first loss sine Aug. 18 in a 7-4 loss to the Dodgers Tuesday. He allowed four runs on nine hits in seven innings, striking out three and walking two.

home_pitcher_note: It's difficult to read too much into Vogelsong's statistics in this injury-marred season of his. But he owns an inflated home ERA of 5.19 -- which is still significantly better than his road ERA of 6.37.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa was masterful in the use of his changeup in his last start, a home win over the Dodgers. The victory tied De La Rosa for the NL lead in wins with 16. No Rockies pitcher has ever finished a year leading that category.

home_pitcher_note: A candidate for a spot in the 2014 starting rotation, Petit's coming off his near-perfect game last Friday against Arizona. In 21 innings as a starter, Petit has struck out 23 and walked just four.
away_pitcher_note: At times Nicasio labored through innings on Friday night at San Diego, but in the end the numbers were good. He got a no-decision but gave up two runs, one earned, on four hits, with seven strikeouts and two walks in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy has been outstanding in two of his last three starts and in the other he tossed a complete game allowing two runs in the inning and two in the ninth. He held the Giants to one run over eight innings last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood's last start was delayed by a bruised right thumb, but he had no issues because of it. Chatwood held the Padres to one run and five hits in six innings, with two walks and two strikeouts, but didn't figure in the decision.

home_pitcher_note: Miley pitched well his last time out as he held the Giants to two runs over seven innings. He did not get a decision in the game, which went 11 innings. He has allowed one run in 12 1/3 innings against the Rockies this year.
away_pitcher_note: In his first outing since July 7, Oswalt entered in relief and pitched three solid innings before giving up four runs while recording just one out in his final inning. Oswalt hopes more stamina will give him greater effectiveness.

home_pitcher_note: Delgado struggled his last time out against the Dodgers. He gave up four homers and lasted just 2 2/3 innings. He has allowed 1.8 homers per nine innings this year. This is his first appearance against the Rockies this year.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin held the Giants to one run and four hits and struck out five in seven innings in his last start. The performance lowered his road ERA for the season to 2.10, and his ERA in August and September is 2.24.

away_pitcher_note: Lynn firmed up his place in the rotation by limiting Milwaukee to just one unearned run on four hits and two walks, while fanning 10 on Wednesday. He had surrendered at least four earned runs in each of his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio has a shot to join Jorge De La Rosa and Jhoulys Chacin in double figures in the win column if he finishes strong. He battled through a high pitch count but held the Giants to one run in five innings his last outing.
away_pitcher_note: On Thursday, Kelly picked up his first loss since he joined the rotation July 6. He gave up four runs -- three earned -- on seven hits and a walk, but still remains the Cardinals' winningest starter of the second half.

home_pitcher_note: The often-efficient Chatwood had his season disrupted by a right thumb injury. In his last start, he lasted just 4 2/3 innings and threw 110 pitches -- with seven hits and six walks -- but the Rockies still beat the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright served up a solo homer, but he limited Seattle to one run on six hits and two walks in a no decision Friday. The Cardinals ace is 5-1 with a 1.17 ERA in eight career games (six starts) versus the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Still building his pitch count up after missing nearly two months with a left hamstring injury, Oswalt saw progress in his last outing at Arizona, when he gave up two runs and seven hits while throwing 83 pitches in 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wacha picked up his first Major League loss Saturday, surrendering two runs on four hits and a career-high four walks vs. Seattle. A two-run fifth inning ended the rookie's consecutive scoreless inning streak at 23 2/3.

home_pitcher_note: It's a nice chance to rebound for Chacin, who yielded seven hits and six runs (four earned) in just four innings while losing to the D-backs at Chase Field. Before that, he went at least seven innings in nine of 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: This will mark Delgado's second straight outing vs. the Rockies as he held them to two runs on five hits in six innings his last time out to earn his first win since Aug. 2. The righty has allowed a combined six homers in three starts this month.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh was effective in place of Jorge De La Rosa Monday, allowing one run over five innings in a win over the Cardinals. It was his best start with the Rockies so far, but he's searching for his first win this year.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill beat the Dodgers in his last start and will be looking to win his fifth consecutive decision when he faces the Rockies. He is 1-2 against them this year but hasn't faced the club since May 22.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio limped through one of his worst outings of the year Tuesday, allowing eight runs over 2 2/3 innings. He walked three and struck out two in his shortest outing since June 25, when he was demoted to Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: The next inning Corbin completes will be his 200th of the year. The lefty is coming off the shortest start of his career, allowing six runs on seven hits over just two-plus innings vs. the Dodgers on Tuesday. Corbin is 3-0 vs. the Rockies in 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood picked up his first loss in four starts after giving up eight hits and four runs over six innings in a loss to the Cardinals. It was the most runs Chatwood had allowed since he surrendered eight July 31.
away_pitcher_note: In his first season since recovering from Tommy John surgery, Lackey has thrown 183 1/3 innings. But innings shouldn't be a concern for the right-hander, who averaged 194 innings a season between 2003 and 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin struggled with his command all day, but he lasted six innings and allowed two runs in a 9-4 win over the D-backs on Friday. It was his 19th quality start, and he enters his last home start with a 3.77 ERA at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy changed his arm slot a few starts ago and is still working on consistency. He's lost just once in nine starts for the Red Sox while posting a 3.68 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The top three of the Dodgers rotation get their finale tuneups before the playoffs against Colorado, starting with ace Clayton Kershaw, who merely struck out 10 in seven scoreless innings against San Diego Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: McHugh's struggles continued in a loss to the D-backs Friday night. He surrendered a season-high six runs and 11 hits over five innings, striking out one. McHugh fell to 0-3 with an 8.05 ERA in four starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Zack Greinke went only five innings in his most recent start in San Diego, but that was by design for added rest, and he allowed only two hits and no runs. Once healed from the broken collarbone, he was Kershaw-like.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio's late-season slide continued Sunday as he gave up seven runs over 2 1/3 innings, tying a season-low. He walked two and struck out one but will have one more chance to bounce back in the Rockies' season finale.

home_pitcher_note: Hyun-Jin Ryu might be a Rookie of the Year favorite if not for Miami's Jose Fernandez. In his previous start against the Giants, Ryu allowed only one run over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: In possibly his final outing with the Rockies, Francis gets the nod in place of Tyler Chatwood, who is dealing with right elbow soreness. It will be Francis' first start since June 18 at Toronto.
