home_pitcher_note: Fernandez, the reigning NL Rookie of the Year, opened 2013 as a 20-year-old fifth starter. Now 21, he has blossomed into an ace and one of the top right-handers in the game. Because of an innings limit last year, his last outing was Sept. 11.
away_pitcher_note: After a strong 2013, the Rockies believe De La Rosa will take the next step if he can execute a sinker inside to right-handed batters. He already has one of the game's best changeups, the fastball tweak enhances that.

home_pitcher_note: The hardest thrower in the rotation, Eovaldi's fastball was clocked as high as 101 mph in Spring Training. Because of his overpowering fastball, he relied heavily on the pitch last year, throwing 70 percent fastballs.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson battled foot and ankle injuries last year while with the Athletics. Traded to the Rockies during the offseason, he has shown why he was an Opening Day starter last year, with his fastball-slider-changeup mix.

home_pitcher_note: In the 2013 finale, Alvarez no-hit the Tigers. He's looking to carry that momentum into 2014. The right-hander mixes a mid-90s fastball with a slow curve clocked around 65 mph. Alvarez gained extra innings in winter ball.
away_pitcher_note: Acquired in the trade that sent outfielder Dexter Fowler to the Astros, Lyles improved his sinker and curveball and induced grounders during Spring Training. He was slated for Triple-A until Tyler Chatwood (left hamstring) was injured.

home_pitcher_note: At 22, Turner remains an unfinished product. Still, the right-hander has already pitched in parts of three seasons before opening in the rotation. A change this spring is Turner is throwing harder, reaching 96 mph.
away_pitcher_note: Morales won the open starter's slot with a 2-1 record and a 2.10 ERA in seven Cactus League games. After years as a reliever, Morales added a cut fastball and made the most of his opportunity to be in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies believe the key to consistency lies in his full offseason of conditioning. The last two winters were spent coming back from injuries. In Spring Training, he developed confidence in a split-finger off-speed pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Delgado won the final spot in the rotation by besting top prospect Archie Bradley and Bo Schultz. The spot in the rotation came open when ace Patrick Corbin underwent season-ending Tommy John surgery.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa struck out six and gave up one run in the first four innings of Monday night's opener, but lost his cool when trouble arose in the fifth and was gone before inning's end. He and catcher Wilin Rosario hope to be on the same page.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy pitched better than his numbers would indicate in his first start of the year against the Giants. The right-hander had a tremendous spring and looked sharp in his debut despite the five runs he allowed.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson was efficient through six innings in his first start, and he was hurt by bad luck and an error in his 4-3 loss to the Marlins in his first start. He'll need to stick to his ground-ball style in his first Coors Field start.
away_pitcher_note: Miley allowed four runs in the first inning last time out against the Giants and then shut them down for the next six innings, giving his team a chance to rally. Miley started on Opening Day for the first time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles, called up when Tyler Chatwood suffered a left hamstring injury, struck out five in five innings while beating the Marlins. He yielded a hit batsman, a walk and a homer in the sixth, and he'll need to prevent such lapses.
away_pitcher_note: For the first time since 2012, Paulino pitched in a big league game during Wednesday's win vs. the Twins, throwing 109 pitches over 5 1/3 and minimizing Minnesota's damage by fanning six. Paulino is 0-1 with a 7.36 ERA over nine games at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Morales allowed three runs on eight hits 5 1/3 innings, striking out four with two walks against the Marlins in his season debut on Thursday in Miami. He was in line for a win before Matt Belisle blew the save with four runs allowed in the ninth.
away_pitcher_note: It only seems fitting that Quintana should start the season with a no-decision, considering he had 17 of them in '13 and has 28 since '12. He once again pitched well enough to win by allowing two earned runs on five hits over six while fanning eight.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio unveiled his split-finger pitch, which he has added to his fastball and slider, and he shut down the D-backs for seven innings on Friday afternoon. Nicasio finished with six strikeouts, and the split forced several grounders.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie struggled throwing his fastball, slider and changeup for strikes, in 4 2/3 innings in a loss to the Royals. Johnson yielded seven runs on 10 hits, walked three and struck out two. This will be his first Interleague start and first at-bat.

home_pitcher_note: At age 24, Bumgarner reached the 50-career-win plateau in his last start. This will be Bumgarner's first appearance of the season at home, where he finished 8-6 with a 3.12 ERA in 17 starts a year ago.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa lost command while striking out the side in the first inning last Saturday. He allowed four runs (three earned) on four hits and three walks, "throwing" instead of pitching, he said, lasting 4 1/3 innings and 101 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: It's believed that location, not lack of stuff, has hampered Cain. He threw too many hittable strikes in his last start, yielding three homers to the Dodgers last Sunday. Cain owns a 3.16 lifetime ERA at AT&T Park, compared to 3.60 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson had his second quality start Sunday, allowing five runs (three earned) in six innings. He battled without his best stuff in his Coors Field debut, getting in and out of jams. The unearned runs made the difference.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson's 4.35 ERA in 11 career starts against the Rockies is inflated by his 7.41 ERA at Colorado's Coors Field. His 15 2/3 innings to start the season without a walk is the highest such total by a Giant since Atlee Hammaker went 21 innings in 1983.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood suffered a slight strain of his left hamstring while legging out a triple in his final Spring Training start and missed his first two turns in 2013. But he fanned eight in 6 1/3 innings of his injury rehab start.

home_pitcher_note: Stults had his off-speed pitches and breaking balls working for him in his last start against the Indians. He allowed one earned run in 5 2/3 innings. Stults got nine ground-ball outs in that start, allowing a two-run home run to Jason Kipnis.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles held the White Sox to one run and five hits in 6 1/3 innings in his last start. Slated to begin the year at Triple-A Colorado Springs, he earned his spot with two strong starts replacing the injured Tyler Chatwood.

home_pitcher_note: Erlin's fastball command and his changeup were sharp in his last start against the Indians, as he allowed one run in six innings. He struck out six and looked sharp after his last long outing, which was three weeks before in Spring Training.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, a five-inning no-decision at home against the White Sox, Nicasio lacked pinpoint fastball location he had in beating the D-backs in his first start. But he kept the score close enough for a comeback.

home_pitcher_note: Cashner continues to look like an ace, as he nearly missed the first no-hitter in club history the last time out, tossing a one-hit shutout against the Tigers. He had a career-high 11 strikeouts and has two one-hit shutouts in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: As he did in his previous two starts, De La Rosa looked electric briefly -- four strikeouts in the first two innings -- but gave up six runs in 4 1/3 innings in a loss to the Giants. He yielded a Madison Bumgarner grand slam.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy scuffled early in his last start against the Tigers, allowing all four of his runs in the first four innings. He had a season-best seven strikeouts and his changeup was the best its been thus far. That's an encouraging sign for him.
away_pitcher_note: Morales has labored with high pitch counts and traffic on the bases in his two starts, but he has managed to 5 1/3 and 6 1/3 innings, respectively, and kept the club close each time. Morales' last appearance was one relief inning.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood came off the disabled list (strained left hamstring) and gave up four runs in six innings against the Giants in his first 2014 start. He was efficient, throwing 74 pitches, and was removed in an offensive substitution.
away_pitcher_note: Pettibone, who opened the season with Triple-A Lehigh Valley, made his 2014 debut Saturday in a victory over the Marlins, allowing two runs (one earned run) on eight hits and one walk while striking out five in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles took a 4-0 lead into the fifth inning against the Padres on Monday, but gave up four hits -- including two doubles and a triple -- to see the lead diminish to one run in a game the Rockies lost. But he had a good strike zone performance.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed three runs (two earned runs) on six hits and three walks while striking out seven in six innings Sunday against the Marlins. He threw 115 pitches, the most he had thrown since Aug. 24, 2012.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio threw 31 pitches and gave up two runs in the first inning against the Padres in his last start, but he allowed only two hits from the second through the sixth, finishing with 99 pitches and earning the win.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez kept the game close Monday against the Braves at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed four hits, two runs, six walks and struck out three in six innings. A two-run homer to Evan Gattis forced him to leave in the hole.

home_pitcher_note: Mixing his pitches and avoiding the tendency to overthrow that marred his first three starts, De La Rosa went six innings on 90 pitches at San Diego in his last outing. Infield hits and other misfortune led to a loss.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong regained his All-Star form in his last start. He sustained his velocity throughout his outing against the Dodgers while throwing first-pitch strikes to 16 of the 21 hitters he faced.

home_pitcher_note: After being moved to the bullpen for one appearance, Morales returned to the rotation and held the Padres to one run, a homer by Xavier Nady, in six innings, with five strikeouts in a win Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner has yet to hit his stride. Opponents are batting .326 against him, compared to .205 last year. But his total of 26 strikeouts in 20 2/3 innings indicates that he still possesses decent stuff.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Chatwood forced the Phillies into 14 groundball outs and held them to two hits and one unearned run in seven innings of a home win. Chatwood also pitched well against the Giants in an earlier start.
away_pitcher_note: Cain has nothing to show for his last two games despite allowing one earned run over 14 innings in that span. He also walked five and struck out 16 in those games. Cain has a 3.50 ERA in three road starts.

home_pitcher_note: He hasn't gone past five innings in any of his three starts, but a 2.57 ERA shows Beckett is healthy and effective enough for a fourth or fifth starter. An inning or two deeper would help the bullpen, though.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles' sinker was as good as it's been all year, inducing 14 groundball outs against five fly-ball outs. He pitched seven without allowing an earned run or extra-base hit, and became the first Rockies starter in '14 to pitch into the eighth inning.

home_pitcher_note: There are teams Maholm matches up well against, but the Rockies aren't one of them. He's 1-8 lifetime against Colorado and, following Beckett, the Dodgers need him to at least eat some innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio didn't have his best stuff Sunday, but left with a lead in a game the Rockies lost by one. He allowed five runs (four earned), including three by homers, yielding seven hits and a walk while striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Ryu bent but didn't break against the Phillies, pitching out of repeated jams and finishing with a quality start of six innings and two runs allowed. He hasn't served up a home run yet this season.
away_pitcher_note: After a rough beginning, signs are pointing to stabilization. He pitched well for six innings in a hard-luck loss at San Diego on April 16. In his last start, he needed 102 pitches for five innings but earned his first win, over the Giants at home.

home_pitcher_note: Miley received a no-decision his last time out against the Cubs when he allowed three runs over five innings. Command has been an issue for him this year as he has walked 16 running up his pitch count early in games.
away_pitcher_note: Morales has held opponents to two runs in 13 innings over his last two games. By relying on his fastball, he held the Giants to one run over seven innings Tuesday while lifting the Rockies to a 2-1 victory at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Bolsinger is making his third start since being brought up to replace Trevor Cahill in the rotation. He earned his first win last Thursday in Chicago, allowing a run on four hits with two walks and seven strikeouts in 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood, who had pitched solidly and efficiently in his previous two starts, gave up three home runs and five runs in six innings of a no-decision against the Giants on Wednesday. But he also escaped bases loaded with no outs.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter is making his fourth start since coming out of the bullpen to replace Randall Delgado in the rotation. He won his last time out on Friday night against the Phillies, tossing six innings of scoreless, four hit ball.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles pitched seven strong innings, held the Dodgers to two runs, struck out four and forced 11 groundouts in his last start -- a no-decision in a Rockies win. Lyles has given up two earned runs in 14 innings his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio struggled with his fastball and gave up eight hits, two home runs, and five runs in 4 1/3 innings in a loss to the Dodgers. In his last two games, he's worked just 9 1/3 innings and has a loss and a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Colon's ERA may be 4.50, but more than half the runs against him came in one start. In his other four outings, he holds a 2.33 ERA with 23 strikeouts and one walk. Colon was not originally scheduled to pitch Thursday, but rain pushed back his start.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa forced 13 ground-ball outs in seven innings in a victory at Dodger Stadium on Sunday -- his strongest start this year. De La Rosa gave up one run and four of the Dodgers' eight hits in the first two innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wheeler pitched well throughout the month of April, but he struggled in the two areas he worked on most heavily this spring: control and efficiency. He has nine walks over his last 16 1/3 innings, a rate of almost five free passes per nine.

home_pitcher_note: Morales picked up the win for a third consecutive start his last time out. He allowed four runs on seven hits and two walks with two strikeouts in five innings Monday vs. the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Mejia had not endured a truly rough outing until his last time out, when the Marlins tagged him for five runs in the sixth inning of a loss. He will look to recover against the Rockies at hitter-friendly Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin is set to make his season debut after starting the year on the disabled list with a right shoulder strain. The right-hander is coming off a career-high 14 wins and a 3.47 ERA in 2013.
away_pitcher_note: Gee is coming off the best outing of any Mets starter this season, firing eight shutout innings Sunday against the Marlins. He struggled in his only outing at Coors Field last season, giving up five runs in 4/23 innings amidst frigid conditions.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles was solid for six innings, holding the D-backs to one run and three hits, but ended up with a no-decision in his start on Wednesday. He was in line for a win, but the Rockies lost it in the late innings.
away_pitcher_note: Perez allowed eight runs in 42/3 innings in his last start against the Athletics on Tuesday. Prior to that he was 4-0 with a 1.42 ERA in his first five starts. He is 2-2 with a 3.34 in five career Interleague starts.

home_pitcher_note: After two short, inefficient starts, Nicasio threw seven scoreless innings and held the Mets to three hits in winning his last start, at Coors Field. Nicasio also helped the offense with one hit and a career-high three RBIs.
away_pitcher_note: Ross allowed ten runs in 31/3 innings in a 12-1 loss to the Athletics on Wednesday. He is 0-2 with a 7.36 ERA in his last three starts. He is 3-0 with a 1.13 ERA in 18 relief appearances and one start in Interleague Play.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis held the Angels to two runs in 52/3 innings in his last start on Friday in Anaheim. Manager Ron Washington said it was the best of his four starts since retutning to the Major Leagues. He walked one and struck out six.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa walked three and battled traffic on the bases in three of his six innings Friday, but he held the Mets to three runs. De La Rosa is 3-1 with a 2.63 ERA in his last four starts, using his fastball and cutter to set up his changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison will be making his third start since coming off the disabled list. He is 5-2 with 2.49 ERA in 10 career starts and four relief appearances in Interleague play.
away_pitcher_note: Morales gave up six runs, five earned, and nine hits in five innings his last time out. He was rescued by his teammates, who erased a 6-0 deficit and eventually beat the Mets, 11-10. Morales struck out five but needs improved location.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto is the first Reds pitcher to throw at least seven innings in his first seven starts of the season since Bucky Walters in 1944. The last Reds pitcher to throw eight or more innings in four consecutive appearances was Jose Rijo (1990).
away_pitcher_note: Chacin, in his first start after sitting out the first month-plus while recovering from a right shoulder strain, gave up four runs and eight hits in five innings of a loss to the Mets in his season debut Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Simon pitched well enough for a quality start by allowing three earned runs over seven innings vs. the Brewers on Sunday for a no-decision. It was the first time he gave up two home runs this season.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, when he held the Rangers to two runs in eight innings pitched, he pitched into the ninth inning for the third time in his career but gave up a hit and was removed. It was the Rockies' longest start of the year.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey issued five walks (one intentional) Tuesday at Boston. Despite his struggles this season, walks hadn't been an issue. Besides facing a Red Sox lineup that did not expand its strike zone, he had trouble commanding his off-speed pitches.
away_pitcher_note: In his latest start, a home win over the Rangers, Nicaso walked five and struck out one. However, he held the Rangers to two hits and a run in five innings (88 pitches) and earned the decision in a lopsided Rockies victory.

home_pitcher_note: Shields worked seven shutouts innings at San Diego on Wednesday, despite not having his best stuff. He survived seven hits, two walks and a hit batter with the help of good defense, grinding it out through 118 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Morales gave up five runs (four earned) in six innings of a loss at Texas in his latest start. Morales' big mistake was a home run he served to Prince Fielder. The Rockies were also uncharacteristically sloppy defensively.

home_pitcher_note: After two lackluster starts, Vargas was back on track Friday at Seattle. He breezed through seven shutout innings, giving up three hits with no walks and six strikeouts. He was adept at changing speeds, hitting his spots and keeping hitters guessing.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin gave up a run in each of the first two innings in his most recent start, but he settled down in a pitchers' duel with the Reds' Johnny Cueto -- six innings, four hits, two strikeouts, strikes on 56 of his 88 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa heads to Kansas City having won four straight. He held the Rangers to two runs on three hits with four strikeouts in his most recent start. He got a ground ball with two out and the bases loaded in the sixth.
away_pitcher_note: Stults allowed two runs in the first inning of his last start against the Marlins but settled down thereafter, burying his fastball and secondary pitches down and away in the strike zone. All told, he allowed two runs in six innings in a victory.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles improved to 5-0 by striking out eight -- a season high and two shy of his career high -- in just six innings as the Rockies beat the Reds in lopsided fashion in his last start, at Great American Ball Park.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing eight runs in a start on April 25, Erlin has allowed a combined four earned runs in his last three starts, covering 20 innings. He struck out seven over 6 1/3 scoreless innings the last time out in a win over the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio had a competitive six-inning outing in last Sunday's loss to the Reds, but he was hurt by errors by Justin Morneau and Nolan Arenado. He gave up four runs (two earned), struck out three and walked one.
away_pitcher_note: Roach, a rookie, makes a start in place of Andrew Cashner, who landed on the disabled list with soreness in his right elbow. Roach has been good in long relief and will likely throw 60 or so pitches in his big league debut Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Morales allowed four runs on eight hits over five innings in his last start against the Royals. The lefty hasn't won since April 28 vs. the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner has defied convention by pitching better away from home instead of relying on AT&T Park to thrive. He has compiled a 1.39 ERA in five road starts, compared with 6.20 in four home assignments.

home_pitcher_note: This will be the fourth start of the season for Chacin, who gave up three runs -- all in the second -- in six innings and retired 12 of the final 14 batters he faced in a 3-2 loss at Kansas City his last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Cain made his Major League debut against the Rockies and has accumulated more appearances against them than any other team except Arizona. He's six victories shy of 100 for his career.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa held the Padres to one hit and no runs in seven innings in his last start, a win at home. De La Rosa dealt with soreness in his back and left middle finger, but it hasn't been an issue in his preparation.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson has recovered from a strained left hip that forced him to miss one start. He has lasted at least eight innings in all but one of his eight starts. Hudson's 0-2 with a 7.41 ERA in six Coors Field assignments.

home_pitcher_note: Through his first three starts, Floyd has avoided the inconsistencies and command issues pitchers often experience when they first return from Tommy John surgery. He's limited right-handed hitters to a .194 batting average.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles had bordered on dominant for the entire season until Saturday night, when he walked a career-high eight and yielded six runs over 3 1/3 innings in a loss to the Padres. He said his control was off, no injuries or anything.

home_pitcher_note: Minor has confidently used his offspeed pitches in any count, as he has allowed just two runs in 12 2/3 innings over his past two starts. Half of the 10 runs he's allowed this year have come via home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio has become the king of the workmanlike performance this year. He gave up nine hits, including two home runs, and four in six innings Sunday at home against the Padres, but left with a lead. Colorado won in 10.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran bounced back from a rough outing to record his second shutout of the year on Tuesday. He allowed one run in seven innings against the Rockies last April to begin a 37-start stretch in which he's posted a 2.55 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Morales held the Giants to five hits and three runs in six innings on Tuesday night, and went blow-by-blow with Madison Bumgarner. Morales, as has been the case when he pitched well, had an effective cut fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed six runs in 5 2/3 innings Wednesday in a loss to the Marlins to make him 0-10 with a 5.11 ERA in 15 starts since Aug. 11, 2013. The first inning has been a problem. He has a 9.00 ERA in the first this season.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin gave up three runs and struck out four in 5 2/3 innings in his last start, a loss to the Giants. Two of the four hits were homers. But Chacin, after missing April with a shoulder strain, is gradually improving.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed three runs on six hits and one walk while striking out six in seven innings Thursday against the Marlins. He earned a no-decision in a 4-3 loss, but he has been pitching better lately after a slow start.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had not given up a hit and faced the minimum through three innings before a rain delay ended his start vs. the Giants. He hasn't given up a run in his last 12 innings and has allowed one hit in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez pitched well in Friday's 2-0 loss to the Dodgers. He allowed seven hits, two runs, four walks and struck out three in 6 1/3 innings, but got no run support. He hopes for a little more on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles pitched well enough to win in his last start, walking one and surrendering only two earned runs in six innings vs. the Braves. However, he was disappointed in his six strikeouts, expressing a desire to pitch to contact.

home_pitcher_note: The Tribe's most dependable starter dazzled his last time out, tossing seven shutout frames to beat the Orioles on Saturday, striking out nine while walking two. He's 3-0 with a 2.02 ERA and 7:1 strikeout-to-walk ratio in five May starts.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio held the Braves to two hits and no runs over six innings in his latest start. He pitched around four walks and struck out five but never let the Braves feel as if they could rally. The Rockies are 7-3 in his starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Bauer was roughed up in his last start, allowing four earned runs on six hits in just 4 1/3 innings Sunday against the Orioles. He's allowed two home runs in each of his last two starts, though all four have been solo shots.
away_pitcher_note: Morales struggled against a right-handed hitting Braves lineup in his latest outing, giving up five runs, including three homers, in 4 2/3 innings. The Indians are more favorable to Morales' style, but he has to keep the ball in the park.

home_pitcher_note: Tomlin's defense let him down last time out, with a two-out error setting up a three-run homer that spoiled an otherwise solid start vs. the White Sox. He finished allowing five runs (two earned) over five innings, with eight strikeouts and one walk.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin pitched well in the early going in his latest start, a loss at Philadelphia. But after giving up a leadoff single to Chase Utley and a homer to Ryan Howard to open the sixth, he left accounting for four runs in five-plus innings.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa escaped a bases-loaded, no-out jam in the third inning and held the Phillies to one run in six innings of a win in his latest start. He is 6-0 with a 1.80 ERA in his past seven starts, despite a middle finger bruise.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson has had a good start to his career, winning his first three starts. But he has been the beneficiary of superb run support. In his last two starts, the D-backs have scored 30 runs behind him while he has given up nine (six earned).

home_pitcher_note: After an effective first seven starts, Lyles has struggled through his last three turns, giving up 10 earned runs and 11 walks over 14 1/3 innings. He lasted just five in a no-decision at Philadelphia on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter had the best start of his career Thursday, tossing a complete-game shutout and facing the minimum while giving up three hits. He was the 13th pitcher since 1914 to face the minimum while giving up three or more hits.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio had given up one run in the first four innings against the Indians in his last start, but in the fifth he yielded four runs on five hits that included three doubles and a home run before being pulled.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo picked up the loss in his outing against the Reds on Friday after giving up a grand slam to Reds catcher Devin Mesoraco. Despite giving up five runs, he went seven innings for the fifth time in his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Butler, the Rockies' No. 2 prospect, will make his big league debut against the Dodgers on Friday. The 23-year-old righty went 4-4 with a 2.49 ERA at Triple-A Tulsa this season.
away_pitcher_note: It wasn't quite the near-perfecto he threw in the previous start, but Ryu was effective Saturday, scattering 10 hits but allowing just two runs in six innings. Ryu had to deal with a few long innings on the bench, thanks to 12 runs from his offense.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin missed April with a right shoulder strain, and since returning has struggled at the beginning of games. In his last start, he gave up three first-inning runs on one hit and three walks.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke surrendered four runs in six innings in a loss to Pitsburgh on Sunday, but that line doesn't quite do him justice. Two of those runs scored on a routine ground ball that became a hit because of an infield shift. He's been a consistent force.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies ace saw his six-game winning streak snapped in Monday's loss to the D-backs. De La Rosa matched his season high in innings pitched, limiting Arizona to three runs across seven innings despite not registering a strikeout.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw was about as economical as it gets in his last start, using just 21 pitches to get through the first three innings and throwing 97 for the game. A two-run home run was the left-hander's only mistake in an otherwise fine performance.
summary: 2014-06-08 - Los Angeles Dodgers @ Colorado Rockies (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: A 24th-round Draft pick in 2010 who has developed into a front-line pitcher at Triple-A Colorado Springs, Bergman will make his Major League debut against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd has given up three earned runs or fewer in every start, but two unearned runs off errors cost him against the Mariners on Tuesday. His 10 hits allowed, however, were his most since May 27, 2012.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio struggled with command of both his fastball and his breaking ball Thursday vs. the D-backs. He was consistently behind in the counts, and when he missed, he missed high, resulting in two homers among 11 hits and seven run in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Minor has allowed two earned runs or fewer in five of his seven starts. Since surrendering six homers in his first five starts, he has prevented opponents from going deep in his past two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Matzek's road has been a winding one since the Rockies selected him 11th overall in the 2009 Draft, but manager Walt Weiss believes he's ready. Matzek battled control issues in the Minors and didn't get above Class A until last year.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran has produced a 1.23 ERA in the four starts he's made since allowing a season-high four earned runs on May 14. He takes his MLB-leading ERA into Coors Field, where he allowed one run in seven innings last year.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin, who missed the first month because of a right shoulder strain, found his sinker and curveball in his last start, but faltered in the seventh and was credited with six-plus innings, three runs. He wants to go deeper.
away_pitcher_note: Santana allowed just one unearned run in seven stress-filled innings on Saturday. Opponents have hit .316 with a .369 on-base percentage in his past five starts. He allowed seven runs in his only previous Coors Field start.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum's WHIP (average walks and hits per inning) has climbed to 1.542, which would be a career worst if he finished with a figure that high. But the Giants are 9-4 in his starts.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa fought through rain in his last start, allowing five runs on 5 1/3 innings against the Dodgers. De La Rosa struck out eight but all four of the walks he issued would come around to score. He has lost two straight.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong matched a career high he'd prefer to ignore last Monday against Washington, yielding six extra-base hits. His ratio of 7.9 strikeouts per nine innings is his best for any season except for 2000, when he made four relief appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Bergman displayed the poise of a veteran in his Major League debut on Monday, scattering five hits and striking out four in six innings. He also recorded one of the Rockies' four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner appears on his way to his best season. His ERA so far is a career low, and he has accumulated nearly five times as many strikeouts (9.8 per nine innings) as walks (2.0). He has three double-digit strikeout performances in 14 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio was rattled after Justin Upton's comebacker just missed his head in the first inning of Tuesday's 13-10 loss to Atlanta. He ended that frame with seven runs, finishing with 10 earned runs off three homers, both career highs, in 3 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ryu suffered his first road loss of the season, giving up four runs on six hits in six innings against the Reds on Wednesday. The left-hander is 2-2 with a 4.71 ERA in four career starts against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: In his Major League debut on Wednesday, Matzek held the Braves to two runs in seven-plus innings, mostly using a fastball and a slider. His next start is at Dodger Stadium, not far from his home in Mission Viejo, Calif.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke had a solid outing against the Reds on Thursday, giving up two runs on four hits in six innings, but took the loss. In 11 appearances (10 starts) against Colorado in his career, he is 3-2 with a 4.20 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: After missing the first month with a shoulder injury, Chacin earned his first win of '14 Thursday, holding Atlanta to two hits in seven shutout frames. With his sinker and two-seam working, Chacin was efficient on the ground, needing just 85 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw followed up his rain-shortened complete-game in Colorado with his third consecutive victory, a seven-inning outing against Arizona. Now he gets the Rockies again. He's 11-5 lifetime against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa left his last start, Friday against the Giants, after three innings with back tightness. However, he felt better the next day, and said neither that nor a bruised left middle finger would keep him from the mound.

home_pitcher_note: In two Major League starts since a callup from Triple-A Colorado Springs, against the Braves and the Giants, Bergman has seven strikeouts agaInst two walks, and has pitched six innings each time.
away_pitcher_note: With top Brewers prospect Jimmy Nelson pitching so well at Triple-A Nashville, there's urgency for Estrada to get back on track. He has allowed 23 home runs this season, by far the most in the Majors.

home_pitcher_note: Friedrich will start after the club optioned Juan Nicasio to Triple-A. It will be Friedrich's first Major League appearance since July 28, 2012.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta was away from the team between his past two starts because an undisclosed family matter in the Dominican Republic, but returned with a strong, seven-inning outing in a win over Arizona. He's won three straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Matzek, pitching in front of at least 50 family members and friends, didn't have his slider and gave up 10 hits, but remained composed and held the Dodgers to three runs in a loss at Dodger Stadium in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse has had trouble in five past starts at Coors Field, where he owns a 6.67 ERA and a .306 opponents' average. But it hasn't been the long ball that's hurt him; Lohse has allowed only two homers in 27 Coors Field innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin gave up home runs to Hanley Ramirez and Matt Kemp at Dodger Stadium in his last start, a loss, but was otherwise impressive in his six innings. He struck out five and prevented the lengthy inning.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn followed up an eight-inning scoreless start with five scoreless innings Wednesday before he ran into trouble in the sixth. Still, the right-hander surrendered two runs in six innings on five hits and four walks.
