home_pitcher_note: Bettis enters with some momentum after a solid outing in his second Major League start this season. He took a no-decision in Colorado's May 19 win over the Phillies, but Bettis didn't walk a batter in six innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson's sinking fastball, if it's working, should be a handy pitch for him to use at Coors Field, where fly balls tend to soar. But he's 0-2 with a 6.80 ERA in nine career starts at the mile-high ballpark.

home_pitcher_note: This could be a pivotal start for the struggling Marquis, who has allowed 10 earned runs and 11 hits over his last two starts -- covering only 6 2/3 innings. Manager Bryan Price has indicated that Marquis' status in the rotation is in question.
away_pitcher_note: Butler's last two starts haven't generated much production. He hasn't lasted more than three innings in either of them, while surrendering eight runs (five earned) and 12 hits.

home_pitcher_note: Following a brief stint in the bullpen, Lorenzen will be making his first start since May 10 vs. the White Sox. He lasted only five innings in that start and was in a jam in almost every inning as his pitch count reached 91 before coming out.
away_pitcher_note: This start goes to Rusin, called up from Triple-A, because Jorge De La Rosa is sidelined with a cut on his left (pitching) hand.

home_pitcher_note: Leake has struggled his last two starts and his command was lacking when he gave up three-straight walks, and five overall vs. Cleveland for the first time in his career on Friday. In three starts vs. Colorado, he has a 6.46 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick has had to pitch nearly perfect as of late. In his last three starts, the Rockies have scored just two runs while Kendrick has been in the game -- one of the reasons he is still searching for his first win since Opening Day.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies' front office must love what they are seeing from Hamels, who remains a top trade candidate. He dominated the Nationals on Saturday and is 5-1 with a 2.23 ERA in his last seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis displayed dramatic difference between his fastball and offspeed pitches, baffling the Giants for 8 1/3 innings in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Harang has been a blessing for the Phillies' rotation this season. He has allowed more than three runs in just one of his first 10 starts. He has allowed two or fewer runs in six starts, never pitching fewer than six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Butler took the place of Jorge De La Rosa, who has a cut finger. Butler made his last start Monday against the Reds, and gave up four runs and nine hits in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Williams hopes to finish May on a high note. He allowed three runs in six innings Tuesday against the Mets, but he is 1-3 with a 6.53 ERA in six starts this month. He posted a 3.80 ERA in four April starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles allowed six runs in his last outing against the Giants before leaving with a sprained left toe that pushed back his start from Friday.

home_pitcher_note: In his last four starts, the rapidly improving Kendrick has held opponents to a .198 batting average.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw has allowed more home runs at Coors Field (12) in his career than at any other park except Dodger Stadium. But in 16 career starts there, he is 7-3. He will look to build on the seven scoreless innings he threw in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa has not started since May 21 because of a cut on his left middle finger. But the last time he faced the Dodgers, he went 7 1/3 scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Dodgers finally settled on giving Nicasio his first start of the season in the opener a doubleheader against his former club. The right-hander's longest outing this year is three innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hale draws this assignment as the Rockies look to win both ends of their twin bill with the visiting Dodgers. In his Colorado debut, Hale defeated the Giants in San Francisco.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke has held opponents to a .149 batting average in three starts on the road this year. In six career appearances at Coors Field, he owns a 2-0 record and has allowed just two home runs.

home_pitcher_note: After flirting with a perfect game in his last outing, Bettis will look to last at least eight innings for a third straight start. Limiting free passes has been a recent key for Bettis, who's walked just two in his previous 16 1/3 frames.
away_pitcher_note: Bolsinger has been steady for the Dodgers since garnering his first start on April 23. His only loss of the year came on the road, however. In two starts away from home, Bolsinger's ERA is 2.31, compared to 0.46 in three home starts.

home_pitcher_note: With his first-strike percentage up, control of his two-seam fastball and confidence in his four-seamer, Butler has moved forward in his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler has had success at Coors Field -- 1-0 with a 2.57 ERA in two starts. On the road in 2015, he is 1-2 with a 7.50 ERA. He's been hurt by two Citi Field starts -- 12 runs in 6 2/3 innings. In three other road starts, he has given up eight runs.

home_pitcher_note: Rusin has made two appearances when pressed into action -- a seven-inning, one-run job in Cincinnati, and a 4 2/3-inning win in Philadelphia. He can be effective if he's aggressive.
away_pitcher_note: Only once in his career has Phelps faced the Rockies, and it came at Coors Field. Phelps gave up two runs in six innings in a no-decision. The right-hander seeks his first win since May 9 vs. the Giants, a span of four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick will have to work to keep the ball in the park, especially with Miami slugger Giancarlo Stanton in town. Kendrick is near the top of the league this year with 15 homers surrendered, including five over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: The outcome didn't go Urena's way, but the rookie made strides in his second big league start, a loss to the Cubs. He worked six innings. To get batters off his fastball, he mixed in offspeed pitches better early in counts.

home_pitcher_note: Hale, recalled from Triple-A Albuquerque, gave up three home runs on Tuesday against the Dodgers, but just four runs and kept the team in the game. He's 2-0, 4.20 in three career games at Coors.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey is 0-1 all-time at Coors Field. In just two starts at the high-altitude stadium, he has been touched for four home runs and nine earned runs over 12 2/3 innings. Lackey has gone seven innings in back-to-back starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, De La Rosa successfully battled through a nagging cut on his left middle finger, and he'll likely have similar circumstances in this outing.
away_pitcher_note: Wacha has been at his best away from Busch Stadium this season. The 23-year-old is unbeaten on the road with a 6-0 record and a 1.58 ERA and has allowed two earned runs or fewer in each of those six starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last three starts, Bettis is 3-0 with a 1.21 ERA, has held opponents to a .165 batting average and has 19 strikeouts against five walks.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez has allowed just three runs over his last 32 1/3 innings. He is coming off a career-best 11 strikeout performance. He has made one appearance (in relief) at Coors Field and allowed four runs on five hits in 1 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Phelps will have a shot at redemption against the Rockies after getting battered around at Coors Field in his last start. His numbers at home, though, aren't great this season -- 0-1 with a 5.50 ERA in five games.
away_pitcher_note: After not facing the Marlins at all in his first 26 Major League appearances, Rusin will see Miami for a second time in as many starts. He dominated Miami the last time out, and Rusin will now move forward as a permanent part of the Rockies rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Urena enters on a wave confidence, having shut down the Rockies offense at dangerous Coors Field in his last outing. This will be Urena's fourth career Major League start and second at home.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick has more wins vs. the Marlins than any other team in his career, and he looks to add to that in his second consecutive start against Miami. Kendrick rebounded with seven strong innings vs. the Marlins last time out but lacked run support.

home_pitcher_note: Latos will be making his first start since landing on the disabled list May 23 with left knee inflammation. The right-hander is winless in five starts at home this season, allowing 23 runs in 20 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Now a permanent part of the Rockies' rotation, Hale will make his fourth start this season in a Colorado uniform. Hale saw the Marlins from his days with the Braves, making a career-high five appearances with no runs yielded in nine relief innings.

home_pitcher_note: Haren has been rolling of late, recording quality starts in four of his past five outings and six of eight since the beginning of May. He has struggled though against the Rockies, as his career ERA of 5.12 is his third-highest vs. an opposing team.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa has had moderate success against the Marlins in his career. In 12 games (11 starts), he's 5-5 with a 5.71 ERA. Only two of those starts have come at Marlins Park, where De La Rosa in 1-1 with a 7.71 ERA over 9 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Making his first ever appearance against the Rockies, Keuchel is coming off only his second loss of the season, a seven-inning stint against the White Sox where a two-run home run from Jose Abreu was his only blemish.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis has logged a quality start in five of his six outings this season. Since May 24, the righty has allowed just six runs in 27 1/3 innings. In his last start on Wednesday, he surrendered three runs in five innings to St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Velasquez's second Major League start. He threw five scoreless innings in his big league debut against the White Sox, a game the Astros would drop, 4-1.
away_pitcher_note: After three strong outings to start his season, Rusin was tagged for six runs and 11 hits vs. Miami on Thursday. Prior to that, the lefty went seven innings in each of his first two starts and allowed just three combined runs.

home_pitcher_note: While Kendrick has struggled this season, he's appeared to get on track in his last two starts. Both came vs. Miami: two runs allowed in seven innings on June 7 and two runs in 6 2/3 innings on Friday.
away_pitcher_note: Oberholtzer dazzled with eight scoreless innings in his last start, a 10-0 win against the Mariners, in which he allowed only three hits and fanned five.

home_pitcher_note: Hale has been competitive in his four starts and has 19 strikeouts in 25 2/3 innings. But he has given up six home runs, and needs to keep the ball in the park against the powerful Astros.
away_pitcher_note: McHugh gave up a career-high eight earned runs, lasting only three innings in his last start, an 8-1 loss to Seattle. McHugh is 2-3 with a 6.86 ERA in his past seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa held the Marlins -- who had pounded other Rockies pitchers -- to one run in seven innings Sunday, and is 4-0 with a 2.56 ERA in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: In what was only his second Major League start, Jungmann pitched five innings, allowed seven hits and two runs while striking out five against the Nationals. He's 1-1 with a 2.25 ERA in his young career.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis has dropped his last two starts, giving up eight runs in 10 innings against the Astros and Cardinals. His ability to handle aggressive teams in early innings is being tested.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander's struggles continue in 2015, as he's allowed 18 home runs in 14 starts. In fact, Lohse has surrendered at least one homer in all but two of his outings.

home_pitcher_note: Rusin was victimized by homer-friendly Minute Maid Park in his last start, a loss at Houston. But in his only home start, he fanned eight and yielded two runs in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garza's ERA jumped over 5.00 after allowing six runs and 13 hits in 6 2/3 innings during his last start. The right-hander looked to have his season on the right track in two previous successful outings.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick will have a chance to make up for his last meeting with the D-backs, on April 28: eight runs and 10 hits, including two homers, in 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson is finally getting wins to show for his strong starts. He's won two straight outings, allowing two runs in 13 innings. His only loss was on April 27 against the Rockies. He has a 4.45 career ERA against Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Hale gave up five runs on 10 hits in five innings his last time out, a loss to the Astros. In his more successful outings, Hale has given up hits but avoided the big innings.
away_pitcher_note: Webster allowed six runs in a loss to the Angels Thursday in his second start of the season. He makes his first career start against the Rockies looking to get through six innings for the first time this season.

home_pitcher_note: After five strong starts, four of them wins, De La Rosa had little working in his last outing -- a home loss to the Brewers on Friday. He expects to rebound vs. the D-backs, against whom he has compiled a 2.98 ERA in 24 games.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa has put a rough stretch behind him as he looks for another good outing. He's allowed just one earned run in his last 15 innings. The righty is 2-0 with a 2.57 ERA in his career against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson is 5-4 with a 4.77 ERA in 18 career starts against Colorado. He has struck out 74 batters and walked 32 in 111 1/3 innings lifetime against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis overcame two rough starts with 6 1/3 strong innings in a win over the Brewers on Saturday. He allowed one run on five hits with five strikeouts, inducing 10 outs on the ground.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum is 11-10 with a 3.96 ERA in 29 lifetime outings against the Rockies. The right-hander has struck out 181 batters and walked 82 in 181 2/3 career innings against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin enters looking to build off his previous success against San Francisco. Rusin has started just once against the Giants in his career, but the left-hander tossed seven scoreless innings at AT&T Park in July 2013.

home_pitcher_note: In 20 career starts against Colorado, Bumgarner owns a 9-6 record and 3.13 ERA. The left-hander has 111 strikeouts and 37 walks in 126 1/3 lifetime innings vs. the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick has given up a whopping 21 homers this season, but the Rockies can live with starts like his last, when he yielded three but went six and beat the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Graveman allowed two runs in seven innings in his last start, an 8-2 win over the Rangers on Wednesday. The right-hander has pitched at least seven innings and surrendered two runs or fewer in each of his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hale has shown some strong stretches, but has had trouble finishing. His last start was fine until the fifth, and he ended with five runs and eight hits in 4 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie righty steps up for Sonny Gray, who was a late scratch. It will be the first start of the season for Bassitt. He made five last year with the White Sox, who traded him to the A's over the offseason as part of the Jeff Samrdzija deal.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa left his last start after five innings (one run, four hits) because of a recurring left middle finger cut. Throwing sessions since have gone well.

home_pitcher_note: Hahn comes into the matchup 3-1 with a 1.53 ERA in day games. The right-hander gave up five runs (three earned) in his last start and is 5-6 with a 3.47 ERA on the year.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis had solid fastball location for most of his six innings in his last start, and he has gone at least six in six of his nine starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson has won just once in his last four starts and is coming off his worst outing when he allowed seven runs on 10 hits in 5 1/3. He is pitching for the first time against the NL West-rival Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin gave up five runs in a loss at AT&T Park in his last start, but just two were earned. Rusin has won on the road in relief but not as a starter.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has won three of his last four starts, but has given up 12 runs over the last two. He has struggled keeping the ball in the park lately, as he has allowed six home runs in two starts after giving up three in his first 13.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing vs. the D-backs, Kendrick allowed three homers but limited the damage to four runs in six innings. The right-hander has a career 6.31 ERA vs. Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin will be making his first start since Sept. 27, 2013. He tore his ulnar collateral ligament during his final Spring Training start in 2014 and underwent Tommy John surgery. Corbin will have a 90-pitch limit.
away_pitcher_note: Hale has become homer-prone - six in 42 1/3 innings this season, including three in his last start - but has attacked the strike zone and avoided walks.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa enters this start on quite a roll. After allowing nine runs to the Dodgers on June 8 he has compiled a 1.30 ERA in his four starts since. At times he can get frustrated and an inning can spiral quickly on him.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa threw seven scoreless innings in his last start, and is 3-1 with a 1.37 ERA in seven road starts. His next strikeout will be the 1,000th of his career.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis, making his 11th start of the season, will be looking for his third victory in four starts. He's struggled in Interleague play (7.27 ERA in 17 1/3 innings) but has never faced the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Heaney will make his eighth career start and his third of the season. In his last outing, he held the Yankees to one run and two hits through seven innings. He has surrendered only six hits in 13 innings this year.

home_pitcher_note: Rusin struck out six in his last outing, but was undone by a Nolan Arenado error, followed by a double he allowed. Rusin enters 2-0 with a 3.46 ERA at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Shoemaker has allowed just two runs in each of his past two starts to drop his ERA from 5.20. He is 2-2 with a 1.67 ERA in four career starts against National League teams.

home_pitcher_note: Homer-prone for much of the year, Kendrick made a forward step in his last start -- a no-decision against the D-backs, when he made it through 5 2/3 innings with three runs allowed.

Germen, claimed off waivers from the Cubs on July 7, will be making his first career start after 60 relief outings with the Mets and Cubs. David Hale was the original scheduled starter, but he pitched Thursday following a rain delay.
away_pitcher_note: Miller bounced back from his worst start of the season by taking on Cole Hamels, and shutting out the Phillies through 6 1/3 innings Sunday. Miller is just 5-4 this season despite a 2.07 ERA thanks to minimal run support during his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Dating back to June 25, De La Rosa has given up just three runs in 18 innings, all while dealing with a lingering cut on his left middle finger.
away_pitcher_note: Wisler has helped the Braves win three of his first four career starts. His 0.90 ground-ball/fly-ball ratio might not play well at Coors Field. But he's shown an ability to miss bats when he commands his slider.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis is coming off his worst career start, as he gave up a career-high 10 runs in 2 1/3 innings. It's a small sample size, but Bettis' career numbers versus Atlanta aren't great either. In six frames, he's surrendered 8 runs, 10 hits and 6 walks.
away_pitcher_note: Wood's start in Thursday’s series opener was limited to just two pitches because of a long rain delay. He’s at his best when he commands his curveball, so it will be interesting how he fares in his first Coors Field experience.

home_pitcher_note: Shields hasn't won in his past seven starts and is 0-3 with a 4.79 ERA in that span after starting the year 7-0 with a 3.58 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa has been Colorado's most consistent starter all season, and he'll look to continue that right out of the break. In 25 career games against San Diego (21 starts), De La Rosa is 8-4 with a 4.90 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Ross has posted quality starts in four of his past five outings and has a 1.85 ERA in that time. He hasn't allowed a home run in his past 14 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis rebounded in his last outing, tossing six innings of three-run ball against the Braves. In four career games against the Padres (one start), he's tossed 6 2/3 scoreless innings with five hits surrendered and one walk.

home_pitcher_note: Cashner has gone at least six innings in each of his past three starts and hasn't given up a home run since June 16.
away_pitcher_note: Butler gets his first after being sent down to Triple-A Albuquerque on June 9. Butler, who i 3-6 with a 4.80 ERA in 11 starts, last faced San Diego on May 1, when he pitched four innings, allowing four hits, five runs (three earned) and walking two.

home_pitcher_note: Rusin looks for his first win since defeating the Milwaukee Brewers on June 21. He pitched just two innings in relief in the game before the All-Star break, allowing two hits to the Atlanta Braves and not figuring in the decision.
away_pitcher_note: The Rangers are recalling Nick Martinez from Triple A Round Rock to pitch against the Rockies. Martinez was optioned to Round Rock on July 2 to give him a break and he pitched six innings over two appearances for the Express.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick (3-10) seeks his first win since June 23 when he defeated the Diamondbacks. The Rockies have lost 13 times this year when Kendrick starts, and he pitched just one inning in his last start against the Braves due to a rain delay.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison is making his second start since returning from back surgery. He allowed six runs in four-plus innings against the D-backs on July 8. Harrison has made two career starts against the Rockies and won both while not allowing a run.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa continues to battle through a cut on his left middle finger, but it hasn't affected his pitching much recently. Over his last 11 starts, the left-hander is 6-2 with a 3.02 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Perez will be making his second start since a 14-month absence while recovering from Tommy John elbow surgery. He allowed three runs in five innings against the Astros on Friday. He gave up nine hits, walked two and struck out two.

home_pitcher_note: Butler returned to the Major Leagues on Sunday, giving up just two hits in four innings before a storm washed out his start and cancelled the game. Butler faced Cincinnati earlier this season, surrendering four runs over six frames on May 25.
away_pitcher_note: While not bothered by the glute muscle issue he had to end the first half, DeSclafani battled with location issues in Saturday’s 9-4 loss to the Indians. He allowed a career-high six earned runs and gave up two home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Rusin has been able to thrive this season at the hitter-friendly Coors Field. In five home appearances this season (four starts), he's is 2-0 with a 3.00 ERA. He's struck out 18, walked just six and has served up only two home runs in 27 innings.
away_pitcher_note: With trade rumors swirling, every start between now and July 31 could be Cueto’s last with the Reds. He’ll certainly want to go out on a better note than Sunday vs. Cleveland. He had six walks, including two with the bases loaded.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick has just one home win and has lasted seven innings just twice this season at Coors Field. He faced the Reds one other time this year, giving up four runs over 7 1/3 frames in a 6-4 Rockies win on May 27.
away_pitcher_note: High pitch counts and strike-zone command continue to have Lorenzen fighting an uphill battle. In a no-decision Monday vs. the Cubs, his two-out walk of the pitcher in the second inning required 15 extra pitches. He had 106 total over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is coming off a loss to the Reds in which he gave up five runs over six innings. He had three straight starts in which he did not serve up a run. The righty faced the Rockies in his first start of the year, and didn't get a decision.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa has thrived against the Cubs over his career. In 10 appearances (six starts), the left-hander is 4-0 with a 2.32 ERA and owns a 2.8 strikeout-to-walk ratio. In those 6 starts, De La Rosa hasn't allowed more than three earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Beeler will make his 3rd big league start. His two previous starts have been as the 26th man in doubleheaders on July 7 against the Cardinals and on July 22 against the Reds. So far, he's given up five earned runs on 10 hits in 7 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Flande will make his first start of the season. Flande was a starter in the Minors this season, and with the Rockies last season. The rotation spot is open because righty Chad Bettis is on the DL with right elbow inflammation.

home_pitcher_note: Lester has heated up in the month of July, posting a quality start in four of his past five outings while allowing a combined six earned runs. He's been a relief to his bullpen, as he's pitched at least seven innings in each start this month.
away_pitcher_note: Butler found some stability in his last start, but the right-hander hasn't had much success away from Coors Field. In eight road starts, Butler is 2-3 with a 4.58 ERA and has surrendered more hits (46) than innings pitched (39 1/3).

home_pitcher_note: Martinez is coming off a career-high eight-inning start and is riding a string of 11 straight quality starts. Martinez showcased a particularly effective sinker in his last outing, which will be key to his efficiency moving forward.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin is 1-2 with a 3.38 ERA in his last seven games, six of them starts. Those games include five quality starts. Despite solid work, he has not won since June 21 vs. the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: As nice a season as Wacha is putting together, he has not been so sharp lately. Over his last three starts (17 innings), Wacha has allowed 13 runs. He has, though, finished six innings in 14 of his 19 starts, including his most recent one.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick was less than stellar in his last start but picked up his second home win this season thanks to 17 runs of support. In 12 career outings versus the Cardinals (10 starts), Kendrick is 6-3 with a 3.53 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn has averaged less than three runs per game in run support but has hardly needed it. His ERA dipped lower than 3.00 in June and has stayed below that benchmark.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa beat the Cardinals on June 9, going seven innings and allowing just two runs. In his career against St. Louis, he's 7-4 with a 4.48 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start since June 24, Garcia threw six innings, holding the Reds hitless until the fourth and scoreless until the sixth, when he gave up a three-run home run. It was only the fourth homer he’s allowed in 54 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Flande picked up the first win of his career on Tuesday after going 0-7 before then. Though he normally works out of the bullpen, he made the second-longest outing this season in his first start since September 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Butler lost his last outing to the Cubs on July 29 on a two-run homer by Anthony Rizzo. He has been solid in two games since returning from Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: The six-time All-Star is having another outstanding season, but he’s coming off a rough start against the D-backs when he gave up seven runs and a season-high 12 hits in 6 2/3 innings. This will be his first time facing the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: The team's top pick in the 2013 MLB First-Year Player Draft, Gray will make his Majors debut. He can reach the upper 90s but sits in the 93-95 range, and has developed his slider and changeup at Triple-A Albuquerque.
away_pitcher_note: Nuno will make his first start for Seattle in place of the traded J.A. Happ. Nuno has a 2.11 ERA in 18 relief appearances since being acquired from Arizona on June 3. He’s 3-13, 4.08 ERA in 31 career starts with the Yankees and D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Rusin homered and singled during his last start on July 30, but also gave up six runs and 10 hits in five innings in his last start -- a no-decision at St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old is coming off a one-hitter in a 6-1 victory over the Twins in which he struck out 11. The Mariners are 9-1 in Walker’s last 10 starts. This will be his first time facing the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann has allowed seven home runs over his last six starts, a number slightly slanted by the three blasts he gave up in his last start vs. the Mets. In eight starts against the Rockies, Zimmermann is 5-0 with a 2.20 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa shook off a mini-slump by throwing 6 2/3 efficient innings while beating the Cardinals on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg will make his first start since July 4, when he was pulled less than four innings in with a strained left oblique. He is 2-3 with a 3.09 ERA in five career starts against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Butler's fourth start since being recalled from Triple-A and 15th with the Rockies this season. This will be his first career appearance against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer, who is known for attacking the strike zone, has walked three batters in each of his last two starts -- the first time he's done that this season. Scherzer is 4-5 with a 2.86 ERA in 10 home starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: In two starts since being pulled out of the bullpen to help an injury-riddled starting rotation, Flande is 1-0 with a 2.70 ERA and seven strikeouts against three walks.

home_pitcher_note: Quietly, Niese has been one of the Mets' best pitchers for more than two months. Since the start of June, he owns a 2.78 ERA with 49 strikeouts and 20 walks in 71 1/3 innings. But Niese has struggled vs. the Rox, going 1-3 with a 4.98 career ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Gray, the Rockies' No. 2 prospect, will be making his second Major League start. He allowed two earned runs in four innings against Seattle in his debut on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Over his last nine starts, Harvey owns a 1.64 ERA. By that measure, it's his best stretch of the season -- better even than the 1.98 mark he posted over his first eight outings. Harvey has also not walked a batter in 20 2/3 consecutive innings.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin will make his first career start against the Mets as he tries to pitch longer than five innings for the first time since July 20. He is 1-3 with a 5.40 ERA on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: deGrom has produced a quality start in 13 of his last 14 trips to the hill, with a 1.56 ERA in 98 innings, 105 strikeouts and 12 walks. He held the Rays to two runs -- both via solo homers -- in 6 1/3 innings last Friday in a 4-3 Mets victory.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa is 5-1 with a 4.54 ERA in 11 career appearances (five starts) against the Mets. This will be his 20th start of 2015, a mark he's reached in six of the previous eight seasons.

home_pitcher_note: Syndergaard's rookie year has been a tale of two seasons, with the 22-year-old fireballer going 6-1 with a 1.57 ERA in eight home starts, while he's 0-5 with a 5.01 ERA in eight road outings. This will be his first career appearance vs. the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Butler will try to cut down on walks after issuing four in his last outing, a 6-1 loss to the Nationals on Saturday in Washington. He is winless since May 30.

home_pitcher_note: His last start, Sunday against the Nationals, was abbreviated because he had to pitch in an extra-inning game days earlier, but he still has been solid through three rotation turns.
away_pitcher_note: Ross had a shaky first inning Saturday vs. the Phillies, allowing two runs early, but settling down to pitch well. He took a loss, allowing five hits and three runs through seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: On a tight pitch count, Gray threw an efficient 75 pitches through six innings, struck out five and left with a lead against the Mets, who prevailed against the Rockies' bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Cashner lost to the Phils his last time out, giving up  three runs on eight hits and striking out four in 6 1/3 innings. Cashner’s last start against the Rockies on July 19 was rained out. He has a 4.50 ERA in five career starts vs. Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: After holding the Mets to one run in six innings at Citi Field in his last start, Rusin returns to Coors Field, where he is 2-1 with a 3.89 ERA in seven games (six starts).
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy won in his last outing, against the Reds on Aug. 10, allowing two hits and one run over five innings. The run came on a homer, the 25th he surrendered this season, which is tied for second in the NL.

home_pitcher_note: Hale returns to the Rockies rotation after spending more than five weeks on the disabled list with a mild left groin strain. In six home outings this season, Hale is 3-1 with a 5.52 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Zimmermann twirled a two-hit gem with a season-high nine strikeouts against the Dodgers, but he ended up losing his third straight decision.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa gave up two runs in six solid innings at Citi Field on Wednesday before being lifted for offense. Since going seven innings June 30 at Oakland, he has gone 6 2/3 once and no longer than six in the other seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start Strasburg struggled in the first, after he was given a lead by a Yunel Escboar leadoff homer, Strasburg allowed two runs in the bottom of the frame and wasn't comfortable on the mound. He then threw five shutout frames.

home_pitcher_note: Flande struggled through a tough opening inning in his last start, but he yielded just one run over his final five frames. Against the Nationals on Aug. 9, Flande gave up three runs in 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last 15 innings (three games), Scherzer has allowed 13 runs and raised his ERA to 2.73. Scherzer said his arm slot is not right and he needs to work on his arm action for hours to get it right.

home_pitcher_note: Gray was strong against New York on Aug. 10, surrendering just one hit and one run over six innings. He's still searching for his first Major League win after bullpen struggles have robbed him of that in his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Colon is 1-7 with a 4.83 ERA in his last 10 starts, but threw seven innings against the Pirates on Friday while giving up a run on five hits in a no-decision his last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Rusin was nearly perfect in his last outing, tossing just the 19th complete-game shutout in franchise history. Since being claimed off waivers last September, Rusin has been one of Colorado's best pitchers at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Niese has won two in row and has gone at least six innings in his last four starts. He picked up a no-decision vs. Pittsburgh in his last outing, allowing five hits, three runs, and two walks while striking out six in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his first game off the disabled list, Hale struggled to put away hitters with two strikes and with two outs, and he gave up eight hits and six runs to the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: The Mets will call on Verrett to make his first career start in place of Matt Harvey, whom the team is skipping due to innings concerns. Verrett stretched out to 86 pitches in each of his final two starts for Triple-A Las Vegas.

home_pitcher_note: As Teheran has found more consistency with his slider and more comfort with his curveball, he has turned things around. He has posted a 2.45 ERA in four August starts and a 2.44 ERA in 12 home starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa managed the Nationals' lineup expertly and threw six scoreless innings last time out. However, he hasn't gone deeper than six frames in each of his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz displayed an overpowering fastball during Thursday's start against the Cubs. But the rookie was once again hurt by an inconsistent slider that has added to his difficulty to go through lineups multiple times.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis went on the disabled list July 18 with right elbow inflammation. In his final rehab appearance, he threw five scoreless innings for Triple-A Albuquerque.

home_pitcher_note: Miller has produced a 3.11 ERA during a 17-start winless streak that’s been plagued by meager run support. The right-hander has allowed two earned runs in 19 of his 25 starts. He has posted a 2.01 ERA in 12 starts at Turner Field.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Flande beat the Nationals by holding them to two runs on three hits in seven innings. He also notched two hits, driving in a run and scoring a run against Max Scherzer.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates have won each of Liriano's last 10 starts, and he is 5-0 with a 3.19 ERA during that stretch. He has struggled a bit of late with a 5.06 August ERA. He's 1-2 with a 5.48 ERA in four career starts vs. the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old, drafted No. 3 overall in 2013, makes his fifth Major League start. Gray, who has yet to figure in a decision, is coming off his shortest outing, (1 2/3 innings, seven runs on eight hits) vs. the Mets last Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Since his shaky Pirates debut on Aug. 4, Happ has allowed only one run in 17 1/3 innings over three starts. Happ has not faced the Rockies since 2011, but he has gone 1-0 with a 1.93 ERA in four career games against them.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin tries to get back on track in his first career start against Pittsburgh. He allowed a season-high 11 runs and 12 hits in two innings to the Mets last Saturday at Coors Field. He’d allowed four runs over 20 innings in his previous three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Morton will look to finish an up-and-down August on a high note. The right-hander has logged three quality starts over his last five outings, but he's permitted five runs without completing six innings in the other two.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa seeks his first win since Aug. 1. He allowed five runs, including two homers, his last time out, Monday in Atlanta. He’s gone at least six innings in all five starts this month.

home_pitcher_note: In his return from right elbow inflammation that struck right after the All-Star break, Bettis held the Braves to one run on five hits for a win Tuesday in Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals scored four runs while sending nine batters to the plate against Ray in the first inning in his last outing. Ray's night ended before he retired a batter in the fourth. He was charged with six runs in the 91-pitch outing.

home_pitcher_note: Flande battled without his best stuff Wednesday, giving up three runs in five innings at Atlanta his last time out. He held the Nationals to two runs and three hits in seven innings in his last home start.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin is making his 11th start after missing all of the 2014 season and the first three months of 2015 while recovering from Tommy John surgery. The team is being cautious with him, limiting him to about 95 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick has been bothered by poor location for much of the season, which has led to 26 home runs allowed in 21 starts. He hopes to be better after missing a month on the disabled list with right shoulder inflammation.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa has had stretches where he has looked like a top-of-the-rotation pitcher, but he also tosses out occasional clunkers. Last time out he allowed five runs in five innings to the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Gray's last outing in Pittsburgh saw him throw a season-high 89 pitches. But he only lasted 4 1/3 innings, which represented his second shortest appearance this year. Entering his sixth start, Gray is still looking for his first decision.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson has pitched well in two outings since a brief demotion. Anderson was optioned to Triple-A Reno on Aug. 18, but after making a cross-country flight, he was immediately recalled when Jeremy Hellickson got hurt.

home_pitcher_note: Rusin's only start against the Giants this year resulted in one of his six no-decisions. On June 27 at AT&T Park, Rusin surrendered five runs (two earned) over 6 1/3 frames. It stands as his fourth-longest outing this year.
away_pitcher_note: Like most pitchers, Vogelsong has had his share of struggles at Coors Field. He's 3-3 there with a 6.63 ERA in 10 appearances, including six starts.

home_pitcher_note: In 25 career games against San Francisco (22 starts), De La Rosa is 9-6 with a 4.05 ERA. He gave up two runs in five innings against the Giants on April 25.
away_pitcher_note: Heston hopes to recover after a bump in the road that saw him yield five earned runs on nine hits in 3 2/3 innings Sunday vs. the Cardinals.  Heston had gone 13 days between his last two starts, and is not expected to have a lot of length Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis had one of his best starts this year against the Giants at Coors Field, tossing 8 1/3 innings of two-run ball on May 24. The outing was his longest this season.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy has struggled on the road, where he's 1-4 with a 4.81 ERA in seven starts. He's coming off an August in which he was 2-2 with a 4.67 ERA in six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Flande hasn't started against the Giants this season, but he did face them once in a relief appearance. He came in for the injured Jordan Lyles on May 23 and yielded six hits and four runs over two innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner has a very real chance to record his first 20-win season. The last San Francisco left-hander to earn this distinction was Ron Bryant, who won 24 in 1973.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy had another solid outing in his last start, but a took a no-decision against Texas, allowing five hits and two runs in seven innings while posting a career-high 12 strikeouts. He has been strong since the All-Star break, posting a 2.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick returned from right shoulder inflammation and tossed four innings of one-run ball against Arizona on Sept. 1. In two starts against the Padres earlier this season, Kendrick surrendered 10 combined runs in 12 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Rea showed poise pitching against the NL West-leading Dodgers in just his fifth career start. He allowed two runs on four hits, struck out six and walked two. He was done after five innings, throwing 76 pitches and taking a hard comebacker.
away_pitcher_note: Gray will face the Padres for a second time this season. Against them on Aug. 15, the right-hander surrendered five hits and one run over five innings. Gray is still looking for his first Major League win.

home_pitcher_note: Shields struggled with command issues in his last outing, walking a career-high six batters. The right-hander allowed three runs (two homers) on three hits, throwing 107 pitches, 60 for strikes, through five innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Rusin threw a complete game against the Giants on Sept. 3, allowing six hits and three runs. Rusin last faced San Diego on Aug. 26 at Coors Field, also throwing a complete game, allowing no runs and five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Ross had a solid outing, but lost in his last start due to the Padres' lack of run support. The right-hander allowed only one run off of five hits through six innings. Ross’ current 3.21 ERA is now the lowest it’s been since his first start.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa won in his last outing against the Giants on Sept. 4, allowing one run off of six hits, while pitching seven innings. De La Rosa took a loss last time he faced San Diego on July 17 at Petco Park, when have gave up three runs (two homers).

home_pitcher_note: The 34-year-old missed 10 weeks in the first half with a lat injury, but is 7-2 with a 3.14 ERA over his last 11 starts and coming off 6 1/3 innings of one-run ball in a win at Oakland. This will be his first time facing the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis lost in his last outing, as the Rockies fell to the Giants on Sept. 5. Bettis allowed four runs off of eight hits. Bettis has not yet faced Seattle in his career.

home_pitcher_note: The 27-year-old is 0-2 with a 4.42 in four starts since being recalled from Triple-A Tacoma in late August, including a 3-0 loss to Texas in his last start when he gave up two earned runs in 5 1/3 innings. This will be his first time facing Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Flande took a loss in his last outing, allowing six runs on eight hits against the Giants on Sept. 6. Flande faced the Mariners on Aug. 5, earning the win with a scoreless inning of relief.

home_pitcher_note: Paxton rejoins the rotation after 15 weeks on the DL with a sprained finger tendon. He was 3-3 with a 3.70 ERA in 10 games after opening the season as theNo. 2 starter and 12-7, 3.05 in 27 career starts. He’s never faced Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick, who made his second start Sept. 2 since coming off the DL Sept. 1 with right-shoulder inflammation, allowed three runs on seven hits and fanning four in five innings to pick up his fifth win of the season vs. the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw continues his campaign, still in play for a fourth Cy Young Award, as well as titles for strikeouts and innings pitched. And he no-hit the Rockies last year.
away_pitcher_note: Gray, the third overall pick in the 2013 Draft, still is looking for his first big league victory. The Rockies are 1-6 in his seven starts since his Aug. 4 callup.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson returns from a calf cramp suffered in his Sept. 6 start in San Diego, so he’s getting three extra days of rest. That said, this is his best and healthiest season since 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin was 3-2 in six starts through the end of June, but 2-6 in 18 starts since then. He was tagged for six runs on eight hits in just three innings in his last start, an 11-4 loss to San Diego.

home_pitcher_note: Wood will be looking to bounce back from his worst start as a Dodger, lasting only 1 2/3 innings in Arizona when he allowed home runs to Welington Castillo and Paul Goldschmidt.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa has been the Rockies' most consistent starter with a team-high nine victories. He is 7-10 in 24 games against the Dodgers, 2-5 at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis, making his 18th start, has a 2.13 ERA in five career games (two starts) against the Padres. Since returning from right elbow inflammation, he is 2-1 with a 3.63 ERA in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy had his worst outing in nearly four months his last time out, against the Giants, allowing seven earned runs in 4 2/3 innings. He has a 3.57 ERA in three starts against the Rockies this season and won at Coors Field on Aug. 16.

home_pitcher_note: Flande has provided mostly solid work since joining the rotation in late June, but in his last two outings he has managed just eight innings total and has given up 10 runs on 14 hits.
away_pitcher_note: Erlin had a left elbow injury in 2014 that caused him to miss three months. He's been in the Minors ever since and was 7-6 with a 5.60 ERA in 24 starts for Triple-A El Paso this season. He's the first lefty to start for the Padres in ’15.

home_pitcher_note: In three starts since returning from right-shoulder inflammation, Kendirck is 2-0 with a 3.86 ERA, 10 strikeouts and six walks.
away_pitcher_note: Shields shined on Monday, allowing only a run on four hits. He walked two and struck out six over seven innings for his 12th win. He's sitting on 200 strikeouts and is about to reach the 200-inning plateau for the for the ninth year in a row.

home_pitcher_note: Gray is looking for his first career win after 8 starts. He pitched 4 2/3 innings and allowed two runs on six hits and two walks while striking out eight in LA on Monday, throwing a career-high 92 pitches. He has a 3.60 ERA in three September starts.
away_pitcher_note: With two solid starts after spending six weeks on the DL with an elbow tendon issue, Burnett goes after his first win since July 20. This will only be his third career start in Coors Field, where he's 0-2 with a 7.30 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After  his second complete game at Coors Field this season -- nine innings of three-run ball vs. the Giants -- Rusin has pitched two road outings and allowed a combined nine runs on 13 hits in nine innings. He is 4-2 with a 4.74 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty has allowed a total of six runs in his last seven starts, while fanning 44 versus seven walks in 41 2/3 innings. This will be Happ’s first career start in Colorado, where he did make one relief appearance in 2009.

home_pitcher_note: Bergman pitched 3 1/3 innings of one-run ball for his third win Saturday, allowing three hits and no walks while striking out three. He’s made one start in 2015, holding the Giants to four hits and two walks while fanning four on the road in April.
away_pitcher_note: Morton takes his second crack at a career-high-tying 10th win. The first inning is a bigger key for him than for most pitchers: He’s allowed first-inning scores in nine of his 20 starts, including the last one, on Thursday against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis was solid Friday, allowing one run on four hits and a walk, while striking out six over five innings. His 96 pitches kept him from going deeper. He threw seven shutout innings in his previous start, and is 2-1 with a 2.76 ERA in September.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start on Friday in Los Angeles, Locke again finished strong after a rocky beginning. To get it quicker, per manager Clint Hurdle, he needs to mix his pitches “from the beginning, not waiting till 10-12 fastballs into the game.”

home_pitcher_note: Hale has made three relief appearances this month and given up seven runs on 12 hits in 8 1/3 innings. He is stepping in for Yohan Flande, who is still recovering from taking a line drive to his left knee in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Bolsinger lasted just 4 1/3 innings his last start, and he doesn't feel the same since being sent down to Triple-A in July. The numbers back it up: Bolsinger has a 6.23 ERA in his last three starts, compared with a 2.83 ERA before being optioned.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick struggled to stay down in the zone on Sunday vs. San Diego, giving up six runs on a walk and six hits -- including five homers -- in four innings. He fell behind in counts, and the Padres made him pay for it.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson allowed five runs in 4 2/3 innings in his last outing, surrendering two home runs to add to his team-high 17. Anderson is a ground-ball master but struggles when he leaves the ball up in the zone.

home_pitcher_note: Rusin was haunted by walks on Tuesday vs. the Bucs, falling behind in counts and walking four. He gave up six runs on eight hits in four innings. All of the runs came with two outs; three of the walks contributed to run-scoring rallies.
away_pitcher_note: Wood pitched well but took the loss in his last outing against the D-backs. He's alternated wins and losses in his last eight starts and has thrown fewer than 79 pitches in each of his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Being efficient with his pitches is a key for Ray as he tries to learn how to pitch deeper into games. Last time out he allowed three hits in six shutout innings against the Dodgers in Chavez Ravine.
away_pitcher_note: Bergman's last appearance, against the Pirates last Tuesday, was his first start since April 14. He gave up seven runs and 10 hits on 79 pitches, but should be more stretched out for this game.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson is making his final start of the year and is hoping to finish with back-to-back good outings after an inconsistent 2015. He struck out a career-high 10 over six innings in his last start against Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: In a year of subpar pitching for the Rockies, Bettis has been one of the brightest developments this season. In his last seven starts, he is 3-1 with a 3.43 ERA, 32 strikeouts and 12 walks.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Corbin's 16th start after missing all of 2014 and the first three months of this year following Tommy John surgery. Though he didn't pitch well his last time out, the five starts prior he had a 1.44 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Hale gave up an early run to the Dodgers in his last start before pitching the Rockies to a win. Mechanical changes over the course of the season are taking hold now.

home_pitcher_note: Heston  has struck out 7.14 batters per nine innings against 3.26 walks. Improved pitch efficiency could make Heston, 27, who was a 12th-round pick out of East Carolina in 2009, a viable big league starter.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies have won three of Kendrick's past four starts. The right-hander makes his 27th start of the season but has not pitched past the sixth inning since June 7.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy has quietly been the Giants' most consistent starter behind Madison Bumgarner. The right-hander has pitched into the sixth inning in 15 of his 16 starts since coming off the disabled list July 3.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin is at one of his favorite stadiums, AT&T Park, where he has a 1.35 ERA in three starts. He's also pitched well overall against the Giants -- 1-0, 2.01 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Cain will be making his first start since Aug. 25 at Wrigley Field. He's made two relief appearances totaling three innings since then. Because Cain hasn't built up the ideal durability to start, his appearance vs. the Rockies is likely to be brief.
away_pitcher_note: Bergman will make just his fourth start of the season to complete a year that saw him develop into a successful relief man. But on April 14 he started and threw four scoreless innings at AT&T Park.
