home_pitcher_note: Greinke will make his first start for the D-backs after signing a six-year, $206.5 million free-agent deal this past offseason. In four Cactus League starts, he had a 1.88 ERA. He also started a pair of Minor League games.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies' all-time leader in several categories, including wins (78) and strikeouts (877), De La Rosa experienced a first last year on July 5, when he pitched five frames and got the decision in a 6-4 Rox win at Chase Field, where he had been 0-7.

home_pitcher_note: Miller will make his first start for the D-backs after being acquired from the Braves in a five-player deal in December. He had 17 losses last season, but he pitched better than that with a 3.02 ERA in 33 starts.
away_pitcher_note: The development of a breaking ball and a cutter as pitches that could cover the glove side helped Bettis go from struggling reliever to promising starter last season. He has shown leadership qualities.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin had an outstanding spring, compiling a 1.71 ERA in five Cactus League starts. He worked hard on refining his changeup, a pitch he intends to throw more this year. He returned from Tommy John surgery last July.
away_pitcher_note: After being out since the end of April 2014 because of Tommy John surgery, Chatwood not only proved his health during Spring Training but demonstrated better efficiency than expected. The Rockies will watch his innings in a common-sense manner.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles has had promising outings over two seasons but missed time in 2014 (broken left hand) and in 2015 (right big toe injury). Still, the arm is healthy. He struggled with command this spring but can cover for that by forcing double-play grounders.
away_pitcher_note: Rea’s fastball maxed out around 93 mph last season, but -- after adding 20 pounds of muscle in the offseason -- he’s been routinely hitting 93-94. He tossed seven scoreless frames against Colorado in his final start of 2015.

home_pitcher_note: In keeping with April struggles in recent years, De La Rosa lost his location after a strong beginning and fanned eight, but yielded eight hits and five runs in 4 2/3 innings vs. the D-backs on Opening Day. The bats and the bullpen bailed him out.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz takes the hill in Colorado, where he spent his first three big league seasons. After two years in Oakland -- spent primarily as a reliever -- Pomeranz is back in the rotation, where he’ll showcase his brand new cutter.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies gave Bettis a 6-2 lead at Arizona in his first start, but he struggled in the sixth inning and was removed. He ended up with a no-decision in a game the Rockies let get away.
away_pitcher_note: Shields’ start was moved up because of Tyson Ross’ injury, but he’s still pitching on normal rest. Shields is 6-1 lifetime against the Rockies and looked sharp - aside from one rough inning - in his first start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: In his first since April 29, 2014, after a long comeback from Tommy John surgery, Chatwood held the D-backs to two runs (one earned) and seven hits, with three strikeouts, in 6 1/3 innings to earn a win.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Samardzija's second of three season-opening starts away from AT&T Park. Barring rainouts, he won't pitch at home until April 22 against Miami. "I'll just go out and be a road warrior for the first month," he said.

home_pitcher_note: In a performance that left him frustrated, Lyles lasted just 3 1/3 innings and gave up five runs on seven hits and three walks in a loss to the Padres in the home opener.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy owns a 7-7 record with a 3.90 ERA in 22 career starts against Colorado. That includes a 5-4 mark with a 4.98 ERA in 11 games at Denver's Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa has started slowly the last four years now. Healthy coming out of Spring Training, De La Rosa has been bested for 15 hits, seven walks and four home runs in 8 2/3 innings over two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cain received a no-decision in his season debut after allowing two runs on six hits and one walk with three strikeouts in six innings against the Dodgers. A pair of RBI singles in the fifth inning hurt Cain the most in what was still a quality start.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks posted a quality start in his first outing -- and got a hit off Zack Greinke. He'd like to improve his fastball command and his changeup vs. right-handed hitters. This will be his first start at home, where he posted at 3.38 ERA last year.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis threw seven innings, struck out six and gave up two runs (one earned) while beating the Padres on Sunday. His experience at Wrigley is limited to a scoreless two-thirds of an inning of relief in 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta helped himself by hitting his first home run, a two-run shot, in his last start. Pitching-wise, he said his offspeed stuff was "just average" but he did well enough against the D-backs to post his 22nd consecutive quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Bergman had his start moved back to Saturday, as he'll face the Cubs for the first time in his career. This will also be Bergman's first start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Lester has posted quality starts in each of his first two outings. He did not get a decision in his last start against the Reds, and admitted he was overthrowing early in the game. He's 1-1 with a 1.93 ERA in two career starts vs. the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: This will be the first career start at Wrigley Field for Chatwood, who pitched solidly with the exception of a pair of two-out, two-run homers in a home loss to the Giants in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: Replacing Tim Melville in the rotation and with Alfredo Simon being moved back, Straily will be making his first start of '16. Given a long-man role after being an April 2 waiver claim, he has a 3.24 ERA over 8 1/3 innings in three games.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles was in fair shape until the third time through the order in his last start,  but he was out after 4 1/3 innings. He went just 3 1/3 his first start.

home_pitcher_note: Stephenson, the Reds' top pitching prospect, was recalled from Triple-A to start in place of Alfredo Simon. Simon has right biceps tendinitis but is expected to make his next start.
away_pitcher_note: After two rough starts to begin the season, De La Rosa was good enough to beat the Giants at Coors Field -- 6 2/3 innings, four runs (three earned) on four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Iglesias wasn’t pleased with himself after allowing a second-inning homer to the Cubs' Kris Bryant on Thursday in a loss. But he otherwise felt like he executed his pitches over five frames. But he threw 93 pitches and gave up two walks and six hits.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis threw six scoreless innings and held the Cubs to three hits while winning his last start, but three walks and a high pitch count had him looking at making adjustments.

home_pitcher_note: Gray suffered an abdominal strain late in Spring Training, but is healthy and has built his pitch count. His strengths are his fastball and changeup, but success could depend on his slider and curve.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir tries to rebound from a pair of rocky starts, both against the Giants, in which he gave up a combined 10 runs in eight innings. He’s 1-0 with a 4.50 ERA in one career start vs. the Rockies, his lone Coors Field outing, but that came in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood threw seven scoreless innings at Wrigley Field in his last start, and has been solid by relying on his fastball and cutter in his three starts.
away_pitcher_note: The dazzling 28-year-old rookie from Japan makes his Coors Field debut. Maeda has pitched at least six innings in all three starts, allowing one run in 19 innings and striking out 15 (against four walks).

home_pitcher_note: After two short starts during which he ran into trouble by the second time through the order, Lyles threw seven innings on 76 pitches while beating the Reds in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Wood must shake off a rough return to Turner Field,  where he allowed six runs (three earned) on seven hits in a season-low four innings. Coors Field has been nightmarish for him: a 12.27 ERA (15 earned runs on 21 hits in 11 innings) in three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis originally was scheduled for Tuesday, but moved up because Jorge De La Rosa has been ill and was delayed a day. Last game, vs. the Reds, he retired 18 of 21 batters, but gave up three runs on two homers.
away_pitcher_note: Locke is coming off a frustrating outing in San Diego. He continued to induce ground balls but wound up allowing eight runs on 11 hits and four walks in three innings. He's 0-1 with a 5.00 ERA in three starts at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa was originally slated for Monday, but he needed an extra day because of the stomach flu. His last start, he struggled with command and concentration and was gone after two innings against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Cole returned to ace-level form Thursday in a win over the Padres, striking out seven without a walk over six scoreless innings. He's faced the Rockies only once in his career, giving up three runs in 5 1/3 innings in 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Gray gave up a triple and two homers in the first, then settled down to retire nine in a row and 12 of 13. He gave up 5 runs on seven hits and set a career high with a filthy slider for 10 strikeouts in five innings en route to a Rockies win.
away_pitcher_note: Niese picked up a win Friday on a tough night to pitch in Arizona, allowing four runs on 10 hits and two homers in 5 1/3 innings. Niese has struggled at hitter-friendly Coors Field, posting a 7.94 ERA in four career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Ray had his worst outing of the season last time out against the Pirates allowing five runs in just three innings. The key for Ray is locating his secondary pitches so hitters can't sit on his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood had little command of any of his pitches Saturday, getting chased with three runs in four innings while laboring through 95 pitches.  Even when he made his pitches, the Dodgers connected, with A.J. Ellis driving a game-winning two-run homer

home_pitcher_note: Greinke has not had  success at Chase Field this year, compiling a 9.72 ERA in three starts there compared to a 1.93 ERA in two road starts. Greinke's usual pinpoint command has not been as good in the games he's struggled.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin made 22 starts and had two complete games last year. After 9 2/3 scoreless relief inning in his last three games, he replaces Jordan Lyles in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Miller had some positives to build off in his last start, but he was not pleased with the numbers, allowing five runs in five innings. He seemed to have his mechanics back in order, however, and his pitches had better life.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis has had dominating stints in his last three starts, but every small mistake has hurt him as the Rockies lost his last two starts. Still, he has 22 strikeouts against eight walks.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran righty remains in search of his first win, despite four quality starts in five outings. The Padres have scored just six times in those five starts. Shields has won six of his last seven decisions vs. Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: The right-handed pitcher took a no-decision after allowing six runs on nine hits and one walk with two strikeouts in 3 2/3 innings against the Pirates in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: Cashner’s last start -- 2 2/3 innings, 6 R, 3 ER vs. San Francisco -- was his shortest since 2013, a disappointing result given his two solid outings before it. He’ll be happy to return home, where he has a 2.71 career ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The righty is making his first start of 2016. He was recalled from Triple-A Albuquerque on April 27 and struck out four batters in two innings in relief. He is 2-0 with a 4.09 ERA in four starts at Triple-A.

home_pitcher_note: It’s been an impressive first two starts for the 24-year-old Vargas, who has allowed just one run over 10 1/3 frames. In four starts this year - two at Double-A and two in the Majors - Vargas has whiffed 23 in 23 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After missing most of the previous two seasons due to Tommy John surgery, Chatwood delivered a healthy and productive April that included a 3-2 record, 2.73 ERA, 1.28 WHIP and 20:7 strikeout-to-walk ratio in 29 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cain threw 108 pitches in his most recent start Saturday at New York, which Giants manager Bruce Bochy believes will help strengthen the veteran's arm. Cain is 17-9 with a 3.41 ERA in 36 lifetime starts against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Moved from the bullpen to the rotation, Rusin held the D-backs scoreless on one hit in five innings before reaching his pitch threshold (76). He won't have as tight a limit this time.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner's day-night splits are intriguing. His evening ERA of 2.99 bests his day figure of 3.11, and yet his daytime winning percentage (38-19, .667) is better than his record at night (50-41, .549).
away_pitcher_note: In four road starts this season, Bettis is 2-0 with a 4.24 ERA. Since a no-decision at Arizona in his first start, he's 2-0 with a 3.00 in starts at the Cubs, the Reds and the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto pitched better than his numbers suggested Monday at Cincinnati in his most recent start. He surrendered six runs in five innings, but all of them were scored in third. He kept the Giants close in a game they ultimately won.
away_pitcher_note: After giving up three hits a walk and two runs to begin Monday's start against the Padres, Gray retired 18 of the next 19 and kept his fastball at or near 97 mph throughout.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija has won three starts in a row for the first time in his career. He has given the Giants the durability they expected, pitching into the eighth inning three times in the last five games and exceeding 110 pitches three times in that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Butler showed flashes when he retired the first 11 he faced in his last start against the Padres, but key mistakes, including a changeup hit for a home run and a slider for a key double, led to five runs and a loss.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood has a 0.33 road ERA and a 24 2/3-inning road scoreless streak; now he has to solve Coors. Chatwood, however, said the difference in his numbers is he has made just two home starts.
away_pitcher_note: With the starters pushed back a day to get some rest, Bradley will make the spot start. The righty started on April 18 against the Giants and went 4 1/3 innings and allowed five runs on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: Rusin lives by contact, but the Giants got the best of him in his last start. He gave up seven runs and 13 hits in 4 1/3 innings and couldn't pull in the win despite a large lead.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa is looking to rebound after struggling a bit in his start against the Marlins when he allowed four runs in 5 2/3 innings. In his two starts prior to that, De La Rosa allowed just one run over 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis has given up six homers this season but notes that solo homers aren't bad. But three-run shots like the one by the Giants' Brandon Crawford that turned his last start must be eliminated.
away_pitcher_note: Ray allowed two runs on six hits in 5 1/3 innings in his last start. The key for Ray is pitch efficiency. When he nibbles at the corners and gets into too many deep counts it limits how many innings he can pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Gray held the Giants to one hit in seven scoreless innings on Saturday. Instead of relying on his heavy fastball, he mixed sliders and curveballs to a greater degree than his previous 12 career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Through seven starts, Harvey owns a 1.61 ERA in the first through fourth innings and an 11.25 mark in innings five and six. He’ll look to reach the seventh for the first time this season at Coors Field, where he has never pitched.

home_pitcher_note: Using his two-seam fastball and occasionally mixing in a curve for speed variance, Butler struck out a career-high six and threw six scoreless innings against the Giants as his maturation continues.
away_pitcher_note: With Steven Matz nursing a sore left elbow, Verrett will fill in Saturday in Denver. His qualifications include eight innings of one-run ball in place of Matt Harvey last August at Coors Field; overall, Verrett owns a 2.36 ERA in six career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood makes his fourth try for his first win at home this  season. His home ERA is 7 ½ runs higher than his 0.33 road ERA. He was done in by a D-backs two-out rally that saw six runs on five hits and a walk between the second and third outs.
away_pitcher_note: After gutting through seven innings of two-run ball last time out in Los Angeles, deGrom feels he is closer to locking his mechanics back in sync. His next challenge will come amid the thin air of Coors Field, where deGrom has never pitched.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia has not allowed an earned run in his last two starts and has allowed only six hits during that 14-inning span. He has kept the ball in the park, too, giving up just two home runs over 179 total batters faced this season.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis tied a career high with eight strikeouts in 6 1/3 innings in his last start, a no-decision in the Rockies' win over Arizona. With a big lead, Bettis gave up four runs in his final 1 1/3 frames and needs to hold his form more consistently.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright has won his last three decisions, including an outing on Thursday in which he allowed a season-high seven runs and 11 hits. He’s still searching for feel of his curveball and has pitched past the sixth just once.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin was solid for the first five innings in his last start, against the D-backs at home, but gave up four runs and didn't make it out of the sixth because of mistake fastballs hit for momentum-turning doubles

home_pitcher_note: Wacha is winless in his last four starts, having allowed 14 runs (10 earned) over 25 innings. His defense committed three errors behind him to complicate his last start, which lasted a season-short four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gray earned his first Major League win by displaying an electric fastball and slider while striking out eight Mets at Coors Field in his last start. He has 24 strikeouts against 10 hits in his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Gerrit Cole is coming off throwing eight scoreless innings in a win against the Cubs. It was the only time Cole has gone more than six innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Butler has won his last two starts by pitching six scoreless innings at San Francisco and bobbing and weaving through four runs in five innings against the Mets. He has 12 strikeouts in his last 16 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Home runs continue to bother Niese, but he put together a second straight quality start Monday, holding the Braves to two runs over six innings. He has allowed 11 homers in 46 innings this season, four in his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood, who threw seven innings in a win over the Mets on Sunday, has challenged the strike zone. He has 34 strikeouts against 14 walks through 50 2/3 innings over eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Facing his former team for the first time this season, Nicasio is coming off another uneven outing. He allowed five runs (three earned) in five innings against the Braves on Tuesday. His last quality start was April 29.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis relied mainly on his sinker -- with a four-seam fastball and a few cutters mixed in -- while forcing 11 ground-ball outs in a victory at St. Louis in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Vogelsong's second spot start of the season. Arguably his best performance thus far came in a similar situation on April 13, when he limited the Tigers to one run while striking out five over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles began the season on Colorado's Opening Day roster and went 1-1 with a 7.64 ERA in four starts before being optioned to Triple-A on April 25. In four starts for Albuquerque, he went 1-1 with a 5.40 ERA, nine walks and 15 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander will make his 10th start, coming off two good outings after fixing the mechanics of his delivery. Last time out, Price went 7 1/3 innings against the Royals - allowing five hits, two runs and one walk with five strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: The lack of command and confidence in his fastball hurt De La Rosa early this season, when he posted a 10.18 ERA in five starts. He went to the DL with a left groin injury, and worked on his sharpness.

home_pitcher_note: The trusty knuckleballer, holding down a 2.52 ERA, returns to the mound after two consecutive losses. His last time out, Wright suffered a 3-2 loss against the Royals, allowing five hits, three runs and one walk with six strikeouts in eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: On Sunday, Bettis threw eight pitches in a no-stress first inning before rain caused the game to be postponed. Bettis held the Cardinals to one run and five hits in six innings while winning his last official start.

home_pitcher_note: The righty took his fourth loss of the season against Cleveland on Friday night, allowing five hits and four runs with four walks through six innings, coming out with a 5.92 ERA. This will be Buchholz’s first career start against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: After giving up nine runs in 3 1/3 innings against the Cardinals in his last start, when he didn't command his fastball or slider, Gray looks to regain his 1.80-ERA form from his previous three outings.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood has been dominant on the road with a 0.53 ERA. He hasn't been as solid at home, but he won his last start at Coors -- over the Mets on May 15, when he gave up three runs and six hits in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: The seemingly resurgent veteran has recorded a 1.71 ERA in his last three starts after posting a 7.84 figure in his first six outings. Cain's 0-2 with a 6.62 ERA in three road starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Butler held the Giants scoreless on four hits in six innings in a 2-0 victory at AT&T Park on Mother's Day. Butler is coming off a scoreless, one-hit, 2 2/3-inning relief appearance at Boston on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner is looking more and more like the 2014 World Series Most Valuable Player. He was 2-2 with a 3.64 ERA in five April starts, yet is 4-0, 0.98 in five starts in May.

home_pitcher_note: Rusin replaced a wild and ineffective Jordan Lyles on Monday in Pittsburgh and threw 4 2/3 scoreless innings. Rusin struggled with the Giants in a May 5 start, giving up 13 hits and seven runs in 4 1/3 innings of a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Part of Cueto's success this year can be attributed to him allowing just two home runs to the 293 batters he has faced. Also, his strikeout-to-walk ratio is an all-time best 5.58.

home_pitcher_note: After going at least six innings in his previous eight starts, Bettis struggled at Boston in his last outing -- seven runs on seven hits in 4 2/3 innings. He held the Reds to three runs and three hits on April 20.
away_pitcher_note: His stuff isn’t razzle-dazzle, but Straily has been the Reds’ best starter this season. Despite tying a career high with 11 strikeouts over seven innings on Wednesday, he was a hard-luck loser in a 3-1 decision.

home_pitcher_note: Gray has displayed the ups and downs of youth. After giving up nine runs and eight hits in 3 1/3 innings at St. Louis on May 19, Gray dominated the Red Sox with two runs, five hits and six strikeouts in 7 1/3 innings in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Moscot will be activated from the DL and make his first start for the Reds since April 27. He’s been out with inflammation in his surgically-repaired left shoulder. In the third of three rehab starts in Triple-A, he worked six scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood is coming off his most impressive home start of the year, holding the Giants to one unearned run and four hits over seven innings. He has thrown at least six innings in each of his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lamb blew a 3-0 first-inning lead Friday before a 9-5 loss to the Brewers. Pitch execution was a shortcoming as he missed over the plate and issued walks. His velocity also seemed down again, manager Bryan Price observed.

home_pitcher_note: A walk, a hit batsman and a Buster Posey home run in the first inning put Butler behind against the Giants, but he ended up with five solid innings (and a no-decision) before being removed in an offensive substitution.
away_pitcher_note: Simon was having a decent day in his last start until he was ejected in the bottom of the fifth for hitting Brewers pitcher Chase Anderson. Following a two-run first inning, he had retired 10 of 11 batters until he plunked Anderson.

home_pitcher_note: Pomeranz has taken the loss in two of his three starts since his last victory on May 11. He gave up six runs in five innings in his last start, a 6-3 loss at Arizona. Pomeranz has walked at least three in eight of his 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin labored, but at least made it through five innings in his last start, a home loss to the Giants. Rusin is 1-1 with a 4.12 ERA in four games, including three starts, against the Padres. He has a 4.56 ERA at Petco Park.

home_pitcher_note: Cashner is 0-2 in two starts since coming off the disabled list May 24. In his last start, he cruised through five scoreless innings, allowing just two hits, before a four-run sixth in a 9-3 loss at Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: In his last 8 1/3 innings over two starts, Bettis has given up 13 home runs and 15 hits. Bettis held the Padres to two runs (one earned) on six hits in a 6-3 victory at Coors Field on April 10.

home_pitcher_note: Perdomo is filling in as the spot starter after the Padres dealt James Shields to the White Sox Saturday morning. He is a rule-five pick who has thrown 24 innings of relief in addition to two innings during a prior spot start this season.
away_pitcher_note: Gray lacked his usual command, with three walks -- one with the bases loaded -- in six innings in his last start. But he fanned four, held the Reds to five hits and coasted to his fifth quality start in his last six outings.

home_pitcher_note: Bolsinger has been slowly working to establish his fastball command since returning from the DL with an oblique injury. He allowed two runs in five innings in his last outing against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: After two solid starts in Rockies wins, Chatwood lost his fastball command and was hit hard at home against the Reds in his last start. A Southern California native, expect him to have a large group of well-wishers in attendance.

home_pitcher_note: After some discussion in the front office, the Dodgers opted to give their precocious rookie a third start. The first two didn’t go too well, but his first career appearance in Los Angeles could give him a push he needs.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies have lost Butler's last four appearances, but it wasn't until his last start -- a home bummer against Cincinnati, when he gave up 11 hits in four innings -- that he pitched poorly.

home_pitcher_note: Maeda showed off his glove as well as his arm in a win over the Braves Friday, allowing one earned run in six innings. It was his first quality start in nearly a month.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin committed a first-inning error and immediately thereafter served up a Matt Kemp home run in his last outing, a loss to the Padres. But after the rough beginning, he pitched a solid seven innings (four hits).

home_pitcher_note: Bettis, who gave up two home runs, but remained competitive despite giving up five runs and 10 hits in five innings in a loss to the Padres, will face the Pirates in a makeup of a scheduled April 28 game.
away_pitcher_note: Locke has won four starts in a row and has not walked a batter in his last two appearances. The lefty followed up his first career shutout in Miami by allowing three runs in seven innings vs. the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies might want to celebrate Gray Day, since he has won his last three starts. The Padres? Not so much. He struck out 11 Padres on May 2, then topped that by fanning 12 in seven innings at Petco Park on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Cashner spent some tinkering with his slider in mid-May to much success. The pitch’s velocity has returned to where it was at the end of 2015. Cashner has already beaten the Rockies twice, allowing three runs in each start.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood was excellent in eight innings at Dodger Stadium during his last time out, allowing just one run. Amazingly, that actually raised his MLB-leading road ERA to 0.65. On the other hand, his ERA at Coors Field is 5.30.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson -- part of the trade haul for James Shields -- is set for his Padres debut. The 26-year-old righty has struggled in his big league career, but the Padres feel he has room to grow. He posted a 2.94 ERA at Triple-A this year.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson, a 2011 first-round Draft pick, will be making his Major League debut. He has a 2.35 ERA over 30 2/3 innings with 30 strikeouts across three levels this season, including a 2.12 ERA over three starts for Triple-A Albuquerque.
away_pitcher_note: Three weeks ago, Friedrich was unsure whether he’d stay in the rotation following a shaky start against L.A. Since then, he’s 3-0 with a 2.41 ERA. Those three wins came after Friedrich had gone nearly four years without one.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa returns to the rotation after three successful outings in relief. He earned a win in his last start, throwing four perfect innings, striking out five. However, he has an 11.41 ERA and a 2.28 WHIP in six starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: After a May where Eovaldi was borderline unhittable and saw his ERA drop almost two full points, June has been a regression for Eovaldi, allowing 18 hits and 10 earned runs in 10 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis is going through a rough patch. He hasn’t made it past the fifth inning and has allowed at least four runs in each of his last four starts. He has an 11.57 ERA over that stretch, thanks in part to allowing six home runs.
away_pitcher_note: The biggest difference for Nova this season after a rough 2014 and 2015 has been his command. Nova is walking a career low 1.5 batters per nine innings this season, barely more than half of his career rate.

home_pitcher_note: Conley last won May 16. Since then, he is 0-2 with a 5.27 ERA. In 27 1/3 innings, he's struck out 24 and walked 13. During the rough span, opponents are hitting .308. He gave up a career-high 11 hits in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Gray has been on fire lately with a 2.66 ERA over four straight quality starts. He has thrown quality starts in seven of his past eight outings, and he walked none and struck out seven in his last start, allowing one earned run over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chen made team history in his win at San Diego. He's the first Marlins pitcher to pick up a win while allowing four home runs. Homers have hurt Chen, who has given up seven in his past two starts, and 15 in 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood has been excellent on the road this season, sporting a Major League-best 0.65 ERA. In his last road start, he held the Dodgers to one run on one hit over eight innings. The Rockies have won five of his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Koehler has been settling into a nice groove. In his last four starts, his ERA is 3.24 in 25 innings, as he's worked at least six in each outing. He's also walked just three in his last three starts, over 18 innings
away_pitcher_note: Anderson was brilliant in his Major League debut against the Padres, surrendering only one run on six hits over 6 1/3 innings while striking out six and walking none. Anderson generated nine groundouts and three flyouts.

home_pitcher_note: Clemens will make his first MLB appearance since 2014 and sixth career start. The 28-year-old was 6-4 with a 4.30 ERA and 66 strikeouts in 75 1/3 innings in 14 starts at Triple-A New Orleans. He takes over Justin Nicolino's turn in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: After an ineffective first six starts and time in the bullpen, De La Rosa returned to the rotation for five solid innings against the Yankees. Improved overall pace and a more consistent windup and delivery have helped.

home_pitcher_note: Nova opens a brief two-game Interleague set against the Rockies in the Bronx hoping to bounce back from a rocky stretch. He has a 6.30 ERA in his last five starts, and he's allowed five runs in two of his past three outings.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis earned his first victory since May 17, when he beat the Yankees on Wednesday. He’s won five times this season, more than half of his career high (8), thanks to 5.43 runs of support per game from the Rockies’ offense.

home_pitcher_note: Since the beginning of May, no one in baseball has a better ERA than Sabathia. The big veteran lefty, having a resurgent season for the Yankees, carries a sparkling 0.82 mark over his last seven starts entering the finale against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start in Miami, Gray struggled for fastball command and searched for his slider through the early innings yet held the Marlins to two runs on six hits with four strikeouts in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Butler will need to limit balls in play if he wants to return to his successful ways. Over three June outings (two starts), Butler has allowed 24 hits and walked six batters in 13 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke has been on a roll in winning each of his last seven starts with a 1.90 ERA over that stretch. In June he is 4-0 with a 0.87 ERA. Greinke threw eight innings and allowed one run against the Phils his last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson's second Major League outing was almost as stellar as his first. He held the Marlins to four hits and struck out four in 5 2/3 innings before being pulled with 102 pitches. The two runs charged to him scored after he left.
away_pitcher_note: Bradley was outstanding last time out against the Phillies allowing one unearned run over six innings. It was a step forward as he channeled his emotions and did not allow things to spiral out of control in the sixth.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa gave up three solo homers but just two other hits through six innings in a win at Miami to end a Rockies losing streak. He has won two straight since regaining his rotation spot.
away_pitcher_note: Miller will look to improve on his second quality start of the year when he gets the ball against Colorado. Miller allowed one earned run while striking out five over 6 2/3 innings his last time out, his longest outing of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis pitched consecutive six-inning starts against the Yankees in his last two starts, allowing two earned runs in each. He has only walked two total batters in his last four starts, lowering his walk rate to a pristine 5.4 percent.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin tossed 6 1/3 innings his last time out in a 4-2 win over the Toronto Blue Jays. The left-hander has now pitched at least 6 1/3 innings in four consecutive games. The 26-year-old is 4-1 in his eight road starts with a 2.68 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Gray exited his last start after four innings with right arm fatigue, breaking his streak of five straight quality starts. He allowed four runs in 5 1/3 innings against the D-backs last season in his sixth career start, striking out just one batter.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada made MLB history his last time out. He went six innings and allowed two hits and three runs in a loss to the D-backs, becoming the first pitcher to make 11 straight starts of six-plus innings with fewer than five hits in each outing.

home_pitcher_note: Butler has struggled lately, allowing at least three runs in his last five appearances. He has had a problem with the long ball lately, allowing eight home runs during that stretch, which ballooned his ERA from 3.58 to 6.71.
away_pitcher_note: Happ labored through five innings his last time out against Arizona. The veteran left-hander picked up the win, surrendering two runs on six hits, but he walked four batters along the way.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson became the second pitcher in franchise history after Jason Jennings to pitch five or more innings and allow two runs or fewer in his first three career starts. However, he is still in search of his first win.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez allowed two runs in six innings for a no-decision against the White Sox in his last start. He is 6-0 with a 3.33 ERA and 70 strikeouts in his last 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Set to make his Dodgers debut, Norris will replace the injured Clayton Kershaw. Norris was 2-1 with a 2.08 ERA in six June appearances after a rough April and May.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa has been excellent since rejoining the rotation on June 15, earning three wins while limiting opponents to four runs over 17 innings. However, he has walked nine during that stretch and allowed three home runs.

home_pitcher_note: After a four-run, 40-pitch first inning in his last start, Kazmir said he will try a pregame simulated inning during warmups, hoping to avoid a repeat.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis has allowed at least three runs in each of his past seven starts, none of which were longer than six innings, raising his ERA from 4.18 to 5.84. However, he has only walked four and hasn't allowed a home run in his past three starts.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy will make his 2016 debut after missing more than a year due to a torn UCL that required Tommy John surgery. He topped at 72 pitches in his rehab assignment and will be under no limitations.
away_pitcher_note: Gray overcame arm soreness from two starts ago to throw 101 pitches in seven innings for a win over the Blue Jays on Monday. He faced the Dodgers on April 22, allowing five runs over five innings in his 2016 debut.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander is looking to bounce back after allowing seven runs (three earned) on five hits and two walks with zero strikeouts in 3 1/3 innings against the A’s on Wednesday. He also gave up two home runs.
