away_pitcher_note: The 27-year-old rookie has pitched well in his first 2 starts. Though he allowed five runs on six hits in six innings against the Nats his last outing, only one run was earned and he's given up just two earned runs in 11 innings in those two outings.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough April, Anderson has seemingly regained the form that made him so successful as a rookie: by eliciting soft contact. Along with a 2.55 ERA in four May starts, batters are hitting an exit velocity of just 79.3 mph against him.
away_pitcher_note: Miranda has turned into Seattle's top starter in an injury-riddled rotation at 4-2 with a 4.22 ERA in 10 games and has a 2.12 ERA with 21 strikeouts in 17 innings over his last three outings. This will be his first time facing the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Paxton returns from a four-week stint on the disabled list with a strained forearm and looks to resume the strong start that saw him go 3-0 with a 1.43 ERA in his first six starts. He threw four innings in a rehab outing Friday at Double-A Arkansas.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela has confidence in his four-seamer and strategically uses his offspeed stuff. He threw eight shutout innings on Friday against the Cardinals, and went to the slider just five times in the first time through the order, facing the minimum.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo threw a season-high 112 pitches on Friday at Fenway Park while giving up seven hits and three runs in 5 1/3 innings in a 3-0 loss. The 31-year-old is 0-5 with a 5.70 ERA in 11 games (10 starts) against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland worked his way out of multiple jams against the Cardinals on Friday, and he turned in his seventh quality start. The left-handed rookie has impressed teammates and staff with his confidence and composure.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander has been strong over his past two starts, allowing four runs in 15 innings. He hasn’t faced the Rockies yet this season, but he pitched seven scoreless innings against them last September.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez held the Cardinals scoreless through five innings before losing some curveball command. Over his past four starts, he is 4-0 with a 1.46 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin spent the first six years of his career pitching for the Rockies. He gets his first chance to pitch against them on Saturday, when he returns to Petco Park, where he’s posted a 0.67 ERA this year.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood allowed a season-high six runs in his last start against the Mariners and lasted a season-low 4 1/3 innings. With Jon Gray returning from the DL in mid-June, he'll need to shore up his control to keep his spot in the Rockies' rotation.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander has struggled to find the zone this season, with 16 walks in 20 innings. The free passes have limited his length, but he’s generally managed to avoid trouble, posting a 3.72 ERA this year as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: After two solid spot starts -- particularly one at Philadelphia, where he was as sharp with baserunners on as without -- Hoffman will come up from Triple-A Albuquerque to replace Tyler Anderson (left knee inflammation) in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Senzatela struck out seven batters in five innings in Seattle, but less than pinpoint fastball command led to four runs and a loss. At Coors Field, he's 5-1 with a 3.00 ERA in six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Clevinger has been solid since being called up from Triple-A last month. Over five starts, he has consistently kept his team in games. He worked through a late Spring Training mechanical glitch which he felt was causing him to throw across his body.

home_pitcher_note: The Denver native has registered a quality start in seven of his last eight outings. He got his June off to a winning start with six innings of two-run ball in his last start vs. the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Bauer had an ERA over 7 in mid-May, but he hasn't allowed more than three runs in five straight starts and has struck out 36 in 25 2/3 innings. His last outing was cut short by rain, but he'll look to continue his turnaround against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Lester picked up his sixth quality start of the season in his last outing, a no-decision against the Cardinals. He has a 2.15 ERA in seven home starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood put on-again, off-again struggles behind him in his last start, and shut down the Padres for eight innings, allowing one run on four hits with eight strikeouts. He has a 2.68 road ERA.

home_pitcher_note: With Kyle Hendricks on the disabled list, Montgomery will make his first start of the year against the Rockies at Wrigley Field. Montgomery has posted a 2.21 ERA out of the bullpen this season, primarily serving in a long-relief role.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez struck out nine in five innings in his last start. Problem was, two mistake fastballs led to two-run homers, and he yielded five runs total in a loss to the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Butler's first game against his former team. He's 2-0 with a 2.63 ERA in his three home starts this year. His next win will be a career high -- he's matched his best of three set in 2015 with the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Hoffman earned more opportunities in the rotation by holding the Padres to three hits and one run and a career-high nine strikeouts in seven innings before an offensive substitution ended his day at 89 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: There's no place like Wrigley Field for Arrieta. He's 3-0 with a 3.04 ERA in four home starts this season. In his last outing against the Marlins, he shrugged off a 34-pitch first and held them to two hits over six-plus innings.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela gave up two runs on five hits, walking three and striking out four over six innings against the Cubs on May 9. The rookie has given up seven runs over his past two starts (5.56 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Taillon will be making his first start since May 3 after undergoing surgery for testicular cancer. He posted a 3.31 ERA in six starts before his diagnosis. He allowed five runs in six innings, striking out nine in his final rehab start at Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland held the Indians to one run and six hits, with five strikeouts in 6 1/3 innings in his last start, a win. He wanted to finish the seventh, but he was pulled at 100 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Cole struggled again in his last start Thursday against the Marlins, surrendering seven runs on 11 hits in only 4 2/3 innings. He has posted a 10.71 ERA (23 earned runs in 19 1/3 innings) in his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his past three road starts, Chatwood has held opponents to nine hits and two earned runs in 21 innings. Those games resulted in wins at Philadelphia on May 24, San Diego on June 3 and Thursday at Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl is coming off back-to-back solid outings, allowing three earned runs in 10 innings in that span. He has never faced the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez has struggled in his past two starts. In a loss at San Diego, he was hit on the right hand by a batted ball, and in a no-decision at Chicago, a tight early strike zone upped his pitch count.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie has walked one in his last three starts and overall has struck out 34 and walked three in 27 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Moore is back on the road, where his fortunes have sagged this year. He’s 0-4 with a 7.94 ERA in seven starts away from AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: Despite his glittering record, the rookie has been hit hard of late, compiling a 6.46 ERA in his last three starts over 15 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija picked up his eighth loss against the Twins last Saturday but threw pretty well, giving up three runs on four hits in six innings. He’s up to 100 strikeouts on the year, and he’s only walked two batters since April ended.

home_pitcher_note: After two solid starts (3 ER, 12 1/3 innings), the rookie struggled in his last outing, giving up four earned runs and nine hits in 5 2/3 innings in a 7-2 loss to the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Cain continues to be hit hard, giving up five runs and two homers in 4 1/3 innings to the Twins last Sunday. But a 13-run effort from the Giants' offense was able to prevent Cain from losing his fifth-straight start.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood has put together a string of strong starts for the first time this season, with a 1.35 ERA over his last three outings, all on the road. In two starts against the Giants this season, he has a 2.40 ERA (four runs in 15 innings).
away_pitcher_note: Blach pitched much better than his stat line indicated Tuesday night against the Royals, giving up seven earned runs on 10 hits in 5 2/3 innings. The defense behind him missed a few tough-but-makeable plays.

home_pitcher_note: Two games, opposite experiences for Marquez against Arizona. He fanned eight in six scoreless innings at Chase Field on April 30, then gave up five runs in six innings May 5.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke has been one of the National League’s best pitchers this season, but a big inning with five earned runs hurt him in his last start against the Tigers on June 13. Greinke allowed just two runs and struck out seven in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hoffman gave up seven hits and three walks in five innings in his last start, at home against the Giants. The good news was he escaped the trouble and gave up just one run.
away_pitcher_note: Walker will be making his second start since rejoining the D-backs rotation after a blister landed him on the DL. Walker allowed one run on six hits and had six strikeouts against Detroit in his first game back.

home_pitcher_note: Senzatela's strikeouts are trending up -- 12 in the last two games, but he managed just 10 total innings and gave up 13 hits and nine runs.
away_pitcher_note: Godley has not allowed more than three runs in any of his starts this year. Last time out against the Phillies, he allowed one run on five hits over 5 2/3 innings. This will be his first start against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: The pitcher of the month for May is shooting for a repeat in June after firing eight innings of three-hit ball against the Reds. Wood is the first Dodger to go undefeated his first 10 starts of the season since Orel Hershiser in 1985.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie is making his third start against the Dodgers this season and first since April 18. In those outings, the Dodgers have scored just two runs in Freeland’s 10 innings, and the Rockies won both.

home_pitcher_note: The southpaw will look to get back on track, after a rough outing in his last start vs. the Mets on June 19. Kershaw tossed a season-high 112 pitches, allowed a career-high four home runs and gave up a season-high six runs.
away_pitcher_note: Opponents have scored two runs or fewer in each of Chatwood’s last four starts dating back to June 3. Chatwood has lowered his ERA nearly a full run during that span, from 5.04 to 4.08.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy worked through six innings of four hit baseball in the Dodgers’ 12-0 win against the Mets on Tuesday earning his first win since May 27. The righty has not not allowed a home run in any of his last three games started dating back to June 6,
away_pitcher_note: Anderson will be making his first start since April 30, when he struggled against the Mariners while battling a knee injury. He has had a rough time against the Dodgers -- 0-3, 5.73 ERA in three starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Last time against the Rockies, Samardzija gave up a season-high eight runs and 11 hits in six innings at Colorado but has been solid as of late. He owns a 4.13 ERA and has struck out 57 batters in 52 1/3 innings over his last eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Marquez had on-and-off command but showed an uncanny ability to make big pitches and held the D-backs to one run in six innings of a win. He is starting on an extra day's rest.

home_pitcher_note: Cain aims to right the ship after a rocky appearance Thursday in Atlanta. He allowed seven runs in four innings and has struggled in June with an 8.84 ERA. Each of his three wins this season have come at home.
away_pitcher_note: Hoffman, a rookie, excelled in his first five starts (2.05 ERA, 34 Ks, 36 IP) before giving up nine third-inning runs against the D-backs Wednesday. He held the Giants to one run and seven hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Blach admitted after his last start he was too quick with his timing. That allowed the Mets to notch 11 hits, matching a season high allowed by the lefty. Blach will look to cap June how it started, as he fired a shutout June 2 in Philly.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie southpaw has fared well in two starts against the Giants this season, going 2-0 with a 0.69 ERA. In his last outing, Freeland gave up five runs on a season-high 10 hits over six innings to the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Arizona’s breakout All Star candidate is 2-0 with 24 strikeouts and a 2.95 ERA in his last three starts. He is third in the National League in opponents’ batting average (.201) on the year.
away_pitcher_note: Colorado's Opening Day starter will return to MLB action for the first time since April 13. Gray (stress fracture in left foot) struggled for consistency in his three starts to begin the year, posting a 4.38 ERA and 1.46 WHIP.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke battled through some command issues on Monday and held the Phillies to one run in five innings while striking out five. He is tied for second in the National League in WAR (2.7) and wins (9).
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood struggled with control in his last start, issuing eight walks while giving up four runs in 3 1/3 innings. He held the D-backs to one run over seven innings on May 7 at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Walker tossed 6 1/3 innings in a no-decision against the Cardinals on Tuesday and finished the outing with no strikeouts for the first time all season. He went 2-0 with a 3.63 ERA in June and surrendered just one homer.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez has already faced the D-backs three times in 2017, going 0-1 with a 3.00 ERA and 14 strikeouts in 18 innings. The 22-year-old was knocked around for five runs over four innings in his last start against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: After a poor start in his last home game, against the D-backs on June 21, Hoffman was much better in his last start, when he held the Giants to two runs in 6 2/3 innings and fanned six.
away_pitcher_note: Castillo is quickly becoming one of the most consistent starters for a struggling Reds rotation this season. In two starts since getting called up from Double-A Pensacola, he has a 3.38 ERA over 10 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland has matching 4-3 records on the road and at home, but otherwise he seems more comfortable pitching in his hometown. He has a 3.21 ERA at Coors Field, and a 4.35 in other venues.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey hasn't performed how the Reds had hoped he would since coming off the DL. In two starts this season, he is 0-2 with a 27.00 ERA (14 runs in 4 2/3 innings) and is yet to see the fourth inning.

home_pitcher_note: Gray struck out 10 in six innings in beating the D-backs on Friday, and showed off a solid plan. He relied on his slider and curve early, then saw his fastball command improve as the innings went on.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman had arguably his best start of the year Friday vs. the Cubs, allowing 2 hits over 7 shutout innings. He struggled with his command early but was able to settle down and use his curve to get whiffs of Chicago batters en route to 7 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: In Chatwood's last start at Coors Field, he allowed two runs over six quality innings against the Giants on June 18. For the season, though, in seven home starts, the right-hander has a 6.39 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Romano, who has a 3.06 ERA for Triple-A Louisville this season, will be recalled to start. It will be his second big league start and first since April 16 vs. the Brewers. In that game, he struggled with command, walking four over three innings.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez will make his first career Interleague start vs. the White Sox. After giving up one run in three consecutive starts, Marquez’s past two outings were not as good, with his ERA rising from 3.92 to 4.41.
away_pitcher_note: Holland took the loss in his first start against his former team his last time out, giving up five runs in 5 1/3 innings against the Rangers on July 1. The left-hander has gone 1-4 since the beginning of June.

home_pitcher_note: Hoffman has rebounded nicely from his June 21 start vs. the D-backs, in which he gave up nine runs in 3 2/3 innings. Hoffman has a 3.29 ERA over his past two starts (five earned runs in 13 2/3 innings), with 10 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: After a stellar June, Quintana kicked off July with a shaky start, only going 4 1/3 innings against the Rangers on July 2. He gave up five runs on six hits, but only three runs were earned. He struck out five, putting him one short of 100 for 2017.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland is in the midst of a slump, as he has given up four or more earned runs in four of his past five starts. Additionally, in his last three starts, Freeland has given up 14 earned runs in 17 1/3 innings (7.27 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: In his second start back from the disabled list, Rodon was sharp against the A’s in picking up his first win of the season. Rodon went 6 1/3 innings and struck out 10, the fifth double-digit strikeout game of his career.

home_pitcher_note: deGrom will be looking to win his sixth consecutive start when he opens the three-game series against the Rockies. He allowed four runs (all solo homers) against the Cardinals on Friday, but made it through seven innings without further damage.
away_pitcher_note: Gray pitched 5⅔ innings and allowed three runs, two earned, in his second start since a broken bone in his left foot sidelined him for two months. He also crushed a 467-foot homer.

home_pitcher_note: Lugo went 3-1 with a 3.55 ERA in four June starts, but allowed six runs on 10 hits July 4 in Washington. He allowed one run on two hits in three innings of relief Sunday in St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: For the last two seasons, Chatwood has been better on the road than at Coors Field. However, his last two road starts are a combined 9 2/3 innings, 10 hits, 10 runs (eight earned), 11 walks, nine strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Matz took a 17-inning scoreless streak into his final start before the break, but was roughed up for five runs on seven hits in 4 1/3 innings by the Cardinals on Sunday. Matz has thrown well, as his 2-2 record and 3.05 ERA in six starts indicates.
away_pitcher_note: Since giving up nine runs in 3 2/3 innings at home vs. the D-backs on June 21, Hoffman is 1-0 with a 3.92 ERA in three starts, and the numbers would be better if not for a few instances of poor pitch selection.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez will be making his first start since July 7, when he beat the White Sox at Coors Field and completed seven innings for the first time since early May. He allowed three runs on nine hits and, for the first time in 2017, didn't walk a batter.
away_pitcher_note: Last season, Perdomo came on strong in the second half after a rocky first few months. He could be headed in that direction again, having finished the first half with a 2.82 ERA over his final four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Senzatela will be making his first Majors start since June 22, when he allowed nine runs in five innings against the D-backs. He has made three bullpen appearances and one Triple-A start since then.
away_pitcher_note: Through eight big league starts, it’s been all or nothing for Lamet, whose three-pitch mix is clearly big league caliber. He’s been spectacular at times, but only when he’s commanding those pitches, which can be a struggle for him.

home_pitcher_note: Gray will be trying to rebound from a rough start July 14 in New York, when he allowed eight runs in two-plus innings against the Mets. Before that, Gray had won two straight starts since coming off the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Hard-luck singles did in Richard in his previous start against the Giants, as he allowed a career-high-tying 11 hits, eight of them singles. Several of his National League-leading 142 hits allowed have simply been grounders finding holes.

home_pitcher_note: Hoffman will slide into the injured Tyler Chatwood’s spot and start on regular rest. His numbers at home (6.44 ERA, 12 walks, 20 K's) are considerably worse than on the road (2.45 ERA, 5 walks, 33 K's).
away_pitcher_note: Williams allowed 10 hits but held the Cardinals to two runs in 5 2/3 innings Sunday at PNC Park. Since a rough first start, Williams owns a 3.95 ERA with a .699 opponents’ OPS in 12 outings. He has never faced the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez pitched well in his last start vs. the Padres, going 6 2/3 innings, giving up 3 runs and matching a career-high 9 strikeouts. He’s faced the Pirates already this year, earning the win after giving up 1 run in 5 innings on June 14.
away_pitcher_note: Kuhl struck out a career-high seven in a 5 2/3-inning, two-run performance against the Brewers on Monday. In nine outings since May 31, Kuhl has posted a 3.47 ERA. The second-year righty has never pitched at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland returns to the rotation after a brief stint in the bullpen to limit his innings. He nearly made Rockies history in his last start on July 9, coming up 2 outs short of the Rockies’ first no-hitter at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Nova allowed 10 hits but held the Brewers to three runs while striking out six in six innings Tuesday. His ERA has ticked up to 3.97 over his last 14 starts, but he is still averaging more than six innings per outing.

home_pitcher_note: Leake is 1-6 with a 5.04 ERA in his past 10 starts after posting a 1.91 ERA through his first nine. He’s acknowledged that he’s not pitching at full strength due to overall body weakness, which could explain the run of shorter starts.
away_pitcher_note: After being held out of the Rockies' rotation for nearly four weeks to slow his innings pace, Senzatela responded by holding the Padres to four hits and four runs (three earned) while winning his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching amid speculation that he could be dealt before the non-waiver Deadline, Lynn has allowed one run over his last 19 1/3 innings. His results have been boosted by increased reliance on his offspeed pitches, including an improving curveball.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, an 18-4 blowout win over the Padres at home, Gray struck out seven in six innings and wound up yielding four runs. But that was a solid rebound from a rough two-inning start against the Mets his previous outing.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez has come out of the All-Star break strong, allowing four earned runs over 13 innings. He leads the Cardinals with 14 quality starts, which would be more apparent in his record if run support was more consistent behind him.
away_pitcher_note: Hoffman struggled in his last start, lasting just three innings and giving up nine hits and seven runs in a loss to the Pirates. But he also was hurt by not getting the call on a number of close pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Perhaps Roark has turned a corner after a rough first half, with a pair of strong starts coming out of the break. His most recent outing in Arizona was his best of the year, as the threw seven innings of two-run ball with 11 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez has held opponents to a .256 batting average and .301 on-base percentage while winning his last three starts, with 23 strikeouts against four walks.

home_pitcher_note: No. 3 prospect Fedde will be promoted from Triple-A to start in place of Stephen Strasburg and make his big league debut in one of the two games in Sunday's doubleheader. Fedde features a low-to-mid-90s fastball and a strong slider.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland's innings slowdown -- a long All-Star break and a three-inning bullpen appearance before his first second-half start -- paid off in solid work on Sunday against the Pirates -- two runs and six hits in six innings of a win.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson will start one of the games in Sunday's doubleheader. The veteran was rocked in his last start vs. Milwaukee for seven runs (three earned), though he has a 7-7 record and 3.84 ERA in his career at Nationals Park.
away_pitcher_note: After giving up a two-run homer in the first inning against the Cardinals on Tuesday, Gray -- despite a high pitch count -- didn't give up another run in five innings and finished with a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Hoffman has lasted a total of seven innings and given up 14 runs (13 earned) and 16 hits in his last two starts, but seems to be hurt badly by not getting borderline calls at key times. Better luck with that could help.
away_pitcher_note: Matz is 0-3 with a 14.18 ERA over his last four starts, his season ERA nearly tripling over that stretch as opposing batters have hit .472 off him. Matz will look to regroup in Coors Field, of all places, where he has never previously pitched.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood has led the National League in walks much of the season and enters this start with 62. But since suffering a right calf injury July 15, he has concentrated on removing unnecessary action from his motion.
away_pitcher_note: Steady with his control in the Minor Leagues, Flexen walked four batters in three innings during his big league debut. The Mets will chalk that up to nerves for now, but need more out of Flexen if he is to stick in the rotation down the stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez was perfect for the first 5 1/3 innings of a solid seven-inning performance at Washington last time out, and has 28 strikeouts over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Terry Collins chastised Montero for walking five in a no-decision last time out, forcing the Mets to rely heavily on their bullpen. Until that outing, Montero had shown some improvement, issuing one free pass in each of his previous two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Over his last four appearances (three starts), Freeland has posted a 2.01 ERA, held opponents to a .198 batting average and struck out 20 against six walks.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez had arguably the second-best start of his career Sunday, pitching seven scoreless innings against the Braves. He has a 2.81 ERA in his last three starts, pitching six or more innings twice.

home_pitcher_note: If you take away one inning in each of his last two appearances, Gray has 10 scoreless innings -- the last six of those (last Saturday at Washington) perfect. But one inning each time kept him out of the win column.
away_pitcher_note: Pivetta’s up-and-down season continues. He allowed one run in six innings Monday against the Braves. But Pivetta has been inconsistent. He posted a 9.37 ERA in his previous three starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, a home win over the Mets, Hoffman needed 101 pitches to get through six innings, but he escaped several sticky situations. He also had his best changeup of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Nola has not allowed more than two runs in eight consecutive starts, tying him for the second-longest streak in franchise history. Cole Hamels holds the record with nine consecutive starts in 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Kluber was brilliant in his last outing, as he pitched a complete game and allowed only one run on three hits with 11 strikeouts against New York. He has struck out at least eight batters in 12 straight starts, and 10 or more in 10 of those outings.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies have won each of Marquez's last five starts, and he has claimed the decision in four. He has held opponents to a .230 batting average with 38 strikeouts to seven walks in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Bauer went seven strong innings against the Yankees in his last start, allowing one run on seven hits with seven strikeouts to pick up the victory. Bauer is 3-0 with a 2.25 ERA and 19 strikeouts in 20 innings over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies skipped Senzatela last time through the rotation to control his innings and hone his fastball command. In two relief outings since his last start, he pitched a combined five innings, struck out four and yielded two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Urena has stepped up, especially in his last two starts, allowing just two runs in 14 innings for a 1.29 ERA. He has given up six hits in those starts. At home, the right-hander's ERA is 3.49 in 59 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gray went seven innings and allowed one run on six hits with four strikeouts to pick up the win against the Phillies in his last time out. He has posted a 2.84 ERA with 18 strikeouts in his past three starts (19 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Making his 1st MLB start since June 24 and 1st appearance since June 28, Nicolino gets another shot in the rotation. He has thrown 20 1/3 innings with 14 strikeouts and a 5.31 ERA for Miami. At Triple-A New Orleans, he posted a 3.19 ERA in 14 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hoffman went seven strong innings against the Phillies on Sunday, when he allowed one run on four hits while striking out eight en route to a no-decision. In his past two outings, he has posted a 2.08 ERA in 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last two starts, Worley has two wins -- both against Washington. The right-hander kept the Nationals in check, allowing just one run in 13 innings. Since the All-Star break, he has a 3.00 ERA in 21 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez held his own while facing off against Corey Kluber on Tuesday. The right-hander went six-plus scoreless innings and only allowed two hits and three walks in a no-decision. He has not taken a loss since June 26.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis will take the mound to complete his comeback from testicular cancer surgery last November. He began chemotherapy in March after finding out the disease had spread, and he went 0-3 with a 4.24 ERA in six games (five starts) in the Minors.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran took the loss in four of his past five starts, including his final three starts in July. He has allowed eight earned runs in 10 innings over his past two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland rejoins the rotation after sustaining a left groin strain that landed him on the disabled list on Aug. 5. He has been lights-out at Coors Field, where he’s 6-4 with a 3.19 ERA in 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Newcomb has lost five of his last seven starts. So far in August, he’s 0-2 with a 4.22 ERA. He allowed three runs (two earned) and five hits in six innings in his last start, a 3-2 loss to the Phillies on Aug. 9.

home_pitcher_note: Gray left one too many pitches up in the zone Friday against the Marlins, but he was able to limit the damage. The righty yielded three runs on eight hits and fanned four over 5 2/3 innings. He's 1-0 with a 0.64 in two career starts vs. the Brave
away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz has had an up-and-down season, and his first two August starts illustrate that. He allowed one run in 6 1/3 innings against the Marlins, then was pounded for six runs in 2 2/3 innings against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Hoffman was hurt by, you guessed it, Giancarlo Stanton in his last start on Saturday. A three-run homer did most of the damage, as Hoffman yielded four runs on seven hits in five innings. He has never faced the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: A 23-year-old rookie, Sims is still searching for his first MLB victory as he prepares for his fourth career start. He allowed five runs (four earned) on 10 hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Cardinals on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez is coming off one of his worst starts of the season, giving up five runs in 4 1/3 innings to the Marlins on Sunday. He’s faced the Brewers once before on the final game last season, allowing two runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garza has not faced the Rockies this season, but he is 2-5 with a 6.10 ERA in seven career starts against them. Garza allowed three earned runs over 5 1/3 innings on Sunday and has not surpassed six innings in five straight starts since July 5.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis makes his second start of the season after an emotional return to the big leagues in which he tossed seven scoreless innings vs. the Braves. The righty played to his strengths Monday, inducing 11 groundouts.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers skipped Woodruff in the rotation on his scheduled start day last Tuesday. The right-hander has made two career MLB starts since being called up on Aug. 4, including 6 1/3 shutout innings in his big league debut at Tampa Bay.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland has pitched better at Coors Field than on the road this season, a rarity for most hurlers. The Denver native’s 3.31 ERA at home is nearly a full run lower than his road ERA of 4.22. Sunday is his 11th home outing.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson will make his first start off the 10-day DL after sustaining a left oblique strain in an at-bat on June 28. He's made two rehab starts with no setbacks since then. He is 3-3 with a 4.92 ERA in 11 career starts against Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Duffy will get the start in the first of a three-game set with the Rockies at Kauffman Stadium. Duffy gave up six hits and four runs over five innings last Wednesday against the A’s.
away_pitcher_note: Gray makes his first career start vs. the Royals on Tuesday. Last time out, he gave up two runs in six innings vs. the Braves. He’s allowed three or fewer runs in his past five starts, good for an ERA of 3.23 in 30 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy will get the start in Game 2 of the series with Colorado. Kennedy was shaky his last time out Friday against the Indians, lasting only 2 2/3 innings while giving up five runs.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela has been in and out of the rotation since June 22 and will take the spot of Jeff Hoffman, recently optioned to Triple-A. Senzatela’s last start came Aug. 9 vs. the Indians, and he gave up two runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Junis is expected to start Thursday’s series finale against the Rockies. Junis last started Aug. 14 and gave up two runs on four hits over six innings in the Royals' 6-2 win over the A’s.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez was plagued by the long ball in his last start, giving up three solo home runs to the Brewers. His home run rate is down from his time in Triple-A last year, as Marquez has allowed 1.13 homers per nine innings.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran was victimized by a couple defensive misfortunes as he pitched better than his line suggested Saturday against the Reds. He found success with a modified slider as he tossed seven scoreless against the Rockies on Aug. 14.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis held the Braves scoreless for seven innings on Aug. 14 in his return from a bout with testicular cancer. In two starts, Bettis has yielded 14 hits in as many innings with eight strikeouts and one walk.

home_pitcher_note: Newcomb's command has improved over his past three starts, as he hasn't missed arm side as frequently as he previously had. He's struggled to consistently create clean innings, but has had a knack for minimizing damage.
away_pitcher_note: Many Rockies pitchers have found pitching on the road easier than at home, but not Freeland, a Denver native. He has a lower ERA at Coors Field (3.30) than on the road (4.22).

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz recorded a career-best 11 strikeouts against the Marlins Aug. 6, but has struggled to command his offspeed pitches as each of his past three starts have turned ugly.
away_pitcher_note: In his last seven starts, Gray has gone at least six innings five times. He's pitched to a 3.53 ERA and opponents have just a .303 on-base percentage over that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: After taking a few starts off to limit his innings, Senzatela rejoined the rotation Wednesday against the Royals and allowed two runs on nine hits in five innings but didn't figure in the decision. He threw 81 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Not since Tommy Bridges and Schoolboy Rowe in 1935 had a Tiger given up seven earned runs in three consecutive starts until Zimmermann. A Coors Field meeting with a hot Rockies offense could stretch that streak to four.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez yielded two solo homers but no other runs in six innings while beating the Royals in his last outing. He is he is 5-1 in his past 10 games, and the Rockies are 7-3. Opponents have hit .247 during tha span, though he has yielded 11 homers.
away_pitcher_note: Fulmer suffered a sharp, sudden flare-up of ulnar neuritis in his right elbow last start, which he blames for him hitting Gary Sanchez with a pitch, but he pitched through it. Barring something unforeseen, he’ll make his next start.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis gave up five runs in his first two innings in his last start, but found his velocity and threw three scoreless frames before exiting in a loss to the Braves. He says his legs are feeling stronger, which could mean a surge is coming.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander will put his stellar Interleague numbers on the line one more time against a difficult Rockies offense in the thin air of Coors Field. He’s 30-5 with a 2.88 ERA in 42 career starts against the National League.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland faced the D-backs once this season, holding them to 1 run over 6 innings on April 28. He’s coming off his worst start since the All-Star Break, when he gave up 4 runs and 10 hits in 6 innings vs. the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Walker picked up his first post-All-Star break win in his last outing, holding the Giants to one run over 6 1/3 innings. He posted a 3.55 ERA in the month of August.

home_pitcher_note: Gray beat the D-backs in his first start recovering from a foot fracture, giving up just 2 runs and striking out a season-high 10 in 6 innings on June 30. The stakes are much higher this time around, but he threw 6 scoreless in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin delivered a stellar seven-inning, eight-strikeout performance last time out as he held the Giants scoreless. Corbin enjoyed a 2.52 ERA in August.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies will skip Antonio Senzatela and start Marquez on regular rest. Marquez was solid his last start, going 6 1/3 innings and matching a career high with 10 strikeouts. Sunday will be his fifth start vs. the D-backs this year.
away_pitcher_note: Godley allowed four runs over six innings against the Dodgers and picked up his second win of August. He struck out 38 batters and walked just 14 in the month.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis’ first two starts were solid, giving up three runs in 14 innings. But he owns a 9.00 ERA over his last two outings. Monday will be his fourth home start, where he has a 3.79 ERA (eight earned runs in 19 innings).
away_pitcher_note: Stratton's original Saturday start was bumped back two days. He has struck out 10 batters in two of his five starts this season, and he threw three scoreless innings at Coors Field back in April as a reliever.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood made one spot start on Aug. 2 after being bumped from the rotation in July, giving up 8 runs in 5 1/3 frames. In six relief outings since, Chatwood’s given up 3 runs in 9 2/3 innings. Tuesday is likely a bullpen day for the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Blach's ERA didn't change after his last start, when he corrected his course, allowing three runs over 5 2/3 innings. Blach hopes to put a challenging August behind him, when he posted a 5.59 ERA amid a successful summer streak.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie left-hander lasted just four innings in his last start, giving up three runs to the D-backs. His pitch count rose quickly, needing 74 to get through the outing. Freeland owns a 2.37 ERA in three starts vs. the Giants this year.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto returned from the disabled list against the Cardinals, allowing two runs over 5 1/3 innings. It was his first start since July 14. Cueto owns a 3.43 ERA in seven career starts at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw will make his first home start since hurting his back on July 23, which then landed him on the disabled list. The southpaw threw six scoreless innings vs. the Padres in his first start back from the DL.
away_pitcher_note: Gray hopes to be more efficient against the Dodgers, as he needed 100 pitches to navigate 5 innings Saturday. Gray’s only runs came off a three-run homer in the first, but he still struggled with command.

home_pitcher_note: Darvish is still working out the kinks of his new mechanics that pitching coach Rick Honeycutt has employed. The righty has struggled lately, posting a 6.16 ERA over his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez has started well his last few outings, but opponents have taken advantage in the later innings by attacking pitches earlier in counts. This was apparent Sunday vs. the D-backs, when he gave up three runs in the sixth inning.

home_pitcher_note: Back from the disabled list, Wood gave up four runs on seven hits against the Padres last Sunday. The left-hander hasn’t picked up a win since Aug. 9.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis scattered three runs over 5 1/3 innings his last time out against the Giants. Though the line was unimpressive, Bettis’ average fastball velocity ticked up to 90.5 mph. His four-seamer averaged 89.3 mph in his first four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hill will face the Rockies for the first time this season. The lefty has recorded a loss in each of his last three starts, starting with his near no-hitter on Aug. 23.
away_pitcher_note: Rockies manager Bud Black expects Chatwood to throw between 60-70 pitches Sunday in the series finale against the Dodgers. Chatwood fired three scoreless innings before eight relievers followed him Tuesday in a win over the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke is tied for the Major League lead in wins and is coming off a seven-inning performance in which he allowed one run and four hits against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland is 1-1 with a 3.60 ERA through two starts against the D-backs this season. He's scuffled of late, going 0-3 with a 5.40 ERA over his last five starts and has also struggled on the road this year with a 4.39 ERA in 12 outings.

home_pitcher_note: After notching a win in which he allowed one run in six innings against the Dodgers last week, Walker has trimmed his ERA to 3.33. He has won his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gray made one of his finest starts of the year Thursday against the Dodgers, allowing a run over six innings as the Rockies won in a duel with Clayton Kershaw. Gray is 3-2 with a 2.43 ERA over his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin went 4-2 with a 2.52 ERA in August, but suffered his worst outing of the second half on Friday, when he gave up eight runs and 11 hits over 4 1/3 innings against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez had an uncharacteristic tough road outing Friday against the Dodgers, allowing four runs (two earned) while walking three in four innings. He has a 2.31 ERA in two starts at Chase Field this season and a 3.90 ERA in 13 road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Godley threw seven strong innings and struck out nine batters last time out against the Padres on Saturday. He retired 16 straight batters at one point, but took a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis picked up his first win of the season -- and his first since his return from a battle with testicular cancer -- Saturday against the Dodgers. He allowed four runs (three earned) while striking out five without a walk over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: His two starts since returning to the rotation on Sept. 5 were with limited pitch counts. But after throwing five innings in Sunday's win over the Dodgers, he could get more leeway.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Richard spun six shutout frames in a win over the Cardinals. Richard has recorded 13 quality starts this season, while going 6-1 with a 1.69 ERA in his quality outings. He has induced a league-leading 342 ground balls this season.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson replaces Kyle Freeland, who was hit on the shoulder and jaw by a line drive in his last outing. Anderson will make his first start since June 25 and his pitch count is set at 50-70 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles will make his third appearance for the Padres this season when he takes on his former club. With the Rockies, Lyles posted a 6.94 ERA in 33 relief outings this year. With San Diego, he's allowed six runs across 9 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gray faced loaded bases with no outs in the third inning of his last start, but yielded just one run on that threat. He went on to pitch seven innings and fan 10. He is 3-1, 2.25 in his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin was charged with four runs on seven hits over five frames in his last outing. The Rockies defeated Chacin on June 3, when he allowed four runs (three earned) and six hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto will make his fourth start since returning from a 1 1/2-month stint on the DL. He lasted 3 2/3 innings (his shortest start as a Giant) during his last outing. His ERA is 4.50 since returning Sept. 1.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez has given up four earned runs in two of his three September starts, including his last outing of 3 2/3 innings at Arizona last Tuesday. In two career starts against the Giants, he has an 11.88 ERA (11 earned runs in 8 1/3 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Moore's season ERA vs. the Rockies (13.50) is highest among all 18 Major League teams he's pitched against this year. Moore lasted 4 1/3 innings vs. the Dodgers in his last outing, his shortest start since July 7 (3 1/3 vs. Miami).
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood's ERA in three starts since rejoining the Rockies' rotation is 0.66 (one run in 13 2/3 innings). In his last start at AT&T Park, he tossed a two-hit shutout on April 15.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander will make his second straight start against Colorado. The Rockies scored four runs off Richard in six innings in his previous start at Coors Field. Richard is 15 innings away from reaching 200 for the first time since 2012.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson was strong in his return to the rotation, tossing six innings of shutout ball in his only meeting this season with the Padres. He has never pitched at Petco Park but has allowed one run in 12 1/3 career innings vs. San Diego.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies roughed up their former teammate in his last start, as Lyles allowed seven runs in four innings. After posting a 6.94 ERA in 33 outings as a Colorado reliever, the right-hander has an 8.78 ERA through three starts as a Padre.
away_pitcher_note: Gray tossed five scoreless frames in his previous start vs. the Padres, but he took a no-decision when the game was delayed by rain. He has excelled this month, posting a 2.35 ERA and allowing a .217 batting average in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin is coming off his first start at Coors Field as a visitor. In a rain-shortened outing, he gave up three runs in 4 1/3 innings. Saturday’s game will be Chacin’s final home start of 2017. He enters with a 1.91 ERA this year at Petco Park.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis didn’t fare too well in his last outing (five runs in 1/3 of an inning), but the Rockies and manager Bud Black feel confident the extra rest and bullpen sessions will get him back on track.

home_pitcher_note: Perdomo’s streak of 10 consecutive starts of at least six innings came to an end his last time out, a 5 1/3-innings win against the D-backs. He tied his career high with six walks in that outing.
away_pitcher_note: The righty benefited from one of his best curveballs in his last start vs. the Giants. He spun six innings of three-run ball. He last won a start on Aug. 18 vs. the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Has Chatwood shaken his Coors Field blues? He is 3-6, 5.85 ERA at home this season, but in his last two outings there he has given up one run and eight hits in 8 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Aside from two home runs, Despaigne was solid against the Mets. He posted a quality start, surrendering three runs over six strong innings. The righty is 2-0 with a 1.65 in 16 1/3 career innings against Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: In three games (two starts) since his return from knee surgery, Anderson is 2-1 with a 1.72 ERA, with 13 strikeouts and three walks in 15 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Urena has emerged as the ace of Miami’s staff, and his last start was another indication why. The right-hander held the Mets to just two runs over eight innings to pick up his 14th win. He’s 9-1 with a 4.09 ERA on the road this year.

home_pitcher_note: Gray's string of 12 starts of holding opponents to three or fewer runs included an Aug. 11 start against the Marlins, when he went 5 2/3 innings and yielded three runs, including a Giancarlo Stanton solo shot.
away_pitcher_note: Conley makes his final start and looks to bounce back after being tagged for seven runs in 1 2/3 innings at Arizona. On the road, the lefty is 5-3 with a 4.45 ERA. He's had two starts this year at 1 2/3 innings, the other on April 28 vs. Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis is one of the Rockies’ fringe candidates to make their postseason roster should they advance, and Thursday’s start against the Dodgers could be a factor. He’s 1-2 with a 7.04 ERA in September.
away_pitcher_note: Ryu, who is competing with Alex Wood for a spot in the NLDS rotation, had his last outing cut short after taking a line drive off his left forearm. The southpaw hasn't won a game since Aug. 24.

home_pitcher_note: September has been a taxing month for the hard-hurling righty. He’s 1-2 with a 5.47 ERA and a season-high 1.74 WHIP. This will be his final regular-season start in what’s been an otherwise standout rookie season.
away_pitcher_note: The Dodgers’ ace is all geared up for the postseason and is expected to make an abbreviated start in the penultimate game of the regular season. Kershaw gave up four runs on six hits when he last faced the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Tyler Anderson was the scheduled starter, but Freeland will make the regular-season finale instead.
away_pitcher_note: Stripling starts the regular-season finale. Stripling, whose postseason relief role is uncertain because of a recent slump, will be making his second start of the year and likely will pitch only two innings.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke is the no-brainer choice after he submitted another Cy Young-worthy campaign. The righty owns a career 3.55 ERA in nine postseason starts (3-3), most recently splitting a pair of decisions in the Dodgers’ 2015 NLDS loss to the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Gray is on a 13-game streak holding opponents to three runs or fewer. In those games, he has 80 strikeouts to 16 walks. He has 20 strikeouts in two regular-season games at Chase Field this year.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin is making his first Opening Day start. He was scheduled to start the 2014 opener, but suffered an elbow injury in his final spring outing. The left-hander was 14-13 with a 4.03 ERA in 33 games (32 starts) for the D-backs last year.
away_pitcher_note: When he takes the Chase Field mound, Gray has plenty to remember (20 strikeouts in 13 1/3 innings over two starts last year) and one night to forget (four runs, seven hits in 1 1/3 innings of last year's NL Wild Card loss).

home_pitcher_note: Ray had a breakout year in 2017, going 15-5 with a 2.89 ERA in 28 starts. Since 2016, he leads all Major League starters in strikeouts/nine innings with an 11.67 mark. Ray was named to his first All-Star team last year.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies were encouraged by Anderson's strong finish to last season. He was 3-1 with a 1.19 ERA in four September games (three starts) after returning from left knee surgery.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke would have started on Opening Day, but he suffered a groin injury on March 14, which set him back a bit. Greinke bounced back from a disappointing 2016 season to go 17-7 with a 3.20 ERA in 32 starts last year.
away_pitcher_note: Of all the Rockies' starters, Marquez will be out to show that Spring Training numbers are meaningless. In four starts, he was 2-1 with a 9.82 ERA while working out his changeup.

home_pitcher_note: The Padres were thrilled to acquire Mitchell from the Yankees in a December trade. The curveball-heavy right-hander has never been given a consistent big league chance, and the Padres believe he'll thrive with exactly that in San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis' last four appearances of the spring were good ones, as he improved his velocity and command. Bettis has not won at Petco Park; he's 0-2 in seven career games (five starts) with a 3.29 ERA there.

home_pitcher_note: Ross won the fifth spot in the Padres’ rotation with an excellent spring, which he attributed to a return to full health. After a rough year with Texas, Ross is looking to regain the form that saw him post a 3.16 ERA in four seasons with San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland has good memories from his only start at Petco Park during his rookie year. He allowed one run and three hits in 6 1/3 innings, with four K's, in a no-decision there on May 4. The Rockies won the game, 3-2.

home_pitcher_note: Richard was excellent in his first Opening Day start, allowing one run in seven innings and tallying 12 ground-ball outs. But in four starts against Colorado last year, Richard posted a 6.75 ERA while allowing 38 hits in 22 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: A 30-pitch, three-run first inning drove up his pitch count in the opener at Arizona. Gray found a groove but was gone after four-plus innings. Gray feels there will be no hangover heading into his next start.

home_pitcher_note: In his big league debut, Lucchesi put a rough first inning behind him and settled in for 4 2/3 solid frames. He recorded only one strikeout, however. That's been a specialty of his at every level. In the Minors, he racked up 204 K's in 181 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson had no command -- a changeup that Nick Ahmed hit for a three-run homer in a five-run first was a clear indication -- during a loss to the D-backs in his season debut. He lost his only start at Petco last year.

home_pitcher_note: Not fazed by traffic (four hits, four walks in five innings), Marquez held the D-backs to one run. He makes the home opener start after going 6-3 with a 4.59 ERA in 13 starts at Coors as a rookie.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy (1-0, 3.38 ERA) went 5 1/3 innings in his first start of the season, a 15-2 win over the Phillies on March 31. The veteran righty allowed two runs on six hits with five strikeouts and three walks.

home_pitcher_note: Last Aug. 14, Bettis held the Braves scoreless for seven innings in his return from testicular cancer. Healthy this year, he debuted by struggling early but eventually pitching five innings of two-run ball to beat the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez will make his first start and begin filling the rotation spot earmarked for the injured Luiz Gohara. The righty was released by the Twins in March. His 4-seam fastball averaged 89.4 mph as he tossed three scoreless relief innings on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland gave up four runs on five hits against the Padres in his first start, although it was two Christian Villanueva homers that did him in. Better velocity on his offspeed stuff would do him good.
away_pitcher_note: Newcomb’s difficulty commanding his curveball left him without an out pitch on Monday, as endured a 37-pitch first inning and allowed six runs, including a homer to Bryce Harper, on Monday night. The key for the young lefty remains fastball command.

home_pitcher_note: After a rocky Opening Day start, Gray found his ace stuff his last time out. He threw seven scoreless innings with seven strikeouts to beat the Padres, and he'll look to keep that momentum going, facing them again at home.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander will make the second of three scheduled starts against the Rockies this month. Richard, who has struggled against Colorado in the past, allowed five runs in the first two frames last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson bounced back from his first start, when he allowed seven runs in 2 1/3 innings, to pitch six scoreless innings with four strikeouts in a no-decision against the Padres on Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie delivered five shutout frames before being removed for a pinch-hitter in his last start. He struck out seven and allowed one hit. Lucchesi, a late roster addition after Dinelson Lamet’s injury, has arguably been the Padres’ best starter.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez struggled with command in his second start, giving up seven runs and six walks (two intentional) over 4 2/3 innings vs. the Braves on Friday. He struggled with his grip in the home opener’s 27-degree game-time temperature.
away_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old right-hander followed a disappointing debut with an excellent effort against the Astros on Friday night. Perdomo allowed one run over five innings while making masterful use of his slider, generally considered his second-best pitch.

home_pitcher_note: In five career starts against the Rockies, Gonzalez is undefeated, carrying a 4-0 record with a 3.58 ERA. He is off to a good start this year in his first two outings, surrendering just two runs in 11 1/3 innings with 13 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis led all Rockies starters with a 2.53 ERA through the club's first two turns through the rotation, most recently holding the Braves to one earned run and four hits. He has yet to exceed 88 pitches this season.

home_pitcher_note: Roark was hampered by his inability to put away hitters with two outs during his last outing against the Mets, which made for some mixed results. He struck out nine in five innings, but he also gave up five runs.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland turned in a quality start on Sunday against Atlanta, but received zero runs of support as the Rockies dropped the series. He has been toying more with a curveball but still hasn't truly implemented it in his repertoire.

home_pitcher_note: If Scherzer can reach double-digit strikeouts again, he would become one of 17 pitchers in MLB history to record three 10+ strikeout games in his team's first 15 games. He is coming off a shutout in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: A few mistake pitches up in the zone marred Gray's outing on Monday that began well. He gave up five runs with two outs in the third inning and wasn't able to recover. The hard-throwing righty is 0-1 with a 5.73 ERA in two starts vs. Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg tossed eight shutout innings in his most recent outing. He has 21 strikeouts with just five walks through his first three starts, picking up where he left off after one of the healthiest years of his career in 2017.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson is coming off consecutive starts against the Padres in which he gave up just two earned runs over 12 innings. Take out a rough showing in Arizona on March 30, and Anderson has a 1.30 ERA over his past six starts dating back to September.

home_pitcher_note: Looking to bounce back after giving up four runs  over five innings in his last outing at Chicago, Brault looks to keep his winning streak intact. He’s won his last three decisions and hasn’t lost one since Sept. 14, 2016, at Philadelphia.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez was having a solid outing in his previous start against the Padres before being ejected for participating in a bench-clearing fracas that erupted during the third inning. He has won both of his career starts against Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Riding a three-game win streak, Williams has been lights out so far this season with two quality starts in three outings. He last pitched at Chicago, limiting the Cubs to four hits and one run while striking out five over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis has been the Rockies' most dominant starter this season. He earned wins in two of his first three starts and has posted a 2.04 ERA. In his last start against Washington, Bettis allowed just one run with five strikeouts over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: After a shaky start in Miami, Kuhl gets another opportunity when he faces a tough Rockies lineup. He went five innings for the second consecutive start, but yielded 11 hits and four earned runs to the Marlins in a 7-2 loss on Friday.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland is looking to build off his last outing where he limited the Nationals to one run on four hits, but had to leave the game after 4 2/3 innings because his pitch count reached 101.He is 1-1 in three starts against Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: For five innings in his last start, Gray held the Nationals to one run and pitched out of some two-out jams. But he yielded four runs and didn't escape the sixth, and his frustrating early season continued.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks posted a quality start in his last outing against the Pirates but took the loss, serving up a pair of home runs for the second straight outing. The problem was fastball command that the righty said will be his focus between starts.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson walked a career-high six in 4 2/3 innings on Sunday at Washington, but was rescued by a comeback offensive effort after he left. Now he needs help earlier. The Rox have given him 2.37 runs of support while he's on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: Darvish was fine through the first four innings in his last outing, but a balk call against him in the 5th created some frustration and led to a loss. He's failed to pitch past the 5th in two of his three starts. This will be his 1st game at Coors.

home_pitcher_note: A devastating combination of a mid-to-upper 90s fastball and a mid 70s curve helped Marquez baffle the Pirates to the tune of two hits and six strikeouts in six innings of a win in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: With 210 strikeouts this season, Marquez is four away from Ubaldo Jimenez's 2010 club record. The development with a slider to go with his fastball and curve have made Marquez a star.
away_pitcher_note: Pivetta has not allowed more than three runs in any of his last five starts, but that is a bit deceiving as manager Gabe Kapler has held a tight leash on him. Pivetta has not pitched more than five innings in those starts.

home_pitcher_note: Senzatela's last start -- seven innings and one earned run in Saturday's win over the D-backs -- was shades of the beginning of last year, when he dominated with the fastball. The changeup and slider were also effective.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta is finishing a disappointing second half that coincided with the team’s late-season fall. He is 3-4 with a 5.09 ERA in 12 starts since the All-Star break and 1-4 with a 6.64 ERA in his last eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Since Aug. 6, Freeland is 7-0 with a 2.10 ERA, and the Rockies are 9-1 in those contests. At home, he is 9-2 with a 2.36 ERA in 14 starts -- 12 of them Rockies wins.
away_pitcher_note: Ross will make his third and final start in what has been a solid 2018 after missing 14 months with Tommy John surgery. In 11 innings, Ross has given up six runs (five earned) with three strikeouts and three walks.

home_pitcher_note: After three poor starts, and after being skipped, Gray returned to the rotation on Monday and held the Phillies to one run while striking out seven in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg makes his 22nd and final start of what has been another injury-riddled season. He never found his rhythm in his last outing where he threw 100 pitches in four innings against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson will start the Rockies’ most critical game of the season as they remain in the hunt to win their first NL West title. The left-hander is coming off two strong starts, but he was scratched on Monday due to left shoulder soreness.

Buehler gets the ball for the Dodgers in Monday's tiebreaker game in L.A. with the NL West title on the line. The rookie has already faced the Rockies five times this season, more than any other team, posting a 2.61 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez starts the NL West tiebreaker game, and he's 2-0 with a 2.57 ERA against the Dodgers this year. Both of those wins came at Dodger Stadium, with Marquez allowing just two runs on four hits over 15 innings in a pair of gems.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Lester's 22nd postseason start and his second Wild Card nod. The lefty has been a workhorse for the Cubs, and this season was the fifth in a row in which he made at least 32 starts. He went 7-4 with a 3.32 ERA at Wrigley Field in '18.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland will make his third career start against the Cubs in the NL Wild Card Game. The 25-year-old took the loss in his lone start vs. the Cubs this season, holding them to three runs on six hits with one walk and five strikeouts in seven innings.
series_status: COL wins NL Wild Card Game

home_pitcher_note: This is a bullpen day for the Brewers, though Woodruff is really a starter. He made 17 Triple-A starts and four in the Majors this year, but was at his best in relief late in the season compiling a 0.73 ERA and 11.7 strikeouts per nine in September.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela returns to Miller Park -- where he made his MLB debut on April 6, 2017 -- to open the NLDS for the Rockies. He hasn't pitched against the Brewers since that first game, when he was sensational, throwing five shutout innings of two-hit ball.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing one hit in 5 2/3 innings against the Cubs in Monday’s tiebreaker, Chacin will make a shortened start on three days' rest for his first postseason appearance on Friday. He has never gone three days between starts in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson starts Game 2 at Miller Park, where the Brewers handed him one of his worst losses of 2018 on Aug. 4, scoring seven runs and hitting three homers in four innings. But he had a 3.25 ERA in his five September starts.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez struck out nine but yielded four runs in 4 2/3 innings in Monday’s NL West tiebreaker against the Dodgers. He has seven straight quality starts at home since the start of July, with 68 strikeouts, 10 walks and a 1.90 ERA in those outings.
away_pitcher_note: He doesn’t light up the radar gun, like G1 initial out-getter Brandon Woodruff, or have a wipeout pitch, like G2 starter Jhoulys Chacin’s slider, but Miley keeps the Brewers in games. In 16 regular-season starts, he never allowed more than 3 ER.
