home_pitcher_note: Urena will make his second straight Opening Day start. He hopes for a better result. The first pitch he threw in 2018 was belted for a homer by the Cubs' Ian Happ, but Urena recovered and finished strongly. In September, he went 5-0 with a 1.20 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland went 17-7, finished fourth in the National League Cy Young Award race and pitched 6 2/3 scoreless innings in last year’s NL Wild Card Game. Not only is this his first Opening Day start, but it’s his first start against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: As a rookie last year, Richards struck out eight Rockies in six innings in a win. Now, with the addition of a curveball, instead of a slider, he's added another quality pitch. A year ago, Richards had a 36.3 strikeout percentage on his changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Last year in a breakout performance, Marquez set a Rockies record with 230 strikeouts and finished eighth in the NL with a 2.95 road ERA. He also was a threat with the bat -- his 18 hits were the most by an NL pitcher since Zack Greinke’s 19 in 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Since his rookie season, Lopez has added about eight pounds of muscle. His average fastball was 92.7 mph. In Spring Training, Lopez regularly touched 94-97 mph, and his curveball has improved. He had a 3.72 ERA in six starts at Marlins Park in 2018.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson had three starts last season during which he pitched 7 2/3 or more scoreless innings. Last year, he set professional highs for starts (32), innings pitched (176) and strikeouts (164).

home_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old has a power fastball. Per Statcast, his four-seamer averaged 95.5 mph as a rookie. Alcantara split time at Triple-A and Miami last year. He had a 2.25 ERA in 16 innings at home. Fastball command is key. His slider averaged 86.1 mph.
away_pitcher_note: Gray ranks seventh in Rockies history in strikeouts with 520, and his 12 games of double-figure strikeouts are second in club history to Pedro Astacio’s 15. Gray has pitched in just three-plus seasons. Gray started the opener the last two years.

home_pitcher_note: Stanek, who started 29 games for the Rays last season in the opener role, will get his first start of 2019 when the Rays host the Rockies. Stanek tossed two scoreless innings in his first relief appearance on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: A recurring blister on his right middle finger forced Bettis to finish last season in the bullpen, but the Rockies are in good shape if Bettis can repeat his work when healthy. For example, last April he was 3-1 and sported a 2.43 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Blake Snell will look to bounce back from an Opening Day loss, when he allowed five runs (three earned) in six innings against the Astros. In Snell’s only career start against the Rockies, the left-hander gave up one hit over six innings in 2016.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland held the Marlins to two hits and just one run in seven innings on Opening Day. He struck out five and created 12 ground-ball outs.

home_pitcher_note: Charlie Morton picked up his first win as a member of the Rays on Friday against the Astros. Of the eight strikeouts Morton recorded in that start, seven came on a curveball.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez limited the Marlins to two hits in six innings and fanned seven while winning his first 2019 start. His curve and slider were especially effective.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson enters the home opener with the third-best home ERA (3.73) in club history, behind Kyle Freeland and Ubaldo Jimenez. He is coming off giving up nine hits and three runs over five innings in a loss at Miami.
away_pitcher_note: Maeda is one of the rare pitchers who actually pitches better in Coors Field than away from it. He is 4-1 with a 3.19 ERA pitching a Mile High, with 35 strikeouts and only eight walks in 31 innings and a 1.065 WHIP.

home_pitcher_note: Gray struck out 10 in 6 2/3 innings and exhibited an effective four-pitch mix in his first start, a loss at Miami that he left with cramping in his right calf. He doesn't expect the injury to linger.
away_pitcher_note: Buehler didn’t have a real Spring Training and it showed in his first start, as he allowed five runs in the fourth inning vs. Arizona. The assignment doesn’t get easier at Coors Field, where he was 0-1 with a 4.00 ERA in three starts last year.

home_pitcher_note: Bettis' first start was marred by two pitches, a mislocated fastball and a decent changeup, that went for home runs in a loss at Tampa Bay. But he has shown a solid fastball-cutter-changeup mix since mid-spring.
away_pitcher_note: In his first MLB start in nearly two years, Urias tossed five scoreless innings vs. the Giants. He’ll eventually head to the bullpen as the team wants to limit his innings, but he’ll keep getting starts until Rich Hill or Clayton Kershaw return.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland gave up three runs in the first inning -- an error didn't help -- in his last start, a loss at Tampa Bay. He struck out 10, but his pitch count ran high as he lasted just 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran struggled through the first couple innings of Wednesday's start against the Cubs but cruised toward the end of his five-inning outing. His velocity was down from his Opening Day start, but he still had some success with his slider.

home_pitcher_note: The weather forecast calls for 72 degrees and partly cloudy. That's much better than last year, when Marquez struggled through 27 degrees and lost to the Braves in the Rockies' 2018 home opener.
away_pitcher_note: Fried will attempt to build off his stellar six scoreless innings against the Cubs last Thursday. The lefty retired the first 17 batters he faced and allowed only one hit. Increased fastball velocity has enhanced the value of his curveball.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija came away with a no-decision in his previous start on Saturday after yielding three runs over 4 2/3 innings against the Rays. He is 4-6 with a 4.00 ERA in 17 games (13 starts) against the Rockies in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Gray started strong against the Dodgers in his last outing, but mistakes in the strike zone in the last inning-plus left him with five runs allowed over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Pomeranz, who spent the first three years of his career with the Rockies, will face his former club for the first time since 2016. He is 2-0 with a 1.29 ERA in four career appearances (two starts) against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Bettis struggled with location while walking four and giving up six runs on seven hits in 2 2/3 innings at home against the Dodgers last time out to raise his ERA to 11.88 after his first two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner is still looking for his first win of the season after yielding five runs over six innings against the Padres on Monday. He is 13-8 with a 3.04 ERA in 30 career starts against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland, who has dropped his last two starts after a nine-game win streak dating back to last season, gave up a career-high seven runs in five innings in his last start against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Holland delivered his longest start of the season for San Francisco on Tuesday, striking out nine and allowing just one run over seven innings against the Padres. He is 1-2 with a 6.23 ERA in four starts against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez is going from a team he struggles against (the Braves, 7.56 ERA) to a park where he struggles (0-3, 7.52 ERA at Oracle Park). His last start ended a string of 15 starts with three or fewer runs against.

home_pitcher_note: Lucchesi became the fourth starter in Padres history to open a season with consecutive scoreless outings. Then he was roughed up by the Giants for seven runs. Still, Lucchesi is the team's most reliable starter. He has 17 Ks in 14 1/3 IP.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela came down with an infected blister on his right heel in Spring Training, but he's up after two Triple-A starts. Senzatela made a postseason start last year and is bidding to stay in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Margevicius could join Chris Young (2010) and Dave Dravecky (1984) as Padres starters to allow one run or fewer in their first four outings. The rookie averages just 88 mph with his fastball, but he has allowed one run in all three of his starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies have only scored two runs in Gray’s three starts this season, all losses. Gray is set to face the Padres for the first time this season after going 4-1 against them with a 3.26 ERA in five 2018 meetings.

home_pitcher_note: Chad Bettis is being skipped to keep Freeland on schedule. Freeland left his last start, a loss to the Giants, after five innings with a left middle finger blister, but he has healed and will start the homestand.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin had a 0.75 ERA through his first two starts before allowing 10 hits and six runs in just four innings Saturday against the Marlins. Eflin thought he had good stuff, despite the fact that Miami hit three home runs off him.

home_pitcher_note: Using pinpoint control with top-level velocity, Marquez held the Giants to one hit and struck out nine on Sunday. In his last home start, however, he yielded an uncharacteristic two homers vs. the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez had a no-hitter through five innings Sunday against the Marlins. He has pitched well so far, posting a 2.25 ERA after three appearances (two starts). It is an encouraging start for a rotation that has struggled this season.

home_pitcher_note: Senzatela showed excellent fastball command and effectively used his curve and slider while shutting down the Padres for 6 2/3 innings Monday in his Major League season debut.
away_pitcher_note: Nola's early-season struggles have been baffling, considering he pitched so well last season. Nola says he is healthy, but for some reason he has had trouble commanding his pitches and throwing strikes. They need him to get going on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Gray has allowed one run in each of his last two starts, spanning 13 2/3 innings. He gave up five runs over six innings in his only home start this season.
away_pitcher_note: Eickhoff makes his first start since joining the rotation after the team optioned Nick Pivetta on Wednesday. Eickhoff is a bulldog on the mound who will fill the strike zone with his fastball, curveball and slider.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson was activated from the injured list to make the start after left knee inflammation had affected his performance.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Hellickson’s first career start at Coors Field. He has transformed himself into a very consistent starter since joining the Nats, giving up three runs or fewer in all but two of his 21 career starts in D.C.

home_pitcher_note: Hoffman, called up from Triple-A, was 0-2 with a 13.89 ERA over 11 2/3 innings in three games with Albuquerque.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin has plenty of experience pitching at Coors Field, but not much success. In 11 games (10 starts) in Colorado, he owns a 6.55 ERA and 1.655 WHIP. Overall, he has made 21 starts against the Rockies in his career, the second most against any team.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez battled through five innings while suffering from pain from an infected tooth in his last start, an eventual Rockies win over the Phillies. The tooth has been pulled, and at 2-1 with a 2.25 ERA he can smile easily.
away_pitcher_note: In two career starts at Coors Field, Sanchez owns a 3.46 ERA with 13 strikeouts and four walks.

home_pitcher_note: Fried has been one of baseball's top early-season surprises. The lefty has increased the velocity of his four-seam fastball and has routinely fooled hitters with his big curveball. He's worked at least six innings in each of his first four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela ran a high pitch count in his last start, but just one pitch -- a breaking ball for Phil Gosselin's three-run double -- cemented a home loss to the Phillies. He is 3-1 with a 1.77 ERA in his last six road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz will be making his season debut. The All-Star hurler missed most of Spring Training because of a right elbow bone spur that began bothering him in his Feb. 24 spring debut.
away_pitcher_note: The advanced numbers look good. Gray's 183 ERA-plus is 83 percent above league average. He has yielded just 23 hits in 32 1/3 innings pitched. For traditional stats, he has 30 strikeouts to 13 walks and a 2.78 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Gausman battled inconsistent velocity and struggled early to command his splitter during Tuesday's loss in Cincinnati. The Denver native will be making his first career start against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: His return from a left knee injury, when he lasted three innings plus three batters in a no-decision against Washington, was a struggle. Anderson’s challenge is to use his fastball aggressively in the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander remained Milwaukee's only reliable starter after a no-decision against the Cardinals on Tuesday left him with a 1.65 ERA through five starts. Davies has not allowed more than two runs in any of his outings.
away_pitcher_note: Kyle Freeland is set to come off the 10-day injured list (left middle finger blister) to start Monday. Freeland has a 1.50 ERA against the Brewers in two career starts, but has never pitched at Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin will look for his first scoreless outing of the year in his seventh start on Tuesday in Milwaukee. He lasted four innings, allowing four runs, in his last start against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Righty German Marquez, who is set to face Venezuelan countryman Jhoulys Chacin, struggled at points early in his last start. But in the end, he held the Nationals to three runs and fanned seven in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson will be making his third start since returning to the rotation after beginning the season in the bullpen. In two starts this season, Anderson has gone 9 2/3 innings, allowing just two runs.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela's last start, a win at Atlanta, called for maturity. He didn't agree with the plate umpire's strike zone, but modified his pitches and got batters to swing. In three starts, he has an adjusted ERA+ of 130.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta is healthy again after dealing with a minor shoulder/chest injury and ready to rejoin the rotation. His Major League debut came against the Rockies a year ago on Mother's Day, a 13-strikeout gem at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Gray yielded two home runs and lasted 4 2/3 innings in Atlanta on Saturday, but the Rockies came back to win. He gave himself an "F" grade in all categories. Manager Bud Black said he wasn't that bad, but his command could improve.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has allowed at least five runs in each of his first four starts. His longest outing is five innings. Opponents are hitting .361 against him, and he has allowed six home runs over 16 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ray got the win last time out against the Cubs when he allowed three runs on five hits over five innings. Over his career, Ray is 1-1 with a 4.15 ERA in five starts at Coors Field and 3-4 with a 5.77 ERA vs. the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland allowed five runs on six hits in six innings on Monday in his first start off the injured list in a loss to the Brewers. Right-handers are hitting just .176 against the southpaw, while lefties are hitting .407.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver got a no-decision in his last start against the Cubs at Chase Field. He allowed three runs on six hits over 4 1/3 innings. All of the runs came via the home run -- a two-run shot by Kris Bryant and a solo homer by Willson Contreras.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez retired the first 15 hitters without a ball being hit past the Rockies' infield in his last start  on Tuesday, but he allowed four runs between the sixth and seventh innings. Marquez still has an impressive 1.55 ERA in four road starts and a 5.29 ERA in three outings at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke outdueled the Yankees’ CC Sabathia in his last start. Sabathia recorded his 3,000th career strikeout in the game, but Greinke got the win, his fifth of the season, after allowing just one run over 7 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Senzatela escaped a few jams without much damage in his last start against Milwaukee, but he couldn't qualify for the win because he needed 86 pitches to go four innings. His stuff is fine, but his efficiency needs improvement. He is 5-0 vs. the Giants in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner shined last Wednesday, striking out eight while holding the Dodgers to one run over six innings. His 18 swinging strikes were his most since Sept. 19, 2016. Bumgarner has a 3.03 ERA in 31 career starts against Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Gray received an early lead and defeated the Brewers in his last start, but his few bad pitches were hit hard. He pitched well against the Giants, allowing one run and five hits in 6 2/3 innings with six strikeouts on April 11.
away_pitcher_note: Holland will be activated off the injured list and return to the rotation after missing one start with a left index finger bone bruise. He has a 6.18 ERA in five career starts against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland hasn't been sharp in two starts since returning from a left middle finger blister. He has left clusters of pitches up in the zone, but he has also shown spurts of well-placed deliveries.
away_pitcher_note: Holland will be activated off the injured list and return to the rotation after missing one start with a left index finger bone bruise. He has a 6.18 ERA in five career starts against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies pushed back RHP Jon Gray to keep Marquez on his regular turn. Marquez is trying to rebound from giving up two homers -- but otherwise pitching well -- in a no-decision against Arizona in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Lauer's numbers aren't noticeably better than his rookie season, but his walks and hits are down while his K rate has stayed the same. That leaves some optimism for a breakout. Lauer returns to Colorado for the first time since his MLB debut.

home_pitcher_note: A rainout this week meant Gray’s start was pushed back from Wednesday, so he’ll face the Padres on extra rest Saturday. Against the Padres, Gray is 9-3 with a 2.59 ERA in 16 career starts -- and 4-1 with 2.74 ERA in eight home starts.
away_pitcher_note: In two Coors Field starts, Lucchesi owns a 1.50 ERA. The Padres believe strongly in his stuff, and perhaps he's experienced some rough batted-ball luck lately. But they desperately want Lucchesi attacking the strike zone a bit more.

home_pitcher_note: After beginning the year on the injured list with an infected right heel blister, Senzatela faced the Padres in his season debut and gave up one run and six hits -- and fanned four -- in 6 2/3 innings of a win at Petco Park.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie left-hander continues to baffle hitters with his four-pitch mix, even if none of those four pitches would qualify as electric. Generally pinpoint with his command, Margevicius has seen a spike in his walk rate lately.

home_pitcher_note: The ace lefty had his best start of the season last time out, when he struck out 14 and allowed three hits over eight innings against the Orioles. After a brutal slump to open the season, Sale has a 1.73 ERA in his last four starts. Sale hasn't faced the Rockies since 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland had his moments in his last start, a no-decision in a 12-11 win over the Giants. But correcting the tempo of his delivery, an issue that has created inconsistent location, is still a work in progress.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty took a big step last time out in his goal to be more economical when he threw seven innings for the first time since 2017 in a win over the Mariners. Rodriguez has been stellar at Fenway Park this season, going 3-0 with a 2.59 ERA
away_pitcher_note: Marquez entered this week with a 1.14 WHIP, in the National League's top 30. He has succeeded because the hits generally come on weak contact and he can get a strikeout (59 in 57 2/3 innings) when the situation calls.

home_pitcher_note: Irvin impressed in his big league debut Sunday, allowing just one run over seven innings against the Royals. Manager Gabe Kapler said the lefty "earned the opportunity to get additional looks" for a potential spot in the Phillies' rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Gray earned the win when he held the Phillies scoreless over six innings in their last matchup on April 21. He is 2-2 on the road this season with a 4.40 ERA, and he is winless in his career at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Nola lasted just three innings following a 52-minute rain delay on Monday vs. the Brewers. It marked the third time in nine starts this season that the Phillies' ace has pitched four or fewer frames -- something he didn't do once in 2018.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela gave up four runs and seven hits over six innings in his last outing against the Phillies on April 20. After that loss, he has recorded a win in two of his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff struggled for the first time this season on Tuesday against the Brewers, allowing five runs in just four innings. That matched the total number of runs he had given up in his first 30 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland won against the Phillies on April 18, when he struck out seven and allowed only two hits in six scoreless innings. He also did not allow a walk. The lefty is 1-1 with a 3.71 ERA in three day games this season.

home_pitcher_note: Archer went just 3 2/3 innings on Wednesday at Arizona in his first start after spending time on the injured list (right thumb inflammation). He allowed seven runs (six earned), four hits and four walks. His walk rate is a career-worst 4.7 per nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez gave up five early runs at Boston in his last start, then settled in and lasted 6 1/3 innings. His 2.55 road ERA ranked sixth in the National League.

home_pitcher_note: DuRapau will serve his second stint as the Pirates' opener after a successful first effort Saturday in San Diego. DuRapau struck out four over two scoreless innings against the Padres, setting up a well-executed bullpen game that the Bucs won, 7-2.
away_pitcher_note: Gray struck out eight but lasted just 4 2/3 innings in his last start, a loss at Philadelphia. He has high strikeouts (59 in 53 1/3 innings), but also has given up 10 home runs in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles is coming off his best start with the Pirates -- seven innings, one run, five hits, one walk and a career-high 12 strikeouts on Friday at San Diego. He’s pitching up in the zone with his fastball, making his curve and other offspeed stuff more effective.
away_pitcher_note: Battling a Phillies lineup that took close pitches and worked counts, Senzatela threw 101 pitches over five innings in his last start. But he limited the damage to two runs.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies called up Hoffman from Triple-A Albuquerque to make the start Friday against Baltimore. It will be his second big league outing this season.
away_pitcher_note: Has there been a bigger surprise in baseball than John Means? A non-prospect heading into this season, the rookie southpaw has been a revelation for the pitching-starved Orioles. Means is 5-4 with a 2.68 ERA overall.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off the shortest non-injury-affected start of his career, Freeland hopes to master the delivery changes he is trying. He is at home at Coors -- his 3.51 home ERA is the lowest by any Rox starter (minimum 100 IP).
away_pitcher_note: Cashner may be pitching his way on to a contender thanks to a revamped four-pitch mix that includes a four-seam fastball clocking in the high-90s again. His Opening Day clunker aside, Cashner is 4-1 with a 3.40 ERA over his past eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez had his fastball working so well early against the Pirates (eight scoreless innings) that he could afford to give his curve three innings to come around. He has been the Rox’s best starter this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Orioles are desperately hoping Hess turns things around, given their lack of rotation depth. Now the right-hander faces his largest challenge yet, the Majors' leader in home runs allowed is set to make his first career start at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: As part of a seven-inning, seven-strikeout performance in a win at Pittsburgh in his last start, Gray averaged 97.1 mph on his fastball. That's the first time the heater averaged such velocity in two years.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke has been outstanding over his last seven starts, going 4-1 with a 1.49 ERA. He has held opponents to a .175 batting average over that stretch. Greinke took the loss last time out despite allowing three runs over seven innings at San Diego.

home_pitcher_note: If inconsistency is central to the human condition, Senzatela has been most human in his last four starts. In two of them, he had a 3.09 ERA, with nine hits in 11 2/3 innings. In the others, he yielded 15 earned runs in eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kelly lasted only 1 2/3 innings in his last start against the Padres as he allowed four runs on five hits. Prior to that, he had allowed three runs over two starts (12 1/3 innings). This is Kelly's first career appearance against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: The last start was forgettable. Hoffman toughed out five innings, allowing five runs on seven hits, but his team pulled out a win. Hoffman simply missed location with all pitches, and will need to be better.
away_pitcher_note: Ray got the win in his last start against the Giants, when he allowed two runs over 5 1/3 innings. Over his last four starts, he is 2-0 with a 2.25 ERA. He started once at Coors Field this year on May 3 and got the win.

home_pitcher_note: While Freeland has been understandably angry at himself, manager Bud Black, coaches and teammates have to get him to see there have been good sequences with the fastball and slider -- and understand how he can produce more.
away_pitcher_note: Clarke has been impressive over his first two career starts, posting a 3.65 ERA in outings against the Rays and Giants. All three of Clarke's big league appearances have come on the road, and this will be his first against the Rockies.

away_pitcher_note: Freeland had a solid outing in his start vs. the Giants on Sunday, allowing two runs over five innings in a Rockies win. Freeland, who had a rough July that produced an 8.66 ERA over four starts, will be making his first start vs. the Padres of 2019.

home_pitcher_note: Paddack gave up a career-high 6 earned runs his last time out against the Dodgers, which raised his ERA to a season-high 3.19. He’s at 104 1/3 innings, up from his previous Minor League career high of 90, which means he’s likely approaching a threshold.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez returns to starting duty after taking the loss in relief Tuesday at Houston. He has allowed no more than three earned runs in any of his four starts, but the Rockies lost all four. His longest outing came in his last start, 5 2/3 innings at Cincinnati on July 27.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander struggled after returning from Tommy John surgery last month. But he finally pieced it all together last week against the Mariners. Lamet carried a no-hitter into the seventh and tied a career high with 12 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez allowed five runs over five innings in his most recent start at Houston on Aug. 6. The right-hander last faced the Padres on June 15, earning the win despite allowing seven runs over 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lambert aims to bounce back from the toughest start of his rookie season. He allowed nine runs and issued four walks, both career highs, in three innings last Wednesday at Houston. He'll face NL West foe Arizona for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing seven runs in each of his previous two starts, Kelly yielded four runs (three earned) on eight hits over six innings in a 7-3 loss to the Phillies at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: This start goes to Hoffman in place of Jon Gray, who was pushed back due to left ankle soreness. Hoffman, still seeking his first quality start of the season, was optioned following his last big league start, on July 25.
away_pitcher_note: Gallen was aquired from Miami on July 31. He had an impressive Arizona debut when he tossed five shutout innings against the Phillies at Chase FIeld during a 6-1 D-backs win.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland had a quality start Friday at San Diego, allowing three runs in six innings. He’s 3-3 with a 5.40 ERA in 10 career starts vs. Arizona and is 1-4 with a 6.91 ERA in six starts since returning from the Minors.
away_pitcher_note: Ray did not get a decision last time out against the Dodgers. He held them to just two runs over six innings during a game the D-backs rallied to tie in the ninth and win, 3-2, in the 11th.

home_pitcher_note: Gray missed his scheduled start Tuesday with ankle soreness. After an eight-inning win against the Dodgers, he has thrown a combined 9 2/3 over two subsequent starts. He pitched five solid innings in San Diego before yielding four unearned runs in the sixth.
away_pitcher_note: Since the All-Star break, Alcantara has a 6.29 ERA. The Marlins' lone All-Star had a 3.82 ERA in the first half. But Alcantara also is coming off one of his best performances, three runs in 7 2/3 innings in a no-decision against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Marquez has the only Rockies win in the eight games through Tuesday, pitching eight innings of three-run ball in San Diego on Sunday. He gave up five hits and two walks while fanning nine. He retired 11 in a row at one point and was particularly effective with his breaking ball.
away_pitcher_note: The 32-year-old makes his third start since being promoted from Triple-A New Orleans, where he was 11-4 with a 3.82 ERA. In his last outing on Sunday against the Braves, he worked six innings and gave up five earned runs. Noesi was hurt by two homers in the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Lambert pitched five innings of three-run ball against the D-backs on Monday, but five walks (one intentional) to one strikeout highlighted his inconsistency. Four walks came in the D-backs' two-run fourth inning. He’s walked 12 in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Yamamoto started off winning his first four decisions this season, but has since leveled off. In his last five starts, the rookie is 0-4 with an 8.28 ERA, including eight home runs. The downturn began on July 21 at the Dodgers. He has a 3.54 ERA on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Gallen held his own at Coors Field last time out, working into and out of trouble to hold the Rockies to two runs over four innings. Opponents are batting .212 against him through his first nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez once again is back in the Majors to fill out the rotation. In his last start, he gave up five runs on eight hits with two walks and three strikeouts in five innings of a no-decision at San Diego.

home_pitcher_note: Young is looking to bounce back after a pair of subpar starts. Over his last two games, he is 0-2 with a 9.72 ERA. Last time out against the Giants, he allowed five runs on eight hits over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Recent starts suggest a couple of ways in which Freeland is emerging from the struggles of the early season -- he has full confidence in his mechanics and his changeup is becoming a weapon.

home_pitcher_note: Leake will make his fourth start since coming over from the Mariners in a deal consummated just minutes before the Trade Deadline on July 31. Last time out against the Giants, he allowed four runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Melville, 29, was called up from Triple-A hours before the game to fill in for Jon Gray, who went on the injured list with a broken left foot. Melville pitched in six MLB games in 2016-17, recording an 11.05 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Mikolas has struggled in his past two starts, giving up 11 runs (10 earned) to the Pirates and Reds, with eight of those runs coming from home runs. On Saturday, Mikolas extended his streak of games with two or fewer walks to 40, breaking the Cardinals' record.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez is looking to stay on a roll, as he's 4-0 with a 3.32 ERA over his last six starts. He's struck out 43 and walked only five during that span. The right-hander is 2-0 with a 1.53 ERA in three career starts vs. the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Flaherty has been among MLB's most dominant second-half starters. In his last eight starts, he has posted a minuscule 0.89 ERA over 50 1/3 innings. Flaherty has struck out 61, walked only 14 and limited opponents to 25 hits during that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Lambert is coming off some solid sequences in his last outing, when he held the Marlins to six hits and three runs in six innings of a no-decision. He gave up a run early in three innings, but didn’t let it grow into more.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson twirled one of the best starts of his young career on Monday when he finished 6 2/3 no-hit innings. It marked the second straight scoreless outing for Hudson, who paces the Cardinals' rotation with 12 wins.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez retired 14 straight at one point in his last start, when he commanded all his pitches while going six innings (two runs, three hits) at Arizona in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: Wacha threw his first scoreless start since June 10 on Tuesday against the Brewers, when he gave up three hits and struck out five in four innings. He's firmly reinstated himself in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies are expected to call up righty Antonio Senzatela from Triple-A Albuquerque to start the series finale. Senzatela has spent a month correcting issues with his delivery and honing offspeed pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Working in a Phoenix-area barbecue joint before being signed by the Rockies in May, Melville was called up from Triple-A on Wednesday and held the D-backs to one run and two hits over seven innings. He also had his first Major League hit.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran held the Rockies hitless before enduring a six-run fifth inning at Coors Field on April 8. The veteran hurler has allowed two earned runs or fewer in eight of his last 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia, 10-6 with a 4.23 ERA in 25 starts across Double-A and Triple-A this season, will be making his Major League debut.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello made a mistake to Bryce Harper and paid for it with two-run homer that cost him the game last time out. This is Porcello's second career start at Coors Field. The first one didn't go well, as he gave up eight hits and nine runs over three innings in 2011.

home_pitcher_note: The adjustment to the Majors seemed smooth when Lambert won his first two starts, but an inability to get batters to chase has led to an alarming walk rate recently.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez has been brilliant lately, allowing no runs over 14 2/3 innings in his last two starts, both wins. The lefty is 11-2 with a 3.14 ERA in his last 17 starts. Rodriguez made his only career start against the Rockies earlier this season, giving up nine hits and five runs over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez, trying to re-establish himself in the Majors after missing time with Tommy John surgery, needs to limit his walks. In eight games (seven starts), the 27-year-old has allowed 21 free passes against 20 strikeouts in 35 Major League innings.
away_pitcher_note: Williams owns a 7.21 ERA in 11 starts since returning from the injured list, but he returned to form Saturday by working six scoreless innings against the Reds. He allowed five runs over 6 2/3 innings in his only career start at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Senzatela can run a fastball better than 97 mph. However, he has bounced between the Rockies and Triple-A Albuquerque this season because he has yet to learn to miss bats.
away_pitcher_note: Agrazal rejoined the Pirates' rotation with an up-and-down start against the Reds on Sunday. The rookie allowed four runs on seven hits over five innings, but he struck out five -- tying his season high -- and picked up his third win of the year.

home_pitcher_note: Melville has posted a 0.75 ERA in two starts, all while throwing his fastball below 92 mph but mixing in a slew of secondary pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Musgrove bounced back from a rough outing vs. the Nationals with a solid start against the Phillies, permitting two runs on five hits while striking out six in six innings on Monday. He has a 3.93 ERA on the road this year, compared to 5.35 at home.

home_pitcher_note: Hoffman last pitched in the Majors on Aug. 13, when he allowed seven runs in two innings vs. Arizona. He pitched three games at Triple-A Albuquerque before rejoining the Rockies for September.
away_pitcher_note: Brault has arguably been the Pirates' best starter since late May, putting together a 2.84 ERA over his last 12 starts. Even without his best stuff on Tuesday, the lefty limited the damage to three runs in five innings against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Buehler was dominant in his last two starts, tossing a combined 13 scoreless innings against the Blue Jays and Padres. He struck out 19 and walked only two. He is 2-0 with a 4.58 ERA in three starts vs. the Rockies this year.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Lambert, 22, gave up five runs in 4 1/3 innings in a loss to the Red Sox. But after his walk rate skyrocketed in previous starts, he walked just one vs. Boston.

home_pitcher_note: Urias returns from suspension to start the second game of the series against the Rockies. He has made only six starts this season, this being the first since July 30, the longest being six innings. He's expected to go three innings. Kenta Maeda was originally to make this start, but he's been moved to the bullpen to prepare for serving that role in the postseason.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez has to fight the trend of his last two starts, which saw him last a total of five innings and give up 12 runs on 10 hits, with seven walks against two strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Ryu is enduring his toughest stretch of the season, as he is 0-3 with an 11.05 ERA over his last three starts. He's given up five of his 15 homers allowed during that stretch, and he is 0-1 with a 4.50 ERA in three starts vs. the Rockies this year.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela, who started a postseason game last year, took a step back this season (much of it in Triple-A). Success in his final few starts will be measured not only by numbers but by whether he can figure out how to use his secondary pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Lamet has made 10 starts since his early-July return from Tommy John surgery. He notched a 5.09 ERA in the first five outings. His 3.54 mark in the last five is more than a run and a half better. Lamet struck out 10 Giants in his last time out.
away_pitcher_note: After posting a 0.75 ERA in his first two starts after being called up from Triple-A Albuquerque, Melville gave up seven hits and five runs in two innings against the Pirates in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: In six August starts, Lucchesi posted a 3.58 ERA, and he was one of the Padres' most reliable starters. In his most recent outing, Lucchesi escaped a bases-loaded jam in the sixth, finishing with six innings of one-run ball against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Hoffman gave up a home run on his first pitch in his last start, at home against the Pirates, but ended up giving up just two runs in five innings. He is internalizing adjustments to make his motion more efficient.

home_pitcher_note: Lauer hasn't taken a loss since July 25, going 3-0 with a 4.45 ERA in seven games (six starts) since then. However, the left-hander has struggled against the Rockies this season, going 0-2 with a 14.90 ERA in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lambert, 22, has struggled to a 10.36 ERA in his last six starts. But he and manager Bud Black both point out that Lambert is taking the right lessons and not losing confidence.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies have lost all nine of Gonzalez’s starts. But both his quality starts have come in his past four outings, including a two-run, 6 1/3-inning effort vs. the Dodgers last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Wacha pitched on three days' rest last time out and was limited to two scoreless innings. He'll be on normal rest against the Rockies, against whom he has posted a 5.28 ERA in six career outings (five starts).

home_pitcher_note: Senzatela had a 4.83 ERA through June, but he has a 16.55 ERA in six starts since, with 41 hits allowed in 20 2/3 innings. Left-handed hitters are batting .371 against his fastball this season.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson has demonstrated some of his best pitching in the Cardinals' run to the postseason. He has a 3.23 ERA in 11 second-half starts, including his one-hit effort over six scoreless innings on Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: Melville held the Padres to two runs in 5 2/3 innings last time out, with a career-high eight strikeouts. He used his four-pitch mix to keep batters off-balance, which helped him get 11 swing-and-misses with his slider.
away_pitcher_note: Mikolas issued a season-high four walks against the Pirates on Friday, but manager Mike Shildt said there was no concern and his starter "wouldn't give in" to batters. He lasted five innings and allowed one run.

home_pitcher_note: Hoffman had a strong outing his last time out in L.A., holding the Dodgers to three runs on five hits over 5 2/3 innings. He struck out a career-high eight and walked only two. He has a 1.50 ERA in two games against San Diego in Denver, allowing one run over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Despite a career-high five walks, the left-hander pitched six scoreless frames against the Rockies last time out. He owns a 1.57 ERA over his last four starts, even as he's moved well past his previous career high in innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lambert held the Padres to one run on five hits and three walks while striking out four over five innings on the road on Sunday. Lambert has not won since winning his first two big league starts, June 6 and 11, both against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Coors Field isn't exactly a pitchers' paradise, but it's been extra tough on Lauer, whose 19.73 ERA there is the highest all-time among pitchers with three starts. Lauer is coming off six innings of one-run ball vs. the Rockies on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez earned his first big league win since 2015 with a 2-1 victory at Coors Field Tuesday, holding the Cardinals to one run on four hits and no walks over six innings. He threw 6 1/3 innings of two-run ball in his previous road start against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Quantrill had solidified himself as one of the rotation's most reliable arms in the second half, allowing eight runs over seven starts. But since then, he's allowed eight runs in three straight starts, the first Padre to do so since Andy Benes in 1993.

home_pitcher_note: After spending the year seeking the right combination of secondary pitches to complement his fastball, Senzatela employed his slider and curve expertly while holding the Cardinals to one run and four hits in six innings in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Four of Matz’s last five starts have come at home, where he’s 7-1 with a 1.94 ERA this season. By contrast, Matz is 3-7 with a 6.08 mark on the road, and his next start will come at one of the most unforgiving road parks in baseball -- Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Melville succeeded in his early outings by staying low in the strike zone. What happens when he's up? Well, four home runs in three innings against the Cardinals in his last outing serve as a cautionary tale.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Stroman recorded an out in the seventh inning for the first time since joining the Mets. The team has implored him to generate more outs early in counts, which he did with success in that start against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: While he has had heavy base traffic, Hoffman's recent outings have been more competitive. Hoffman is coming off a win over the Padres in his last start. He walked six in 5 1/3 innings but held the damage to four runs.
away_pitcher_note: Syndergaard specifically asked to pitch to Tomas Nido or Rene Rivera last time out, but the Mets gave him Wilson Ramos and it didn’t end well. Syndergaard has a 5.20 ERA throwing to Ramos this year, and a 2.22 mark pitching to the other two.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw got back on track in his last start, holding the Mets to two runs in 6 1/3 innings to snap a three-start losing streak. He's only pitched against the Rockies once this season, going seven innings but allowing five runs in a loss in June.
away_pitcher_note:
Forced into the rotation because of injuries to others, the 22-year-old Lambert has struggled 
with location. The Rockies like his mental toughness but need him to clean up his delivery issues.

home_pitcher_note: Buehler's only tough start over his last six outings came against the Rockies on Sept. 2. He allowed six runs in five innings, but he still earned the win. Last time out, the right-hander allowed two runs on two hits in five innings in a no-decision against the Mets.

After three consecutive losses, Ryu got back on track with seven scoreless innings against the Mets in New York last time out, allowing only two hits. He still hasn't notched a win since Aug. 11, but his last outing was an encouraging one.
away_pitcher_note: Despite his struggles, Senzatela has seen his offspeed pitches improve. He can steal a strike with his slider, and he has increased the frequency of his curveball.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner will make his penultimate start of the season against the Rockies as the Giants kick off their final homestand. San Francisco is 19-14 in his starts this year but has lost his last three outings.
away_pitcher_note: Hoffman has gotten through five innings in each of his four starts since rejoining the Rockies in September. In those games, he has a 4.64 ERA (11 earned runs in 21 1/3 innings), with 18 strikeouts and 10 walks.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija will make the final start of his 2019 campaign on Wednesday. The 34-year-old veteran is 6-7 with a 3.89 ERA in 20 career appearances against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Melville has given up seven home runs in his last two starts, which seems concerning. But it might not be an issue Wednesday. Those homers were at Coors Field, where he has served up eight of the nine long balls hit off him this season.

home_pitcher_note: Beede will close out his rookie season on Thursday with his third career start against the Rockies. He was charged with the loss in his most recent start against Colorado on Aug. 4, when he yielded five runs over 3 2/3 innings at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland was sharp in his return from the injured list on Sept. 21, holding the Dodgers scoreless in two innings. Twenty-one of his 29 pitches went for strikes. He'll be limited to a range of 45-60 pitches against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Senzatela's late-season trial has seen some high moments, but his last start -- four runs, seven hits in four innings against the Dodgers, after entering the fifth scoreless -- was not one of them. Location and change of speeds haven't been consistent strengths.
away_pitcher_note: Davies needs 7 1/3 innings to qualify for the ERA title. If he finishes short of 162, the Brewers will have zero qualifying pitchers for the first time in franchise history.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, González entered after Kyle Freeland's brief start and shut down the Dodgers -- five innings, two unearned runs and two hits in the Rockies' only victory this season at Dodger Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez has a 1.47 ERA in his first five September appearances, the last two of which were out of the bullpen following Brandon Woodruff. This will be the lefty's fourth career start at Coors Field, where he has a 4.60 ERA over 15 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hoffman left his last start, against the Giants, after 3 1/3 innings when he was hit on the outside of the right knee with a line drive. But ball missed bone, and Hoffman won't miss his final start.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers are holding Brandon Woodruff for either a tiebreaker game or the NL Wild Card Game and starting Houser in Game 162, which requires a win and a Cardinals loss to the Cubs to extend Milwaukee's division hopes.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn is making his first career Opening Day start. It will also be his first start against the Rockies since 2017. He is 2-2 with a 2.76 ERA and a 1.16 WHIP against Colorado over seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Márquez will make his first Opening Day start and first regular-season appearance against the Rangers at their new ballpark. Last season, Márquez went 7-3 with a 3.67 ERA in 15 road starts, and he finished with 175 total strikeouts in 174 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Minor was an All-Star and the Rangers’ Pitcher of the Year in 2019. He has made seven career starts and two relief appearances against the Rockies and is 3-2 with a 5.24 ERA and a 1.30 WHIP.
away_pitcher_note: Father's Day 2018 was a low point for Gray, when a four-run lead through five turned into a deficit, en route to a 13-12 Rockies loss to the Rangers. New year, new park, new Gray, who comes off a 135 ERA+ in '19.

home_pitcher_note: Kluber makes his first start for the Rangers after being acquired from the Indians last winter. He will be taking the mound for the first time since May 1, 2019, vs. the Marlins when he was hit by a line drive, fracturing his right arm.
away_pitcher_note: Walks and poor location led to a 3-11 record and a 6.73 ERA in 22 starts last season. In preparation for this season, Freeland's fastball and a more effective changeup are more reminiscent of his 17-win 2018.

home_pitcher_note: Expected to begin the season in the bullpen, Mengden instead finds himself back in the rotation due to A.J. Puk's shoulder strain. Mengden went 5-2 with a 4.83 ERA in 13 games (nine starts) for the A's in 2019.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela hopes his step back last season (6.71 ERA) leads to a forward leap. He's developed his curve and regained his changeup -- two pitches that should help his development.

home_pitcher_note: Montas will look to go deeper in his second start of the year after 81 pitches limited him to just four innings in the A's Opening Day win over the Angels. This will be his second career start against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Márquez took a no-hitter into the sixth inning on Opening Day and gave up just two hits and one run in 5 2/3 innings in that outing vs. Texas.

home_pitcher_note: The Opening Day starter in 2017 and '18, Gray gets the '20 home opener. At Texas on Saturday, he grew fatigued but still just yielded one run on three hits in 4 2/3 innings. Three walks is high, though, for a strike-thrower.
away_pitcher_note: In his 10-year career, mostly with the Angels, Richards has never pitched at Coors Field. He was sharp in his first outing, using two dominant breaking pitches to hold Arizona scoreless over five.

home_pitcher_note: After fanning five in six solid innings against Texas in his first start, Freeland faces a team that has not been easy for him. He's 2-3 with a 4.09 ERA in nine games (seven starts) against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start, Lucchesi worked only 3 2/3 frames, and it's possible the Padres continue to limit his workload. He's been strong in his first two trips through an opposing order but has struggled after that.

home_pitcher_note: The early pitch count was a concern, but some encouraging info came from Senzatela's five innings in a win at Oakland. He didn't have his best fastball early, but secondary pitches carried him.
away_pitcher_note: Davies' Padres debut was a smooth one on Tuesday. He held the Giants to three runs (two earned) over five-plus innings. He's made only one appearance at Coors Field, allowing one run and two hits in five frames for Milwaukee last September.

home_pitcher_note: The decision came down to González or Jeff Hoffman. González’s 2019 late-season surge, his spring and summer outings and his pitch mix won him the decision.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto came away with a no-decision after allowing four runs over 3 2/3 innings against the Padres on Wednesday at Oracle Park. He is 5-2 with a 3.26 ERA in eight career starts at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Márquez has pitched superbly in his first two starts. He will be starting on five days' rest. Manager Bud Black gave the extra day because the games have been tight.
away_pitcher_note: Gausman will make his second career start for the Giants, seeking his first win of the season. Gausman has never pitched at Coors Field before.

home_pitcher_note: Gray had a resourceful 5 2/3 innings against the Padres last time out. He wanted to rely on off-speed stuff but didn't have it. So he pumped fastballs, and only an inning of poor defense cost him runs.
away_pitcher_note: Webb struggled with his command Friday in his second start of the year, yielding two runs (one earned) and walking four over 3 2/3 innings against the Rangers. He was picked up by the Giants' bullpen, which  combined for 5 1/3 scoreless innings of relief. Webb has pitched 7 2/3 innings over two starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: A Denver native, Freeland lost his Coors Field magic last year (2-4, 9.25 ERA in 10 starts). But his first home start of '20 was impressive: six innings, no runs, two hits, four strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson, a former first-round Draft pick of the Rockies, will make his first start against his former team as the Giants go for a split of this four-game series on Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: Kikuchi pitched one of his best games since signing with Seattle on Saturday against the A's with 6 scoreless innings on 3 hits, 1 walk and 9 strikeouts, with 20 swing and misses among his 89 pitches. This will be his first time facing the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela fanned six -- one shy of his career high -- and held the Padres to one run in six innings in his last start. He has nine strikeouts in 11 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Margevicius moves from the bullpen to fill in for the injured Kendall Graveman. The 24-year-old posted a 6.79 ERA in 17 outings (including 12 starts) last year for the Padres after being jumped from Double-A ball to the big leagues.
away_pitcher_note: Castellani had cleanup surgery on his right elbow last year. Since, he has had a strong Arizona Fall League, Spring Training and Summer Camp. He subs for Chi Chi Gonzalez (right biceps tendinitis).

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old rookie breezed through 4 scoreless innings with 1 hit before getting KO'd in the fifth by the A's on Monday. He's 0-3 with a 6.18 ERA in his first 10 games with the Mariners, including 9 starts since being promoted late last year.
away_pitcher_note: Márquez fanned nine in 7 1/3 innings to lift the Rockies to a 5-2 victory over the Giants at Coors Field in his last outing. His slider forced seven swings and misses, and was called for strikes 16 times. His fastball topped out at 97.8 mph.

home_pitcher_note: Gray has been strong at Coors Field. His .694 home winning percentage is second in club history to Jorge De La Rosa's .726. But in five home starts against the D-backs, he is 0-2, 6.08.
away_pitcher_note: Ray continues to tweak his mechanics in search of what will get him back on track. In addition to a shorter arm path, he has added a glove tap to his delivery. In his last start, he got the win despite allowing six runs in five frames vs. the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland will be fueled by how his last start ended. Scoreless through 6 2/3 against the Giants, two were on and manager Bud Black kept him in. He yielded a first-pitch Mauricio Dubón homer, which ended his chance at a win.
away_pitcher_note: Gallen once again turned in a quality outing last time out against the Astros, allowing two runs on six hits over six innings. Gallen has one career start at Coors Field in which he allowed two runs in four innings on Aug. 13, 2019.

home_pitcher_note: Senzatela is one of seven Rockies starters since 2000 to begin a season 3-0. He has held opposing hitters to a .227 batting average in his three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver threw three innings in his last start, which was the plan after he struggled in the fourth inning in his first two starts of the year. Whether he will be allowed to pitch deeper in this outing remains to be seen.

home_pitcher_note: Castellani went four-plus innings in his Major League debut Saturday, without allowing a hit or runs. An injury replacement, Castellani was limited to 60 pitches. The ceiling should rise to around 75.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn started against the Rockies on Opening Day and threw six scoreless in 1-0 victory. He allowed two hits, four walks, and he struck out nine. Lynn is 1-1 with a 2.84 ERA in four career starts in Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: The last time he faced the Rangers on Opening Day, Márquez limited Texas to two hits and one run in 5 2/3 innings. He hasn't given up more than two earned runs in any of his three starts since.
away_pitcher_note: Gibson is making his first career start against the Rockies. He has made 20 career starts against National League teams and is 4-11 with a 5.40 ERA and a 1.59 WHIP.
