away_pitcher_note: Senzatela held the D-backs to four hits in eight scoreless innings on April 7, but he is 2-4 with a 5.08 ERA in nine career games at Chase Field. He uncharacteristically walked three in five innings against the Phillies in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner tossed a seven-inning no-hitter in his last start against the Braves in the second game of a doubleheader on Sunday. The only baserunner the Braves got was Ozzie Albies, who reached on a throwing error by Nick Ahmed.
away_pitcher_note: Gray's growth this season was seen in a win over the Phillies in his last start. He gave up two Bryce Harper solo homers, but no other runs in six innings of a win. Gray searched for his slider early, but he avoided base traffic.

home_pitcher_note: Gallen was outstanding in his last start in the first game of a doubleheader against the Braves. Gallen allowed just one hit and two walks while tossing a seven-inning shutout for his first win of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Gomber has had three solid starts and two tough ones. His last outing was the latter -- nine runs allowed on seven hits and four walks in 1 2/3 innings at San Francisco. His curveball, which gets strikes and weak contact, did not bite.

home_pitcher_note: Kelly had his best start of the year last time out against the Padres, as he held them to just one run on four hits over six innings. He faced the Rockies earlier this year and allowed six earned runs in six innings at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: In three starts, González has posted a 3.00 ERA with his pitch-to-contact, ground-ball style. In his only previous career start at Chase Field on Aug. 19, 2019, González allowed two runs over six innings in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: In last Wednesday's loss, Márquez had a tough second inning in which he gave up four runs -- two on bases-loaded walks, which he had only one of in his career prior to that. The right-hander now faces the Giants for the second straight start.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez gave up only one hit over 4 2/3 innings in his last start Tuesday against the Rockies, but he issued a season-high five walks, which led to two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Castellani is making his season debut after getting called up to serve as the 27th man on the roster for the doubleheader.
away_pitcher_note: Wood took a no-hitter into the sixth inning Wednesday vs. the Rockies in his last start, striking out a season-high nine batters. The Giants have won each of his three starts this year.

home_pitcher_note: Gray is a strike-thrower. He doesn't walk many, and decisions come quickly. But last time out at Arizona, he gave up five runs (four earned) on nine hits in a loss. This start, he'll be back at Coors Field, where he has a 1.85 ERA this season.
away_pitcher_note: Webb gave up three runs over six innings in his last start against the Padres on Friday. He is 2-0 with a 4.35 ERA in four career appearances against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Flaherty was dynamite yet again last Saturday, getting better as the game went on, with nine strikeouts against the Pirates. Most encouraging? The Cardinals' bats have given him ample support this season, scoring 61 runs in his first six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gomber will face his old club for the first time since being part of the deal that sent third baseman Nolan Arenado to St. Louis. Gomber has to improve his performance on the road, where he is 1-2 with a 7.20 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: How strong is the Tsunami now? Martínez is riding an immaculate three-game stretch, allowing only two earned runs for a 0.84 ERA as well as a 0.750 WHIP in the string of starts. Last time out? Eight shutout frames against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: A pitcher who wins with finesse rather than power, González has generally been effective a couple of times through the lineup. However, in his last start at Arizona on Sunday, some poorly located pitches led to him lasting just 4 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright earned his first win of the season on Monday despite allowing five runs over 5 2/3 frames. Call it a pick-me-up after he took a nine-inning complete-game loss -- the first by a Cardinal since he did the same in 2007 -- on April 26.
away_pitcher_note: The past two starts have been rough for Márquez -- two walked-in runs in one, eight runs and just two outs in another. Both were against the Giants, but Márquez's real problem has been a delivery flaw that has cost him command.

home_pitcher_note: Senzatela will make his first start since going on the 10-day injured list with a right groin strain on May 1. The righty is 7-2 with a 3.08 ERA in 15 games (nine starts) against San Diego for his career.
away_pitcher_note: Lamet, who dealt with right forearm tightness last month, pitched two innings in his return from the IL last Tuesday, but his velocity dipped noticeably in the second. Jayce Tingler said Lamet's leash will be dependent on the cold, rainy weather in Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Gray has been effective at Coors, going 4-0 with a 2.08 ERA so far this season. He also has pitched at least six innings in each of his last four outings.
away_pitcher_note: Darvish has been the Padres' best pitcher this season, though he's coming off his first start in which he didn't complete at least six innings since Opening Day. Darvish has not allowed a hit to the last 75 hitters who reached two strikes against him.

home_pitcher_note: Gomber has struggled through seven outings, but Friday's loss in St. Louis was his first start without a walk this year.
away_pitcher_note: Snell walked six and allowed four runs for the first time as a Padre on Friday night against the Giants. But despite his early struggles, Snell's stuff remains as hard to hit as ever, as he allowed only one hit against San Francisco.

home_pitcher_note: González has struggled with the first batters of innings this year -- 16 of the 30 he has faced have reached base. González believes a swing-and-miss pitch to end long at-bats is the correction he needs.
away_pitcher_note: Castillo is still searching for his old form. In seven starts this season, he has allowed four earned runs or more in four of his outings. In two previous starts against the Rockies, Castillo has allowed 10 earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Márquez put an end to a period of uncharacteristic control problems when he struck out six and held the Cardinals to two runs in six innings on Sunday. For the most part, Márquez was effective with his breaking ball.
away_pitcher_note: Miley, coming off last Friday's no-hitter against Cleveland, in which he tallied eight strikeouts to one walk and threw 114 pitches, gets an extra day of rest for this start.

home_pitcher_note: Jhoulys Chacín will make his first start of the 2021 season after having already made six appearances out of the bullpen for the Rockies. In his career as a starter, he has posted a 4.03 ERA in 226 career starts. He has a 75-86 record as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: Mahle went 5 1/3 innings on Monday, when he gave up one run in a win against the Pirates. In all but one of his seven outings this season, Mahle has pitched at least five innings, but has struggled at home, posting a 4.32 ERA in three home starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his return from a right groin injury, Senzatela was scoreless for his first four innings Tuesday before giving up a Manny Machado two-run homer in the fifth and putting the first two batters on before exiting in the sixth.
away_pitcher_note: Hoffman gave up three runs on four hits and two walks against the Pirates on Tuesday. He has pitched past the fifth inning only once this season and he'll look to give the Reds some distance in the finale of the four-game series against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: After five straight outings in which he lasted at least six innings and allowed one run or fewer, Darvish hasn't completed the sixth in consecutive starts. That said, he has been the Padres' most reliable starter. They've won seven of his eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gray faces the Padres for the second straight game, this time at Petco Park. He mostly dominated Wednesday at Coors Field -- just one of the four runs charged to him was earned, with the other three crossing the dish on a grand slam yielded by the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: It has been a grind for Snell this season, as evidenced by his 15% walk rate and the fact he's yet to complete six innings. But, for the most part, Snell has managed to limit the damage. He has 49 strikeouts over just 34 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gomber has been up and down this season, but his last start was solid with six strikeouts and one run (zero earned) allowed in 5 1/3 innings in an eventual team home win over the Padres. Gomber has struggled across five road starts (1-3, 7.56 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Musgrove averaged 6.5 innings in his first four Padres starts. He averaged 4.5 over his next four. Musgrove's biggest issue has been command. His breaking pitches remain electric, but in his last start, he threw more first-pitch balls than strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Keys for González are early contact and grounders. In his last start -- seven scoreless innings in a home win over the Reds -- González threw 88 pitches and forced 10 ground-ball outs. Prior to that outing, he had not gone more than five innings in any start.

home_pitcher_note: Márquez’s ERA is a career high, but he has pitched well in two starts since an eight-run outing on May 4 vs. the Giants. He has gone six innings in his past two starts with a 3.75 ERA and 14 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Frankoff makes his second start of the season after allowing two runs in 4 2/3 innings pitched against the Nationals on Saturday. Manager Torey Lovullo was encouraged by Frankoff's ability to attack the zone.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies are 1-7 in Senzatela’s starts, but he is coming off a quality start vs. the Reds on Sunday (seven innings, one run). His slider (.610 opponents’ slugging) has been far less effective than in years past.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner exited his last start early after having a spasm in his left adductor muscle. The left-hander felt the injury during his pregame warmups, but he made it through four innings against the Dodgers before leaving the game.

home_pitcher_note: Gray has thrived at Coors Field (4-1, 2.00 ERA in six starts), including 6 2/3 innings of one-run ball vs. Arizona on April 8. He’ll look to bounce back from a seven-run outing on Monday in San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Widener will come off the IL to start after missing a month due to a right groin strain. The right-hander posted a 2.82 ERA in four April starts, his first opportunity to be a member of a big league rotation.

home_pitcher_note:
The lefty is 1-1 with a 3.95 ERA (six earned runs in 13 2/3 innings) with five walks and 16 strikeouts in three starts at home. He's holding right-handed hitters to a .200 (22-for-110) batting average
compared to a .375 (12-for-32) mark against fellow southpaws.
away_pitcher_note: Gomber has quietly put together a solid streak this month. In his last four starts, he is 1-1 but has a 3.22 ERA and a .227 batting average against.

home_pitcher_note: deGrom missed two Major League starts because of right side tightness. He had a rehab assignment on Thursday and struck out eight of the 10 batters for Low-A St. Lucie. deGrom also threw a bullpen session on Sunday in Miami without any problems.
away_pitcher_note: The development of a changeup took Freeland to a higher level last year, but a left shoulder strain that he sustained on March 23 during a Spring Training game has kept him sidelined. Freeland was strong in two injury rehab starts at Triple-A Albuquerque, and his 2021 debut with the Rockies will come against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Stroman will pitch Game 1 of Thursday's doubleheader after his originally scheduled start on Wednesday was postponed. He is 0-2 with a 3.86 ERA in May, after going 3-2 with a 1.86 ERA in April.
away_pitcher_note: Maybe a horrid game against the Giants isn't so bad for Márquez. After giving up 11 runs in 2 2/3 innings on July 15, 2019, Márquez posted a 1.80 ERA in his next three outings. His ERA is 2.37 in three starts since giving up eight runs in two-thirds of an inning on May 4.

home_pitcher_note: The Mets have been careful not to let Lucchesi see an opposing lineup more than two times through the order. Last time out, they limited him to four innings and 43 pitches despite a dominant, scoreless performance.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela spent all his last outing searching and experimenting, and mostly succeeding. He didn't give up a run until three scored in the sixth in a no-decision against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Brubaker will look to rebound and get some run support after losses in his last two outings.
away_pitcher_note: Gray has a sparkling 2.36 ERA at Coors Field, but he will need to improve his 6.36 road ERA. While he has found some consistency at Coors, he has not spotted his fastball and slider as well away from home.

home_pitcher_note: Keller gave up eight hits, including two homers, against the Braves in a five-run start last time out. It was the first time all year he gave up more than one home run in a start.
away_pitcher_note: In April, Gomber walked 18 in 23 innings pitched, and a 6.65 ERA over five starts was the result. Gomber, whose past does not suggest being walk-prone, has issued just three walks in 30 1/3 May innings and has a 2.97 ERA in five starts.

After missing the first seven weeks with a left shoulder strain, Freeland held the Mets to one run in four innings in his first start Tuesday. The Mets didn't offer at his changeup, which drove up his pitch count. Expect more fastball usage.

home_pitcher_note: Márquez will take the mound against the Rangers, whom he faced twice last season with some success -- he gave up three earned runs in 11 2/3 innings (2.31 ERA). Since a poor outing against the Reds on May 14, the right-hander has looked more like himself, posting a 0.69 ERA over his past two outings.
away_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old right-hander is scheduled to make his 11th start of the season in the series opener at Colorado. He's looking for a bounce-back outing after allowing a career-high seven runs to the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Senzatela has struggled to find his 2020 form so far this season, and he will look to put a difficult May behind him -- (4.91 ERA in four starts). He'll be making his first career start against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles has gradually gone deeper into games, notching six-inning starts over his last three outings. Over that span, he's lowered his ERA from 6.63 to 5.79.

home_pitcher_note: Gomber gave up a first-pitch homer in his last start -- a loss at Pittsburgh -- but over his last four starts, he has a 1.93 ERA with 26 strikeouts and three walks across 23 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz has hit his stride in his last two starts, yielding only nine hits, two runs and three walks with four strikeouts through 14 innings. He looks to carry that momentum into a start against Colorado in the final game of the Rangers’ road trip.

home_pitcher_note: Gray, coming off a rough start at Pittsburgh (3 ER, 4 H, 3 BB in 3 IP), would seem to be in an interesting comfort zone for this one. He is 4-1 with a 2.36 ERA in seven starts at home, and he is 8-1 with a 3.06 ERA against American League teams.
away_pitcher_note: Montas has taken the loss in his last three starts but has pitched well over that stretch, posting a 3.24 ERA. He's 0-2 with a 4.82 ERA in two career starts against Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland missed the season's first seven weeks with a left shoulder strain and has made two encouraging, if inefficient road starts. He has gone four innings in each, throwing 74 and 84 pitches with seven walks against six strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Irvin is looking to shake off a tough stretch over his last three outings in which he's allowed at least four earned runs in each start.

home_pitcher_note: In his last five starts, Márquez has a 1.97 ERA, has struck out 35 and walked 12, and held opposing batters to a .202 batting average. The uncontrollables haven't always broken his way in that span: He is 2-2 and the team is 3-2.
away_pitcher_note: Kaprielian is looking to bounce back from what was his shortest outing of the season his last time out, lasting just 3 2/3 innings and allowing four runs in a loss to Seattle. Still, the rookie has been solid since joining the club last month, posting a 2.95 ERA through his first four starts.

home_pitcher_note: López, who was originally slated to start Monday's makeup game in Boston, received an extra day of rest. He struck out a career-high-tying nine batters last Wednesday against the Blue Jays, but he lasted just four innings.
away_pitcher_note: After a rocky start to the season, Senzatela has put together a consistent run of strong outings, posting a 2.28 ERA over his last four starts. The right-hander has never started against the Marlins, but in four career relief appearances against them, he's given up two runs on three hits over nine innings.

home_pitcher_note: With Cody Poteet on the injured list, Garrett will fill in. Miami's seventh-ranked prospect made two starts in 2020, and a three-inning-relief outing last month in Los Angeles.
away_pitcher_note: Gomber looks to continue a tremendous run over which he owns a 1.53 ERA in five starts since May 12. He's only made one appearance against Miami in his career, giving up two runs over an inning of relief while with the Cardinals in 2018.

home_pitcher_note: The reigning two-time NL Rookie of the Month retired 13 of the last 14 batters he faced following a two-out, two-run single by Bryan Reynolds in the second on Saturday. That was Rogers' only mistake across six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez will make a spot start for the injured Jon Gray, who is on the 10-day injured list with a right forearm flexor strain. Gonzalez was hit hard in his last relief appearance, which came when Gray was injured last Friday -- he gave up three runs on seven hits over 4 1/3 innings against the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Since giving up seven earned runs in two innings on May 20, Mahle is 3-0 with a 1.04 ERA in his last three starts. During Saturday's 5-2 win, he allowed two earned runs over seven innings and threw first-pitch strikes to 20 of 27 batters.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland will start the series opener against the Reds. He wasn’t sharp in Saturday's start against the A's, giving up five runs on 10 hits to go with one walk and one strikeout on 80 pitches (49 strikes).

home_pitcher_note: Miley tossed five scoreless innings in his last start Sunday against the Cardinals and exited with a seven-run lead, but he ultimately took a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Márquez was brilliant in Colorado’s 3-1 victory over Oakland to avoid a sweep on Sunday. The right-hander yielded one run on four hits, while walking one and striking out six in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Reds will call up Santillan -- their No. 9 prospect -- from Triple-A Louisville to make his Major League debut. A big right-hander, he has a 2.51 ERA in six starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela pitched six innings and allowed four runs on nine hits with a career-high eight strikeouts in a loss to the Marlins on Tuesday. That’s a pretty high number of K’s since he is considered a ground-ball pitcher.

home_pitcher_note: Since May 12, Gomber is 3-1 with a 1.57 ERA (fifth lowest in the National League over that span). And in four home starts, he is 2-1 with a 1.33 ERA, while limiting opponents to a .149 batting average.
away_pitcher_note: Lamet had his longest outing of the season last time out, pitching five-plus innings and allowing four runs against the Cubs. The right-hander pitched five scoreless innings, but he was unable to record an out in the four-run sixth.

home_pitcher_note: The Marlins touched González for eight runs in five innings in his last start on Thursday. But in five games, including two starts at Coors Field, González is 2-0 with a 2.95 ERA, with four double-play grounders in 21 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Darvish is coming off a masterful performance against the Cubs, his former team, allowing just two runs across seven innings with eight strikeouts. Darvish's last outing in Denver was his shortest of the year, only going four innings and allowing one unearned run in Game 1 of a doubleheader.

home_pitcher_note: Freeland's first four starts since his return from a left shoulder strain have been a struggle, as he's posted a 9.00 ERA. The problem is simple -- poor location. He tied a club record by giving up five homers on Friday at Cincinnati.
away_pitcher_note: Snell couldn't record an out in the fifth inning of his last outing, in which he allowed three earned runs and three walks across four-plus innings. After the game, Snell said he was more comfortable on the mound and that his best starts are yet to come.

home_pitcher_note: Márquez had a 1.89 ERA over his previous six starts before matching a season high with eight earned runs (in five innings) at Cincinnati on Saturday. But many of the hits off him were soft, and a seeing-eye double through a drawn-in infield accounted for the final runs.
away_pitcher_note: Woodruff's 1.52 ERA and 0.72 WHIP is the best of the Brewers' three aces. He's coming off seven efficient innings last Friday against the Pirates, in which he threw 98 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Senzatela has a 3.83 ERA in 47 home innings this year, as opposed to a 6.94 in 23 1/3 road innings. One difference is he has kept the ball in the park at Coors (two home runs) as opposed to other parks (five).
away_pitcher_note: Burnes is coming off a four-inning outing against the Pirates in which he was charged with four runs (three earned), marking his first outing all season in which he didn't complete at least five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Remember when the going wisdom was curveballs were not good at Coors Field? Well, according to MLB Quality of Pitch, Gomber's knuckle curve ranks in the top four percent in MLB in overall quality.
away_pitcher_note: Since allowing a season-high six runs against the Reds on May 21, Houser has a 1.71 ERA in his last four outings, one of which was an extended relief appearance.

home_pitcher_note: González's simple toughness won him points in his last start. He yielded four runs in the first two innings against the Padres on Tuesday, but four scoreless innings later, the Rockies had a chance to win.
away_pitcher_note: The big inning has been Lauer's undoing in many of his Brewers starts. He surrendered four runs in his first two innings against the Reds his last time out, then rebounded to pitch three scoreless frames.

home_pitcher_note: Flexen is coming off the best start of his career, throwing eight shutout innings with eight strikeouts against the Twins. The right-hander has been a reliable innings eater in recent starts, going at least six innings in each of his last four outings.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland's re-entry to active pitching has been difficult -- a 9.58 ERA in five starts after recovering from a left shoulder strain. But he has faced the Mariners twice, both in Seattle, and is 1-0 with a 2.45 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Sheffield was lit up in his last start against the Twins, allowing a season-high seven earned runs on 10 hits in five innings. Sheffield has allowed two home runs in each of his three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Márquez held the Brewers to one hit and no runs over six innings in his last start before leaving with cramps -- something that has happened on several occasions at Coors Field. Seattle may be less of a problem.
